## Completion summary

Issue #7 has been implemented as a **derived clarification of existing authority**, not as a new product decision.

### What changed

- The canonical execution-form term is now **mechanical execution**. It denotes executable, non-agent-mediated progression and does **not** imply computational determinism, output determinism, an identical path, an identical trace, replay, or run reproducibility.
- The canonical control term is now **workflow-owned control** / **workflow-declared orchestration**. It constrains global progression to possibilities authorized by executable workflow semantics; it does not require one possible successor.
- Probabilistic, nondeterministic, externally dependent, event-driven, LLM-produced, and agent-produced results may select among declared continuations. Their origin or variability neither makes a consuming mechanical rule agent-mediated nor grants the producer global orchestration authority.
- Explicit main-agent and independent-agent regions retain local semantic/discretionary authority to explore, edit, test, react, and choose tactics. That local authority does not authorize implicit reconstruction or modification of the enclosing graph.
- An underspecified global control point that expects an agent to infer what the workflow should do next remains non-conformant.
- No completion/handoff mechanism, fairness rule, liveness guarantee, executable TLA+ model, or new invariant was introduced.

### Authority and affected artifacts

Normative product contract modified:

- `docs/specification/turnlock-spec.md`

Existing invariant identities preserved and clarified:

- `TL-INV-001` — workflow-owned control may admit multiple runtime results/continuations, but each global transition must be workflow-authorized;
- `TL-INV-002` — executing a declared rule against runtime data is not topology invention;
- `TL-INV-003` — mechanical execution is non-agent-mediated, not computationally deterministic;
- `TL-INV-013` — local agent discretion is permitted, hidden global agent orchestration is not;
- `TL-INV-030` — identity preserved; title updated to **Workflow-owned-control / probabilistic-result invariant** and wording broadened from probabilistic leaves to varying runtime results selecting declared continuations.

Synchronized formal/explanatory artifacts:

- `formal/verification.yaml`
- `docs/formal/invariant-mapping.md` (generated)
- `README.md`
- `docs/adr/README.md`
- `docs/vision/turnlock-vision.md`

No accepted ADR body was edited. Historical wording is retained and explicitly interpreted through the current consolidated specification.

### Terminology inventory and classification

<details>
<summary>Relevant current and historical uses</summary>

| Surface | Uses | Classification / current interpretation |
|---|---|---|
| Spec §0.1, §0.7, §0.10, §2.4, `TL-INV-003`, `024`, `029`, `031`, short form | mechanical execution/work/step | Execution class defined by executable progression without missing agent-supplied orchestration judgment. It may be deterministic, nondeterministic, probabilistic, externally dependent, or event-driven. |
| Spec §0.8, §0.8A, §0.10A–D, §2.7, `TL-INV-001`, `002`, `013`, `019`, `027`, `030`, `031`, `032` | workflow-owned/workflow-declared control and orchestration | Authority property: permitted global continuations originate in executable workflow semantics. Multiple outcomes and continuations are allowed. |
| Spec §0.10D, §2.4, `TL-INV-003`, `030` | probabilistic/nondeterministic/external/event/LLM/agent results | Result variability and origin are independent of orchestration authority. Results may select but do not create declared possibilities. |
| Spec §0.8, §2.7, `TL-INV-006`, `013`, `030`, `032` | local agent authority/discretion | Legitimate inside declared agentic regions; it does not confer implicit global scheduling or graph-rewriting authority. |
| Remaining current-spec uses of `deterministic` | explicit contrasts, optional deterministic operations, and non-goals | They negate an implied guarantee or acknowledge that a particular operation may genuinely be deterministic; none defines the mechanical class or workflow-owned control as mathematically deterministic. |
| ADR-001 | “mechanical steps can remain deterministic” | A mechanical operation may genuinely be deterministic; this is not a requirement on all mechanical execution. |
| ADR-004 | “deterministic control”, “progressively more deterministic”, mixed deterministic/agentic wording | Historical reliability/control shorthand. The accepted decision itself says the invariant is execution authority and non-agent mediation, which controls the current interpretation. |
| ADR-005 and ADR-007 | “deterministic code” / “determinism outside agentic regions” | A genuinely deterministic operation remains possible; broader class/control shorthand is clarified by the current spec as mechanical execution and workflow-owned progression. |
| ADR-011 and ADR-014 | deterministic orchestrator/workflow/orchestration | Historical term for workflow-owned, workflow-declared global control rather than output or trace determinism. |
| ADR-012 | deterministic computation spectrum; deterministic orchestration/control; deterministic escalation | The spectrum's current consolidated term is mechanical execution. Control/escalation wording means declared orchestration rules; the ADR explicitly rejects deterministic leaf-output requirements. |
| ADR-013 | deterministic computation/code and deterministic orchestrator/orchestration | Mechanical execution or workflow-owned control according to context; “deterministic code for exact work” remains an example of an operation that may genuinely be deterministic. |
| ADR-017 and governance/tooling prose | deterministic projection; mechanically invertible/checkable | Literal tooling/reproducible transformation terminology, unrelated to TURNLOCK execution-form or control-authority semantics. |

All accepted ADR bodies remain immutable historical records. No conflicting accepted requirement for identical outputs, traces, replay, or a single successor was found.

</details>

### Formal handoff to #1

The following existing planned property names remain planned and require #1's property-level review under the clarified authority semantics:

- `DeclaredControlFlowOnly`
- `EngineDoesNotInventTopology`
- `MechanicalExecutionNotAgentMediated`
- `AgentCannotAdvanceUndeclaredGlobalControl`
- `ProbabilisticLeafCannotOwnGlobalControl`

`formal/verification.yaml` now records that their future formulas must authorize global control transitions without requiring one successor/output/schedule/trace, must permit varying results to select declared continuations, and must preserve legitimate local agent discretion. No property was marked `modeled` or `checked`, and no planned property name was opportunistically migrated in #7.

### Future run-evaluation boundary

The separate exploration is preserved at:

- `docs/vision/future-workflow-run-evaluation.md`

It is explicitly **non-normative**, has **no authority**, records **no accepted product decision**, creates **no TURNLOCK semantics**, and creates **no invariant**. It separates core orchestration correctness from optional future run observability, property-relative comparability, and reproducibility/evidence profiles. YADA-core / Implicit-Free Execution is cited only as a conceptual precedent.

No guarantee of run comparability, reproducibility, content-addressed workflow definitions, persisted activations, replayable external operations, mandatory metrics, or run proof was added to TURNLOCK core.

### Discovery classification

- #7 terminology clarification: `derived-from-existing-authority` (`normative-contract`, with synchronized `formal-model-or-analysis` and documentation effects).
- Durable run-evaluation exploration: `no-normative-impact` (`repository-governance-or-documentation`).
- Any future standard run model, event contract, stable identity, comparison/reproducibility profile, persistent log, or execution-proof obligation: `decision-required` unless independently derived from then-current authority; deliberately unresolved here.
- Exact TLA+ formulas and property-level obligation/evidence structure remain formal-model choices owned by #1; they were not promoted into normative semantics.

No additional unresolved product ambiguity was discovered in #7. Existing open completion/handoff and fairness/liveness questions remain untouched.

### Validation and publication

Executed successfully:

```text
python3 -m venv .venv
.venv/bin/python -m pip install --requirement requirements.txt
.venv/bin/python scripts/render-formal-mapping.py
.venv/bin/python scripts/adr-metadata.py render
.venv/bin/python scripts/tests/test-adr-metadata.py  # 12 tests, OK
.venv/bin/python scripts/adr-metadata.py check       # 17 structured ADRs, OK
.venv/bin/python scripts/check-formal-traceability.py # 32 invariants, OK
git diff --check
```

Additional checks confirmed 32 stable invariant IDs, no `checked` formal status, no executable `formal/Turnlock.tla`, no accepted ADR-body change, and a clean synchronized `main` at `5b9a001`.

Published commits directly relevant to this work:

- `6a68bcf` — primary normative terminology clarification;
- `26a0ef6` — non-normative future run-evaluation note;
- `5b9a001` — formal traceability and explanatory synchronization.

## Handoff from #7 — control-authority terminology clarified

Issue #7's derived clarification is published on `main` at `5b9a001` (primary semantic change in `6a68bcf`; formal synchronization in `5b9a001`).

The following planned properties remain owned by #1 for property-level obligation/evidence classification and semantic-correspondence review:

- `DeclaredControlFlowOnly`
- `EngineDoesNotInventTopology`
- `MechanicalExecutionNotAgentMediated`
- `AgentCannotAdvanceUndeclaredGlobalControl`
- `ProbabilisticLeafCannotOwnGlobalControl`

Constraints established by current authority and recorded in `formal/verification.yaml`:

1. The formulas must constrain every global control transition to workflow-authorized semantics; they must not encode one successor, output, schedule, path, trace, or replay.
2. Runtime inputs, results, state, and events may select among continuations already declared by executable workflow semantics. Selection is not invention of topology.
3. Mechanical execution means non-agent-mediated executable progression, not computational determinism; it may consume probabilistic, nondeterministic, external, event, LLM, or agent results.
4. Declared main-agent and independent-agent regions retain legitimate local semantic/discretionary authority. `AgentCannotAdvanceUndeclaredGlobalControl` must not prohibit that local judgment.
5. `ProbabilisticLeafCannotOwnGlobalControl` is retained as a planned name for #1's review and must not be read as exhausting the broader varying-result rule.

No TLA+ identifier was added or renamed, no formula/model was introduced, no property became `modeled` or `checked`, and no fairness/liveness choice was made by #7.

Validated and completed. The canonical terminology registry, non-authoritative review inventory, checker, regression tests, and repository governance updates are published on `main` through commits `43372a9`, `e28d8e0`, `3aab18e`, and `b16927e`. Repository-required validation and independent semantic review passed.

## Dependency pressure from accepted execution inspectability

ADR-018 and `TL-INV-033` now distinguish actual completed execution behavior from a workflow definition displayed during later inspection.

The derived constraint is narrow:

```text
an inspection surface must not present a later/current workflow definition alone
as proof of what a previous execution actually did
```

This makes Issue #4 consequential to future inspection design because a trustworthy surface may need to establish which definition governed relevant execution points. It does **not** decide Issue #4 or imply snapshot semantics, live-edit semantics, SHA-256/Git identity, a revision object, copy-on-start, or another binding mechanism.

Issue #4 remains the B-class authority gate for definition binding. No blocked-by relationship is asserted: ADR-018's minimum product intent can be accepted while the binding mechanism remains undecided, provided later inspection work does not conflate a current definition with historical execution truth.

Published authority: ADR-018 and specification Sections 3.31 and 5.15 in commits `fdeb8b3`, `20cc8a6`, and `4cb5800`.

## Resolution — product decision ratified and synchronized

The product decision is made: a completed TURNLOCK execution must not become opaque. TURNLOCK exposes execution truth at its own semantic boundary; the user or a higher-level system keeps evaluation criteria, comparison, and optimization.

### Published authority

- **ADR-018** — `docs/adr/adr-018-require-completed-workflow-execution-inspectability.md` (accepted, 2026-09-14). Outgoing relations: none (this is a new decision; it does not retroactively "clarify" ADR-001/ADR-014). The optional/profiled alternative, native evaluator/optimizer, concrete tracing architecture, reasoning visibility, and replay/comparability/reproducibility/proof alternatives were all evaluated and rejected with justification.
- **Normative specification** synchronized: §0.13B (product intent, refinement loop), §0.2 (governing promise completed), §2.9 (canonical term `execution inspectability`), §3.31 (`TL-INV-033`), §4 (reopened and sharpened boundaries), §5.15 (architectural implication), §6 (non-goals), §7 (product test), §8 (synopsis).
- **`TL-INV-033` — Completed-execution inspectability invariant** admitted through the classification pass: one distinct universal obligation, with the full derivation recorded in ADR-018 under "Derived invariant admission". Illustrative boundary facts receive no separate invariant identity.
- **`formal/verification.yaml`**: conservative entry, `partial` / `pending-model` / `not-yet-modeled`, planned property `CompletedExecutionExposesActualBoundaryFacts` only. The manifest does not claim TLA+ proves semantic sufficiency for evaluation.

### Files changed

| Commit | Files |
| --- | --- |
| `fdeb8b3` | `README.md`, `docs/adr/README.md`, `docs/adr/adr-018-require-completed-workflow-execution-inspectability.md` (new), `docs/adr/index.md`, `docs/vision/future-workflow-run-evaluation.md` |
| `20cc8a6` | `docs/specification/turnlock-spec.md`, `docs/specification/terminology-inventory.yaml` |
| `4cb5800` | `docs/formal/invariant-mapping.md`, `formal/verification.yaml` |
| `857f81e` | `scripts/tests/test-adr-metadata.py` |

The last fix repairs a governance test whose "unlisted ADR" fixture hard-coded `adr-018-unlisted-record.md`; it now collides with the real ADR-018, so the fixture derives the next retained number. Without it the suite failed for an identifier-availability reason, not a behavior change.

### Validation executed

```text
.venv/bin/python scripts/tests/test-adr-metadata.py          → OK (12 tests)
.venv/bin/python scripts/tests/test-normative-terminology.py → OK (13 tests)
.venv/bin/python scripts/adr-metadata.py check               → OK (18 structured, 0 legacy)
.venv/bin/python scripts/check-normative-terminology.py      → OK
.venv/bin/python scripts/check-formal-traceability.py        → OK (33 invariants)
git diff --check                                             → clean
```

Generators executed: `scripts/adr-metadata.py render`, `scripts/render-formal-mapping.py`, and regeneration of `terminology-inventory.yaml` from the registry. Independent hostile review passed after corrections (PASS), plus a dedicated Oracle audit.

### Downstream discovery classification (A/B/C/D/E)

**A — derived from accepted authority (no new invariant identity beyond TL-INV-033)**

| Discovery | Derivation |
| --- | --- |
| Every completed execution exposes enough actual TURNLOCK-visible behavior for practical understanding/evaluation without recollection. | Directly accepted statement; the single distinct universal obligation; admitted as `TL-INV-033`. |
| An inspection surface must not present a later/current definition alone as proof of what a previous execution actually did. | "Actual behavior" would otherwise be falsely represented; folded into `TL-INV-033` without a separate identity. |
| Scope covers workflow-mediated structure, execution boundaries, explicitly exposed inputs/results, and progression-relevant TURNLOCK-visible facts. | Accepted scope of the statement; no universal event catalog. |
| Evaluation criteria, comparison, and optimization remain outside TURNLOCK core responsibility. | Directly accepted responsibility boundary; recorded in ADR-018 and §0.13B. |

**B — decision-required**

| Discovery | Routing |
| --- | --- |
| Exact minimum fact set and sufficiency criteria per workflow shape. | **Issue #13** (new, Backlog/Specification/Follow-up/P1). |
| Applicability to failed, cancelled, interrupted, or otherwise non-completed executions. | **Issue #13**; ADR-018 explicitly limits the decision to "completed" and leaves this open. |
| Minimum availability, retention, access, and privacy semantics. | **Issue #13**; distinct from storage mechanisms. |
| Visibility inside agentic regions beyond explicitly exposed results and boundary facts. | **Issue #13**; private reasoning is not required. |
| Workflow-definition binding for active invocations. | **Issue #4**; pressure comment published; no snapshot/live-edit/identity semantics selected. |
| Provenance strength, definition/revision identity, authenticity, execution proof. | Remains a consequence of #4; undecided, unpromoted. |
| Native evaluation API, metrics, run comparison, experiments, optimization. | Existing **Issue #12**, retained as a separate Backlog/Specification/Finding/P2 authority. |
| Replay, cross-run comparability, reproducibility profiles, execution proofs. | Explicitly non-implied; remain orthogonal open questions listed in §4, unpromoted. |

**C — formal/modeling choice**

- Abstract representation of boundary facts (state/history) and the formally checkable subset of `TL-INV-033`: `partial` + `pending-model` in the manifest, planned property only.
- Executable TLA+ identifiers, bounds, and configurations will be chosen with the model; none was invented to make traceability look complete.

**D — implementation/architecture choice**

- Event schema, persistent log, database, telemetry, timestamps, IDs, hashes, serialization, query API, UI: explicitly replaceable and not decided by ADR-018. None of `Run`, `RunSpec`, `RunProof`, `runId`, `activationId`, event sourcing, OpenTelemetry, SQLite, workflow SHA, content addressing, revision IDs, canonical timestamps, retention policy, replay engine, comparability, reproducibility levels, experiment framework, evaluation profiles, or automatic optimization was established.

**E — integration/conformance constraints**

- Every supported harness must realize the abstract inspectability contract without claiming private-reasoning visibility; an adapter limitation cannot weaken core semantics.
- Future conformance must distinguish actual execution facts from reconstruction or a current definition presented as proof; the exact test mechanism remains open.

### Preserved non-decisions

No event, storage, retention, identity, replay, comparability, reproducibility, proof, or optimization semantics were created because they were convenient. The non-normative note `future-workflow-run-evaluation.md` was corrected only where it contradicted the new authority (accepted minimum vs. stronger layers still open); its speculative layers were not promoted.

### Related work

- **#4**: definition-pressure comment published; binding undecided.
- **#12**: retained as the authority for the native evaluation/optimization question.
- **#13**: created for minimum inspectability semantics (fact set, sufficiency, non-completed outcomes, retention/access/privacy, agentic-region visibility).

All acceptance criteria of Issue #11 are satisfied.

## Priority rationale — reclassified `P2` → `P1`

**Scope:** work-management classification only. This comment records no product
semantics and does not resolve the boundary this Issue tracks.

### Why `P1`

The engineering profile defines `P1` as "should be completed in the current
phase". The Project's `Now` view is filtered to `Phase: Specification`, so the
current phase is the Specification phase, and this item is a Specification-phase
product-intent decision gate.

`P1` also matches the Project's convention for Specification-phase items that
are not blockers of the pre-TLA+ semantic-readiness sequence:
[#13](https://github.com/fanilosendrison/turnlock-rust/issues/13) is
`Specification / Follow-up / P1`.

### Why not `P0`

The Specification-phase `Finding` items currently at `P0` are the
semantic-readiness decisions tracked by
[#9](https://github.com/fanilosendrison/turnlock-rust/issues/9): #2, #4, #5, #6,
and #8. ADR-018 does not make the native evaluation/optimization question one of
those blockers, and no current correctness, authority, traceability, or
verification invariant is compromised while it remains open.

If that assessment changes — that is, if this decision is later found to block
model or specification progress — the classification should be raised to `P0`
at that point.

### Changed provenance

Issue #11 was resolved on 2026-09-14 by ADR-018 and `TL-INV-033`. ADR-018
accepts evaluable completed execution as the universal minimum and explicitly
reserves the native evaluation/optimization question as a separate product
decision. #11's resolution record had classified this Issue as `P2`; this
reclassification to `P1` follows repository-owner review of that default.

ADR-018 bounds this decision without foreclosing it: an accepted alternative
must remain compatible with the accepted separation between execution truth and
evaluation, or explicitly amend it through the required authority process.

### Unchanged by this reclassification

- `Status` remains `Backlog`: `Ready` requires no unresolved product semantics,
  and this decision is open.
- `Kind` remains `Finding`: a validated concern awaiting adjudication.
- Priority continues to control scheduling only and cannot substitute for the
  required ADR-level decision.

## Priority rationale superseded — reclassified `P1` → `P0`

**Scope:** work-management classification only. This comment records no product
semantics and does not resolve the boundary this Issue tracks. It supersedes the
earlier "Priority rationale — reclassified `P2` → `P1`" comment on this Issue.

### Why `P0`

The engineering profile defines `P0` as work that "blocks current progress or
protects a critical correctness, authority, traceability, or verification
invariant". The second branch applies here.

This Issue is the only open decision that can **expand TURNLOCK's product
definition**. While it remains open, downstream work — #13's minimum
inspectability contract, the provenance-strength questions retained by #4, and
any future runtime, evaluation, or conformance architecture — can acquire
evaluation or optimization semantics implicitly unless every reviewer
independently notices the ADR-018 reservation. `P0` marks that authority
boundary as requiring action rather than ordinary backlog attention.

### Project convention

Every open Specification-phase `Finding` in this Project is `P0`: #2, #4, #5,
#6, and #8 (verified live). The operative class is "open product/semantic
decision", not "blocks the first safety-only model".

That distinction is demonstrated by #2, which is `P0` while the readiness matrix
in #9 records it as "Not blocking when liveness is excluded". Non-blocking-ness
of the safety-only model therefore does not place a product-semantic decision
below `P0`. The earlier `P1` rationale invented a "Specification-phase
non-blocker" class that no live item instantiates; it is withdrawn.

### What `P0` does not mean

- It does not mean the first safety-only TLA+ model is blocked. ADR-018
  explicitly reserves this question as a separate product decision, and the
  non-goal "does not block the first safety-only TLA+ model merely by existing"
  remains accurate.
- It is a scheduling and authority-risk signal, not a semantic claim. It
  neither strengthens nor weakens any alternative below.

### Boundaries unchanged

- `Status` remains `Backlog`: `Ready` requires no unresolved product semantics,
  and this decision is open.
- `Kind` remains `Finding`: a validated concern awaiting adjudication.
- ADR-018 is untouched; priority controls scheduling only and cannot amend an
  accepted decision.
- #13 remains `P1`: it is a `Follow-up` operationalizing accepted semantics.
- Priority cannot substitute for the required ADR-level decision.

### Provenance

Raised during repository-owner review of the priority default, following the
finding that #12 had been the only open Specification-phase `Finding` below
`P0`.

## Resolution — product decision ratified and synchronized

The product decision is made: TURNLOCK core is the workflow execution substrate and orchestration engine; it does not own evaluation or optimization policy. TURNLOCK makes workflows evaluable under ADR-018, but it is not the evaluator or optimizer.

```text
TURNLOCK makes workflows evaluable and optimizable
!=
TURNLOCK core is the evaluator or optimizer
```

### Published authority

- **ADR-019** — `docs/adr/adr-019-keep-evaluation-and-optimization-policy-outside-turnlock-core.md` (accepted, 2026-09-14). A refinement of Alternative A. Outgoing relation: `clarifies ADR-018`. Decision-body SHA-256: `74f8c280a5bd4f5539dfb4cfdfd648179410b9de37e414e7a7fc5f6f37d93722`.
- **Normative specification** synchronized: new §0.13C (product boundary), §0.14 conformance-rule additions, §3.32 `TL-INV-034`, §4 open-question updates, §5.16 (architectural implication), §6 non-goal strengthened, §7 product test, §8 synopsis.
- **`TL-INV-034` — Evaluation/optimization-policy boundary invariant** admitted: core MUST NOT define a universal evaluation objective, universal quality metrics, a default superiority relation, experiment policy, or an autonomous workflow optimizer; objectives come from an explicitly responsible actor; authored evaluation or optimization behavior gains no privileged runtime authority; refinement is authorship. Manifest entry: `architecture+conformance`, `not-applicable`, `not-yet-modeled`; no TLA+ property was added and no existing property was promoted.
- **Non-normative note** `docs/vision/future-workflow-run-evaluation.md` was updated to state the accepted boundary while preserving future design space; it remains non-normative with no authority.

### What ADR-018 had already fixed (not reopened)

- Completed-execution inspectability is a universal obligation (`TL-INV-033`).
- TURNLOCK exposes execution truth at its semantic boundary.
- The user or a higher-level system keeps evaluation criteria, comparison, and change decisions.
- Comparison and optimization are not implied by inspectability.

### What Issue #12 newly resolves

- TURNLOCK core does not gain native or privileged evaluation or optimization responsibility in the current product definition.
- Evaluation or optimization may be ordinary authored workflow behavior, or a user, coding-agent, external-evaluator, or higher-level-system capability. None of those becomes core policy machinery.
- No standard evaluator abstraction, universal metrics, universal run-comparison contract, experiment concept, or optimizer becomes core merely because evaluation is a supported goal.
- Workflow refinement is authoring. The runtime never silently optimizes or mutates authored orchestration; the visibility of artifact edits to an active invocation remains owned by #4.
- Any future native evaluation or optimization facility requires a new accepted product decision.

### Downstream discovery classification

**A — derived from the accepted decision**

- A core that defines a universal objective, defaults a superiority relation, or autonomously optimizes workflows contradicts `TL-INV-034`.
- Evaluation or optimization expressed with accepted primitives as an ordinary TURNLOCK workflow conforms to existing semantics and gains no privileged authority.
- A refinement produced outside the runtime, or by an authored workflow, remains authorship under `TL-INV-032`.

**B — decision-required (open, routed)**

- Exact minimum inspectability fact set, sufficiency rules, non-completed-execution semantics, availability, retention, access, and privacy: **#13**, unchanged and independent.
- Workflow-definition binding for active invocations: **#4**, unchanged and independent.
- Any future native evaluation or optimization facility: new accepted product decision required.
- Cross-run comparability, reproducibility, replay, and execution proofs: remain open in specification §4.

**C — formal/modeling choice**

- None added. `TL-INV-034` is `not-applicable`; the state-machine consequences of silently changing declared progression are already covered by `TL-INV-001`, `TL-INV-002`, `TL-INV-013`, `TL-INV-030`, and `TL-INV-032`. No identifier, bound, fairness assumption, or TLC claim was invented.

**D — implementation/architecture choice**

- None decided. No evaluation API, metric set, telemetry, storage, event schema, experiment database, optimizer algorithm, dashboard, or run model was created or implied.

**E — integration/conformance constraints**

- A conforming harness or integration must not present a core-defined universal objective, quality score, or superiority relation as TURNLOCK semantics.
- Conformance review must distinguish execution truth (`TL-INV-033`) from evaluation and optimization policy (`TL-INV-034`).

### Preserved non-decisions

No run identity, event schema, persistence, retention, replay, comparability, reproducibility, metric, experiment, or optimizer architecture was created. `bounded` semantics, Issue #13's fact-set contract, and Issue #4's binding semantics remain untouched.

### Validation performed

```text
.venv/bin/python scripts/adr-metadata.py render
.venv/bin/python scripts/render-formal-mapping.py
.venv/bin/python scripts/tests/test-adr-metadata.py           → OK (12 tests)
.venv/bin/python scripts/tests/test-normative-terminology.py  → OK (13 tests)
.venv/bin/python scripts/adr-metadata.py check                → OK (19 structured, 0 legacy)
.venv/bin/python scripts/check-normative-terminology.py       → OK
.venv/bin/python scripts/check-formal-traceability.py         → OK (34 invariants)
git diff --check                                              → clean
```

A hostile consistency review checked the accidental-strengthening patterns (inspectability implies native evaluator; evaluation implies universal metrics or comparability; an optimization use case implies a core optimizer; an optimizer workflow implies privileged authority; refinement implies mutation of an active invocation; cost or latency data implies a mandatory metrics contract; future optional tooling becomes current core semantics). None is present. The review's single gap — the missing explicit #13 relationship statement in ADR-019 — was corrected, and a follow-up confirmation review returned PASS.

Published commits: `944b098` (decision and synchronization) and `473750f` (repository-governance priority clarification for open semantic decisions).

All acceptance criteria of Issue #12 are satisfied. Issue #12 is closed as completed; ADR-019 and the synchronized specification are the authority for this boundary.

## Handoff from #8 — bounded raw-LLM and independent-agent semantics

Issue #8 is published on `main` in commits `84fc580`, `1afa9c3`, `ea22ca2`, `18b9226`, and `158aedb`. ADR-020 and ADR-021 are accepted, and the normative specification and formal traceability are synchronized.

Issue #1 retains property-level metamodel migration, obligation classification, property naming/splitting, and evidence/status handling. It must consume these semantic constraints:

1. `IndependentAgentCanBeWorkflowDeclared` represents direct workflow declaration as a positive capability; it must not imply eventual start or completion.
2. `IndependentAgentHasDistinctLineage` must preserve a fresh lineage distinct from the main agent, a declared local task, and local rather than global authority.
3. `IndependentAgentContextIsExplicitlyDeclared` must encode no implicit main-agent cognitive-context inheritance and initial cognitive context supplied through workflow semantics. Explicit main-agent-derived inputs remain allowed, information may be acquired during execution, and internally spawned main-agent children are outside this rule unless workflow-declared as first-class regions.
4. `RawLLMIsBoundedLeaf` and `RawLLMDoesNotCreateAgentLoop` must preserve one TURNLOCK semantic operation with explicit instruction/context, a constitutive result boundary if/when completion occurs, no autonomous loop, no persistent independent lineage, and no global orchestration authority.
5. `ProbabilisticLeafCannotOwnGlobalControl` remains non-exhaustive: raw-LLM results and independent-agent completion/output may influence only continuations permitted by workflow semantics, while independent agents retain legitimate local discretion.

## Resolution — ADR-026 accepted

**Decision:** [ADR-026: Define a realizable semantic-boundary capture handoff](https://github.com/fanilosendrison/turnlock-rust/blob/main/docs/adr/adr-026-define-a-realizable-semantic-boundary-capture-handoff.md). It clarifies ADR-024 and ADR-025 and amends neither. Alternative B (realizable capture boundary) is accepted as the universal core floor, Alternative A (instantaneous availability) is a conforming special case when acquisition is realizable as part of the boundary interaction, and Alternative E (profile/layer guarantees) remains available above the floor. Alternatives C and D were rejected as universal contracts.

**Semantic floor:** For every effective execution condition covered by `TL-INV-036`, TURNLOCK MUST preserve the required condition-specific provenance and governed-scope attribution until that provenance participates in a realizable semantic-boundary capture handoff. A handoff is realizable only when an eligible conforming capture context could be established in time to acquire the required provenance as part of the semantic-boundary interaction — without inaccessible transient internal state, accidental timing against TURNLOCK's internal execution, or reconstruction from later mutable state, human recollection, or agent recollection.

**Answers to the Issue questions**

- **Sufficiency / falsifiability:** defined by realizable participation, not by elapsed time. No minimum wall-clock duration, workflow transition count, scheduler turn, process lifetime, scope lifetime, or invocation lifetime is part of the contract. Internal momentary existence, or acquisition that depends on accidentally matching implementation-defined internal timing, does not satisfy `TL-INV-036`.
- **Instantaneous opportunity:** yes, when capture is realizable as part of the boundary interaction itself.
- **Actual consumer presence:** not universally required. A runtime that exposes a structurally realizable capture capability an eligible context could have configured in time does not become non-conforming solely because no consumer was attached; consumer absence does not create an indefinite retention obligation.
- **Delivery / acknowledgment:** not required. Also no consumer processing, persistence, retry-until-success, exactly-once or at-least-once delivery, queue durability, backpressure, indefinite blocking, or TURNLOCK-operated persistent buffering.
- **Discard boundary:** once the handoff is discharged, `TL-INV-036` alone no longer requires continued capturability. Another accepted invariant, ADR, profile, integration contract, or Issue #13 resolution may independently require later availability.
- **Occurrence / aggregation:** batching or grouping multiple occurrences through one boundary interaction is permissible when each occurrence's condition-specific provenance and governed-scope attribution survive; one semantic occurrence is not required to be one physical event, message, or callback.
- **Failure / cancellation / interruption:** later failure cannot retroactively erase an already-incurred capture obligation for a condition that governed execution. The complete terminal-outcome lifecycle remains Issue #13's.
- **Authorization / privacy:** separate. No identity, ACL, RBAC, capability, disclosure, encryption, or privacy model is introduced; ADR-025's known-protected rule remains in force underneath any consumer view.
- **Issue #13:** its scope is preserved without merger. A coordination comment has been added there.

**Invariant admission:** No new invariant. `TL-INV-036` is clarified and keeps its stable identity; no invariant number was reserved.

**Formal status:** `TL-INV-036` remains `formalization: partial`, `verification: not-yet-modeled`, `mapping: pending-model`. No executable TLA+ model or TLC configuration exists, and no property, state variable, action, or evidence identifier was invented. ## Resolution: stable governing definition per accepted invocation

The product-owner decision for #4 is accepted and synchronized.

### Accepted semantics

- Every accepted TURNLOCK workflow invocation has one **governing workflow definition**, determined no later than invocation acceptance. It is the source of declared topology for that invocation and remains stable for that invocation's lifetime.
- An invocation MUST NOT become accepted without a governing definition; binding is not deferred to the first executed step and is not tied to the moment the user typed a slash command unless that moment independently is acceptance.
- Ordinary later modification of the source artifact does not alter the active invocation's governing definition or its remaining declared topology.
- Every nested invocation is a distinct invocation that establishes its own governing definition no later than its own acceptance. A caller's governing definition does not transitively bind or freeze future callees; `A/D1 → B/E2 → return → A/D1 continues` is valid.
- Live observation of ordinary artifact edits is rejected: declared topology needs a stable per-invocation meaning, and effective governing-definition attribution must correspond to what actually governed the invocation.
- A root/run-wide transitive dependency snapshot is rejected as the universal default; genuine runtime composition is preserved, including workflows selected from a main-agent region. A future explicit version-pinned reference or stronger reproducibility profile would require its own semantics.
- Implicit dynamic mutation of an active governing definition is rejected. If deliberate replacement, replanning, or mutation of an active definition is ever supported, it requires a separate explicit product decision.
- No representation is selected: no Git commit/SHA binding, hash, content addressing, snapshots, AST copies, copy-on-write, database revisions, locks, concrete version identifier, persistence, retention, crash recovery, replay, reproducibility, comparability, or DSL/API syntax. Resolution and version-selection syntax remain independently governable. Source artifacts themselves do not become immutable.

### Authority artifacts

- **ADR-027** — Bind each accepted invocation to a stable governing workflow definition (`docs/adr/adr-027-bind-each-accepted-invocation-to-a-stable-governing-workflow-definition.md`), accepted 2026-09-16. ## Disposition

Issue #25 is closed without adopting the proposed one-active-session-root
semantics.

The product analysis that motivated this Issue assumed that TURNLOCK needed to
define the interaction of multiple independent top-level TURNLOCK invocations
simultaneously attached to the same coding-agent session. That assumption is
not part of the current product intent.

The currently specified execution shape remains:

```text
coding-agent session
↓
TURNLOCK invocation
↓
workflow execution
↓
coding-agent session resumes
```

During an active workflow, additional workflow executions may arise through the
composition mechanisms that TURNLOCK actually specifies, including structured
nested invocation and workflow-owned concurrency where applicable.

A separate situation in which multiple external actors, processes, API calls,
launchers, or harness operations attempt to establish multiple independent
top-level TURNLOCK invocations concurrently against the same coding-agent
session is outside the currently specified execution model.

No TURNLOCK semantic behavior is selected for that unsupported situation.

In particular, this disposition does **not** define that TURNLOCK must:

* accept both invocations;
* reject the later invocation;
* queue it;
* serialize it;
* wait for the existing invocation;
* reinterpret it as a nested invocation;
* replace or preempt the existing invocation;
* arbitrate between independent top-level invocations;
* clone or fork the session's main-agent cognitive lineage.

Those alternatives remain undesignated because TURNLOCK has no current product
requirement to support concurrent independent top-level entry into one
coding-agent session.

If such support becomes an explicit product requirement in the future, it must
be introduced through a new separately governed semantic decision rather than
being inferred from this Issue.

### Repository effect

This disposition creates no new TURNLOCK product semantics.

Therefore:

* no ADR is created;
* no accepted ADR is amended;
* no normative specification text is changed;
* no new `TL-INV-*` identity is created;
* no existing invariant is broadened;
* `formal/verification.yaml` is unchanged;
* no TLA+ property or state is introduced;
* no harness/conformance requirement is introduced;
* no implementation mechanism is introduced.

Issue #25 is therefore closed as a rejected/out-of-scope proposed semantic
extension, not as an accepted product decision.

## Audit adjudication

The current TURNLOCK repository evidence is sufficient to resolve the main
question of this finding:

**TURNLOCK does require an explicit cross-cutting governed-identity discipline.**

The demonstrated mechanisms do **not** justify a rule that every governed entity
has one universal canonical serialization.

The minimum common rule supported by the repository is instead:

```text
For every governed state whose sameness, change, currentness, projection,
evidence binding, preservation, or reproducibility matters to repository
governance, the governing contract MUST define an unambiguous identity for that
scope.

That identity MUST bind every state dimension that is significant for that
scope and MUST either:

1. treat the exact representation as significant; or
2. define a deterministic canonicalization that removes only dimensions that
   governing authority declares non-significant.

Dependent evidence and projections MUST bind to the applicable governed
identity, and identity changes MUST invalidate currentness exactly where the
dependent contract requires it.
```

Additional constraints already justified by existing TURNLOCK mechanisms:

- **Authority and identity are distinct.** A canonical owner/source does not by
  itself define the identity of the state it owns.
- **Identity is scope-relative.** The same artifact may legitimately have
  different identities for different purposes (for example packet byte identity
  versus reviewed semantic-subject identity).
- **Canonical representation is not universally required.** Exact bytes are
  correct when representation itself is significant.
- **Canonicalization must be authority-derived.** It may not erase a dimension
  merely to stabilize hashes or reduce invalidation.
- **No silent partial fingerprinting.** If a state dimension can affect the
  governed claim, it must participate in the applicable identity unless accepted
  authority explicitly excludes it.
- **Currentness must fail closed when identity cannot be established.**
- **Historical evidence remains bound to its historical identity.** A current
  authority change does not rewrite historical evidence.
- **Mechanically derivable identity rules should be mechanically enforced.**
- **Artifact-specific stronger contracts remain stronger.** This discipline is
  a floor, not a replacement for Gate A packet identity, ADR body hashes,
  content-addressed schemas, exact verification evidence, or other existing
  mechanisms.

### Concrete repository correction indicated

The cleanest TURNLOCK-local correction is to add one repository-governance
contract dedicated to governed identity/canonicalization and bind it from
`AGENTS.md`.

That contract should:

1. define the terms above without introducing a universal IR or serialization;
2. define the trigger for when an explicit governed identity is required;
3. define exact-representation versus canonicalized-identity modes;
4. require explicit significance/exclusion boundaries;
5. define dependent currentness/invalidation behavior;
6. require fail-closed behavior when required identity cannot be established;
7. state that Projection Integrity governs secondary representations while this
   contract governs the identity of the state those representations/evidence
   bind to;
8. include the current TURNLOCK mechanisms as concrete examples, not duplicated
   authorities;
9. require new governed surfaces to state their identity policy rather than
   relying on agent inference.

No TURNLOCK product-semantic ADR is currently required: this correction can be
made as repository governance without changing product meaning. If the detailed
inventory exposes a case where semantic significance itself is not determined
by current product authority, that case must be split into a separate
`decision-required` Product Semantics finding rather than resolved here.

This adjudication remains TURNLOCK-local. No proto-ring extraction is authorized
by it.

## Ruu confrontation result

The cross-consumer confrontation has now been performed against current Ruu
governance and recorded as
`fanilosendrison/ruu#49`.

Ruu confirms the need for a governed-identity discipline but strengthens the
Turnlock adjudication in one important direction: the discipline must protect
against **over-identification** as well as under-identification.

Concrete Ruu evidence shows that:

- stable logical identity may intentionally survive exact-state revision
  (ADR-049);
- content identity may intentionally exclude lifecycle/topology (ADR-045);
- branch/ref/path/name representation is not automatically identity (ADR-049);
- physical Git occurrence identity is not managed semantic identity and a
  universal transition fingerprint is explicitly rejected (ADR-076);
- delivery/event occurrence identity is not semantic-operation identity
  (ADR-080);
- historical evidence identity and current-state identity are distinct facts
  (ADR-080 and qualification);
- exact-byte preservation and canonicalized semantic equivalence are both valid
  modes depending on scope.

Therefore the emerging rule should be strengthened from merely
"unambiguous identity for the governed scope" to:

```text
Each governed role whose identity matters must have a minimum-sufficient,
scope-specific authoritative identity.

The identity must include every dimension significant to that role and exclude
dimensions that belong to distinct identity domains unless governing authority
explicitly makes them part of the role.

Representation, provenance, occurrence/delivery identity, logical identity,
exact-state identity, and historical/currentness identity must not be silently
collapsed into one another.
```

This remains a consumer-confrontation result, not shared proto-ring authority.

Turnlock #35 and Ruu #49 should now be resolved independently in their own
repositories. Only the resulting concrete governance contracts should then be
compared for a proto-ring extraction candidate.

## Qualification sémantique — `CONFIRMED` (analyse bornée, non-campagne)

**Objet et limite du verdict.** La faiblesse **de décomposition d'assurance / de correspondance normative** est confirmée pour la conséquence positive d'éligibilité après retour normal d'une invocation *workflow-declared*. Cela **ne confirme pas** un défaut du Product Intent, du modèle TLA+ canonique (absent), d'une exécution TURNLOCK, ni des 83 claims pris comme un théorème global. La conclusion reste soumise à la revue indépendante requise pour la clôture de cette Issue.

**Révisions exactes.** Corpus TURNLOCK examiné : `5656eb822398e6faef38ac838166b7b20382d10b`; l'expérience Proto-Scope a été construite contre `44c2a55009e17ba3500bfef6a1ae310f6d0fcbb9`. Le diff Git entre ces deux révisions ne modifie ni `docs/specification/turnlock-spec.md`, ni `formal/verification.yaml`, ni ADR-023/036/041. La conclusion reste valable au snapshot déclaré par #70. Sources fixes :

### Obligation, dérivation et divergence

Pour chaque occurrence acceptée de *workflow-declared invocation*, sa **fin normale reconnue** restaure le **même contexte appelant immédiat** et rend **éligible**, selon la topologie englobante, **sa continuation post-call préservée**, dans l'état sémantique résultant. Ce point est directement imposé par §0.6, TL-INV-019, TL-INV-035 et ADR-023/036 : aucune nouvelle sémantique produit n'est requise. En contraste, `TL-CLAIM-011` garantit le retour exact et « authorizes only the continuation appropriate to that caller » ; aucun lien accepté `Authorized(Correct) => Eligible(PostCall)` n'est démontré. `Eligible => Authorized` est compatible mais insuffisant.

Sur une occurrence *workflow-declared* normale dans une topologie **séquentielle admissible** (aucune obligation de join supplémentaire), considérons :

```text
accepted=true; normal=true; declared=true; topology_allows=true
caller_preserved=true; continuation_preserved=true; return_link=true
exact_return=true; right_authorized=true; wrong_authorized=false
no_ancestor_rewrite=true; postcall_eligible=false
sibling_continues=true
```

Ce témoin satisfait une formalisation **positive et favorable** de C011 et des contraintes compatibles C010/C020/C023/C031/C061/C068, mais viole l'éligibilité exigée. Les autres claims ont été examinés **conjointement**, notamment C021/C022/C032/C059/C060/C080, et les obligations pertinentes C030/C031 (join), C039 (IA-region completion), C061 (rejet) et C083 (liveness). Aucun ne donne l'implication positive manquante pour le retour **ordinaire workflow-declared**. Notamment C061 porte sur le rejet, C031 sur le post-join, C083 seulement sur la progression d'une occurrence déjà éligible.

### Reproduction, contrôles, et réfutation adversariale

Reproduction locale avec Python + **SymPy 1.14.0** de l'interprétation propositionnelle bornée de l'expérience [Proto-Scope à commit fixe](https://github.com/fanilosendrison/proto-scope/tree/2d10de2b75a071f8824991afbbc78dbd6114b5f7/docs/research/specification-methodology/2026-10-15/experiences) : `T1 SAT`, `T2 UNSAT`, `T3 UNSAT`, `T4 SAT`, `T5 SAT`, `T6 UNSAT`, `T7 SAT`, `T8 SAT`, `T9 UNSAT`, `T10 HOLDS VACUOUSLY` (contrôle logique non-SAT de la vivacité conditionnelle), `T11: 2 modèles` (table de vérité : éligible vrai/faux). Les neuf tests SAT/UNSAT et deux contrôles ont passé. Source archivées : [script](https://github.com/fanilosendrison/proto-scope/blob/2d10de2b75a071f8824991afbbc78dbd6114b5f7/docs/research/specification-methodology/2026-10-15/experiences/turnlock_claim011_semantic_correspondence.py), [rapport](https://github.com/fanilosendrison/proto-scope/blob/2d10de2b75a071f8824991afbbc78dbd6114b5f7/docs/research/specification-methodology/2026-10-15/experiences/turnlock_claim011_semantic_report.md), [résultats](https://github.com/fanilosendrison/proto-scope/blob/2d10de2b75a071f8824991afbbc78dbd6114b5f7/docs/research/specification-methodology/2026-10-15/experiences/turnlock_claim011_semantic_results.txt).

**Tentatives de réfutation évaluées :**
1. « authorize » signifie déjà « make eligible » : **non établi** par l'autorité, ce pont hypothétique rend le témoin UNSAT, mais ne peut pas être admis comme prémisse simplement pour le réfuter.
2. Les claims adjacents apportent l'éligibilité : **non** dans le scénario séquentiel déclaré décrit ci-dessus ; C031 ne s'applique pas comme post-call générique.
3. C083 règle le retard : **non** ; sur une boucle infinie inéligible, l'antécédent de C083 reste faux.
4. Une règle d'éligibilité universelle est-elle acceptable ? **Non** : *main-agent-selected* doit reprendre la même région main-agent sans rendre prématurément éligible la continuation du workflow englobant ; *independent-agent-selected* reprend la même lignée indépendante. Les témoins T5–T7 distinguent ces cas.
5. « only » bloque les autres branches ? **Non** : portée locale à l'appel/retour ; T8/T9 préservent la progression de siblings indépendants admissibles.

**Effet sur couverture déclarée :** le `canonical_operational_coverage: full` sans résidu n'est **pas suffisamment justifié pour l'obligation d'éligibilité concernée** dans TL-INV-008, TL-INV-019 et TL-INV-035. Il ne s'agit pas d'une affirmation que toute leur couverture serait fausse, ni d'une preuve de défaut de vérification mécanique.

- **Statement** : la décomposition d'assurance déclarée ne porte pas explicitement la conséquence positive normative du retour normal *workflow-declared*.

- **Affected layers** : `formal-model-or-analysis`, `verification-or-qualification-evidence`.
- **Required authority** : gouvernance de Formal Architecture pour toute modification ultérieure de `formal/verification.yaml`, aucune nouvelle décision produit.
- **Next action** : correction dans un travail **distinct**, après qualification ; pas de modification du manifest, du produit, du protocole, ni du runner sous #70.

**Limites** : expérimentation propositionnelle bornée, interprétation indépendante du langage naturel, sans modèle TLA+ canonique, sans preuve sur les 83 claims, sans garantie sur traces infinies ou processus réels, sans campagne officielle Gate A. ## Read-only architectural audit candidate — independent review still required

**Audit revision:** `be76128d2007eec3e3906d13c0bf00d861fcaa10` (current `main` at inspection). **Historical baseline:** `5656eb822398e6faef38ac838166b7b20382d10b`. The intervening [#74 correction](https://github.com/fanilosendrison/turnlock-rust/commit/be76128d2007eec3e3906d13c0bf00d861fcaa10) introduces required `TL-CLAIM-084`, changing the Gate A semantic subject without changing the applicable review protocol. This is an independent, **non-authoritative, unreviewed analytic candidate** for #71. It is not a Gate A campaign, a product decision, a protocol amendment, or permission to change runner construction.

### 1. Formalization timing and dependency witness

**Qualified result: no established logical sequencing cycle or contradiction.**

[ADR-015, Decision](https://github.com/fanilosendrison/turnlock-rust/blob/be76128d2007eec3e3906d13c0bf00d861fcaa10/docs/adr/adr-015-evolve-the-normative-and-formal-specifications-together.md#L44-L100) calls for early normative/formal coevolution and implementation-independent integrated/focused model checking. [ADR-041, Relationship to ADR-015](https://github.com/fanilosendrison/turnlock-rust/blob/be76128d2007eec3e3906d13c0bf00d861fcaa10/docs/adr/adr-041-establish-turnlock-formal-assurance-architecture.md#L521-L545) **expressly amends** its overly direct assurance chain while retaining early formalization as discovery pressure.

[ADR-041, Gates](https://github.com/fanilosendrison/turnlock-rust/blob/be76128d2007eec3e3906d13c0bf00d861fcaa10/docs/adr/adr-041-establish-turnlock-formal-assurance-architecture.md#L443-L521) separates:
- Gate A: qualify assurance decomposition and permit candidate canonical formal-model authoring; **no TLC/checker evidence is required**;
- Gate B: hostile-review the actual candidate formal semantics, including non-vacuity and compositional adequacy, then potentially promote them as canonical for the modeled scope;
- Gate C: qualify claim/property bindings, verification profiles, assumptions/bounds, correspondence and evidence lifting before checker runs support assurance.

The dependency graph does not require `Gate A passed` as a prerequisite for **non-canonical diagnostic reasoning** about a claim. The scoped bounded propositional/SAT diagnostic supporting [#70](https://github.com/fanilosendrison/turnlock-rust/issues/70) happened before any candidate `formal/Turnlock.tla` existed, with its explicitly bounded conclusions and no Gate A evidence promotion. This is a constructive witness of possible early falsification, **not** a blanket authorization to author the governed `Turnlock.tla` candidate before Gate A.

A material normative finding from post-A formal-model exploration may change authority/claims/coverage, invalidate `S`, and require a new Gate A review. Such iteration can have significant cost, but is **not a logical cycle**. The elapsed development schedule may lag ADR-015's ideal of early integrated mathematical pressure; its quality/latency consequences have not been measured by this audit. Do not declare an invented second mandatory formalization pipeline or new gate.

### 2. Gate A attack-objective / normative-coverage correspondence

The current manifest [`policy.hostile_review.required_attack_objectives.assurance-decomposition`](https://github.com/fanilosendrison/turnlock-rust/blob/be76128d2007eec3e3906d13c0bf00d861fcaa10/formal/verification.yaml#L25-L57) requires **14** objectives. The [current initial-reviewer prompt](https://github.com/fanilosendrison/turnlock-rust/blob/be76128d2007eec3e3906d13c0bf00d861fcaa10/formal/reviews/prompts/gate-a-initial-review-v1.md) gives their meanings and explicitly orders all 14 attempted exactly once.

| Audited obligation | Relevant declared objective(s) | Assessment |
|---|---|---|
| Semantic weakening / strengthening | `semantic-weakening`, `semantic-strengthening` | Explicit |
| Valid behavior omitted / behavior invented | `omitted-valid-behavior`, `invented-behavior` | Explicit |
| Unsupported abstractions or exclusions | `hidden-assumption`, `omitted-valid-behavior`, `cross-feature-interaction-failure` | Covered indirectly; no dedicated named abstraction/exclusion objective |
| Incorrect quantification / invocation scope | `wrong-quantification`, `wrong-occurrence-scope` | Explicit |
| Safety / reachability / liveness confusion | `modality-mismatch`, `vacuity` | Explicit |
| Vacuity | `vacuity` | Explicit |
| Unsupported `full` normative coverage | `coverage-gap`, `semantic-weakening` | Explicit obligation to attack, not proof of sufficiency |
| Cross-feature interactions | `cross-feature-interaction-failure` | Explicit |
| Normative distinctions / unresolved interpretations | `collapsed-normative-distinction`, `invented-formal-distinction`, `alternative-compatible-interpretation` | Explicit |

Evidence integrity is strong **for its defined class**: [formal/reviews/README.md](https://github.com/fanilosendrison/turnlock-rust/blob/be76128d2007eec3e3906d13c0bf00d861fcaa10/formal/reviews/README.md#L562-L632) requires independent qualifying reviewer executions, exact `(S,P)`, identical canonical packet/prompt, all objectives per execution, content-addressed raw and receipt evidence, one-to-one finding normalization, hostile materiality/refutation challenges, no surviving material finding, and stale-protocol re-adjudication. It explicitly rejects majority voting as a semantic refutation.

**However:** an objective's mere appearance in a valid structured output does not establish a deep or successful challenge to that objective. In particular, `canonical_operational_coverage: full` means *declared assurance decomposition*; it is not a theorem that the claims entail every normative consequence. [#70's](https://github.com/fanilosendrison/turnlock-rust/issues/70) positive post-call eligibility countermodel demonstrated a scoped coverage weakness subsequently repaired by `TL-CLAIM-084`. It does **not** establish that a conforming Gate A campaign would or would not have found that weakness, because none has run.

### 3. Atomic evidence-observability finding

**Statement:** the accepted [raw reviewer schema v1](https://github.com/fanilosendrison/turnlock-rust/blob/be76128d2007eec3e3906d13c0bf00d861fcaa10/formal/reviews/schemas/raw-review-output-v1.schema.json) requires an `objective_assessments` entry with `objective` and `finding_ids` for every objective, but **has no per-objective explanation/evidence field when `finding_ids=[]`**. The [current prompt](https://github.com/fanilosendrison/turnlock-rust/blob/be76128d2007eec3e3906d13c0bf00d861fcaa10/formal/reviews/prompts/gate-a-initial-review-v1.md) explicitly permits zero findings once all objectives are assessed. A syntactically correct response containing all 14 distinct objectives with empty `finding_ids` and `findings=[]` therefore has no inspectable record of what specific negative attacks were attempted. The schema and attack-list checks cannot distinguish thoughtful negative assessment from mechanically filling fourteen empty entries.

**Evidence:** the exact prompt/schema above; this is an output-observability witness, **not** a simulated real qualifying campaign (active P6 has no eligible reviewer profiles). A reviewer might actually have reasoned deeply and found nothing; the record simply cannot demonstrate that depth. A fuller narrative would improve inspection but still would not mathematically prove that the reviewer actually searched all alternatives.

**Existing authority:** [ADR-041 hostile review](https://github.com/fanilosendrison/turnlock-rust/blob/be76128d2007eec3e3906d13c0bf00d861fcaa10/docs/adr/adr-041-establish-turnlock-formal-assurance-architecture.md#L311-L366) requires adversarial attempts and durable review evidence, not absolute proof of natural-language equivalence; ADR-042/045 and the active P6 schema govern the evidence format.

**Semantic disposition:** `no-normative-impact`.

**Affected layers:** `verification-or-qualification-evidence`, `formal-model-or-analysis`, and (only if a new mandatory output/evidence field is proposed) `repository-governance-or-documentation`.

**Required authority:** no product decision. Before any claimed *protocol* insufficiency is accepted, obtain independent review of this bounded observability limitation against the accepted Gate A assurance strength. A substantive new evidence duty would need separately authorized protocol/evidence-contract work, not an informal reinterpretation of today's schema.

**Next action:** test whether structured, independently reproducible negative controls (e.g. historically omitted positive eligibility, accidentally universal post-call eligibility, sibling-exclusivity error) are actually detected by isolated adversarial diagnostic reviewers before changing P. Preserve raw outputs and distinguish diagnostic reviewer sensitivity from official Gate A evidence. This is a proposed *qualification experiment*, not a new mandatory pipeline.

### 4. Additional unqualified boundaries (not confirmed defects)

- **Mathematical falsification:** current Gate A protocol **does not require SAT/SMT/TLC witnesses** before accepting an assurance decomposition. ADR-015 justifies early mathematical exploration, and diagnostic experiments are feasible; it does not follow that every Gate A review must itself execute a checker. Whether optional targeted bounded falsification should become a mandatory pre-A acceptance obligation is unqualified and requires its own justification.
- **Declared formal scope and exclusions:** the formal graph has an `operational` semantic domain, coverage, modalities and residual claims; [ADR-041 Gate A](https://github.com/fanilosendrison/turnlock-rust/blob/be76128d2007eec3e3906d13c0bf00d861fcaa10/docs/adr/adr-041-establish-turnlock-formal-assurance-architecture.md#L447-L469) additionally requires an explicit intended operational scope and interaction closure or justified nondistorting exclusions. This audit has not proven that the existing domain/claim/coverage representation is inadequate for that obligation. Qualifying reviewers should challenge the **specific** exclusions and cross-feature effects rather than infer adequacy from the existence of a `formal_semantic_domains` entry.
- **Current campaign adequacy:** no real Gate A campaign has been executed, so no claim of measured reviewer sensitivity or successful detection of known defects is available. [P6](https://github.com/fanilosendrison/turnlock-rust/blob/be76128d2007eec3e3906d13c0bf00d861fcaa10/formal/reviews/protocols/gate-a-campaign-protocol-v6.json) intentionally has `reviewer_profiles=[]` and `reviewer_acquisition.profile_order=[]`; the current gate is blocked for missing qualifying review evidence. Empty profiles are intentional protocol configuration, **not** a newly established failure of assurance architecture.

### 5. Construction impact (S / P / claims / evidence / runner)

| Examined outcome | Immediate impact |
|---|---|
| No established ADR-015/041 logical contradiction | No change to `S`, `P`, claims, protocol, or runner |
| Review objectives and challenge/traceability obligations already explicit | No change to `S`, `P`, or runner |
| Confirmed negative-assessment observability limitation; semantic adequacy not yet qualified | **No currently authorized mutation**; a later evidence-schema/prompt/protocol revision would affect **P**, and may require compatible runner/evidence handling; **not automatically S** |
| Early SAT/SMT diagnostics permitted as separate non-canonical research | No change to `S`/`P`, no new gate, no modification to C9-I or NIB-T from this analysis |
| Existing `TL-CLAIM-084` change | Already published; changed `S` to `7171ccc03b7ccf698e31a2880ac235636e1c2a178102ee0a8b3acb38c69b6a1f`, **not P** |
| Current official Gate A blocking condition | Existing current-protocol reviewer/evidence admission and campaign execution responsibility; **not a reason to rewrite the current Campaign Runner construction pack** |

[#28](https://github.com/fanilosendrison/turnlock-rust/issues/28) owns Campaign Runner construction and expressly excludes reviewer admission and the first real Gate A campaign. The active C9-I Git Dependency Contract remains an independent construction responsibility. No current finding in this audit blocks its safe continuation.

### 6. Provisional disposition and review required to complete #71

- **REFUTED within examined scope:** asserted inherent circular dependency `Gate A -> mathematical diagnostic -> Gate A`; ADR-041's express amendment of ADR-015 prevents an unamended direct-chain contradiction.
- **CONFIRMED within examined scope:** the structured raw-output contract has no independently inspectable explanation for zero-findings objective assessments. This is a bounded *evidence-observability limitation*, **not** a proof of reviewer ineffectiveness or a demonstrated failure of an actual Gate A campaign.
- **ALREADY SPECIFIED:** attack-objective labels, per-reviewer objective coverage, protocol-qualified independence, review evidence integrity and adversarial challenge semantics.
- **UNDETERMINED / requires independent qualification:** whether that observability limit is materially insufficient for the accepted Gate A assurance responsibility; empirical sensitivity to seeded omissions and interaction counterexamples; whether additional early math-based evidence is necessary or merely useful; adequacy of intended formal scope/exclusion descriptions under hostile review.
- **DOWNSTREAM:** any claim-to-canonical-model correspondence and non-vacuity witnesses belong to Gate B, and bound checker-result lifting to Gate C.

**The nine #71 acceptance conditions are addressed analytically, but this write-up has NOT received the independently required source-to-conclusion review. Do not close #71, check its acceptance boxes, modify formal authority, select a new current protocol, execute a real campaign, or change runner NIBs on the basis of this report alone.**

**Scope:** Independently falsify the bounded audit in [the current #71 analysis comment](https://github.com/fanilosendrison/turnlock-rust/issues/71#issuecomment-6219317796). This order records **how to conduct the outstanding review**; it is not a review result, a change to accepted authority, or official Gate A campaign evidence.

### Reviewer execution requirements

Prefer the already operationally established reviewer surfaces used in #70/#74 (DeepSeek and Mistral) if still available. Verify reported effective provider/model identities from actual execution, not requested names or guesses; do not replace a reviewer because of an inconvenient conclusion. The orchestrating coding agent handles only input preparation, mechanical invocation, output capture, validation and publication. It must not act as a reviewer or adjudicate disputed semantics.

**Pass B — adversarial audit of the author's report.** Only after both Pass A outputs are separately sealed, provide the exact #71 author-audit comment to each reviewer in its own session. ### Evidence and adjudication boundaries

Preserve immutable raw output for each reviewer/pass, source/input packet hashes, prompts, requested and actual reported identities, isolated-session IDs, technical failures, timestamps where available, and exit/validation results. All reviewers must produce auditable *arguments* rather than hidden reasoning or approval votes.
