L000859 model, retry rule, timeout rule, cancellation rule, failure-propagation rule, or
L000860 resource budget.
L000861 
L000862 ## 0.11 Session continuity is part of the product value
L000863 
L000864 The motivation for a main-agent step is not merely access to model intelligence. It is access to the user's ongoing coding-agent working context.
L000865 
L000866 The main agent may already have useful continuity from the session: prior discussion, repository understanding, decisions, user corrections, current working assumptions, available tools, and the natural interaction channel with the user.
L000867 
L000868 The product therefore seeks to preserve the following conceptual continuity:
L000869 
L000870 ```text
L000871 user ↔ main agent
L000872         ↑      ↓
L000873         workflow
L000874 ```
L000875 
L000876 rather than forcing every agentic phase into:
L000877 
L000878 ```text
L000879 user ↔ main agent
L000880 
L000881 workflow → unrelated agent
L000882 ```
L000883 
L000884 The exact amount and mechanism of session/context continuity that can be guaranteed across different coding harnesses remains an implementation and capability question, but replacing the main-agent concept with arbitrary stateless completions would not satisfy the product intent.
L000885 
L000886 ## 0.11A Why a main-agent handoff is not equivalent to spawning a fresh agent
L000887 
L000888 The requirement to return control to the main agent exists for a product reason, not because TURNLOCK prefers one process topology.
L000889 
L000890 A fresh agent can often be given the same repository, prompt, model family, tools, or selected conversation excerpts. That is useful, but it creates a new agentic lineage whose working state must be reconstructed from whatever the caller chooses to transfer. The surrounding main session and the spawned agent can then learn different things and make different local assumptions. Conceptually:
L000891 
L000892 ```text
L000893 main session before spawn:  A B C D E
L000894                               |
L000895                               +--> spawned agent receives A B C
L000896                                       and learns F G H
L000897 
L000898 main session afterwards:     A B C D E
L000899 spawned lineage:              A B C F G H
L000900 ```
L000901 
L000902 The system must now reconcile two cognitive lineages through summaries, artifacts, patches, messages, or another synchronization mechanism. Even a very good reconstruction is still a reconstruction boundary.
L000903 
L000904 A TURNLOCK main-agent handoff seeks a different semantic shape:
L000905 
L000906 ```text
L000907 main session:  A B C D E
L000908                   ↓
L000909               workflow
L000910                   ↓
L000911               same ongoing agentic lineage
L000912                   ↓
L000913               A B C D E F G H
L000914 ```
L000915 
L000916 The product value is therefore not merely "same model" or "same repository". It is **continuation of the user's current agentic working relationship without requiring a context export/import and later cognitive reconciliation merely because execution temporarily entered a workflow**.
L000917 
L000918 This yields a stronger invariant:
L000919 
L000920 > **Crossing a workflow boundary MUST NOT create a new cognitive lineage merely because a workflow requests main-agent continuation. Independent cognitive lineages are a required TURNLOCK capability, but they are a different execution form and MUST NOT be silently treated as equivalent to a main-agent step.**
L000921 
L000922 This invariant is semantic rather than process-specific. A future harness mechanism that can prove equivalent continuation semantics without literally reusing the same OS process may satisfy it. TURNLOCK therefore does not require "same process" as a product invariant; it requires preservation of the continuing main-agent lineage.
L000923 
L000924 ## 0.11B A main-agent phase restores ordinary interactive agency, not an AI request/response call
L000925 
L000926 The main agent is valuable not only because it carries context but because it is already embedded in an interactive coding harness with its ordinary operating loop. During a main-agent phase, TURNLOCK should be able to rely on the agent behaving as the user's normal coding agent rather than being reduced to a single function call.
L000927 
L000928 A main-agent phase may therefore need to permit the ordinary class of behavior available in that session, such as:
L000929 
L000930 ```text
L000931 reason over the repository
L000932 inspect files and prior tool results
L000933 edit code
L000934 run tools and tests
L000935 change direction after new evidence
L000936 use harness-native capabilities
L000937 interact with the user when judgment requires it
L000938 continue until the phase's completion condition is satisfied
L000939 ```
L000940 
L000941 The governing distinction is:
L000942 
L000943 ```text
L000944 not:  workflow calls AI(prompt) and receives one result
L000945 
L000946 but:  workflow suspends its local execution authority
L000947       → ordinary main-agent agency is active for this region
L000948       → that region completes/yields
L000949       → workflow resumes
L000950 ```
L000951 
L000952 The restored ordinary agency can include repository edits according to the
L000953 capabilities of the surrounding environment, including edits of workflow
L000954 artifacts. Such local edits are authoring actions, not orchestration mutations:
L000955 they do not alter the governing definition or the declared global progression of
L000956 the already accepted invocation (Section 0.13E, `TL-INV-037`). A later
L000957 invocation may bind to an edited artifact under its own resolution semantics,
L000958 and active replanning or rebinding of the current invocation remains outside
L000959 the current product contract. Section 0.8B defines the responsibility boundary
L000960 between environment-provided local capability and TURNLOCK orchestration
L000961 authority.
L000962 
L000963 A one-shot LLM request/response is nevertheless a valid **separate** TURNLOCK primitive when that narrower semantic execution form is what the workflow requests. The prohibition here is only against implementing a declared main-agent continuation as though it were such a call.
L000964 
L000965 This lets TURNLOCK combine two properties that are otherwise often traded
L000966 against each other:
L000967 
L000968 ```text
L000969 mechanical, workflow-owned progression outside agentic regions
L000970 +
L000971 full coding-agent agency inside explicitly agentic regions
L000972 ```
L000973 
L000974 The workflow controls **when** agentic work occurs and what boundary it occupies. It does not need to reimplement or artificially narrow **how** the coding agent performs that work.
L000975 
L000976 ## 0.12 Supported coding harnesses are execution environments, not the product definition
L000977 
L000978 The motivating environment includes coding agents such as Claude Code, Pi, Codex, and similar interactive coding harnesses.
L000979 
L000980 TURNLOCK is not conceptually defined as a feature of only one of them.
L000981 
L000982 The product-level abstraction is:
L000983 
L000984 ```text
L000985 supported interactive coding harness
L000986   → workflow entry
L000987   → workflow-owned execution
L000988   ↔ main-agent handoffs
L000989   → return to interactive harness
L000990 ```
L000991 
L000992 Different harnesses may expose different integration capabilities. Those differences may constrain implementation or conformance tiers, but the workflow semantics should not be redefined merely because one harness exposes a different API.
L000993 
L000994 Portability does not mean every harness must use the same mechanism. It means the product should preserve the same user-facing control semantics wherever support is claimed.
L000995 
L000996 ## 0.12A Pi is the first reference harness, not the semantic definition of TURNLOCK
L000997 
L000998 TURNLOCK is intended to become **harness-agnostic**, but product development will first concentrate on making the model work deeply and naturally inside **Pi**.
L000999 
L001000 This is a sequencing decision, not a semantic narrowing of the product. The dependency direction is normative:
L001001 
L001002 ```text
L001003 TURNLOCK workflow semantics
L001004         ↓
L001005 harness integration contract
L001006         ↓
L001007 Pi realization first
L001008         ↓
L001009 later realizations for other supported harnesses
L001010 ```
L001011 
L001012 Pi-specific APIs, lifecycle events, extension hooks, skill/frontmatter conventions, or session mechanics MAY be used aggressively to realize the best possible first implementation. They MUST NOT silently become the definition of a TURNLOCK workflow primitive when the product-level concept can be stated independently of Pi.
L001013 
L001014 A workflow author should reason in TURNLOCK terms such as:
L001015 
L001016 ```text
L001017 mechanical execution
L001018 main-agent region
L001019 nested workflow invocation
L001020 return to immediate caller
L001021 ```
L001022 
L001023 not in Pi-internal operations required only to implement those semantics.
L001024 
L001025 The first implementation may expose capability gaps that force refinement of the abstract contract. Such refinement is allowed, but any rule that makes a Pi-specific mechanism part of the normative semantics requires an explicit product decision rather than accidental leakage from the reference integration.
L001026 
L001027 ## 0.13 The user can encode working method rather than prompt an agent to simulate it
L001028 
L001029 A central product outcome is that a recurring process can become an executable artifact.
L001030 
L001031 The distinction is:
L001032 
L001033 ```text
L001034 prompt/skill model:
L001035   "Agent, follow this procedure."
L001036 
L001037 TURNLOCK model:
L001038   procedure executes itself
L001039   and calls the main agent only at explicit agentic boundaries
L001040 ```
L001041 
L001042 This matters because the procedure should remain the procedure even if the main agent would otherwise choose a different order, omit a mechanical step, or reinterpret an instruction.
L001043 
L001044 The workflow therefore acts as a durable expression of the user's process, while agentic steps remain deliberate escape points into flexible reasoning and coding.
L001045 
L001046 ## 0.13A Workflow authoring is developer-native and agent-native
L001047 
L001048 TURNLOCK does not require a separate graphical workflow builder or a second AI product in order for users to create workflows. The intended authoring surface is developer experience: a developer can write a workflow directly, or ask the coding agent already present in the session to write or modify that workflow.
L001049 
L001050 Both paths target the **same workflow artifact** and the same TURNLOCK primitives:
L001051 
L001052 ```text
L001053 developer intent
L001054   → developer writes TURNLOCK workflow
L001055 
L001056 or
L001057 developer intent
L001058   → coding agent writes TURNLOCK workflow
L001059 
L001060                     ↓
L001061           same kind of workflow artifact
L001062                     ↓
L001063           same TURNLOCK execution semantics
L001064 ```
L001065 
L001066 Authorship does not confer runtime orchestration authority. A developer, coding
L001067 agent, LLM planner, or higher-level system may produce the artifact; once
L001068 execution begins, the artifact remains authoritative for its declared
L001069 orchestration and TURNLOCK executes it. Authorship does not prevent an author
L001070 that is also available under an existing execution form from later
L001071 participating. Any local authority then comes from an explicit workflow region,
L001072 including a main-agent continuation when the author is the existing main agent.
L001073 
L001074 TURNLOCK therefore provides **workflow primitives**, not a separate semantic language for human-authored versus agent-authored workflows. A coding agent generating a workflow is acting as a code author over TURNLOCK's public primitives, not invoking a privileged hidden generator protocol.
L001075 
L001076 The product requirement is not yet a concrete syntax. The exact language, library shape, file format, typing model, or packaging convention remains open. The invariant is that the authoring model must be simple and explicit enough that:
L001077 
L001078 ```text
L001079 a developer can inspect and edit it directly
L001080 a coding agent can generate and modify it from natural-language intent
L001081 the resulting artifact remains understandable as workflow code
L001082 control flow is expressed through TURNLOCK semantics rather than harness plumbing
L001083 ```
L001084 
L001085 TURNLOCK MAY later provide higher-level authoring tools, templates, or visualizations, but they are optional layers over the same underlying workflow artifact and primitives. They MUST NOT become necessary to express the core execution model.
L001086 
L001087 ## 0.13B Realized execution remains inspectable for iterative refinement
L001088 
L001089 A TURNLOCK workflow is a reusable executable representation of part of a user's
L001090 working method. Its execution MUST NOT become an opaque event when it reaches a
L001091 TURNLOCK-observed terminal or cessation outcome. For every accepted invocation
L001092 for which TURNLOCK observes normal completion or another terminal or cessation
L001093 outcome, the realized execution or realized prefix must remain sufficiently
L001094 inspectable for a user or higher-level system to determine how the workflow
L001095 progressed in practice without reconstructing it from human or agent
L001096 recollection.
L001097 
L001098 The scope is:
L001099 
L001100 ```text
L001101 accepted invocation
L001102 + TURNLOCK-observed normal completion or terminal/cessation outcome
L001103 → execution inspectability applies
L001104 
L001105 successful completion
L001106 → the realized execution
L001107 
L001108 observed non-success
L001109 → the realized prefix + actually known terminal facts
L001110 ```
L001111 
L001112 The realized prefix may be empty when the invocation was accepted and then
L001113 ceased before its first workflow occurrence. Unrealized downstream progression
L001114 MUST NOT be represented as executed, and unknown cause or state MUST NOT be
L001115 converted into an invented completion, failure cause, or other terminal fact. A
L001116 hard loss that prevents TURNLOCK from observing or exposing a terminal boundary
L001117 does not, by itself, create a crash-durable post-mortem evidence guarantee.
L001118 
L001119 The broader product loop is:
L001120 
L001121 ```text
L001122 author workflow
L001123 → execute workflow
L001124 → inspect and evaluate actual behavior
L001125 → refine workflow
L001126 → execute again
L001127 ↺
L001128 ```
L001129 
L001130 Debugging is one use of this capability, not its complete purpose. The product
L001131 value is that real execution can inform user- or system-led iterative refinement
L001132 of the reusable workflow artifact.
L001133 
L001134 Execution inspectability is a semantic sufficiency criterion, not an event-count
L001135 or event-catalog requirement. Inspection must preserve enough actual
L001136 TURNLOCK-visible execution truth for an eligible inspection context to determine
L001137 the realized workflow-mediated progression. When necessary, that includes
L001138 occurrence distinctions, multiplicity, structural and causal relationships,
L001139 effective control resolutions, explicitly exposed boundary inputs and results,
L001140 defined outcomes, and actually known terminal facts. A fact need not be
L001141 represented separately when it is unambiguously derivable from the actual
L001142 governing workflow definition together with the remaining inspectable execution
L001143 truth, so lossless semantic compression is permitted.
L001144 
L001145 Explicitly exposed boundary inputs, results, and defined outcomes remain
L001146 attributable to the occurrences that consumed or produced them when that
L001147 attribution is necessary to understand realized progression. Concurrent
L001148 occurrences that TURNLOCK semantics do not causally order MUST NOT be given an
L001149 artificial total order merely from scheduler timing. Private agent reasoning,
L001150 private chain-of-thought, arbitrary agent-interior activity, and internal tool
L001151 calls remain outside the universal minimum unless they become explicitly
L001152 exposed results or another TURNLOCK-visible progression fact.
L001153 
L001154 Inspection may rely on the invocation's actual governing workflow definition as
L001155 decoding and compression context, but a later or current mutable workflow
L001156 artifact cannot substitute for the definition that actually governed the
L001157 invocation or for historical execution truth.
L001158 
L001159 Required execution truth must survive until a realizable terminal inspection
L001160 handoff; Section 2.9 defines that handoff. Actual consumer participation,
L001161 successful delivery, processing, acknowledgment, persistence, and retention
L001162 duration are not universally required, and once TURNLOCK completes its side of a
L001163 conforming handoff this obligation alone does not require continued
L001164 post-handoff availability, persistence, or retention. Underlying execution
L001165 truth is distinct from a consumer-visible disclosure view: access or privacy
L001166 policy may give a particular consumer a more restrictive or redacted view, but
L001167 required execution truth must not be irreversibly substituted away before an
L001168 eligible conforming inspection context can acquire a semantically sufficient
L001169 representation through the required handoff.
L001170 
L001171 TURNLOCK owns the minimum execution-truth responsibility at its semantic
L001172 boundary. That boundary includes workflow-mediated structure, execution
L001173 boundaries, explicitly exposed inputs and results, and TURNLOCK-visible facts
L001174 relevant to declared progression. A user, the main agent, an external evaluator,
L001175 or a higher-level workflow or system defines what good means, performs any
L001176 evaluation or comparison, decides what should change, and modifies or optimizes
L001177 the workflow.
L001178 
L001179 This requirement does not make TURNLOCK itself an evaluator, benchmark system,
L001180 run comparator, experiment manager, or workflow optimizer. It does not require
L001181 disclosure of private agent reasoning or automatically require every tool call
L001182 inside an agentic region to be recorded. Nor does it imply replay,
L001183 computational or output determinism, identical traces, cross-run comparability,
L001184 reproducibility, permanent retention, execution proofs, or a particular tracing,
L001185 storage, telemetry, or user-interface mechanism.
L001186 
L001187 ## 0.13C Evaluation and optimization policy remain outside TURNLOCK core
L001188 
L001189 Section 0.13B requires TURNLOCK to expose enough actual execution truth for
L001190 evaluation. Exposing that truth is distinct from owning evaluation or
L001191 optimization policy, and the product does not treat those responsibilities as
L001192 one implied package.
L001193 
L001194 TURNLOCK core is the workflow execution substrate. It MUST NOT define a
L001195 universal evaluation objective, universal quality metrics, a default
L001196 superiority relation between workflows or executions, experiment policy, or an
L001197 autonomous workflow optimizer. Nothing in the product definition requires a
L001198 privileged evaluator abstraction, and neither workflow evaluation nor workflow
L001199 optimization becomes a core TURNLOCK capability merely because completed
L001200 executions are inspectable.
L001201 
L001202 Evaluation objectives and criteria are supplied and owned outside TURNLOCK core
L001203 policy by an explicitly responsible user, coding agent, evaluator, higher-level
L001204 system, or ordinary TURNLOCK workflow. Those actors may interpret execution
L001205 truth, form assessments, compare executions where their own contracts make
L001206 comparison meaningful, and propose or author an improved workflow.
L001207 
L001208 Evaluation or optimization logic MAY itself be expressed as an ordinary
L001209 TURNLOCK workflow. That execution is ordinary authored behavior under the same
L001210 TURNLOCK semantics and authority boundaries as any other workflow; it does not
L001211 become privileged runtime machinery merely because it evaluates another
L001212 execution or proposes a workflow change.
L001213 
L001214 If evaluation or optimization produces an improved workflow artifact, that
L001215 result is workflow authorship. It does not authorize the TURNLOCK runtime to
L001216 mutate the orchestration of a currently executing invocation, and it does not
L001217 transfer execution authority to the evaluator or optimizer.
L001218 
L001219 The product rule is:
L001220 
L001221 ```text
L001222 TURNLOCK makes workflows evaluable and optimizable
L001223 !=
L001224 TURNLOCK core is the evaluator or optimizer
L001225 ```
L001226 
L001227 The relationship is:
L001228 
L001229 ```text
L001230 workflow W
L001231     → TURNLOCK executes W
L001232     → inspectable actual execution truth
L001233     → user / coding agent / evaluator / higher-level system / ordinary workflow
L001234     → evaluation against an explicitly supplied objective
L001235     → possible authoring of workflow W'
L001236     → TURNLOCK later executes W'
L001237 ```
L001238 
L001239 This boundary does not prohibit future TURNLOCK-adjacent modules, libraries,
L001240 profiles, or tools for evaluation and optimization. It establishes that they
L001241 are not part of the current core product contract and that any future proposal
L001242 adding native evaluator interfaces, experiment concepts, comparison contracts,
L001243 optimizer machinery, privileged mutation authority, or stronger evaluation
L001244 guarantees requires its own accepted product decision.
L001245 
L001246 ## 0.13D Effective execution-condition provenance remains capturable
L001247 
L001248 TURNLOCK MUST preserve the attribution of effective execution conditions that it
L001249 selects, binds, explicitly supplies, or resolves at its semantic boundary to the
L001250 execution scopes they govern. That relationship must remain semantically
L001251 distinguished and exposable or capturable at an execution boundary rather than
L001252 existing only as hidden transient adapter state or requiring reconstruction from
L001253 later mutable state, human recollection, or agent recollection.
L001254 
L001255 The product layers remain distinct:
L001256 
L001257 ```text
L001258 workflow execution
L001259         ↓
L001260 actual execution truth
L001261 +
L001262 effective execution-condition provenance
L001263         ↓
L001264 external evaluation or optimization policy
L001265 ```
L001266 
L001267 This obligation exists now because evaluation, comparison, reproducibility, and
L001268 replay features can be added later, while provenance discarded when TURNLOCK
L001269 possesses the governing information may not be recoverable later. It does not
L001270 accept any of those future features.
L001271 
L001272 The universal floor applies to conditions TURNLOCK itself selects, binds,
L001273 explicitly supplies, or resolves. Conditions outside TURNLOCK's observation or
L001274 control MAY remain unavailable or unknown. Unknown MUST NOT be presented as
L001275 known-equal across executions or as evidence that no relevant difference
L001276 exists.
L001277 
L001278 Exact-value disclosure is not required by this provenance floor. When TURNLOCK
L001279 knows a specific effective condition but its underlying value is protected or
L001280 unsafe to disclose, a semantic representation containing information specific
L001281 to that known condition MUST remain bound to its effective-condition occurrence
L001282 and governed execution scope and capturable through TURNLOCK's required
L001283 realizable semantic-boundary capture handoff. Protection or redaction MUST NOT
L001284 substitute away that condition-specific information before or during the
L001285 handoff. An occurrence label or generic protected marker alone is not
L001286 condition-specific information. Such a marker MAY be a consumer-visible view,
L001287 but it is insufficient as the sole provenance representation when TURNLOCK
L001288 possessed more specific condition provenance.
L001289 
L001290 The required semantic-boundary capture opportunity is the realizable
L001291 semantic-boundary capture handoff, not a minimum storage duration or retention
L001292 interval. Before TURNLOCK may irreversibly lose provenance required by this
L001293 obligation, that provenance must reach a semantic-boundary interaction through
L001294 which an eligible conforming capture context could acquire the required
L001295 condition-specific provenance and governed-scope attribution as part of that
L001296 boundary interaction. Acquisition must not depend on inaccessible transient
L001297 internal state, accidental timing against TURNLOCK's internal execution, or
L001298 later reconstruction from mutable state, human recollection, or agent
L001299 recollection. Sufficiency is therefore not defined by elapsed time, and a
L001300 logically instantaneous opportunity may conform when capture is realizable as
L001301 part of the boundary interaction itself.
L001302 
L001303 The handoff is discharged when TURNLOCK completes its side of that
L001304 semantic-boundary interaction through a structurally realizable capture
L001305 capability: an eligible conforming capture context could have been established
L001306 in time to participate and acquire the required provenance, whether or not such
L001307 a context was actually attached. Discharge does not require actual receiver
L001308 participation, successful delivery, consumer processing, persistence, or
L001309 acknowledgment. Mere internal existence without such a boundary interaction does
L001310 not discharge the obligation.
L001311 
L001312 The universal floor does not require an actual capture consumer for every
L001313 invocation, successful delivery, consumer processing or acknowledgment,
L001314 retry-until-success, buffering, or TURNLOCK-operated persistence. The absence
L001315 of an attached consumer does not by itself make a conforming runtime
L001316 non-conforming when a real semantic capability exists through which an eligible
L001317 capture context could have been established in time to participate. In that
L001318 no-consumer case, TURNLOCK must still complete its side of the semantic-boundary
L001319 interaction described above; structural capability without that boundary
L001320 interaction does not itself discharge the obligation. Conversely, a runtime
L001321 that keeps required provenance only as inaccessible transient internal state
L001322 does not satisfy this obligation.
L001323 
L001324 Once TURNLOCK has completed a conforming realizable semantic-boundary capture
L001325 handoff as defined above, this obligation does not by itself require the
L001326 provenance to remain capturable. Post-handoff availability, persistence, and
L001327 retention remain separately governed, and another accepted invariant, decision,
L001328 profile, or integration contract may require them.
L001329 
L001330 The contract therefore distinguishes absence of TURNLOCK knowledge from a known
L001331 condition whose value is protected. Consumer-visible disclosure and underlying
L001332 provenance capture capability are not equivalent: a particular consumer MAY
L001333 receive a more restrictive view, while access to the underlying provenance available through the realizable
L001334 semantic-boundary capture handoff remains subject to separately governed policy. This rule defines no authorization model,
L001335 additional consumer context, post-boundary availability, persistence, or
L001336 retention, and does not require disclosure through ordinary UI, logs, CLI
L001337 output, telemetry, or inspection surfaces.
L001338 
L001339 The relevance of a condition remains relative to an externally supplied
L001340 property:
L001341 
L001342 ```text
L001343 Are executions E1 and E2 comparable for property P?
L001344 ```
L001345 
L001346 TURNLOCK core does not define which conditions matter to `P`, decide whether two
L001347 executions are comparable, select a superior execution, or own the objective or
L001348 optimization policy. Those judgments remain with the explicitly responsible
L001349 actor under Section 0.13C.
L001350 
L001351 Semantic distinction, runtime availability, exposability, capture, persistence,
L001352 and retention are separate responsibilities. This obligation requires semantic
L001353 distinction, attribution, and an execution-boundary means of exposure or
L001354 capture. It does not require a TURNLOCK-owned database, post-execution
L001355 persistence, permanent retention, canonical event log, run model, replay
L001356 facility, or reproduction guarantee.
L001357 
L001358 Once an effective condition governs part of an accepted invocation, its
L001359 attribution does not become semantically nonexistent solely because the
L001360 invocation later fails, is cancelled, or is interrupted. This rule does not
L001361 define those terminal outcomes or the detailed inspectability of non-completed
L001362 executions.
L001363 
L001364 ## 0.13E An accepted invocation keeps its governing workflow definition
L001365 
L001366 Every accepted TURNLOCK workflow invocation has a governing workflow
L001367 definition. TURNLOCK must determine that definition no later than invocation
L001368 acceptance, and it remains the source of declared workflow topology for the
L001369 lifetime of that invocation. An ordinary subsequent edit of the workflow source
L001370 artifact does not alter the governing definition of an invocation that has
L001371 already been accepted, so the active invocation does not silently begin
L001372 following a later definition merely because its source artifact changed.
L001373 
L001374 Each nested workflow invocation is a distinct invocation. It establishes its
L001375 own governing workflow definition no later than its own acceptance. A caller's
L001376 governing definition does not, merely by governing the caller, transitively
L001377 bind or freeze the definitions of workflows that may later be invoked from
L001378 inside the caller.
L001379 
L001380 ```text
L001381 artifact W = D1
L001382 
L001383 accept invocation I of W
L001384 → governing definition(I) = D1
L001385 
L001386 artifact W later changes:
L001387 D1 → D2
L001388 
L001389 I continues under D1
L001390 
L001391 later accept invocation J of W
L001392 → J receives the definition the applicable resolution semantics determine
L001393   for J at J's acceptance
L001394 ```
L001395 
L001396 This requirement concerns which definition governs an active invocation, not
L001397 how that definition is identified or represented. It does not make source
L001398 artifacts immutable, and it does not define how a workflow reference resolves
L001399 to a definition or whether an unqualified workflow name selects the latest
L001400 version.
L001401 
L001402 Ordinary artifact editing is not an operation that mutates the governing
L001403 definition of an active invocation. Source-artifact self-authoring may occur
L001404 when the surrounding execution environment permits it; it does not rebind,
L001405 replan, or replace the orchestration of the invocation that is already accepted.
L001406 The current invocation continues under its governing definition, and a later
L001407 invocation may bind to the edited artifact under its own resolution semantics.
L001408 A recursive invocation follows the same rule: when the active definition's
L001409 already-declared semantics invoke the workflow again, the new invocation
L001410 independently resolves and binds its own governing definition.
L001411 
L001412 Active replanning, active rebinding, and replacement of the governing workflow
L001413 definition of an accepted invocation are outside and contrary to the current
L001414 product contract. They are not an open future feature, not a reserved
L001415 transition, and not a forward-compatibility obligation. A later proposal to
L001416 introduce such behavior would explicitly change the governing product semantics
L001417 and would have to reconcile with `TL-INV-037` and the decisions that state this
L001418 boundary.
L001419 
L001420 The requirement is distinct from replay and reproducibility: keeping one
L001421 invocation's governing definition stable does not make execution deterministic,
L001422 repeatable, comparable, or reproducible, and it does not require a transitive
L001423 snapshot of an entire execution tree. Whether the surrounding environment
L001424 permits an execution resource to edit the source artifact of a workflow that

L002152 
L002153 ## 2.1 Main agent
L002154 
L002155 <a id="term-main-agent"></a>
L002156 
L002157 The **main agent** is the coding agent participating in the user's surrounding interactive session.
L002158 
L002159 It is the agent that has the user-facing conversational continuity before workflow entry and to which the workflow returns when execution finishes.
L002160 
L002161 A main-agent step temporarily makes that agent active inside workflow execution.
L002162 
L002163 The main agent does not thereby become the owner of the workflow's global control flow.
L002164 
L002165 ## 2.2 Workflow
L002166 
L002167 <a id="term-workflow"></a>
L002168 
L002169 A **workflow** is an executable user-defined process that owns progression across its steps after entry and until termination.
L002170 
L002171 A workflow may contain mechanical phases, bounded raw-LLM inference phases, independent-agent phases, main-agent continuation phases, control-flow/composition operations, and nested workflow invocations.
L002172 
L002173 It is not merely a prompt describing desired sequencing.
L002174 
L002175 The workflow must retain enough execution truth to resume after temporary main-agent control.
L002176 
L002177 ## 2.2A Execution region
L002178 
L002179 <a id="term-execution-region"></a>
L002180 
L002181 An **execution region** is a workflow-declared semantic scope in which one
L002182 execution form performs declared work with local execution authority, without
L002183 thereby acquiring authority over the enclosing workflow's global orchestration.
L002184 The declaration identifies the region's place and continuation in workflow
L002185 semantics; a runtime occurrence is one execution of that declared region.
L002186 
L002187 This distinction requires no `Region` data type, stable activation identifier,
L002188 process, thread, coroutine, or other runtime representation. It provides only
L002189 the structural boundary needed to distinguish entry, local activity, and an
L002190 applicable completion transition without implying that completion must occur.
L002191 
L002192 ## 2.3 Workflow invocation surface
L002193 
L002194 <a id="term-workflow-invocation-surface"></a>
L002195 
L002196 A **workflow invocation surface** is the session-local user interaction through which a TURNLOCK workflow is selected and started.
L002197 
L002198 For supported coding-agent harnesses, the ordinary invocation surface is a **natural slash command comparable to invoking a native skill**. The concrete command name, namespace, registration mechanism, and mapping between commands and workflows are intentionally not fixed yet.
L002199 
L002200 The invocation surface should be small in semantic responsibility: it selects/starts workflow-owned execution rather than embedding the workflow's orchestration into the main-agent prompt.
L002201 
L002202 ## 2.3A Workflow artifact and TURNLOCK primitives
L002203 
L002204 <a id="term-workflow-artifact"></a>
L002205 
L002206 A **workflow artifact** is the developer-readable executable representation of a TURNLOCK workflow. A developer may author it directly or a coding agent may author it on the developer's behalf. Those are two authorship paths to the same semantic object, not two workflow classes.
L002207 
L002208 <a id="term-turnlock-primitives"></a>
L002209 
L002210 **TURNLOCK primitives** are the author-facing operations that express TURNLOCK's control semantics. Their exact syntax and full set are not fixed yet, but they must represent product concepts at TURNLOCK level rather than require workflow authors to reproduce harness-specific control plumbing.
L002211 
L002212 Pi-specific APIs may implement these primitives in the first integration; they are not themselves automatically TURNLOCK primitives.
L002213 
L002214 ## 2.4 Mechanical execution and mechanical step
L002215 
L002216 <a id="term-mechanical-execution"></a>
L002217 
L002218 **Mechanical execution** is non-agent-mediated progression governed by
L002219 executable workflow semantics together with runtime inputs, results, state, or
L002220 events. The term identifies execution and control authority, not computational
L002221 or output determinism. Mechanical execution may be deterministic,
L002222 nondeterministic, probabilistic, dependent on external state, or event-driven.
L002223 
L002224 <a id="term-mechanical-step"></a>
L002225 
L002226 A **mechanical step** is a workflow phase that uses mechanical execution. Its
L002227 progression does not require discretionary agent judgment to supply a missing
L002228 orchestration decision. It may consume an LLM or agent result without inheriting
L002229 the producer's local authority; a declared rule that branches on that result
L002230 remains mechanical.
L002231 
L002232 This specification intentionally does not yet fix which mechanical primitives
L002233 exist or how they are expressed.
L002234 
L002235 A mechanical step may produce state or evidence consumed by later steps,
L002236 including a main-agent step.
L002237 
L002238 ## 2.4A Raw LLM inference and raw LLM inference step
L002239 
L002240 <a id="term-raw-llm-inference"></a>
L002241 
L002242 **Raw LLM inference** is a bounded, non-agentic semantic operation in which an
L002243 explicit instruction and explicit context are supplied to a model and produce a
L002244 result. `Bounded` identifies one declared TURNLOCK operation with an input and
L002245 result boundary. It does not establish an autonomous observe/reason/act loop, a
L002246 persistent independent cognitive lineage, or global workflow-orchestration
L002247 authority.
L002248 
L002249 The operation is one-shot at the TURNLOCK semantic level only. It does not
L002250 require exactly one provider request, one physical model call, one attempt, no
L002251 internal retry, or no streaming. Nor does its boundary select a token, cost,
L002252 time, request, or other resource limit or guarantee that an occurrence
L002253 completes. If and when a result is produced, workflow semantics may consume it
L002254 only through declared progression.
L002255 
L002256 <a id="term-raw-llm-inference-step"></a>
L002257 
L002258 A **raw LLM inference step** is the workflow phase that supplies the explicit
L002259 instruction and context to, and receives the constitutive result of, raw LLM
L002260 inference.
L002261 
L002262 Its semantic shape is:
L002263 
L002264 ```text
L002265 explicit instruction + explicit context → model inference → result
L002266 ```
L002267 
L002268 It may be executed singly or as part of declared parallel fan-out.
L002269 
L002270 ## 2.4B Independent agent and independent-agent step
L002271 
L002272 <a id="term-independent-agent"></a>
L002273 
L002274 An **independent agent** is an agentic execution resource that operates within a
L002275 fresh cognitive lineage distinct from the main agent for a workflow-declared
L002276 local task. Its initial cognitive context consists only of information supplied
L002277 explicitly through workflow semantics; it receives no implicit inheritance of
L002278 the main agent's cognitive history. It may then acquire information through the
L002279 capabilities available during its autonomous multi-turn reasoning, tool use,
L002280 observation, and adaptation.
L002281 
L002282 For independent-agent execution, `bounded` means that the workflow declares the
L002283 local task, initial cognitive-context provenance, place in the workflow, and
L002284 continuation, while the agent exercises only local available authority. It does
L002285 not mean that all physical effects remain inside the region, impose a maximum
L002286 number of turns, tokens, tool calls, cost, or time, require a timeout or
L002287 cancellation rule, or guarantee completion.
L002288 
L002289 The workflow owns the declared task boundary. The agent owns its local plan,
L002290 tactics, exploration, ordering of local actions, and hypothesis changes while
L002291 exercising available authority. It cannot create additional authority merely by
L002292 wanting it and cannot acquire global workflow-orchestration authority through
L002293 local autonomy. These rules do not prescribe a capability manifest, tool list,
L002294 permission system, context format, or resource budget.
L002295 
L002296 <a id="term-independent-agent-step"></a>
L002297 
L002298 An **independent-agent step** is the execution region in which workflow semantics
L002299 declare the local task, initial cognitive context, and continuation for an
L002300 independent agent. Its semantic shape is:
L002301 
L002302 ```text
L002303 workflow-declared local task
L002304 + fresh distinct cognitive lineage
L002305 + explicitly supplied initial cognitive context
L002306 → autonomous multi-turn local work
L002307 → normal completion if reached
L002308 → optional declared output
L002309 → workflow-owned continuation
L002310 ```
L002311 
L002312 Effects, output, and completion are distinct. Effects are changes caused during
L002313 execution and may persist beyond the region. Output is a business value exposed
L002314 to workflow semantics when the declared contract requires one; a non-empty
L002315 business payload is otherwise not mandatory. Completion is the fact that a
L002316 runtime occurrence reached its normal boundary. If normal completion occurs,
L002317 TURNLOCK can recognize it, workflow-owned progression follows the declared
L002318 continuation, and any contract-required output becomes available. This
L002319 conditional rule does not guarantee that every started occurrence completes.
L002320 
L002321 Fresh lineage does not mean absence of runtime or system instructions, tool
L002322 descriptions, harness environment, or technical execution state. Explicitly
L002323 supplying main-agent-derived summaries, artifacts, files, or prior results also
L002324 does not constitute implicit lineage inheritance.
L002325 
L002326 An agent spawned internally by the main agent during a main-agent region remains
L002327 local delegation under ordinary main-agent agency unless workflow semantics
L002328 explicitly declare it as a first-class TURNLOCK independent-agent region. The
L002329 fresh-lineage context-provenance rule does not automatically apply to such an
L002330 internal child. Multiple workflow-declared independent-agent steps may execute
L002331 concurrently, whether they perform the same task or different tasks.
L002332 
L002333 ## 2.5 Main-agent handoff and main-agent step
L002334 
L002335 <a id="term-main-agent-handoff"></a>
L002336 
L002337 A **main-agent handoff** is the temporary transfer of local execution authority
L002338 from an active workflow to the main agent defined in Section 2.1, followed by a
L002339 return of execution authority to the workflow at the declared continuation. It
L002340 uses the existing main-agent cognitive lineage and ordinary interactive agency;
L002341 a raw LLM call or fresh independent agent is not an equivalent handoff.
L002342 
L002343 <a id="term-main-agent-step"></a>
L002344 
L002345 A **main-agent step** is the workflow phase bounded by that handoff and return.
L002346 Its defining lifecycle is:
L002347 
L002348 ```text
L002349 workflow active
L002350 → handoff to main agent
L002351 → main agent active
L002352 → main-agent phase reaches its completion boundary
L002353 → workflow resumes
L002354 ```
L002355 
L002356 The completion boundary mechanism is not specified yet.
L002357 
L002358 ## 2.6 Invocation context and caller stack
L002359 
L002360 <a id="term-immediate-caller-context"></a>
L002361 
L002362 An **immediate caller context** is the execution context that invoked a workflow and to which normal completion of that workflow returns.
L002363 
L002364 For a top-level workflow, the caller is the surrounding main-agent interaction.
L002365 For a nested workflow, the caller is the calling execution context inside the
L002366 enclosing workflow. For a main-agent-selected invocation, that context is the
L002367 main-agent region. For a workflow-declared invocation, that context is the
L002368 workflow execution context that performs the declared call. For an
L002369 independent-agent-selected invocation admitted under explicitly delegated
L002370 nested-workflow invocation authority, that context is the independent-agent
L002371 region that selected the call.
L002372 
L002373 A caller context preserves a call continuation while the callee executes. The continuation is not itself the caller context; it is the preserved return state of that context.
L002374 
L002375 <a id="term-caller-stack"></a>
L002376 
L002377 A **caller stack** is the conceptual structured nesting of suspended immediate
L002378 caller contexts and active workflow invocations. Nested invocations therefore
L002379 form a caller stack conceptually:
L002380 
L002381 ```text
L002382 main session
L002383   workflow A
L002384     main-agent region A
L002385       workflow B
L002386         main-agent region B
L002387           workflow C
L002388         ←
L002389       ←
L002390     ←
L002391   ←
L002392 main session
L002393 ```
L002394 
L002395 This is a semantic model, not a requirement to implement a literal process stack. The invariant is structured suspension and return to the immediate caller.
L002396 
L002397 ## 2.7 Control ownership and workflow-owned control
L002398 
L002399 <a id="term-control-ownership"></a>
L002400 
L002401 **Control ownership** is the authority to direct execution within the currently
L002402 active phase or context. It is phase-local and does not by itself grant authority
L002403 over the enclosing workflow's global progression.
L002404 
L002405 <a id="term-workflow-owned-control"></a>
L002406 
L002407 **Workflow-owned control** is the arrangement in which the workflow program is
L002408 the source of truth for declared global orchestration decisions, topology, and
L002409 permitted continuations, while TURNLOCK is the engine that executes and tracks
L002410 that progression. Runtime inputs, results, state, or events may select among
L002411 those declared possibilities; they do not create undeclared continuations.
L002412 
L002413 ```text
L002414 outside workflow:
L002415   main agent owns ordinary interaction
L002416 
L002417 inside mechanical phase:
L002418   workflow semantics govern permitted progression
L002419   TURNLOCK performs mechanical execution
L002420 
L002421 inside raw-LLM phase:
L002422   workflow owns progression and the model produces a bounded semantic result
L002423 
L002424 inside independent-agent phase:
L002425   independent agent owns local autonomous execution for its bounded task
L002426   workflow remains the enclosing progression authority
L002427 
L002428 inside main-agent phase:
L002429   main agent temporarily owns local interactive execution
L002430   workflow remains the enclosing progression authority
L002431 
L002432 after workflow termination:
L002433   control returns to the immediate caller
L002434 ```
L002435 
L002436 This distinction is central to TURNLOCK.
L002437 
L002438 ## 2.8 Parallel and nested composition
L002439 
L002440 <a id="term-parallel-fan-out-fan-in"></a>
L002441 
L002442 **Parallel fan-out/fan-in** is workflow-declared composition in which independent
L002443 branches may execute concurrently and are synchronized or collected before the
L002444 workflow takes its declared continuation. Each branch retains the semantics of
L002445 its execution form, and the workflow owns the branch topology and join.
L002446 
L002447 <a id="term-nested-workflow-invocation"></a>
L002448 
L002449 A **nested workflow invocation** is a workflow invocation made from an immediate
L002450 caller context inside an enclosing workflow while the continuation of that
L002451 calling context is suspended. The invocation MAY be declared by the enclosing
L002452 workflow program, selected by the main agent while it legitimately owns a
L002453 main-agent region, or selected by a workflow-declared independent-agent region
L002454 that has been explicitly delegated nested-workflow selection/invocation
L002455 authority. Every selected invocation remains independently subject to the
L002456 authority and admissibility rules applicable to its caller context. The nested
L002457 workflow owns its own declared progression, and normal completion returns to
L002458 that same immediate caller context.
L002459 
L002460 ## 2.8A Nested-composition admissibility
L002461 
L002462 <a id="term-nested-composition-admissibility"></a>
L002463 
L002464 **Nested-composition admissibility** is the semantic condition under which an
L002465 otherwise authorized attempted nested workflow invocation may be accepted in its
L002466 caller and surrounding execution context.
L002467 
L002468 An attempted invocation is composition-admissible only when the workflow
L002469 definition that would govern the callee if accepted preserves every
L002470 admissibility restriction whose accepted scope applies to that composition.
L002471 
L002472 Such restrictions may depend on facts outside the callee in isolation,
L002473 including declared causal ordering, co-reachability, mutual exclusion,
L002474 cognitive-lineage identity, caller provenance, surrounding parallel topology,
L002475 or restriction-specific ancestry.
L002476 
L002477 When a restriction's accepted scope extends into descendant invocation, later
L002478 nested attempts remain subject to that restriction at their own admission
L002479 boundaries.
L002480 
L002481 If required preservation cannot be established at an attempted invocation's
L002482 acceptance boundary, that invocation is not admissible for acceptance.
L002483 
L002484 This definition specifies a semantic relation, not an effect system, capability
L002485 lattice, static-analysis algorithm, graph representation, proof object, runtime
L002486 token, or implementation data structure.
L002487 
L002488 ## 2.9 Execution inspectability
L002489 
L002490 <a id="term-execution-inspectability"></a>
L002491 
L002492 **Execution inspectability** is the semantic property that applies to an
L002493 accepted workflow invocation for which TURNLOCK observes normal completion or
L002494 another terminal or cessation outcome, and that preserves enough actual
L002495 TURNLOCK-visible execution truth for an eligible inspection context to determine
L002496 the workflow-mediated progression that was actually realized or, for an
L002497 observed non-success outcome, the realized prefix together with the terminal
L002498 facts TURNLOCK actually knows.
L002499 
L002500 Sufficiency is semantic, not an event-catalog or event-count requirement.
L002501 Inspection must preserve the TURNLOCK-semantic distinctions and relationships
L002502 needed to distinguish actually different realized progressions, including
L002503 occurrence distinctions, multiplicity, structural and causal relationships,
L002504 effective control resolutions, and attribution of explicitly exposed boundary
L002505 inputs, results, and defined outcomes when those distinctions are necessary. A
L002506 fact need not be represented separately when it is unambiguously derivable from
L002507 the invocation's actual governing workflow definition and the remaining
L002508 inspectable execution truth; lossless semantic compression is permitted.
L002509 Semantically unordered concurrent occurrences must not receive an invented total
L002510 order from scheduler timing.
L002511 
L002512 Its semantic boundary comprises workflow-mediated structure, execution
L002513 boundaries, explicitly exposed inputs and results, and TURNLOCK-visible facts
L002514 relevant to declared progression. Private or internal reasoning of raw LLM
L002515 inference, independent agents, and the main agent remains outside the universal
L002516 minimum unless information from such a region becomes an explicitly exposed
L002517 result or another TURNLOCK-visible progression fact. An inspection that relies
L002518 on a governing workflow definition may use only the definition that actually
L002519 governed the invocation; a later or current mutable workflow artifact cannot
L002520 substitute for it.
L002521 
L002522 Execution inspectability enables evaluation and refinement; it does not mean
L002523 that TURNLOCK defines evaluation criteria, compares executions, or optimizes the
L002524 workflow. The term does not prescribe a run model, event schema, identifier,
L002525 storage, telemetry, retention, replay, comparison, reproducibility, proof, or
L002526 user-interface mechanism.

L003738   after every workflow step.
L003739 - The concrete scheduler mechanism, runtime representation of a progression
L003740   occurrence, and formal WF/SF or other fairness encoding used to realize
L003741   `TL-INV-042`; the occurrence-scoped conditional non-starvation obligation

L003746 # 5. Architectural implications already forced by the intent
L003747 
L003748 This section records only implications that follow directly from the current invariants. It deliberately avoids selecting concrete mechanisms.
L003749 
L003750 ## 5.1 There must be an execution authority outside ordinary main-agent reasoning
L003751 
L003752 Because the workflow owns progression and mechanical steps must execute independently of agent interpretation, some execution authority must exist that is not merely the main agent following prose.
L003753 
L003754 This does not determine whether that authority is implemented as a script process, extension runtime, embedded interpreter, supervisor, harness plugin, protocol peer, or another mechanism.
L003755 
L003756 ## 5.2 There must be a bidirectional control boundary
L003757 
L003758 The architecture must support both transitions:
L003759 
L003760 ```text
L003761 workflow → main agent
L003762 main agent → workflow
L003763 ```
L003764 
L003765 Supporting only workflow → agent invocation is insufficient.
L003766 
L003767 ## 5.3 There must be an explicit structured return path
L003768 
L003769 The architecture must support workflow completion as a return to the immediate caller:
L003770 
L003771 ```text
L003772 workflow → immediate caller context
L003773 ```
L003774 
L003775 For a top-level invocation, that caller is the surrounding main-agent interaction. For a nested invocation, that caller is the calling execution context inside the enclosing workflow: the suspended main-agent region that selected the invocation, or the workflow execution context that performs a workflow-declared invocation. The implementation may use any mechanism, but it must preserve this structured return relationship.
L003776 
L003777 ## 5.4 Workflow progression cannot live only in prompt context
L003778 
L003779 Because the workflow resumes after main-agent execution and may do so repeatedly, continuation position and sufficient execution state require a representation independent of the main agent's memory.
L003780 
L003781 ## 5.5 Harness integration is a capability boundary
L003782 
L003783 Claude Code, Pi, Codex, and other harnesses may expose different control primitives.
L003784 
L003785 TURNLOCK will therefore eventually need to distinguish:
L003786 
L003787 ```text
L003788 product semantics
L003789 from
L003790 harness-specific realization capability
L003791 ```
L003792 
L003793 The implementation may need different integration strategies, but those strategies must be evaluated against the same reference scenario rather than defining separate products.
L003794 
L003795 ## 5.6 The main-agent capability surface must survive handoff
L003796 
L003797 Because a main-agent region restores ordinary interactive agency and may invoke another TURNLOCK workflow, the integration must preserve enough of the session's workflow-discovery/invocation surface for the main agent to use available workflows while inside a handoff region.
L003798 
L003799 This does not require a particular frontmatter format, command registry, or harness API. It requires only that workflow entry through TURNLOCK not erase the main agent's ability to discover, select, or invoke workflows that the session exposes.
L003800 
L003801 ## 5.7 Nested invocation requires structured suspension, not replacement
L003802 
L003803 The execution model must be able to suspend a caller context while a nested workflow runs and later resume that same caller context. A flat "current workflow" slot that is overwritten by nested invocation would violate the immediate-caller return invariant unless it provides equivalent structured semantics by another mechanism.
L003804 
L003805 ## 5.8 Authoring primitives must sit above harness plumbing
L003806 
L003807 Because both developers and coding agents author workflows against TURNLOCK semantics, the public workflow-authoring surface must not require knowledge of Pi-specific control hooks merely to express a main-agent region, mechanical step, nested invocation, or structured return.
L003808 
L003809 The first Pi implementation may internally translate those primitives to Pi-specific mechanisms. That translation belongs below the workflow artifact.
L003810 
L003811 ## 5.9 Pi should be optimized as the first integration without owning the ontology
L003812 
L003813 The first implementation should use Pi's capabilities fully rather than artificially pretending every harness is identical. However, every Pi-specific mechanism introduced should be classifiable as either:
L003814 
L003815 ```text
L003816 TURNLOCK semantic concept realized through Pi
L003817 ```
L003818 
L003819 or:
L003820 
L003821 ```text
L003822 Pi adapter implementation detail
L003823 ```
L003824 
L003825 If it fits neither category, the architecture has likely allowed the reference harness to leak into the product model and requires an explicit decision.
L003826 
L003827 ## 5.10 The runtime needs more than one semantic execution adapter
L003828 
L003829 Because raw LLM inference, independent-agent execution, and main-agent continuation have different semantics, the runtime cannot treat them as one generic "AI call" without losing product meaning. The architecture must preserve their distinct lifecycle and context contracts even if one harness/provider happens to implement multiple forms through related APIs.
L003830 
L003831 ## 5.11 Parallel orchestration must exist outside agent judgment
L003832 
L003833 Workflow-owned fan-out/fan-in requires an execution authority capable of starting independent branches, tracking their completion/results, and resuming declared continuation without asking the main agent to remember or schedule the parallel graph.
L003834 
L003835 That authority must support heterogeneous parallel graphs rather than assuming all branches use one execution primitive. A single fan-out may combine mechanical execution, bounded raw LLM calls, and
L003836 bounded independent agents, while preserving the distinct lifecycle and context
L003837 contract of every branch.
L003838 
L003839 This implication does not select a concurrency mechanism, scheduler, worker model, or process topology.
L003840 
L003841 ## 5.12 Context construction becomes an explicit boundary
L003842 
L003843 Independent agents and raw LLM calls derive value from deliberately supplied
L003844 context. TURNLOCK therefore needs an architectural place where instructions,
L003845 task inputs, and context are assembled without conflating explicit workflow data
L003846 flow with implicit inheritance of the main-agent cognitive lineage.
L003847 
L003848 For a workflow-declared independent agent, initial cognitive context must be
L003849 attributable to explicit workflow semantics. This requirement does not apply
L003850 automatically to child agents created through ordinary local main-agent
L003851 delegation. The exact representation, serialization, context API, and dataflow
L003852 mechanism remain open.
L003853 
L003854 ## 5.13 The orchestration core must remain richer than a prompt sequencer
L003855 
L003856 Because workflows may combine general computation, concurrency, semantic calls, independent agency, main-agent continuation, and nested composition, TURNLOCK cannot satisfy the product intent by merely expanding prompts sent to an agent. Its executable control layer must represent the declared topology directly.
L003857 
L003858 ## 5.14 The runtime is an orchestration engine, not an orchestration author
L003859 
L003860 TURNLOCK requires real execution authority: it must schedule declared regions, track workflow state, coordinate parallel branches, realize harness handoffs, and resume continuations. That makes TURNLOCK an orchestration engine.
L003861 
L003862 However, the source of declared global orchestration decisions remains the workflow program. The runtime architecture must therefore separate:
L003863 
L003864 ```text
L003865 workflow semantics / authored topology
L003866 from
L003867 runtime execution / scheduling machinery
L003868 ```
L003869 
L003870 A scheduler, adapter, optimizer, or execution backend may select equivalent mechanisms for fulfilling a declared primitive, but it must not silently become a policy engine that invents a different workflow.
L003871 
L003872 ## 5.15 Execution inspectability requires a realizable terminal inspection boundary
L003873 
L003874 Because execution inspectability applies to the realized execution or realized
L003875 prefix of an accepted invocation for which TURNLOCK observes normal completion
L003876 or another terminal or cessation outcome, the architecture must make sufficient
L003877 actual TURNLOCK-visible behavior available at a realizable terminal inspection
L003878 boundary. That behavior includes enough workflow-mediated structure, execution
L003879 boundaries, explicitly exposed inputs and results, and progression-relevant
L003880 facts to support the obligation in `TL-INV-033`.
L003881 
L003882 The inspection boundary must preserve the distinction between actual execution
L003883 facts and a workflow definition displayed later. It may show a current or later
L003884 definition, but it cannot use that definition alone as proof of previous
L003885 execution behavior. When inspection relies on a governing definition, it must
L003886 correspond to the definition that actually governed the invocation. This
L003887 pressure makes the workflow-definition binding decision consequential;
L003888 `TL-INV-037` fixes that binding rule without selecting snapshot semantics,
L003889 live-edit semantics, revision identity, copy-on-start, or another binding
L003890 mechanism.
L003891 
L003892 This implication requires enough runtime and integration state and
L003893 terminal-boundary behavior to satisfy `TL-INV-033` and the realizable terminal
L003894 inspection handoff. It requires:
L003895 
L003896 ```text
L003897 no required persistent event log
L003898 no event schema
L003899 no Run object
L003900 no run ID
L003901 no UUID
L003902 no database
L003903 no telemetry product
L003904 no timestamp scheme
L003905 no retention duration
L003906 no replay
L003907 no comparison API
L003908 no evaluator
L003909 no optimizer
L003910 ```
L003911 
L003912 A concrete architecture is non-conforming if required execution truth exists
L003913 only in inaccessible transient state or requires an accidental race to acquire
L003914 before destruction. An architecture may hand the required execution truth to an
L003915 external persistence or evaluation layer and has no universal post-handoff
L003916 retention duty from `TL-INV-033` alone. Under ADR-038, a semantically conforming
L003917 harness-native inspection or tracing mechanism may be used as a candidate
L003918 realization asset for the mechanism side of this boundary and does not become
L003919 TURNLOCK semantic authority.
L003920 
L003921 ## 5.16 Evaluation and optimization are layered above the execution substrate
L003922 
L003923 Because evaluation objectives and optimization policy are not core TURNLOCK
L003924 semantics, the architecture must let evaluation and optimization be composed
L003925 above the execution substrate. TURNLOCK's responsibility includes executing
L003926 declared workflow semantics, exposing sufficient actual execution truth
L003927 (`TL-INV-033`), and preserving effective execution-condition provenance
L003928 (`TL-INV-036`) at its semantic boundary. It does not extend to owning evaluation
L003929 or optimization policy.
L003930 
L003931 Evaluation or optimization logic requires no privileged runtime interface. It
L003932 can be implemented by a user, the main agent, an external evaluator, or another
L003933 higher-level system, and, where expressible using accepted primitives, by an
L003934 ordinary TURNLOCK workflow. Such behavior remains ordinary authored execution
L003935 and gains no runtime authority over the executions it inspects or the
L003936 workflows it proposes to change. Any resulting workflow refinement is authored
L003937 through the same artifact class as any other workflow change.
L003938 
L003939 This implication does not select an evaluation API, metric set, experiment
L003940 model, comparison contract, optimizer algorithm, storage, or user interface.
L003941 
L003942 ## 5.17 Effective governing conditions require an attribution boundary
L003943 
L003944 Because TURNLOCK must preserve effective execution-condition provenance, runtime
L003945 and adapter architecture must keep each condition TURNLOCK selects, binds,
L003946 explicitly supplies, or resolves attributable to the execution scope it governs
L003947 and provide a realizable semantic-boundary capture handoff through which that
L003948 relationship can be acquired before the required provenance is irreversibly
L003949 lost.
L003950 
L003951 The architecture may distinguish unavailable or unknown conditions and need not
L003952 observe conditions outside TURNLOCK's boundary. It must not manufacture known
L003953 equality from missing information or convert a known protected condition into
L003954 unknown merely because its value is not disclosed. For a TURNLOCK-known
L003955 protected condition, the boundary must preserve a representation containing
L003956 condition-specific information rather than substitute an occurrence label or one
L003957 generic protected marker for all known condition provenance before or during
L003958 the realizable semantic-boundary capture handoff.
L003959 
L003960 A particular consumer MAY receive a more restrictive view than the underlying
L003961 provenance made capturable through the realizable semantic-boundary capture
L003962 handoff, under separately governed policy. This implication
L003963 does not select an authorization or privacy model, require another consumer
L003964 context, exact-value disclosure, post-boundary availability or retention, or
L003965 that all capturable information appear through ordinary inspection surfaces. Whichever workflow
L003966 definition governs an invocation under `TL-INV-037` must remain attributable
L003967 when TURNLOCK binds or resolves it, without this implication selecting a
L003968 concrete representation.
L003969 
L003970 This boundary does not select who captures the attribution, how long it remains
L003971 available, whether another layer persists it, or any database, event, identifier,
L003972 hash, snapshot, telemetry, run-model, replay, comparison, or reproduction
L003973 mechanism. It also establishes no public or cross-run stable identity and no
L003974 equality or difference evidence.
L003975 
L003976 Architecture must make it structurally possible for an eligible conforming
L003977 capture context to be established in time to participate in this handoff.
L003978 When no consumer is attached, conformance still requires TURNLOCK to complete
L003979 its side of the semantic-boundary interaction through that structurally
L003980 realizable capability; mere internal existence is not a discharge event.
L003981 Actual receiver participation, successful delivery, consumer processing, and
L003982 acknowledgment are not required. Consumer absence, participant failure, or
L003983 delivery failure does not by itself create a universal retention obligation.
L003984 Once TURNLOCK has completed that conforming handoff, `TL-INV-036` alone does
L003985 not require continued capturability, and any stronger post-handoff
L003986 availability, persistence, or retention guarantee remains separately governed.
L003987 The capture boundary remains distinct from delivery acknowledgment, ordinary
L003988 inspection surfaces, and any storage mechanism.
L003989 
L003990 ## 5.18 Governing-definition stability requires execution-level attribution
L003991 
L003992 Because every accepted invocation must retain one governing workflow definition,
L003993 the execution architecture must preserve a stable governing-definition
L003994 relationship for each active invocation independently of later mutation of the
L003995 source artifact. This implication prescribes no snapshot, hash, copy, lock,
L003996 database, revision, or file-system mechanism; it requires only that an ordinary
L003997 later source edit cannot silently replace the definition that governs an active
L003998 invocation's remaining declared topology, while each nested invocation
L003999 establishes its own governing definition at its own acceptance.
L004000 
L004001 ## 5.19 Externalizable execution realizations require a runtime composition boundary
L004002 
L004003 Because `TL-INV-038` requires a runtime composition path when a concrete
L004004 execution realization is not fixed by TURNLOCK semantics and a semantically
L004005 preserving alternative is technically realizable at runtime in a supported
L004006 harness or execution environment, the architecture must provide at least one
L004007 public runtime composition capability through which such an alternative can be
L004008 supplied or established before the causal use it is intended to govern.
L004009 Modification or recompilation of Core cannot be the only substitution path in
L004010 that case.
L004011 
L004012 The absence of that public runtime composition capability cannot itself be used
L004013 to classify the otherwise runtime-realizable alternative as unsupported. A
L004014 genuine harness or execution-environment capability limitation may bound what is
L004015 technically realizable; a missing Core composition boundary is not such a
L004016 limitation.
L004017 
L004018 The boundary may be realized differently by different architectures or
L004019 supported harnesses. It does not require a plugin system, hook system,
L004020 dependency-injection framework, IPC protocol, process topology, or resource
L004021 registry.
L004022 
L004023 The architecture must also preserve the accepted realization for the governed
L004024 use: once TURNLOCK has accepted an external realization as governing that use,
L004025 the runtime cannot silently bypass it with another realization unless the
L004026 applicable TURNLOCK semantics authorize that alternative.
L004027 
L004028 This architectural requirement concerns realizations that remain external to
L004029 TURNLOCK's semantic responsibilities. It does not make every internal algorithm
L004030 or external determinant replaceable, does not create a general environment
L004031 permission system, and does not move evaluation or optimization policy into
L004032 Core.
L004033 
L004034 ## 5.20 Engine scheduling must preserve occurrence-scoped conditional progress
L004035 
L004036 Because `TL-INV-042` requires eventual advance of every particular
L004037 TURNLOCK-owned progression occurrence that remains continuously eligible and
L004038 applicable, the execution architecture must preserve enough progress state to
L004039 ensure that such an occurrence cannot remain unadvanced indefinitely. This
L004040 applies both when TURNLOCK continues other activity and when no competing
L004041 progression is selected.
L004042 
L004043 This implication requires no particular scheduler, queue, worker topology,
L004044 thread/process model, priority scheme, fairness algorithm, runtime identifier,
L004045 or persistence mechanism.
L004046 
L004047 It also does not require TURNLOCK to make an external resource, agentic region,
L004048 workflow invocation, branch, or workflow eventually complete. The architectural
L004049 obligation begins only after governing semantics make the relevant
L004050 TURNLOCK-owned progression continuously eligible and applicable.

L004242 # 8. Derived synopsis
L004243 
L004244 This section is a non-authoritative synopsis derived from the specification's
L004245 owning sections. It introduces no lexical definition, product promise, or
L004246 invariant. If compressed wording here diverges, Section 0 governs product intent,
L004247 Section 2 governs terminology, and Section 3 governs obligations and stable
L004248 invariant identities.
L004249 
L004250 TURNLOCK can currently be summarized as:
L004251 
L004252 > **A harness-independent orchestration engine for coding-agent sessions that executes workflow-declared control, using the same TURNLOCK primitives whether authored by a developer or coding agent, and composes mechanical execution, bounded raw LLM inference, bounded independent agents, continuation of the user's main coding agent, concurrency, and nested workflows. The workflow program owns the declared orchestration logic; TURNLOCK executes it, keeps the realized execution or realized prefix sufficiently inspectable for every TURNLOCK-observed terminal or cessation outcome, and preserves effective execution-condition provenance for conditions it selects, binds, explicitly supplies, or resolves. TURNLOCK Core provides runtime composition for semantically preserving alternative execution realizations not fixed by TURNLOCK semantics when such composition is technically realizable in the supported harness or execution environment. External actors retain evaluation and optimization policy. Pi is the first reference harness used to prove the model.**
