L004256 - workflow, workflow artifact, and TURNLOCK primitives: Sections 2.2 and 2.3A;
L004257 - mechanical execution and mechanical step: Section 2.4;
L004258 - raw LLM inference and raw LLM inference step: Section 2.4A;
L004259 - independent agent and independent-agent step: Section 2.4B;
L004260 - main agent, main-agent handoff, and main-agent step: Sections 2.1 and 2.5;
L004261 - immediate caller context and caller stack: Section 2.6;
L004262 - control ownership and workflow-owned control: Section 2.7;
L004263 - workflow invocation surface: Section 2.3; and
L004264 - parallel fan-out/fan-in and nested workflow invocation: Section 2.8;
L004265 - execution inspectability: Section 2.9; and
L004266 - effective execution-condition provenance: Section 2.10.
L004267 
L004268 The guiding allocation rule remains the product principle in Section 0.10 and
L004269 the obligation in `TL-INV-029`: use the minimum sufficient form of computation
L004270 or cognition for each region.
L004271 
L004272 Evaluation and optimization policy remain outside TURNLOCK core: evaluation
L004273 objectives come from an explicitly responsible actor or authored workflow, and
L004274 the runtime never silently optimizes authored orchestration. TURNLOCK preserves
L004275 its own effective governing-condition attribution without deciding which
L004276 conditions matter to a property or whether executions are comparable.
L004277 
L004278 The product is successful only if these roles remain distinct in the real execution model and if known orchestration decisions can remain in the workflow rather than being pushed back into an agent merely because the workflow lacks expressive power.
L004279 
L004280 # 9. Formal specification governance
L004281 
L004282 TURNLOCK maintains a formal state-machine specification alongside this normative prose specification for semantics that materially involve state, control ownership, lifecycle, invocation/return, nesting, concurrency, synchronization, failure, cancellation, or temporal progress. ADR-015 governs this relationship.
L004283 
L004284 The prose specification remains the normative statement of product meaning. The TLA+ model is an abstract executable model used to test relevant state/temporal consequences and to discover counterexamples before implementation choices harden. It MUST remain implementation-independent and harness-agnostic at the core semantic layer.
L004285 
L004286 Every invariant in Section 3 has a stable `TL-INV-xxx` identifier. Section numbering and titles may evolve; published invariant IDs are stable traceability identities.
L004287 
L004288 Formal traceability is maintained in the machine-readable manifest:
L004289 
L004290 ```text
L004291 formal/verification.yaml
L004292 ```
L004293 
L004294 A human-readable mapping in `docs/formal/invariant-mapping.md` is generated from that manifest. For every formally modeled invariant, the manifest is intended to trace the stable product ID to its TLA+ module/property, the state variables and actions/transitions used by that formalization, the focused/integrated TLC configurations that exercise it, and later implementation/conformance tests. The mapping MUST also be mechanically invertible so that a changed TLA+ property, state variable, or action can identify potentially affected product invariants.
L004295 
L004296 The manifest describes verification intent and traceability. Actual TLC execution evidence is a separate machine-readable artifact class under `formal/results/`, governed by `formal/tlc-result.schema.json`. A `checked` claim MUST identify successful run evidence for a concrete repository revision, TLC/model configuration, checked properties, and explicit finite bounds. Presence in the manifest MUST NOT be interpreted as successful TLC verification.
L004297 
L004298 Automated traceability checks SHOULD enforce referential integrity once mappings become executable: referenced TLA+ modules, properties, variables, actions/transitions, and TLC configurations must exist. Such checks do not prove semantic correspondence between prose and formula; that correspondence remains a formal-review obligation.
L004299 
L004300 TURNLOCK's formal verification organization has two complementary modes:
L004301 
L004302 ```text
L004303 focused exploration
L004304 → restrict the same semantic model to a mechanism/property for fast diagnosis
L004305 
L004306 integrated exploration
L004307 → exercise all currently-formalized core mechanisms together within finite bounds
L004308 ```
L004309 
L004310 Focused configurations are development accelerators, not substitutes for integrated verification. At least one integrated configuration MUST remain capable of composing all currently-formalized core execution forms in one state space. The project should maintain multiple integrated exploration budgets such as smoke, standard, and stress.
L004311 
L004312 A semantic change affecting the formal state machine should normally run the relevant focused checks plus an integrated smoke exploration. Larger integrated runs are governed by CI/release policy.
L004313 
L004314 TLC exploration is necessarily finite. "Integrated" means the formalized
L004315 mechanisms are connected in the same abstract model; it does not claim exhaustive
L004316 exploration of an unbounded real-world system. A finite TLC domain or exploration
L004317 bound is a formal-modeling choice, not a TURNLOCK product resource limit,
L004318 timeout, termination guarantee, or fairness premise.
L004319 
L004320 Safety and liveness are distinct obligations. For example:
L004321 
L004322 ```text
L004323 safety:  normal completion of a nested workflow never restores the wrong caller
L004324 liveness: a TURNLOCK-owned progression occurrence that remains continuously enabled and applicable is eventually advanced by TURNLOCK
L004325 ```
L004326 
L004327 The liveness obligation does not assert that the event or execution resource
L004328 which would enable the progression eventually completes. The concrete
L004329 occurrence representation and fairness formula used to encode the obligation
L004330 belong to the formal model and MUST NOT strengthen the normative product
L004331 promise.
L004332 
L004333 The obligation does not require competing progression or a scheduler-choice
L004334 cause: an indefinitely enabled and applicable occurrence that is never advanced
L004335 violates the product contract even if TURNLOCK performs no other progression.
L004336 
L004337 Not every product invariant is necessarily expressible or useful as TLA+. DX and semantic-quality requirements may be explicitly marked `not-applicable`; state, ordering, ownership, lifecycle, nesting, concurrency, synchronization, and progress rules are strong formalization candidates.

L000027 # ADR-008: Allow nested workflow invocation from main-agent regions and return to the immediate caller
L000028 
L000029 - **Status:** Accepted
L000030 - **Date:** 2026-09-13
L000031 - **Decision order:** 008
L000032 - **Clarifies:** ADR-002, ADR-005, ADR-006, and ADR-007
L000033 - **Governs:** workflow composability, nested invocation, suspension, and return semantics
L000034 
L000035 ## Context
L000036 
L000037 ADR-002 established that TURNLOCK workflows are exposed naturally inside the coding-agent session through a skill-like slash-command surface. ADR-007 established that a main-agent region restores the ordinary interactive agency of the current main coding agent rather than reducing it to a one-shot model call.
L000038 
L000039 Those two decisions combine into a further product consequence: **while a workflow has handed control to the main agent, the main agent still has the session capabilities it ordinarily has, including the ability to invoke another TURNLOCK workflow that is available to that session.**
L000040 
L000041 The motivating coding-agent environments commonly make session skills/commands discoverable to the main agent for the lifetime of the session. TURNLOCK must not accidentally erase that capability merely because the agent currently owns control inside a workflow handoff.
L000042 
L000043 Therefore the following sequence must be meaningful:
L000044 
L000045 ```text
L000046 main agent
L000047   → workflow A
L000048     → mechanical A1
L000049     → main-agent region A
L000050       → workflow B
L000051         → mechanical B1
L000052         → main-agent region B
L000053         → mechanical B2
L000054         → workflow B terminates
L000055       → main-agent region A resumes
L000056     → mechanical A2
L000057     → workflow A terminates
L000058   → main agent resumes
L000059 ```
L000060 
L000061 Without an explicit decision, several incompatible semantics are possible:
L000062 
L000063 ```text
L000064 nested invocation forbidden
L000065 nested invocation replaces workflow A
L000066 workflow B returns directly to the root main session
L000067 workflow B completion implicitly completes main-agent region A
L000068 workflow B completion implicitly completes workflow A
L000069 ```
L000070 
L000071 Those semantics would break composability and weaken the meaning of restored ordinary main-agent agency.
L000072 
L000073 ## Decision
L000074 
L000075 TURNLOCK permits **structured nested workflow invocation from a main-agent region**.
L000076 
L000077 Whenever the main agent owns control, a TURNLOCK workflow that is available to that coding-agent session MAY be invoked, including when the current main-agent control was reached through a handoff from an enclosing workflow.
L000078 
L000079 A nested invocation has these semantics:
L000080 
L000081 ```text
L000082 1. the immediate caller is suspended;
L000083 2. the nested workflow becomes the active workflow execution;
L000084 3. the nested workflow owns its own declared progression;
L000085 4. normal nested completion returns to the immediate caller;
L000086 5. the caller resumes from the point after the nested invocation;
L000087 6. the enclosing workflow remains suspended until its own main-agent region completes;
L000088 7. the enclosing workflow then resumes at its own declared continuation.
L000089 ```
L000090 
L000091 The general return rule is therefore:
L000092 
L000093 ```text
L000094 workflow completion → immediate invocation context
L000095 ```
L000096 
L000097 not:
L000098 
L000099 ```text
L000100 workflow completion → root main-agent session unconditionally
L000101 ```
L000102 
L000103 For a top-level workflow, the immediate invocation context is the surrounding main-agent interaction, so the existing top-level lifecycle remains:
L000104 
L000105 ```text
L000106 main agent → workflow A → main agent
L000107 ```
L000108 
L000109 For a nested workflow:
L000110 
L000111 ```text
L000112 main-agent region A → workflow B → main-agent region A
L000113 ```
L000114 
L000115 Nested workflows therefore form a structured caller stack conceptually:
L000116 
L000117 ```text
L000118 main session
L000119   workflow A
L000120     main-agent region A
L000121       workflow B
L000122         main-agent region B
L000123           workflow C
L000124         ←
L000125       ←
L000126     ←
L000127   ←
L000128 main session
L000129 ```
L000130 
L000131 This ADR does not require a literal process stack, recursive process spawning, or any specific runtime representation. It requires equivalent **structured suspension and immediate-caller return semantics**.
L000132 
L000133 The semantic model MUST NOT assume that only one nesting level can exist. An implementation may later define explicit resource or safety limits on accepted nesting depth, but such limits must not change the return semantics of invocations it accepts.
L000134 
L000135 ## Rationale
L000136 
L000137 A workflow exposed as a skill-like session capability should remain usable wherever the main agent has ordinary agency. Otherwise TURNLOCK would restore the main agent only partially: the agent could reason, edit, and use tools, but could not compose the user's existing workflow abstractions.
L000138 
L000139 Nested invocation also lets workflows become reusable units of work rather than only top-level automations. The main agent can recognize that a subproblem matches an existing workflow and invoke that workflow without becoming the orchestrator of the enclosing workflow.
L000140 
L000141 This preserves the key authority split:
L000142 
L000143 ```text
L000144 workflow A owns workflow A progression
L000145 main-agent region A owns temporary local agency
L000146 workflow B owns workflow B progression
L000147 ```
L000148 
L000149 Invoking workflow B does not give the main agent authority to rewrite workflow A's control flow. It only lets the main agent use another available capability during the region in which it legitimately owns control.
L000150 
L000151 ## Consequences
L000152 
L000153 - TURNLOCK workflows are composable from main-agent regions, not only invocable by the user at the top level.
L000154 - The session's TURNLOCK workflow discovery/invocation surface must remain available to the main agent during handoff regions.
L000155 - A nested workflow suspends rather than replaces its immediate caller.
L000156 - Completion returns to the immediate caller, not automatically to the root session.
L000157 - The runtime needs semantics equivalent to a caller stack even if implemented with another representation.
L000158 - A single flat `current_workflow` state that is overwritten by nested invocation is insufficient unless additional state preserves the suspended caller and exact return target.
L000159 - Outer workflow orchestration remains independent of nested workflow orchestration.
L000160 - Nested invocation is distinct from sibling or top-level workflow concurrency; this ADR does not decide whether multiple independent workflows may run concurrently in one session.
L000161 
L000162 ## Alternatives considered
L000163 
L000164 ### Forbid workflow invocation while inside a main-agent region
L000165 
L000166 Rejected. It contradicts the ordinary-agency goal of ADR-007 and prevents the main agent from using session-available workflow capabilities exactly when agentic judgment may identify them as useful.
L000167 
L000168 ### Allow nesting but always return to the root main agent
L000169 
L000170 Rejected. It skips the immediate caller, destroys structured composition, and can strand the enclosing workflow in an undefined suspended state.
L000171 
L000172 ### Let a nested workflow replace the enclosing workflow
L000173 
L000174 Rejected. Invocation of a reusable capability must not implicitly cancel or overwrite the caller.
L000175 
L000176 ### Treat nested workflows as subagents rather than workflows
L000177 
L000178 Rejected. A nested workflow retains TURNLOCK workflow semantics: it may itself contain mechanical regions, main-agent handoffs, and further nested workflow invocations.
L000179 
L000180 ### Require a specific frontmatter or skill-loading mechanism
L000181 
L000182 Rejected as an architectural invariant. Skill frontmatter loaded by a harness is one motivating realization of discoverability, but TURNLOCK specifies the capability semantics rather than one vendor-specific discovery mechanism.
L000183 
L000184 ## Verification obligation
L000185 
L000186 A conforming implementation must demonstrate at least this sequence:
L000187 
L000188 ```text
L000189 main agent
L000190 → workflow A
L000191 → mechanical A1
L000192 → main-agent region A
L000193 → workflow B
L000194 → mechanical B1
L000195 → main-agent region B
L000196 → mechanical B2
L000197 → workflow B completes
L000198 → main-agent region A resumes
L000199 → main-agent region A completes
L000200 → mechanical A2
L000201 → workflow A completes
L000202 → root main-agent interaction resumes
L000203 ```
L000204 
L000205 The verification must show that:
L000206 
L000207 1. workflow A remains intact while workflow B executes;
L000208 2. workflow B completion returns to main-agent region A, not directly to the root session;
L000209 3. main-agent region A can continue after workflow B returns;
L000210 4. workflow A resumes only when region A itself completes;
L000211 5. the same semantics remain valid for another level of nesting, subject only to any explicit accepted resource limit.

L000025 # ADR-022: Allow workflow-declared invocation with structured call/return semantics
L000026 
L000027 ## Context
L000028 
L000029 TURNLOCK treats a workflow as an executable orchestration program and TURNLOCK
L000030 as the engine that executes its declared topology (ADR-014). The
L000031 workflow-declared orchestration surface must already be expressive enough that
L000032 known composition decisions remain executable workflow logic rather than being
L000033 delegated back to an agent for lack of orchestration primitives. Sections 0.1,
L000034 0.2, and 2.2 and `TL-INV-031` list nested workflow invocation and structured
L000035 return among the composition capabilities a workflow must be able to express,
L000036 and ADR-014 requires TURNLOCK to provide the execution authority needed to
L000037 realize declared semantics, including nested invocation and structured return,
L000038 without inventing undeclared strategy.
L000039 
L000040 Current authority defines only one invocation decision owner. ADR-008 accepted
L000041 agent-selected invocation from a main-agent region, and Section 2.8 canonically
L000042 defines `nested workflow invocation` as an invocation made from a main-agent
L000043 region while that immediate caller context is suspended. No accepted decision
L000044 defines a workflow-declared invocation, its immediate caller, its suspension
L000045 scope, its return target, or its relationship to ADR-008. The canonical
L000046 definition is therefore narrower than the composition language that references
L000047 it, and the corpus does not uniquely decide whether the references already
L000048 require a declared invocation.
L000049 
L000050 That gap blocks the first TLA+ safety model. The model must distinguish who
L000051 authorized an invocation, what execution context is the immediate caller, which
L000052 continuation is suspended, what workflow invocation is active, and where normal
L000053 completion returns. Reusing ADR-008's main-agent-selected transition for a
L000054 workflow-declared invocation would misattribute decision ownership. Adding a
L000055 generic declared-invocation transition without accepted semantics would create
L000056 product meaning inside a model. Issue #5 owns this decision, and the discovery
L000057 classification records the existence question as
L000058 `authority-conflict-or-uncertain` with a candidate derived-from-authority
L000059 derivation, and the exact transition semantics as `decision-required`.
L000060 
L000061 ## Decision
L000062 
L000063 A TURNLOCK workflow program MAY declaratively invoke another TURNLOCK workflow
L000064 as part of its authored orchestration. The decision to invoke that workflow
L000065 belongs to the invoking workflow program, and TURNLOCK MUST execute an admitted
L000066 declared invocation directly rather than requiring a main-agent handoff solely
L000067 to reproduce an invocation decision already present in the executable topology.
L000068 
L000069 For every admitted invocation, whether workflow-declared or agent-selected:
L000070 
L000071 - the caller context preserves a structured call continuation;
L000072 - the calling continuation is suspended with respect to that call;
L000073 - the callee executes its own declared progression;
L000074 - normal completion returns to the same immediate caller context and enables
L000075   only the caller's declared post-call continuation;
L000076 - the callee MUST NOT replace, rewrite, skip, or capture the caller's
L000077   continuation or the enclosing workflow's declared progression;
L000078 - the enclosing workflow's orchestration remains governed by its own program.
L000079 
L000080 Suspension is local to the calling continuation. An invocation MUST NOT be
L000081 interpreted as implicitly suspending concurrently active contexts that the
L000082 declared topology permits to continue. The local rule must not be generalized
L000083 into unconditional whole-workflow suspension.
L000084 
L000085 The decision owners remain distinct. The workflow program owns a declared
L000086 invocation; the main agent owns an agent-selected invocation only during a
L000087 main-agent region where it legitimately holds local authority (ADR-008). ADR-008
L000088 remains valid and its accepted scenario is unchanged. The structural guarantees
L000089 above do not decide whether an implementation, model, primitive, action, or
L000090 runtime path is shared; that factorization is a modeling and architecture
L000091 choice, not product semantics.
L000092 
L000093 This decision does not decide recursion, cyclic call graphs, or the
L000094 admissibility of invocation in restricted contexts. Issue #6 owns that
L000095 admissibility boundary, and an admitted invocation is one that existing
L000096 authority and that boundary permit. Concrete nesting depth, stack size,
L000097 resource budgets, and cancellation or failure behavior remain policy or
L000098 implementation concerns.
L000099 
L000100 The canonical term remains `nested workflow invocation`. Its Section 2.8
L000101 definition is generalized to cover an invocation whose immediate caller is a
L000102 context inside an enclosing workflow, regardless of whether the workflow
L000103 program declared the invocation or the main agent selected it, while the
L000104 decision owner remains explicit. This decision introduces no parallel
L000105 terminology.
L000106 
L000107 ## Alternatives considered
L000108 
L000109 - **Reject declared invocation and keep agent-selected nesting only:** Rejected
L000110   because a known declared call would have to be reproduced through main-agent
L000111   judgment, delegating a decision the workflow program already owns and
L000112   contradicting `TL-INV-031` and ADR-014.
L000113 - **Execute a declared call as an internal main-agent handoff:** Rejected
L000114   because it misattributes decision ownership and moves declared orchestration
L000115   back into agent judgment.
L000116 - **Define invocation as unconditional whole-workflow suspension:** Rejected
L000117   because it contradicts declared concurrency and fan-out/fan-in semantics
L000118   (`TL-INV-024`, `TL-INV-027`, ADR-013).
L000119 - **Decide a shared primitive, model action, or runtime representation:**
L000120   Rejected as a modeling and architecture choice that does not change product
L000121   semantics.
L000122 - **Introduce a new general term instead of broadening `nested workflow
L000123   invocation`:** Rejected because the existing canonical term already identifies
L000124   the structural relation; broadening its definition removes the ambiguity with
L000125   less terminology and traceability churn.
L000126 - **Decide recursion, cyclic admissibility, placements, and depth limits here:**
L000127   Rejected as outside the smallest necessary semantic delta; Issue #6 owns
L000128   admissibility and concrete limits remain policy.
L000129 - **Edit ADR-008's accepted body to broaden it:** Rejected because accepted
L000130   decision bodies are immutable; this later ADR records the generalization while
L000131   ADR-008 remains valid.
L000132 
L000133 ## Consequences
L000134 
L000135 ### Benefits
L000136 
L000137 - Resolves the Section 2.8 definitional conflict and gives the first TLA+ safety
L000138   model a decision-owner-neutral invocation transition with a defined caller and
L000139   return structure.
L000140 - Keeps known composition decisions in executable workflow logic instead of
L000141   returning them to agent judgment.
L000142 - Preserves ADR-008 unchanged while placing both invocation paths under the same
L000143   applicable structural guarantees.
L000144 - Introduces no representation, primitive, or factorization obligation.
L000145 
L000146 ### Costs and obligations
L000147 
L000148 - The normative specification must generalize the immediate-caller and nested
L000149   invocation definitions, state the declared-invocation obligation, and carry it
L000150   in a new stable invariant identity without broadening the published meanings
L000151   of `TL-INV-016`–`TL-INV-019`.
L000152 - The terminology review inventory must be refreshed for moved definition-like
L000153   occurrences.
L000154 - `formal/verification.yaml` may record intended properties only; no model, no
L000155   TLC run, and no `checked` claim exist.
L000156 - The first model must scope recursion, cyclic, and restricted-placement behavior
L000157   consistently with Issue #6 rather than enabling it accidentally.
L000158 - Conformance tests for the declared path and for local suspension under
L000159   declared concurrency are required later but are not created by this decision.
L000160 
L000161 ## References
L000162 
L000163 - `docs/specification/turnlock-spec.md`
L000164 - `docs/adr/adr-008-allow-nested-workflow-invocation-from-main-agent-regions.md`
L000165 - `docs/adr/adr-014-define-turnlock-as-the-orchestration-engine-and-the-workflow-as-the-orchestration-program.md`

L000025 # ADR-023: Clarify caller-context and continuation semantics across nested workflow invocations
L000026 
L000027 ## Context
L000028 
L000029 ADR-022 accepted workflow-declared invocation and stated that the caller context
L000030 preserves a structured call continuation. That wording distinguishes the caller
L000031 context from its continuation, but the synchronization of ADR-022 into the
L000032 normative specification collapsed the two notions. Sections 0.6, 2.6, and 5.3
L000033 described the immediate caller of a workflow-declared invocation as the
L000034 "suspended call continuation of the caller context", which is a category error:
L000035 the caller is an execution context, while the continuation is the preserved
L000036 return state of that context.
L000037 
L000038 ADR-022 also stated, for every admitted invocation, that normal completion
L000039 "enables only the caller's declared post-call continuation". That phrasing
L000040 describes a workflow-declared invocation, whose post-call continuation is
L000041 declared by the workflow program, but it does not describe ADR-008's
L000042 agent-selected path. There, normal completion resumes the same main-agent
L000043 region, and the region then continues its local execution under the main agent's
L000044 legitimate local authority before the enclosing workflow's own continuation
L000045 becomes available.
L000046 
L000047 Section 0.6 additionally retained an ADR-008-specific sentence stating that the
L000048 enclosing workflow continues "only when its own main-agent region completes".
L000049 That statement is false for a workflow-declared invocation, which requires no
L000050 main-agent region.
L000051 
L000052 Finally, `TL-INV-035` states the callee's no-rewrite obligation, but its formal
L000053 traceability did not reference the existing actor-neutral planned property
L000054 `NestedInvocationCannotRewriteOuterContinuation` already used for `TL-INV-019`.
L000055 
L000056 The discovery classification records the caller/continuation category error and
L000057 the overgeneralized return phrasing as `authority-conflict-or-uncertain`, the
L000058 stale Section 0.6 sentence as `derived-from-existing-authority`, and the formal
L000059 traceability gap as `no-normative-impact`. This decision introduces no new
L000060 invocation capability.
L000061 
L000062 ## Decision
L000063 
L000064 1. An immediate caller context and its call continuation are distinct semantic
L000065    notions.
L000066 2. The immediate caller context is the execution context that performs an
L000067    admitted workflow invocation and to which normal completion returns.
L000068 3. That caller context preserves a return-bearing continuation while the callee
L000069    executes. The continuation is not itself the caller context.
L000070 4. For a workflow-declared invocation:
L000071    - the caller is the workflow execution context performing the call;
L000072    - its preserved post-call continuation is declared by the workflow program;
L000073    - normal callee completion makes that preserved continuation eligible,
L000074      subject to the enclosing workflow topology.
L000075 5. For an agent-selected invocation under ADR-008:
L000076    - the immediate caller is the main-agent region;
L000077    - normal callee completion resumes that same main-agent region at the point
L000078      following the nested invocation;
L000079    - subsequent local execution remains under the main agent's legitimate local
L000080      authority;
L000081    - this return does not itself complete the main-agent region;
L000082    - the enclosing workflow's own declared continuation remains unavailable
L000083      until that main-agent region completes according to its semantics.
L000084 6. A callee cannot select, replace, rewrite, skip, or capture the caller's
L000085    preserved return target.
L000086 7. "Only the caller continuation is enabled by this return" is local to that
L000087    call/return relationship. It MUST NOT mean that independently active
L000088    concurrent contexts permitted by the enclosing topology are disabled,
L000089    suspended, or required to stop.
L000090 8. Suspension remains local to the calling continuation. ADR-022's rejection of
L000091    unconditional whole-workflow suspension remains unchanged.
L000092 9. Nothing here decides recursion, cyclic-call admissibility, restricted
L000093    placements, concrete depth limits, stack or frame representation, activation
L000094    identifiers, TLA+ variables or actions, DSL syntax, Rust APIs, process
L000095    topology, failure, cancellation, or timeout semantics.
L000096 
L000097 This decision preserves the substantive decisions of ADR-008 and ADR-022 while
L000098 removing the caller/continuation ambiguity. ADR-008 and ADR-022 remain accepted
L000099 and are not edited.
L000100 
L000101 ## Alternatives considered
L000102 
L000103 - **Define the immediate caller as the suspended continuation:** Rejected as a
L000104   category error; the caller is an execution context and the continuation is the
L000105   preserved return state of that context.
L000106 - **Keep "declared post-call continuation" for both decision owners:** Rejected
L000107   because an agent-selected invocation resumes the main-agent region, whose
L000108   subsequent local work is not a workflow-declared continuation.
L000109 - **Edit ADR-022's accepted body to correct the wording:** Rejected because
L000110   accepted decision bodies are immutable; this later ADR records the
L000111   clarification.
L000112 - **Create a new planned property for the `TL-INV-035` no-rewrite obligation:**
L000113   Rejected because the existing actor-neutral property already covers it and a
L000114   duplicate name would fragment traceability.
L000115 - **State that a normal return disables other continuations of the caller:**
L000116   Rejected because the effect is local to the call/return relationship;
L000117   independently active concurrent contexts permitted by the declared topology
L000118   are not implicitly suspended.
L000119 
L000120 ## Consequences
L000121 
L000122 ### Benefits
L000123 
L000124 - Restores one non-ambiguous model: the caller context owns and preserves a
L000125   continuation, the relevant continuation is suspended during callee execution,
L000126   and normal return restores the continuation appropriate to that caller.
L000127 - Preserves ADR-008 and ADR-022 without editing either accepted body.
L000128 - Gives the first TLA+ model distinct abstract notions of caller context and
L000129   preserved continuation without selecting a representation.
L000130 
L000131 ### Costs and obligations
L000132 
L000133 - Sections 0.6, 2.6, 5.3, and `TL-INV-035` require synchronized correction.
L000134 - The terminology review inventory must be refreshed for moved definition-like
L000135   occurrences.
L000136 - `formal/verification.yaml` must add the existing planned property
L000137   `NestedInvocationCannotRewriteOuterContinuation` to `TL-INV-035` and record
L000138   ADR-023 as a governing ADR; no formalization, verification, or mapping status
L000139   changes, and no `checked` claim.
L000140 - Issues #5, #6, and #9 require work-state updates to reflect ADR-022 and
L000141   ADR-023. Issue #6 remains the owner of restricted-placement, transitive, and
L000142   recursive- or cyclic-admissibility questions.
L000143

L000029 # ADR-032: Allow main-agent participation in workflow-owned concurrency without cognitive-lineage fork
L000030 
L000031 ## Context
L000032 
L000033 ADR-013 accepted heterogeneous workflow-owned parallel fan-out/fan-in across mechanical execution, bounded raw-LLM inference, and independent-agent execution, but explicitly left main-agent continuation in a concurrent branch unresolved.
L000034 
L000035 ADR-007 establishes that a main-agent continuation preserves the continuing cognitive lineage of the surrounding coding-agent session rather than creating a fresh or reconstructed agent. ADR-014 requires declared global orchestration to remain workflow-owned rather than being manufactured by runtime scheduling or agent judgment.
L000036 
L000037 The unresolved question is therefore not merely whether a main-agent region may execute while unrelated work also progresses. The product must define whether main-agent continuation may participate in workflow-owned concurrent topology while preserving the fact that one continuing main-agent cognitive lineage is not an independently forkable execution resource.
L000038 
L000039 The relevant semantic distinction is between:
L000040 
L000041 ```text
L000042 one main-agent continuation
L000043 coexisting with independent sibling work
L000044 ```
L000045 
L000046 and:
L000047 
L000048 ```text
L000049 the same continuing main-agent cognitive lineage
L000050 forked into multiple unordered concurrent continuations
L000051 ```
L000052 
L000053 Runtime timing cannot define that distinction because scheduler order is an execution accident rather than declared workflow causality.
L000054 
L000055 GitHub Issue #22 records the product-owner decision from which this ADR is derived.
L000056 
L000057 ## Discovery classification
L000058 
L000059 ### B — main-agent continuation in workflow-owned concurrency
L000060 
L000061 ADR-013 deliberately left main-agent participation in a concurrent branch unresolved.
L000062 
L000063 The product decision is:
L000064 
L000065 ```text
L000066 A main-agent continuation MAY participate
L000067 as a branch of workflow-owned concurrent execution.
L000068 ```
L000069 
L000070 This is new product authority.
L000071 
L000072 ### A — non-forkability of one continuing main-agent cognitive lineage
L000073 
L000074 Once concurrent main-agent participation is accepted, ADR-007's cognitive-lineage semantics require:
L000075 
L000076 ```text
L000077 one continuing main-agent cognitive lineage
L000078 MUST NOT be forked or duplicated across
L000079 independently concurrent, non-causally-ordered continuations
L000080 ```
L000081 
L000082 ### A — scheduler order is not semantic causal order
L000083 
L000084 ADR-014 requires orchestration to remain declared by workflow semantics.
L000085 
L000086 Therefore:
L000087 
L000088 ```text
L000089 runtime scheduling order
L000090 MUST NOT manufacture semantic causal ordering
L000091 that the declared workflow does not provide
L000092 ```
L000093 
L000094 ### A — a concurrent main-agent handoff is branch-local
L000095 
L000096 A main-agent continuation reached within one declared concurrent branch suspends only that branch's calling continuation.
L000097 
L000098 It does not implicitly suspend unrelated sibling branches that remain enabled by the declared workflow topology.
L000099

100 ## Decision
L000101 
L000102 TURNLOCK permits main-agent continuation as a participant in workflow-owned concurrent execution.
L000103 
L000104 A declared parallel region may therefore contain, subject to the rules below:
L000105 
L000106 ```text
L000107 mechanical execution
L000108 raw LLM inference
L000109 independent-agent execution
L000110 main-agent continuation
L000111 ```
L000112 
L000113 A main-agent concurrent branch remains continuation of the existing session main-agent cognitive lineage. TURNLOCK MUST NOT silently realize it as a fresh independent agent, a reconstructed child agent, or another cognitive lineage.
L000114 
L000115 ### Branch-local handoff
L000116 
L000117 When a concurrent branch reaches a main-agent continuation, the handoff is local to that branch's calling continuation.
L000118 
L000119 Conceptually:
L000120 
L000121 ```text
L000122 parallel
L000123 ├── mechanical ------------------------>
L000124 ├── raw LLM --------------------------->
L000125 ├── independent agent ----------------->
L000126 └── main-agent continuation ----------->
L000127 
L000128 join
L000129 ↓
L000130 declared continuation
L000131 ```
L000132 
L000133 The main-agent handoff does not implicitly pause or suspend independently enabled sibling branches.
L000134 
L000135 Completion of the main-agent branch also does not itself complete the enclosing parallel region or release the join. The workflow's declared join semantics remain authoritative.
L000136 
L000137 ### One continuing main-agent lineage is non-forkable
L000138 
L000139 An admitted TURNLOCK topology MUST NOT permit the same continuing main-agent cognitive lineage to continue through two independently concurrent, non-causally-ordered continuations.
L000140 
L000141 Therefore this topology is inadmissible for one main-agent lineage:
L000142 
L000143 ```text
L000144 parallel
L000145 ├── main-agent M/A
L000146 └── main-agent M/B
L000147 ```
L000148 
L000149 when the declared orchestration establishes neither:
L000150 
L000151 ```text
L000152 M/A before M/B
L000153 ```
L000154 
L000155 nor:
L000156 
L000157 ```text
L000158 M/B before M/A
L000159 ```
L000160 
L000161 and does not otherwise establish mutual exclusion.
L000162 
L000163 The prohibition concerns declared causal structure, not wall-clock overlap.
L000164 
L000165 ### Runtime scheduling does not create semantic ordering
L000166 
L000167 A topology does not become admissible merely because one execution happens to schedule or complete one main-agent use before another main-agent use reaches the resource.
L000168 
L000169 For example:
L000170 
L000171 ```text
L000172 parallel
L000173 ├── main-agent M/A
L000174 └── mechanical
L000175       ↓
L000176       main-agent M/B
L000177 ```
L000178 
L000179 is not rendered valid by an execution in which `M/A` happens to finish before `M/B` is reached.
L000180 
L000181 TURNLOCK MUST NOT interpret accidental runtime order as declared workflow order.
L000182 
L000183 ### No hidden serialization
L000184 
L000185 TURNLOCK MUST NOT repair unordered concurrent uses of the same main-agent lineage by silently serializing them.
L000186 
L000187 Such serialization would manufacture an observable cognitive causal order that the workflow did not declare and would therefore change workflow meaning.
L000188 
L000189 TURNLOCK likewise MUST NOT repair the conflict by:
L000190 
L000191 ```text
L000192 choosing first arrival
L000193 cloning or duplicating the main-agent lineage
L000194 substituting an independent agent
L000195 changing one execution form into another
L000196 inventing an undeclared order
L000197 ```
L000198 
L000199 ### Declared causal order permits repeated main-agent use
L000200 
L000201 The number of main-agent continuation occurrences is not itself restricted.
L000202 
L000203 Repeated use is valid when the workflow declares the relevant causal order.
L000204 
L000205 For example:
L000206 
L000207 ```text
L000208 main-agent M/A
L000209 ↓
L000210 main-agent M/B
L000211 ```
L000212 
L000213 is valid.
L000214 
L000215 Likewise:
L000216 
L000217 ```text
L000218 parallel
L000219 ├── main-agent M/A
L000220 └── mechanical
L000221 join
L000222 ↓
L000223 main-agent M/B
L000224 ```
L000225 
L000226 is valid because the declared join establishes an ordering boundary before the later main-agent continuation.
L000227 
L000228 ### Established mutual exclusion permits multiple syntactic uses
L000229 
L000230 Multiple syntactic occurrences of the same main-agent lineage may exist in concurrent topology when declared workflow semantics establish that the uses cannot become unordered concurrent continuations.
L000231 
L000232 For example:
L000233 
L000234 ```text
L000235 parallel
L000236 ├── if X:
L000237 │     main-agent M/A
L000238 └── if !X:
L000239       main-agent M/B
L000240 ```
L000241 
L000242 may be admissible when the applicable declared semantics establish mutual exclusion.
L000243 
L000244 The normative rule is not:
L000245 
L000246 ```text
L000247 one main-agent occurrence per parallel region
L000248 ```
L000249 
L000250 The normative rule concerns unordered co-reachability of the same continuing cognitive lineage.
L000251 
L000252 This ADR selects no representation, proof system, static analysis, solver, graph algorithm, effect system, or other mechanism for establishing mutual exclusion or causal ordering.
L000253 
L000254 ### Fail closed when compatibility cannot be established
L000255 
L000256 If a topology potentially exposes the same continuing main-agent lineage to unordered concurrent continuations and the required declared ordering or mutual exclusion cannot be established, that topology or invocation MUST NOT be admitted under full TURNLOCK semantics.
L000257 
L000258 TURNLOCK MUST NOT change workflow meaning in order to make the topology executable.
L000259 
L000260 ### Structured nested continuation is not a concurrent fork
L000261 
L000262 Structured nested main-agent use remains valid.
L000263 
L000264 For example:
L000265 
L000266 ```text
L000267 main-agent region A
L000268 ↓
L000269 invoke workflow B
L000270   ↓
L000271   main-agent region B
L000272   ↓
L000273 return to main-agent region A
L000274 ```
L000275 
L000276 uses structured suspension and immediate-caller return.
L000277 
L000278 The outer main-agent continuation is suspended while the nested invocation executes and later resumes according to the accepted nested-call semantics.
L000279 
L000280 That is sequential continuation of one cognitive lineage through structured call/return, not two independently concurrent continuations of that lineage.
L000281 
L000282 ## Invariant consequence
L000283 
L000284 The invariant-admission test admits a new stable invariant identity.
L000285 
L000286 `TL-INV-014` already owns preservation of main-agent cognitive lineage across a handoff.
L000287 
L000288 `TL-INV-024` owns heterogeneous parallel composition.
L000289 
L000290 `TL-INV-027` owns workflow-owned parallel fan-out/fan-in.
L000291 
L000292 `TL-INV-030` owns the requirement that global control transitions remain workflow-authorized.
L000293 
L000294 None of those existing invariant identities independently states the universal prohibition against exposing the same continuing main-agent cognitive lineage to unordered concurrent continuations.
L000295 
L000296 The new obligation therefore receives:
L000297 
L000298 ```text
L000299 TL-INV-039
L000300 Main-agent concurrent-lineage non-forkability invariant
L000301 ```
L000302 
L000303 `TL-INV-039` does not replace or broaden `TL-INV-014`. It owns the concurrency-specific non-forkability obligation.
L000304 
L000305 ## Formal applicability
L000306 
L000307 The concurrency-specific non-forkability obligation is a core safety property suitable for future formalization.
L000308 
L000309 The current repository contains no executable TLA+ model for this obligation, so:
L000310 
L000311 ```text
L000312 formalization: planned
L000313 verification: not-yet-modeled
L000314 ```
L000315 
L000316 The intended future model must distinguish declared causal structure from runtime scheduler order well enough to prevent unordered concurrent continuations of one main-agent lineage.
L000317 
L000318 It may abstract established mutual exclusion.
L000319 
L000320 It MUST NOT turn a particular static-analysis algorithm, solver, scheduler, lock, token, or proof representation into normative product semantics.
L000321 
L000322 No successful TLA+/TLC verification is claimed by this ADR.
L000323 
L000324 ## Rationale
L000325 
L000326 TURNLOCK benefits from allowing the user's continuing main agent to participate in a parallel region while independent work continues elsewhere. For example, mechanical work or independent-agent investigation need not stop merely because one branch currently requires the main agent.
L000327 
L000328 At the same time, the main agent is not a stateless interchangeable worker. Its value is continuation of one session-specific cognitive lineage.
L000329 
L000330 Allowing the same lineage to fork into unordered concurrent continuations would either require multiple divergent cognitive histories or force the runtime to invent an ordering that the workflow did not declare.
L000331 
L000332 The accepted semantics therefore combine:
L000333 
L000334 ```text
L000335 main-agent participation in workflow-owned concurrency
L000336 +
L000337 branch-local handoff
L000338 +
L000339 one non-forkable continuing main-agent lineage
L000340 +
L000341 workflow-declared causal order
L000342 ```
L000343 
L000344 ## Alternatives considered
L000345 
L000346 ### Forbid main-agent continuation in all parallel regions
L000347 
L000348 Rejected. A single main-agent continuation can coexist coherently with independent sibling work without transferring global orchestration authority to the main agent.
L000349 
L000350 ### Allow arbitrary concurrent forks of the same main-agent lineage
L000351 
L000352 Rejected. It contradicts the cognitive-lineage continuity that distinguishes main-agent continuation from independent agents.
L000353 
L000354 ### Silently serialize conflicting main-agent branches
L000355 
L000356 Rejected. Serialization would introduce cognitive causal ordering absent from the declared workflow topology.
L000357 
L000358 ### Use runtime first-arrival order
L000359 
L000360 Rejected. Scheduler timing is not workflow semantics.
L000361 
L000362 ### Clone or reconstruct the main agent for each branch
L000363 
L000364 Rejected. A clone or reconstructed agent is a distinct cognitive lineage unless a separate capability establishes equivalent continuation semantics; it cannot silently stand in for the same continuing main agent.
L000365 
L000366 ### Permit only one syntactic main-agent occurrence per parallel region
L000367 
L000368 Rejected. Declared causal ordering or established mutual exclusion may make multiple syntactic occurrences semantically compatible.
L000369 
L000370 ### Require a particular mutual-exclusion proof mechanism
L000371 
L000372 Rejected. The product requires the semantic property, not a specific implementation or analysis technique.
L000373 
L000374 ## Consequences
L000375 
L000376 * Main-agent continuation becomes an accepted branch type in heterogeneous workflow-owned parallel composition.
L000377 * Main-agent handoff inside one concurrent branch is branch-local.
L000378 * Independently enabled sibling branches are not implicitly suspended by that handoff.
L000379 * Main-agent branch completion does not itself satisfy the enclosing join.
L000380 * One continuing main-agent cognitive lineage cannot occupy unordered concurrent continuations.
L000381 * Multiple main-agent uses remain valid when declared causal ordering or established mutual exclusion makes them compatible.
L000382 * Runtime scheduler order cannot manufacture the required ordering.
L000383 * Potentially conflicting topology fails closed when compatibility cannot be established.
L000384 * Structured nested suspension/return remains valid and is not classified as a concurrent lineage fork.
L000385 * The mechanism used to establish causal ordering, co-reachability, or mutual exclusion remains an architecture, modeling, implementation, or conformance choice rather than normative product semantics.
L000386 
L000387 ## Verification obligation
L000388 
L000389 A conforming realization must demonstrate at least:
L000390 
L000391 1. a declared parallel region containing one main-agent continuation alongside independently progressing sibling work;
L000392 2. that reaching the main-agent continuation does not implicitly suspend unrelated siblings;
L000393 3. that completion of the main-agent branch does not release the join while required sibling work remains incomplete;
L000394 4. rejection of a topology exposing the same main-agent lineage to two unordered concurrent continuations;
L000395 5. rejection does not become acceptance merely because one concrete runtime schedule would serialize those uses;
L000396 6. repeated main-agent use after an explicit causal boundary remains permitted;
L000397 7. multiple syntactic uses may remain permitted when declared mutual exclusion is established; and
L000398 8. structured nested suspension/return remains distinguishable from a concurrent fork.
L000399 
L000400 The demonstration must not depend on a particular scheduler, lock, ownership token, effect system, graph-analysis algorithm, static theorem prover, Rust representation, DSL syntax, process model, or harness-specific implementation.

L000031 # ADR-033: Permit recursive and cyclic workflow invocation under ordinary invocation semantics
L000032 
L000033 ## Context
L000034 
L000035 TURNLOCK already supports structured nested workflow invocation through both
L000036 main-agent-selected and workflow-declared invocation paths.
L000037 
L000038 ADR-008 establishes nested invocation from a main-agent region and return to the
L000039 same main-agent caller. ADR-022 establishes workflow-declared invocation with
L000040 structured call/return semantics. ADR-023 distinguishes the immediate caller
L000041 context from its preserved return-bearing continuation.
L000042 
L000043 Those decisions deliberately did not decide whether the workflow-definition
L000044 call graph may contain direct recursion or cycles.
L000045 
L000046 ADR-027 subsequently established that every accepted invocation, including a
L000047 nested invocation, independently binds one governing workflow definition no
L000048 later than its own acceptance and keeps that definition stable for its lifetime.
L000049 A caller's governing definition does not transitively freeze definitions of
L000050 future callees.
L000051 
L000052 The remaining product question is therefore whether an otherwise authorized and
L000053 admissible workflow invocation may target a workflow already represented among
L000054 its invocation ancestors.
L000055 
L000056 Representative structures are:
L000057 
L000058 ```text
L000059 direct recursion:
L000060 
L000061 A1
L000062 ↓
L000063 invoke A
L000064 ↓
L000065 A2
L000066 ````
L000067 
L000068 and:
L000069 
L000070 ```text
L000071 indirect recursion:
L000072 
L000073 A1
L000074 ↓
L000075 B1
L000076 ↓
L000077 A2
L000078 ```
L000079 
L000080 and more generally:
L000081 
L000082 ```text
L000083 A1
L000084 ↓
L000085 B1
L000086 ↓
L000087 C1
L000088 ↓
L000089 A2
L000090 ```
L000091 
L000092 GitHub Issue #23 records the explicit product-owner decision resolving that
L000093 question.
L000094 
L000095 ## Discovery classification
L000096 
L000097 ### B — recursive and cyclic workflow invocation is permitted
L000098 
L000099 Existing authority deliberately left recursion and cyclic call graphs
L000100 unresolved.
L000101 
L000102 The product decision is:
L000103 
L000104 ```text
L000105 TURNLOCK permits recursive workflow invocation
L000106 and cyclic workflow call graphs.
L000107 ```
L000108 
L000109 Direct recursion, mutual recursion, and longer cyclic call graphs are therefore
L000110 not prohibited merely because a workflow definition occurs more than once in the
L000111 ancestry of an invocation occurrence.
L000112 
L000113 ### A — each recursive or cyclic occurrence remains an ordinary distinct invocation
L000114 
L000115 Once recursive/cyclic composition is permitted, existing invocation semantics
L000116 require every accepted occurrence to remain distinct.
L000117 
L000118 Therefore:
L000119 
L000120 ```text
L000121 workflow identity may repeat
L000122 but
L000123 invocation identity does not collapse
L000124 ```
L000125 
L000126 For example:
L000127 
L000128 ```text
L000129 A1 != A2
L000130 ```
L000131 
L000132 even when `A1` and `A2` resolve to definitions associated with the same workflow
L000133 artifact.
L000134 
L000135 ### A — structured caller/continuation semantics remain unchanged
L000136 
L000137 Recursive/cyclic composition creates no alternate return semantics.
L000138 
L000139 Each accepted recursive/cyclic callee has an immediate caller, and normal
L000140 completion returns to that immediate caller according to the ordinary structured
L000141 invocation rules.
L000142 
L000143 ### A — governing-definition binding remains per invocation occurrence
L000144 
L000145 ADR-027 already requires each accepted nested invocation to establish its own
L000146 governing definition at its own acceptance boundary.
L000147 
L000148 Recursive/cyclic permission does not change that rule.
L000149 
L000150 ### A — recursion creates no authority or admissibility escape
L000151 
L000152 Permission for recursive/cyclic topology is independent from authority to invoke
L000153 a workflow and independent from whether a particular invocation is admissible in
L000154 its current context.
L000155 
L000156 A recursive edge does not create new authority, reset restrictions, or widen the
L000157 caller context.
L000158 
L000159 ## Decision
L000160 
L000161 TURNLOCK permits direct recursive workflow invocation and cyclic workflow call
L000162 graphs.
L000163 
L000164 Permission applies to otherwise ordinary TURNLOCK workflow invocation.
L000165 
L000166 No separate recursive invocation primitive or recursive execution form is
L000167 introduced.
L000168 
L000169 ### Direct recursion
L000170 
L000171 A workflow MAY invoke the same workflow again through an invocation path that is
L000172 otherwise authorized and admissible.
L000173 
L000174 For example:
L000175 
L000176 ```text
L000177 invocation A1
L000178 ↓
L000179 invoke A
L000180 ↓
L000181 invocation A2
L000182 ```
L000183 
L000184 is permitted.
L000185 
L000186 `A2` is a new invocation occurrence.
L000187 
L000188 It is not a continuation, mutation, restart, replacement, or rebinding of
L000189 `A1`.
L000190 
L000191 ### Indirect recursion and cyclic call graphs
L000192 
L000193 A workflow invocation chain MAY revisit a workflow already represented among its
L000194 ancestors.
L000195 
L000196 For example:
L000197 
L000198 ```text
L000199 A1
L000200 ↓
L000201 B1
L000202 ↓
L000203 A2
L000204 ```
L000205 
L000206 and:
L000207 
L000208 ```text
L000209 A1
L000210 ↓
L000211 B1
L000212 ↓
L000213 C1
L000214 ↓
L000215 A2
L000216 ```
L000217 
L000218 are permitted invocation structures.
L000219 
L000220 The repeated workflow in the call graph does not collapse the corresponding
L000221 invocation occurrences into one invocation.
L000222 
L000223 ### A cycle in the call graph does not imply infinite concrete execution
L000224 
L000225 A cyclic workflow-definition call graph is distinct from an infinite execution.
L000226 
L000227 For example:
L000228 
L000229 ```text
L000230 implementation
L000231 ↓
L000232 review
L000233 ↓
L000234 if correction_required:
L000235     invoke implementation
L000236 else:
L000237     complete
L000238 ```
L000239 
L000240 contains a cyclic workflow relationship but a concrete execution may terminate
L000241 after any finite number of invocation occurrences.
L000242 
L000243 Therefore:
L000244 
L000245 ```text
L000246 cyclic workflow call graph
L000247 !=
L000248 infinite execution
L000249 ```
L000250 
L000251 and:
L000252 
L000253 ```text
L000254 recursion permitted
L000255 !=
L000256 termination guaranteed
L000257 ```
L000258 
L000259 TURNLOCK neither requires recursive execution to continue indefinitely nor
L000260 guarantees that every recursive execution terminates.
L000261 
L000262 ### Every occurrence uses ordinary invocation semantics
L000263 
L000264 Each accepted recursive or cyclic invocation occurrence has its own:
L000265 
L000266 ```text
L000267 immediate caller
L000268 preserved return-bearing continuation
L000269 acceptance boundary
L000270 governing workflow definition
L000271 invocation lifetime
L000272 ```
L000273 
L000274 The ordinary structured lifecycle applies:
L000275 
L000276 ```text
L000277 caller
L000278 ↓
L000279 callee occurrence
L000280 ↓
L000281 normal completion
L000282 ↓
L000283 same immediate caller
L000284 ```
L000285 
L000286 A recursive/cyclic callee MUST NOT skip outward over its immediate caller merely
L000287 because the same workflow definition appears elsewhere in the ancestry.
L000288 
L000289 For example:
L000290 
L000291 ```text
L000292 A1
L000293 ↓
L000294 B1
L000295 ↓
L000296 A2
L000297 ```
L000298 
L000299 returns, on normal completion, as:
L000300 
L000301 ```text
L000302 A2
L000303 ↓
L000304 B1
L000305 ↓
L000306 A1
L000307 ```
L000308 
L000309 according to the applicable caller-continuation semantics.
L000310 
L000311 It does not return directly from `A2` to `A1`.
L000312 
L000313 ### Recursive invocation does not mutate an ancestor invocation
L000314 
L000315 Accepting a recursive/cyclic invocation MUST NOT replace, rewrite, capture,
L000316 replan, or rebind any active ancestor invocation.
L000317 
L000318 The relationship is composition:
L000319 
L000320 ```text
L000321 active caller
L000322 ↓
L000323 new invocation occurrence
L000324 ```
L000325 
L000326 not mutation:
L000327 
L000328 ```text
L000329 active caller
L000330 → different governing invocation
L000331 ```
L000332 
L000333 ### Governing-definition binding remains per occurrence
L000334 
L000335 ADR-027 applies independently to every recursive/cyclic invocation occurrence.
L000336 
L000337 For example:
L000338 
L000339 ```text
L000340 artifact A = D1
L000341 
L000342 accept A1
L000343 → governingDefinition(A1) = D1
L000344 
L000345 artifact A later changes:
L000346 D1 → D2
L000347 
L000348 A1 later reaches an invocation of A
L000349 that is already authorized by A1's governing orchestration
L000350 
L000351 accept A2
L000352 → resolve A2 under the applicable workflow-resolution semantics
L000353 → governingDefinition(A2) may be D2
L000354 
L000355 A2 completes
L000356 → return to A1
L000357 
L000358 A1 continues under D1
L000359 ```
L000360 
L000361 The semantic distinction is:
L000362 
L000363 ```text
L000364 A2 binds D2
L000365 !=
L000366 A1 rebinds from D1 to D2
L000367 ```
L000368 
L000369 A new recursive invocation boundary may therefore observe a definition different
L000370 from an active ancestor when the applicable resolution semantics select that
L000371 definition.
L000372 
L000373 This ADR does not define workflow-version syntax, unqualified-name resolution,
L000374 or "latest version" semantics.
L000375 
L000376 ### Recursive/cyclic permission creates no invocation authority
L000377 
L000378 The fact that recursive/cyclic composition is permitted does not authorize an
L000379 actor or execution resource to invoke workflows.
L000380 
L000381 The rule is:
L000382 
L000383 ```text
L000384 recursive/cyclic structure permitted
L000385 +
L000386 invocation path independently authorized
L000387 +
L000388 invocation independently admissible
L000389 → invocation may be accepted
L000390 ```
L000391 
L000392 It is not:
L000393 
L000394 ```text
L000395 recursion permitted
L000396 → all execution resources may invoke workflows
L000397 ```
L000398 
L000399 Existing invocation-decision-owner rules remain independently authoritative.
L000400 
L000401 In particular, this ADR does not grant independent-agent regions a
L000402 workflow-invocation capability.
L000403 
L000404 ### Recursive/cyclic composition creates no admissibility escape
L000405 
L000406 Crossing a recursive or cyclic edge MUST NOT itself reset, erase, widen, or
L000407 bypass restrictions that apply to the invocation context.
L000408 
L000409 Conceptually:
L000410 
L000411 ```text
L000412 restriction R
L000413 ↓
L000414 A
L000415 ↓
L000416 B
L000417 ↓
L000418 A
L000419 ↓
L000420 C
L000421 ```
L000422 
L000423 does not imply:
L000424 
L000425 ```text
L000426 C without R
L000427 ```
L000428 
L000429 Issue #6 owns the general transitive composition-admissibility contract.
L000430 
L000431 This ADR establishes only that recursive/cyclic composition is a permitted
L000432 topological form to which the ordinary authority and admissibility rules apply.
L000433 
L000434 ### Root acceptance does not require infinite expansion
L000435 
L000436 Permitting recursion does not require TURNLOCK to infinitely expand, pre-resolve,
L000437 or prove the complete possible future recursive invocation tree when accepting a
L000438 root invocation.
L000439 
L000440 Later invocation occurrences retain their own boundaries:
L000441 
L000442 ```text
L000443 caller reaches invocation X
L000444 ↓
L000445 X resolves under the applicable semantics
L000446 ↓
L000447 applicable authority/admissibility rules are evaluated
L000448 ↓
L000449 X is accepted or rejected
L000450 ```
L000451 
L000452 This ADR does not define the complete admissibility algorithm.
L000453 
L000454 Issue #6 owns that broader contract.
L000455 
L000456 ### No termination or resource guarantee
L000457 
L000458 Permission for recursive/cyclic invocation introduces no guarantee or
L000459 requirement concerning:
L000460 
L000461 ```text
L000462 eventual termination
L000463 maximum recursion depth
L000464 minimum recursion depth
L000465 unbounded nesting capacity
L000466 memory availability
L000467 compute availability
L000468 token availability
L000469 wall-clock availability
L000470 absence of stack/resource exhaustion
L000471 automatic cycle breaking
L000472 retry
L000473 timeout
L000474 cancellation
L000475 failure propagation
L000476 crash recovery
L000477 ```
L000478 
L000479 A future implementation, harness, profile, or environment may have explicit
L000480 resource constraints.
L000481 
L000482 This ADR does not select such constraints or make any concrete limit part of the
L000483 TURNLOCK product semantics.
L000484 
L000485 ## Invariant consequence
L000486 
L000487 The invariant-admission test creates no new stable invariant identity.
L000488 
L000489 No `TL-INV-040` is introduced.
L000490 
L000491 The accepted recursion/cycle semantics are carried by existing invariant
L000492 responsibilities:
L000493 
L000494 ```text
L000495 TL-INV-017
L000496 → nested invocation may revisit an ancestor workflow and nesting is not
L000497   semantically limited to an acyclic definition graph
L000498 
L000499 TL-INV-018
L000500 → normal completion returns to the immediate caller at every recursive depth
L000501 
L000502 TL-INV-019
L000503 → recursive/cyclic nesting does not rewrite enclosing orchestration
L000504 
L000505 TL-INV-031
L000506 → required composition capability includes recursive/cyclic composition through
L000507   ordinary nested invocation
L000508 
L000509 TL-INV-035
L000510 → workflow-declared invocation may target an ancestor workflow and participate
L000511   in cyclic call graphs
L000512 
L000513 TL-INV-037
L000514 → each recursive occurrence independently binds and preserves its own governing
L000515   workflow definition
L000516 ```
L000517 
L000518 `TL-INV-030` continues to prohibit execution resources or runtime results from
L000519 creating undeclared global continuations; recursion creates no exception to that
L000520 existing rule.
L000521 
L000522 The recursion decision does not require a second invocation mechanism and does
L000523 not justify broadening an unrelated invariant identity.
L000524 
L000525 ## Formal applicability
L000526 
L000527 Recursive/cyclic invocation is relevant to the future core state-machine model,
L000528 but the product decision does not require the first executable TLA+ model to
L000529 represent unbounded recursion.
L000530 
L000531 The normative distinction is:
L000532 
L000533 ```text
L000534 product semantics:
L000535 recursive/cyclic invocation is permitted
L000536 
L000537 formal-model scope:
L000538 may use a finite abstraction or bounded invocation universe
L000539 when that bound is explicitly a modeling choice
L000540 ```
L000541 
L000542 A finite model bound, bounded caller stack, restricted explored depth, or focused
L000543 configuration MUST NOT be presented as a TURNLOCK product recursion limit.
L000544 
L000545 The future model must not encode acyclicity of workflow definitions as a product
L000546 requirement.
L000547 
L000548 The future model must preserve distinct invocation occurrences, structured
L000549 caller/continuation semantics, per-occurrence governing definitions, and
L000550 ordinary admission boundaries when recursive/cyclic traces are represented.
L000551 
L000552 No TLA+ variable, recursion encoding, stack representation, configuration bound,
L000553 or model-checking algorithm is selected by this ADR.
L000554 
L000555 No successful TLA+/TLC verification is claimed.
L000556 
L000557 ## Rationale
L000558 
L000559 Ordinary workflow composition is more expressive when an invocation target may
L000560 be a workflow already present in the ancestry.
L000561 
L000562 Patterns such as:
L000563 
L000564 ```text
L000565 implementation
L000566 → review
L000567 → implementation
L000568 ```
L000569 
L000570 can naturally represent iterative processes without requiring the workflow
L000571 author to manufacture distinct semantic workflow definitions solely to avoid a
L000572 cycle in the call graph.
L000573 
L000574 The semantic safety does not come from forbidding cycles.
L000575 
L000576 It comes from retaining the ordinary invocation boundaries at every occurrence:
L000577 
L000578 ```text
L000579 distinct invocation occurrence
L000580 +
L000581 stable governing definition
L000582 +
L000583 preserved immediate caller
L000584 +
L000585 preserved continuation
L000586 +
L000587 ordinary authority
L000588 +
L000589 ordinary admissibility
L000590 ```
L000591 
L000592 This also preserves the distinction between source evolution and active
L000593 invocation mutation.
L000594 
L000595 A later recursive occurrence may bind a newer definition while its active
L000596 ancestor continues under its existing stable definition.
L000597 
L000598 ## Alternatives considered
L000599 
L000600 ### Require workflow call graphs to be acyclic
L000601 
L000602 Rejected. It would prohibit ordinary recursive composition without a semantic
L000603 need.
L000604 
L000605 ### Permit direct recursion but forbid mutual recursion
L000606 
L000607 Rejected. The distinction would be arbitrary at the product-semantics level;
L000608 ordinary invocation semantics apply equally to both.
L000609 
L000610 ### Require proof of termination before accepting recursion
L000611 
L000612 Rejected. TURNLOCK does not guarantee termination for ordinary execution, and
L000613 the presence of a call-graph cycle does not imply infinite execution.
L000614 
L000615 ### Freeze the complete recursive dependency tree at root acceptance
L000616 
L000617 Rejected. ADR-027 establishes per-invocation governing-definition binding rather
L000618 than a root-wide transitive snapshot.
L000619 
L000620 ### Treat recursive invocation as active rebinding
L000621 
L000622 Rejected. A recursive call creates a new invocation occurrence; it does not
L000623 change the governing definition of the active caller.
L000624 
L000625 ### Add a dedicated recursive-call primitive
L000626 
L000627 Rejected. Recursion is ordinary invocation in a topology where the callee may
L000628 equal or reach an ancestor workflow.
L000629 
L000630 ### Select a recursion depth limit
L000631 
L000632 Rejected. Resource and depth limits are not determined by this semantic
L000633 decision.
L000634 
L000635 ### Select a cycle detector or termination-analysis algorithm
L000636 
L000637 Rejected. Those are implementation, modeling, or conformance mechanisms rather
L000638 than product semantics.
L000639 
L000640 ## Consequences
L000641 
L000642 * Direct workflow recursion is permitted.
L000643 * Indirect recursion and cyclic workflow call graphs are permitted.
L000644 * Repeated workflow identity never collapses distinct invocation occurrences.
L000645 * Each recursive/cyclic occurrence retains ordinary immediate-caller and
L000646   continuation semantics.
L000647 * Normal completion returns one caller boundary at a time.
L000648 * Each occurrence independently binds its governing workflow definition.
L000649 * A later recursive occurrence may bind a different definition from an active
L000650   ancestor without rebinding that ancestor.
L000651 * Recursive/cyclic permission creates no invocation authority.
L000652 * Recursive/cyclic composition creates no admissibility escape.
L000653 * Root acceptance need not expand or resolve an infinite future call tree.
L000654 * A cyclic call graph does not imply infinite concrete execution.
L000655 * No termination, depth, compute, memory, token, timing, retry, timeout,
L000656   cancellation, failure, or crash-recovery guarantee is introduced.
L000657 * No new stable invariant identity is admitted.
L000658 * Issue #6 remains responsible for the general transitive
L000659   composition-admissibility contract.
L000660 
L000661 ## Verification obligation
L000662 
L000663 A conforming realization must be capable of demonstrating, subject to otherwise
L000664 applicable authority and admissibility rules:
L000665 
L000666 1. direct recursive invocation `A1 → A2`;
L000667 2. indirect recursion `A1 → B1 → A2`;
L000668 3. structured normal return `A2 → B1 → A1`;
L000669 4. distinct invocation identity for every recursive occurrence;
L000670 5. stable governing-definition binding independently for ancestor and recursive
L000671    descendant occurrences;
L000672 6. an ancestor remaining under its original definition while a later recursive
L000673    occurrence binds another applicable definition;
L000674 7. no automatic invocation authority created by recursion;
L000675 8. no restriction reset merely because a recursive/cyclic edge is crossed; and
L000676 9. a cyclic workflow-definition graph whose concrete execution can terminate.
L000677 
L000678 The demonstration MUST NOT require a product-level recursion depth, cycle
L000679 detector, termination prover, stack representation, scheduler, Rust structure,

L000681 mechanism selected by this ADR.

L000035 # ADR-034: Delegate nested-workflow invocation to independent-agent regions without main-agent reachability
L000036 
L000037 ## Context
L000038 
L000039 TURNLOCK already treats workflow-declared independent agents as first-class
L000040 execution resources with fresh cognitive lineages, declared semantic missions,
L000041 autonomous multi-turn local strategy and tactics, and workflow-owned global
L000042 continuation.
L000043 
L000044 ADR-020 establishes that independent-agent local autonomy does not confer global
L000045 workflow-orchestration authority and that an independent agent may exercise
L000046 available authority but cannot create additional TURNLOCK-governed authority
L000047 unilaterally.
L000048 
L000049 ADR-021 separates independent-agent normal completion, optional business output,
L000050 and persistent effects.
L000051 
L000052 ADR-022 and ADR-023 establish structured nested invocation with an immediate
L000053 caller context and preserved return-bearing continuation.
L000054 
L000055 ADR-029 keeps generic filesystem, tool, repository, sandbox, ACL/RBAC, and
L000056 environment permission policy outside TURNLOCK Core.
L000057 
L000058 ADR-033 permits recursive and cyclic workflow invocation through ordinary
L000059 invocation semantics.
L000060 
L000061 Current authority does not determine whether a workflow may explicitly delegate
L000062 to one of its independent-agent regions the authority to select and invoke
L000063 nested TURNLOCK workflows dynamically during that agent's autonomous local work.
L000064 
L000065 Without such delegation, an independent agent that discovers a useful reusable
L000066 workflow during investigation would have to end or escape its local cognitive
L000067 episode merely to request that some external caller perform the nested
L000068 composition.
L000069 
L000070 Unrestricted delegation would create a different problem. A fresh independent
L000071 cognitive lineage could indirectly cause a nested workflow to reach the coding
L000072 session's existing main-agent cognitive lineage, crossing the accepted boundary
L000073 between independent local autonomy and workflow-owned transition into the main
L000074 interactive lineage.
L000075 
L000076 GitHub Issue #24 records the product-owner decisions resolving both questions.
L000077 
L000078 ## Discovery classification
L000079 
L000080 ### B — explicit delegated independent-agent invocation capability
L000081 
L000082 Existing independent-agent autonomy does not grant workflow invocation authority.
L000083 
L000084 The product decision is:
L000085 
L000086 ```text
L000087 A workflow MAY explicitly delegate
L000088 nested TURNLOCK workflow-selection/invocation authority
L000089 to a workflow-declared independent-agent region.
L000090 ```
L000091 
L000092 This creates a specific TURNLOCK semantic capability.
L000093 
L000094 ### B — independent-agent-selected invocation cannot reach the session main-agent lineage
L000095 
L000096 The delegated capability is bounded by an explicit composition restriction:
L000097 
L000098 ```text
L000099 an invocation subtree causally rooted in
L000100 an independent-agent-selected nested invocation
L000101 
L000102 MUST NOT transitively reach
L000103 
L000104 the coding session's main-agent cognitive lineage
L000105 ```
L000106 
L000107 The restriction applies through any number of nested workflow boundaries.
L000108 
L000109 ### B — no universal parent-enumerated exact-callee whitelist
L000110
