L000035 # ADR-035: Define transitive nested-composition admissibility and fail-closed invocation acceptance
L000036 
L000037 ## Context
L000038 
L000039 TURNLOCK supports structured nested workflow invocation from multiple semantic
L000040 decision owners.
L000041 
L000042 ADR-008 permits a main-agent region to select a nested workflow.
L000043 
L000044 ADR-022 permits workflow-declared nested invocation.
L000045 
L000046 ADR-034 permits a workflow to explicitly delegate dynamic nested-workflow
L000047 selection/invocation authority to a workflow-declared independent-agent region.
L000048 
L000049 ADR-032 permits main-agent continuation inside workflow-owned concurrency while
L000050 forbidding unordered concurrent continuation of the same main-agent cognitive
L000051 lineage.
L000052 
L000053 ADR-033 permits direct recursion and cyclic workflow call graphs.
L000054 
L000055 ADR-034 additionally establishes that an invocation subtree selected by an
L000056 independent-agent region MUST NOT transitively reach the coding session's
L000057 main-agent cognitive lineage.
L000058 
L000059 These decisions make nested composition expressive, but they create a general
L000060 closure requirement.
L000061 
L000062 A restriction imposed by an enclosing execution context must not be bypassable
L000063 merely by crossing one or more nested workflow boundaries.
L000064 
L000065 For example, a same-main-lineage concurrency conflict remains a conflict when
L000066 one occurrence is hidden behind a nested workflow:
L000067 
L000068 ```text
L000069 parallel
L000070 ├── main-agent M/A
L000071 └── workflow B
L000072       └── main-agent M/B
L000073 ````
L000074 
L000075 Likewise, ADR-034's isolation restriction must survive arbitrary nested workflow
L000076 boundaries:
L000077 
L000078 ```text
L000079 IA1
L000080 ↓
L000081 B
L000082 ↓
L000083 C
L000084 ↓
L000085 D
L000086 ↓
L000087 main-agent continuation
L000088 ```
L000089 
L000090 The remaining product question is the general semantic contract under which an
L000091 otherwise authorized nested invocation may be accepted inside a context that
L000092 carries such restrictions.
L000093 
L000094 GitHub Issue #6 records that decision.
L000095 
L000096 ## Discovery classification
L000097 
L000098 ### B — nested invocation is permitted inside parallel or otherwise restricted contexts when admissible
L000099 
L000100 Existing nested invocation authority did not by itself establish every placement
L000101 in which such invocation may occur.
L000102 
L000103 The accepted decision is:
L000104 
L000105 ```text
L000106 a nested workflow invocation MAY occur
L000107 inside a workflow-owned parallel branch
L000108 or another context carrying admissibility restrictions
L000109 
L000110 when
L000111 
L000112 the invocation is independently authorized
L000113 and
L000114 the resulting composition preserves every applicable restriction
L000115 ```
L000116 
L000117 Nested workflow invocation is composition inside a branch's declared
L000118 progression; it is not a new execution form.
L000119 
L000120 ### B — admissibility is decided per attempted invocation before acceptance
L000121 
L000122 Each attempted nested invocation has its own admission boundary.
L000123 
L000124 Before TURNLOCK accepts that invocation, the invocation must independently
L000125 satisfy its invocation-authority rules and its composition-admissibility rules.
L000126 
L000127 The general shape is:
L000128 
L000129 ```text
L000130 attempt invocation
L000131 ↓
L000132 determine the workflow definition
L000133 that would govern the callee if accepted
L000134 ↓
L000135 check invocation authority
L000136 ↓
L000137 check composition admissibility
L000138 ↓
L000139 accept or reject
L000140 ```
L000141 
L000142 ### B — inability to establish required compatibility fails closed
L000143 
L000144 When preserving an applicable admissibility restriction is required for
L000145 acceptance and that preservation cannot be established at the invocation's
L000146 acceptance boundary, TURNLOCK MUST NOT accept the invocation.
L000147 
L000148 The runtime MUST NOT manufacture compatibility through silent serialization,
L000149 first-arrival ordering, execution-form substitution, hidden topology rewriting,
L000150 or another undeclared repair.
L000151 
L000152 ### B — pre-acceptance rejection creates no callee invocation
L000153 
L000154 When an invocation attempt is rejected before acceptance, no accepted callee
L000155 invocation exists.
L000156 
L000157 The caller is not allowed to treat that rejection as successful completion of
L000158 the nonexistent callee.
L000159 
L000160 ### A — nesting cannot erase an existing restriction
L000161 
L000162 ADR-014 requires workflow-owned declared topology rather than runtime-invented
L000163 global orchestration.
L000164 
L000165 ADR-032 and TL-INV-039 define a same-main-lineage concurrency restriction whose
L000166 meaning depends on declared causality rather than runtime timing.
L000167 
L000168 ADR-034 and TL-INV-040 define a transitive no-main-lineage reachability
L000169 restriction for IA-selected invocation subtrees.
L000170 
L000171 Therefore crossing a workflow boundary cannot silently erase either restriction
L000172 without contradicting the accepted semantics that created it.
L000173 
L000174 The general derived rule is:
L000175 
L000176 ```text
L000177 nested composition does not reset
L000178 an applicable admissibility restriction
L000179 ```
L000180 
L000181 ### A — recursion and cycles do not reset restrictions
L000182 
L000183 ADR-033 already requires recursive/cyclic invocation to remain ordinary nested
L000184 invocation and states that recursion does not create an admissibility escape.
L000185 
L000186 Therefore revisiting a workflow identity cannot create a fresh unrestricted
L000187 context.
L000188 
L000189 ### A — invocation authority and composition admissibility are distinct
L000190 
L000191 ADR-034 explicitly distinguishes delegated IA invocation authority from
L000192 composition admissibility.
L000193 
L000194 The same distinction applies generally:
L000195 
L000196 ```text
L000197 authorized
L000198 !=
L000199 admissible
L000200 ```
L000201 
L000202 Both are required for acceptance.
L000203 
L000204 ### A — the admitted workflow definition must be the accepted governing definition
L000205 
L000206 ADR-027 requires every accepted invocation to bind one governing workflow
L000207 definition no later than acceptance and keep it stable for that invocation's
L000208 lifetime.
L000209 
L000210 An admissibility decision would not protect the accepted composition if
L000211 TURNLOCK could validate one definition and bind another.
L000212 
L000213 Therefore the workflow definition whose composition is admitted MUST be the
L000214 definition that becomes governing for that invocation if acceptance succeeds.
L000215 
L000216 ## Decision
L000217 
L000218 Every attempted nested TURNLOCK workflow invocation is subject to an
L000219 implementation-independent composition-admissibility boundary before acceptance.
L000220 
L000221 The admission decision concerns the attempted invocation in its actual caller
L000222 and surrounding semantic context.
L000223 
L000224 ### Authorization and admissibility are independent requirements
L000225 
L000226 An attempted nested invocation may be accepted only if both conditions hold:
L000227 
L000228 ```text
L000229 invocation is independently authorized
L000230 +
L000231 composition is admissible under every applicable restriction
L000232 ```
L000233 
L000234 Invocation authorization answers whether the relevant decision owner is allowed
L000235 to attempt/create the nested invocation.
L000236 
L000237 Composition admissibility answers whether accepting the callee in that context
L000238 would preserve the restrictions that govern that composition.
L000239 
L000240 Neither question substitutes for the other.
L000241 
L000242 ### Applicable restrictions remain closed under nested composition
L000243 
L000244 When an accepted restriction's normative scope extends into nested descendants,
L000245 every accepted nested invocation within that scope remains subject to that
L000246 restriction.
L000247 
L000248 Crossing a workflow boundary MUST NOT by itself:
L000249 
L000250 ```text
L000251 erase
L000252 reset
L000253 weaken
L000254 widen
L000255 bypass
L000256 satisfy
L000257 or terminate
L000258 ```
L000259 
L000260 such a restriction.
L000261 
L000262 The same rule applies across recursive and cyclic workflow invocation.
L000263 
L000264 `TL-INV-041` does not extend a restriction beyond the scope assigned by the
L000265 decision or invariant that owns that restriction.
L000266 
L000267 It preserves each restriction according to its own accepted scope.
L000268 
L000269 ### Admissibility may depend on surrounding topology
L000270 
L000271 Composition admissibility is not necessarily a property of the callee in
L000272 isolation.
L000273 
L000274 Applicable restrictions may require considering semantic facts such as:
L000275 
L000276 ```text
L000277 caller context
L000278 surrounding declared topology
L000279 sibling branches
L000280 declared causal ordering
L000281 co-reachability
L000282 established mutual exclusion
L000283 cognitive-lineage identity
L000284 caller provenance
L000285 declared conditions
L000286 restriction scope
L000287 ```
L000288 
L000289 For example:
L000290 
L000291 ```text
L000292 parallel
L000293 ├── main-agent M/A
L000294 └── workflow B
L000295       └── main-agent M/B
L000296 ```
L000297 
L000298 is inadmissible for one continuing main-agent lineage when the declared topology
L000299 allows `M/A` and `M/B` to be unordered co-reachable continuations.
L000300 
L000301 The nested workflow boundary around B does not hide that conflict.
L000302 
L000303 ### Workflow invocation may occur inside a parallel branch
L000304 
L000305 A workflow-owned parallel branch MAY contain nested workflow invocation as part
L000306 of that branch's declared progression.
L000307 
L000308 For example:
L000309 
L000310 ```text
L000311 parallel
L000312 ├── mechanical
L000313 └── workflow B
L000314       └── raw LLM
L000315 ```
L000316 
L000317 may be admitted.
L000318 
L000319 Nested invocation inside a branch remains subject to ordinary invocation
L000320 authority and this ADR's composition-admissibility contract.
L000321 
L000322 Nested workflow invocation is composition; it is not a fifth parallel execution
L000323 form alongside mechanical execution, raw LLM inference, independent-agent
L000324 execution, and main-agent continuation.
L000325 
L000326 ### Declared causality or mutual exclusion may establish compatibility
L000327 
L000328 An admissibility restriction that concerns co-reachability does not prohibit
L000329 multiple syntactic occurrences merely because they both exist in the workflow
L000330 artifact.
L000331 
L000332 For example:
L000333 
L000334 ```text
L000335 parallel
L000336 ├── if X:
L000337 │     main-agent M/A
L000338 └── workflow B
L000339       └── if !X:
L000340             main-agent M/B
L000341 ```
L000342 
L000343 may be admissible when the applicable declared semantics establish that the
L000344 same-lineage uses are mutually exclusive.
L000345 
L000346 The product requires the semantic property.
L000347 
L000348 It does not select the mechanism used to establish it.
L000349 
L000350 ### Runtime scheduling does not establish admissibility
L000351 
L000352 A composition MUST NOT become admissible merely because one concrete runtime
L000353 schedule happens to avoid the conflict.
L000354 
L000355 Runtime order is not a substitute for workflow-declared causal order.
L000356 
L000357 TURNLOCK MUST NOT repair an inadmissible topology by silently:
L000358 
L000359 ```text
L000360 serializing branches
L000361 using first-arrival order
L000362 dropping a branch
L000363 changing a callee
L000364 substituting an execution form
L000365 cloning a cognitive lineage
L000366 lifting invocation authority
L000367 inventing a causal edge
L000368 rewriting the declared topology
L000369 ```
L000370 
L000371 ### Fail closed when required preservation cannot be established
L000372 
L000373 If acceptance requires TURNLOCK to establish that an applicable restriction is
L000374 preserved and that compatibility cannot be established at the attempted
L000375 invocation's acceptance boundary, the invocation MUST NOT be accepted.
L000376 
L000377 The accepted rule is:
L000378 
L000379 ```text
L000380 required compatibility cannot be established
L000381 →
L000382 invocation not accepted
L000383 ```
L000384 
L000385 It is not:
L000386 
L000387 ```text
L000388 required compatibility cannot be established
L000389 →
L000390 accept and rely on runtime luck
L000391 ```
L000392 
L000393 This decision chooses a semantic outcome, not a proof or analysis algorithm.
L000394 
L000395 ### Admission occurs per invocation occurrence
L000396 
L000397 TURNLOCK does not need to pre-expand or pre-resolve the complete future nested
L000398 call tree when accepting a root or parent invocation.
L000399 
L000400 Each later nested invocation occurrence retains its own admission boundary.
L000401 
L000402 Conceptually:
L000403 
L000404 ```text
L000405 accept A
L000406 ↓
L000407 A later attempts B
L000408 ↓
L000409 admit or reject B
L000410 
L000411 if B is accepted and later attempts C
L000412 ↓
L000413 admit or reject C
L000414 ```
L000415 
L000416 A parent's acceptance does not pre-authorize descendants.
L000417 
L000418 A parent's acceptance does not guarantee that every later nested invocation will
L000419 be admissible.
L000420 
L000421 A later nested rejection therefore does not imply that the parent should
L000422 necessarily have been rejected at its earlier admission boundary.
L000423 
L000424 This ADR introduces no progress or termination guarantee.
L000425 
L000426 ### Direct behavior of the candidate composition remains constrained
L000427 
L000428 The absence of root-wide future expansion does not permit the workflow
L000429 definition currently being admitted to directly violate a restriction that
L000430 already applies to the composition.
L000431 
L000432 For example, under the TL-INV-040 restriction:
L000433 
L000434 ```text
L000435 IA1
L000436 ↓
L000437 attempt B
L000438 
L000439 B directly permits:
L000440 main-agent continuation
L000441 ```
L000442 
L000443 B cannot be accepted when the admitted semantics make that main-agent
L000444 continuation reachable and no accepted semantic ordering or exclusion removes
L000445 that reachability.
L000446 
L000447 By contrast, if B later attempts another nested workflow C, C receives its own
L000448 admission boundary with the still-applicable restrictions.
L000449 
L000450 ### Recursive/cyclic calls preserve admission context
L000451 
L000452 ADR-033 permits recursion and cycles.
L000453 
L000454 For example:
L000455 
L000456 ```text
L000457 A1
L000458 ↓
L000459 B1
L000460 ↓
L000461 A2
L000462 ```
L000463 
L000464 Every occurrence remains distinct.
L000465 
L000466 Every later nested attempt is checked at its own boundary.
L000467 
L000468 A recursive/cyclic edge MUST NOT create a fresh unrestricted admissibility
L000469 context merely because a workflow identity repeats.
L000470 
L000471 ### The admitted definition becomes the governing definition
L000472 
L000473 Before accepting an attempted invocation, TURNLOCK may resolve or otherwise
L000474 identify the workflow definition that would govern the invocation if accepted
L000475 to the extent required to establish admission.
L000476 
L000477 That evaluation does not itself create an accepted invocation.
L000478 
L000479 The required semantic relationship is:
L000480 
L000481 ```text
L000482 attempt B
L000483 ↓
L000484 definition DB is the definition evaluated for admission
L000485 ↓
L000486 B accepted
L000487 ↓
L000488 governingDefinition(B) = DB
L000489 ```
L000490 
L000491 TURNLOCK MUST NOT:
L000492 
L000493 ```text
L000494 evaluate D1 for admission
L000495 then accept the same invocation under D2
L000496 ```
L000497 
L000498 without performing a new admission decision for D2.
L000499 
L000500 If the attempt is rejected:
L000501 
L000502 ```text
L000503 no accepted B invocation exists
L000504 no governing definition is bound for B
L000505 ```
L000506 
L000507 This rule selects no definition identifier, hash, snapshot, storage mechanism,
L000508 workflow-reference syntax, resolution algorithm, or locking mechanism.
L000509 
L000510 ### Pre-acceptance rejection creates no callee lifecycle
L000511 
L000512 When a nested invocation is rejected before acceptance:
L000513 
L000514 ```text
L000515 no accepted callee invocation exists
L000516 no callee lifetime exists
L000517 no callee governing definition is bound
L000518 no callee call/return episode exists
L000519 no normal callee completion occurs
L000520 ```
L000521 
L000522 The caller remains the immediate calling context.
L000523 
L000524 Its preserved/local continuation is not consumed by the nonexistent callee.
L000525 
L000526 Suspension for the nested call becomes effective only for an accepted
L000527 invocation.
L000528 
L000529 For a main-agent-selected invocation, rejection leaves the same main-agent
L000530 region as caller.
L000531 
L000532 For an independent-agent-selected invocation, rejection leaves the same
L000533 independent-agent region as caller.
L000534 
L000535 For a workflow-declared invocation, rejection MUST NOT silently enable the
L000536 normal successful post-call continuation as though the rejected callee had
L000537 completed.
L000538 
L000539 The rejection must remain attributable or observable at the relevant execution
L000540 boundary.
L000541 
L000542 This ADR does not select retry, fallback, abort, catch, alternate-callee,
L000543 failure-propagation, cancellation, timeout, or user-interaction semantics.
L000544 
L000545 ### TL-INV-039 is preserved through nested composition
L000546 
L000547 The same continuing main-agent cognitive lineage MUST NOT obtain unordered
L000548 concurrent continuations merely because one occurrence appears inside a nested
L000549 workflow.
L000550 
L000551 Declared causal ordering or established mutual exclusion may make repeated uses
L000552 compatible.
L000553 
L000554 Scheduler order cannot do so.
L000555 
L000556 ### TL-INV-040 is preserved through nested composition
L000557 
L000558 An invocation subtree causally rooted in an independent-agent-selected nested
L000559 invocation remains prohibited from reaching the coding session's main-agent
L000560 cognitive lineage.
L000561 
L000562 Nested calls, recursion, cycles, conditions, and parallel branches do not reset
L000563 that restriction.
L000564 
L000565 The restriction ends only according to TL-INV-040's already-accepted scope.
L000566 
L000567 ### No normative effect/capability representation
L000568 
L000569 This ADR defines a semantic admissibility relation.
L000570 
L000571 It does not require the implementation or formal model to encode that relation
L000572 as:
L000573 
L000574 ```text
L000575 effect sets
L000576 capability sets
L000577 bitmasks
L000578 type effects
L000579 graph summaries
L000580 transitive closure tables
L000581 static annotations
L000582 runtime tokens
L000583 proof objects
L000584 ```
L000585 
L000586 Any such representation is a later modeling, architecture, implementation, or
L000587 conformance choice.
L000588 
L000589 ## Invariant consequence
L000590 
L000591 The invariant-admission procedure admits exactly one new stable invariant:
L000592 
L000593 ```text
L000594 TL-INV-041
L000595 Nested-composition admissibility-closure invariant
L000596 ```
L000597 
L000598 `TL-INV-041` owns the universal requirement that an attempted nested invocation
L000599 must not be accepted unless it is independently authorized and preserves every
L000600 applicable composition-admissibility restriction.
L000601 
L000602 It also owns:
L000603 
L000604 ```text
L000605 transitive preservation of restrictions whose scope extends into descendants
L000606 
L000607 fail-closed rejection when required preservation cannot be established
L000608 
L000609 scheduler order not manufacturing admissibility
L000610 
L000611 rejected pre-acceptance attempts creating no callee invocation
L000612 
L000613 the admitted workflow definition matching the definition bound at acceptance
L000614 ```
L000615 
L000616 Existing invariants retain their specific responsibilities:
L000617 
L000618 ```text
L000619 TL-INV-024
L000620 → heterogeneous workflow-owned parallel composition
L000621 
L000622 TL-INV-035
L000623 → workflow-declared nested invocation
L000624 
L000625 TL-INV-037
L000626 → stable governing definition per accepted invocation
L000627 
L000628 TL-INV-039
L000629 → same-main-lineage concurrent non-forkability
L000630 
L000631 TL-INV-040
L000632 → IA-selected subtree main-lineage isolation
L000633 ```
L000634 
L000635 No second new invariant is admitted.
L000636 
L000637 ## Formal applicability
L000638 
L000639 `TL-INV-041` is a core safety obligation for the first executable TURNLOCK
L000640 state-machine model.
L000641 
L000642 A future model must be able to distinguish:
L000643 
L000644 ```text
L000645 attempted invocation
L000646 accepted invocation
L000647 rejected pre-acceptance attempt
L000648 ```
L000649 
L000650 and must represent enough abstract context to decide whether each modeled nested
L000651 invocation transition is admissible.
L000652 
L000653 The model must preserve the distinction:
L000654 
L000655 ```text
L000656 invocation authority
L000657 !=
L000658 composition admissibility
L000659 ```
L000660 
L000661 The model must also preserve enough declared topology to represent, where
L000662 relevant:
L000663 
L000664 ```text
L000665 causal ordering
L000666 co-reachability
L000667 mutual exclusion
L000668 restriction scope
L000669 caller context
L000670 main-agent lineage identity
L000671 IA-selected-subtree provenance
L000672 ```
L000673 
L000674 The model may abstract these facts.
L000675 
L000676 The model may use:
L000677 
L000678 ```text
L000679 sets
L000680 predicates
L000681 relations
L000682 finite workflow universes
L000683 finite invocation depth
L000684 abstract summaries
L000685 flags
L000686 ```
L000687 
L000688 when appropriate.
L000689 
L000690 Those choices are modeling decisions, not TURNLOCK product semantics.
L000691 
L000692 The first model does not need to pre-expand an unbounded recursive call graph.
L000693 
L000694 Later nested invocations may be checked at their own abstract admission
L000695 boundaries.
L000696 
L000697 No TLA+ state variable, action, effect representation, capability lattice,
L000698 static-analysis algorithm, graph algorithm, theorem prover, scheduler, Rust
L000699 representation, DSL representation, or runtime validation strategy is selected
L000700 by this ADR.
L000701 
L000702 No successful TLA+/TLC verification is claimed.
L000703 
L000704 ## Rationale
L000705 
L000706 TURNLOCK permits reusable nested composition while preserving explicit
L000707 workflow-owned orchestration.
L000708 
L000709 That composition is only safe if restrictions established by one semantic layer
L000710 cannot be bypassed merely by adding another workflow boundary.
L000711 
L000712 At the same time, requiring root-wide pre-expansion of all possible future
L000713 nested calls would conflict with per-invocation definition binding, dynamic
L000714 workflow selection, and recursive/cyclic composition.
L000715 
L000716 The accepted design therefore uses a compositional rule:
L000717 
L000718 ```text
L000719 each invocation has an admission boundary
L000720 +
L000721 applicable restrictions remain in force across descendants
L000722 +
L000723 later nested invocations are checked at their own boundaries
L000724 +
L000725 unknown required compatibility fails closed
L000726 ```
L000727 
L000728 This gives the formal model a definite invocation-admission contract without
L000729 forcing TURNLOCK to adopt a particular effect system or graph-analysis
L000730 architecture.
L000731 
L000732 ## Alternatives considered
L000733 
L000734 ### Check only the direct syntactic step at the caller
L000735 
L000736 Rejected. Nested workflow boundaries could bypass restrictions transitively.
L000737 
L000738 ### Reject every nested workflow invocation from a parallel branch
L000739 
L000740 Rejected. Workflow invocation is valid branch-local composition when the
L000741 resulting topology preserves applicable restrictions.
L000742 
L000743 ### Accept every authorized invocation and rely on descendant checks
L000744 
L000745 Rejected as a universal rule. The candidate composition itself may already
L000746 directly violate an applicable restriction.
L000747 
L000748 ### Require full root-wide transitive workflow expansion before acceptance
L000749 
L000750 Rejected. Future nested occurrences have their own admission boundaries, and
L000751 recursive/dynamic invocation does not require a transitive root snapshot.
L000752 
L000753 ### Silently serialize incompatible topology
L000754 
L000755 Rejected. Serialization would manufacture semantic causal ordering absent from
L000756 the workflow definition.
L000757 
L000758 ### Use runtime first-arrival order as admissibility
L000759 
L000760 Rejected. Scheduler timing is not declared workflow semantics.
L000761 
L000762 ### Validate one workflow definition and bind another
L000763 
L000764 Rejected. The admitted composition must correspond to the governing definition
L000765 of the accepted invocation.
L000766

L000035 # ADR-036: Define occurrence-scoped conditional orchestration progress without universal completion
L000036 
L000037 ## Context
L000038 
L000039 TURNLOCK's accepted control semantics define reversible main-agent handoff,
L000040 structured workflow invocation/return, immediate-caller restoration, and
L000041 workflow-owned fan-out/fan-in.
L000042 
L000043 The formal traceability manifest historically associated several of those
L000044 invariants with planned property names containing `Eventually` or otherwise
L000045 grouped them under `safety+liveness`.
L000046 
L000047 Those names did not establish product semantics and left three materially
L000048 different obligations conflated:
L000049 
L000050 1. whether an execution resource or workflow eventually produces completion;
L000051 2. what control-state consequence follows when a completion/yield/return/join
L000052    condition is recognized;
L000053 3. whether TURNLOCK may indefinitely starve orchestration progression that is
L000054    already continuously enabled.
L000055 
L000056 Issue #2 resolves that ambiguity.
L000057 
L000058 The distinction must preserve TURNLOCK's role as the orchestration engine
L000059 without turning TURNLOCK into a guarantor that arbitrary computation,
L000060 agentic work, external dependencies, recursive workflows, or branch sets always
L000061 terminate.
L000062 
L000063 ## Discovery classification
L000064 
L000065 ### Derived from existing authority — completion determines the structural return/continuation consequence
L000066 
L000067 Existing handoff, invocation/return, immediate-caller, and join semantics already
L000068 require a determinate control consequence when their applicable completion
L000069 condition occurs.
L000070 
L000071 Normal completion does not create an additional product choice about which
L000072 caller or continuation is restored.
L000073 
L000074 At the semantic level, once TURNLOCK recognizes the relevant completion/yield
L000075 condition, the resulting control consequence is established by that control
L000076 transition.
L000077 
L000078 This semantic requirement does not require implementation-level transaction
L000079 atomicity or any particular scheduler/runtime mechanism.
L000080 
L000081 ### Decision-required, resolved — occurrence-scoped conditional non-starvation
L000082 
L000083 Existing authority did not uniquely decide whether a continuation that remains
L000084 eligible may be indefinitely ignored by TURNLOCK's own scheduling.
L000085 
L000086 The accepted decision is:
L000087 
L000088 ```text
L000089 for each TURNLOCK-owned progression occurrence P:
L000090 
L000091 if P is eligible,
L000092 and P remains continuously eligible,
L000093 and P remains applicable under the governing workflow semantics,
L000094 
L000095 TURNLOCK must not indefinitely fail to advance P
L000096 solely because TURNLOCK's own scheduling keeps selecting other progression
L000097 ```
L000098 
L000099 Progress by another occurrence does not satisfy this obligation.
L000100 
L000101 This is a product-level conditional liveness guarantee.
L000102 
L000103 ### Scope clarification — no universal completion guarantee
L000104 
L000105 TURNLOCK does not universally guarantee that every started execution region,
L000106 workflow invocation, parallel branch, branch set, or workflow eventually
L000107 completes.
L000108 
L000109 In particular, the conditional liveness obligation does not assert that the
L000110 completion/yield/result condition which enables later orchestration progression
L000111 will eventually occur.
L000112 
L000113 This preserves the existing absence of universal completion guarantees for
L000114 bounded cognition and recursive/cyclic workflow execution and applies the same
L000115 boundary consistently to the affected handoff, invocation, return, and join
L000116 semantics.
L000117 
L000118 ### Formal-modeling choice — occurrence representation and fairness encoding
L000119 
L000120 The representation of an occurrence and the TLA+ fairness mechanism used to
L000121 encode this product obligation are formal-modeling choices.
L000122 
L000123 ADR-036 does not select weak fairness, strong fairness, a scheduler algorithm,
L000124 an occurrence identifier, a state-variable representation, or a parameterized
L000125 action shape.
L000126 
L000127 Issue #3 owns that formal representation.
L000128 
L000129 Issue #1 owns the property-level verification/evidence metamodel.
L000130 
L000131 ## Decision
L000132 
L000133 TURNLOCK separates execution-resource completion from TURNLOCK-owned
L000134 orchestration progress.
L000135 
L000136 ### 1. No universal work-completion promise
L000137 
L000138 TURNLOCK does not promise that every execution resource, region, invocation,
L000139 branch set, or workflow eventually reaches normal completion.
L000140 
L000141 A product or workflow primitive may acquire stronger semantics through a
L000142 separate accepted decision, but no such universal guarantee is introduced here.
L000143 
L000144 ### 2. Recognized completion has an immediate semantic control consequence
L000145 
L000146 When TURNLOCK recognizes a completion/yield/return-ready/join-satisfied
L000147 condition whose governing workflow semantics determines a control consequence,
L000148 the semantic state resulting from that control transition MUST already reflect
L000149 that consequence.
L000150 
L000151 Examples include:
L000152 
L000153 ```text
L000154 main-agent region completes/yields
L000155 → declared workflow continuation becomes eligible
L000156 
L000157 workflow-declared callee normally completes
L000158 → correct caller relationship is restored
L000159 → preserved post-call continuation becomes eligible
L000160 
L000161 agent-selected callee normally completes
L000162 → same immediate caller agent region resumes
L000163 
L000164 declared join requirements become satisfied
L000165 → declared post-join continuation becomes eligible
L000166 ```
L000167 
L000168 This is semantic transition structure, not a requirement that one implementation
L000169 operation perform all internal work atomically.
L000170 
L000171 ### 3. Continuously enabled TURNLOCK-owned progression is not starved
L000172 
L000173 For every particular TURNLOCK-owned progression occurrence, if that occurrence
L000174 is eligible, remains continuously eligible, and remains applicable under the
L000175 governing workflow semantics, TURNLOCK MUST NOT indefinitely fail to advance
L000176 that occurrence solely because its own scheduling selects other progression.
L000177 
L000178 ### 4. The obligation is occurrence-scoped
L000179 
L000180 Progress of another invocation, caller continuation, branch, join, or workflow
L000181 does not discharge the progress obligation of the continuously enabled
L000182 occurrence.
L000183 
L000184 ### 5. The obligation ends if applicability legitimately ends
L000185 
L000186 If governing workflow semantics make an occurrence no longer eligible or no
L000187 longer applicable, the conditional progress obligation no longer applies to
L000188 that occurrence from that point.
L000189 
L000190 This decision does not define cancellation, timeout, failure, race, preemption,
L000191 or invalidation semantics.
L000192 
L000193 ### 6. External or agentic completion is not converted into engine liveness
L000194 
L000195 TURNLOCK's conditional progress obligation begins only after the relevant
L000196 TURNLOCK-owned progression is enabled.
L000197 
L000198 It does not require a main agent, independent agent, raw LLM operation,
L000199 mechanical/external operation, nested workflow, parallel branch, or recursive
L000200 workflow to eventually produce the trigger that would enable that progression.
L000201 
L000202 ### 7. Formal fairness and runtime scheduling mechanisms remain unspecified
L000203 
L000204 This decision does not select weak fairness, strong fairness, FIFO, round-robin,
L000205 priority scheduling, work stealing, timing bounds, retries, watchdogs, runtime
L000206 IDs, UUIDs, counters, tokens, handles, threads, processes, or any equivalent
L000207 formal or implementation mechanism.
L000208 
L000209 ## Invariant admission
L000210 
L000211 The occurrence-scoped conditional non-starvation guarantee is a distinct
L000212 universal temporal obligation and is not independently owned by the existing
L000213 local handoff, invocation/return, immediate-caller, or fan-out/fan-in
L000214 invariants.
L000215 
L000216 Therefore a new stable invariant is admitted:
L000217 
L000218 ```text
L000219 TL-INV-042 — Conditional orchestration-progress invariant
L000220 ```
L000221 
L000222 `TL-INV-004`, `TL-INV-008`, `TL-INV-018`, and `TL-INV-027` retain their existing
L000223 identities and are reclassified to remove the previously conflated liveness
L000224 meaning.
L000225 
L000226 No other new invariant is introduced.
L000227 
L000228 ## Formal-traceability consequence
L000229 
L000230 The existing planned names:
L000231 
L000232 ```text
L000233 InvocationEventuallyReturnsUnderFairness
L000234 CorrectCallerEventuallyResumesUnderFairness
L000235 JoinEventuallyReleasesUnderFairness
L000236 ```
L000237 
L000238 are removed because they can be read as promising universal completion of their
L000239 triggering work.
L000240 
L000241 `HandoffCanResume` is retained only as a capability/reachability obligation.
L000242 
L000243 No replacement TLA+ property identifier is invented before an executable model
L000244 contains it.
L000245 
L000246 `TL-INV-042` is recorded as planned/not-yet-modeled with no TLA+ property,
L000247 state-variable, action, configuration, occurrence representation, or fairness
L000248 formula selected yet.
L000249 
L000250 ## Consequences
L000251 
L000252 * TURNLOCK remains responsible for executing workflow-owned orchestration.
L000253 * TURNLOCK cannot satisfy the contract while indefinitely starving one
L000254   continuously enabled, still-applicable progression occurrence through its own
L000255   scheduling.
L000256 * TURNLOCK does not become responsible for guaranteeing termination of arbitrary
L000257   computation, agentic work, external dependencies, recursive workflows, or
L000258   parallel branch sets.
L000259 * Normal completion determines the appropriate return/eligibility consequence
L000260   structurally rather than creating an additional scheduling decision about
L000261   what the continuation should be.
L000262 * Formal occurrence scope and fairness encoding remain downstream modeling
L000263   responsibilities.
L000264 * No runtime scheduling algorithm or identity mechanism becomes product
L000265   semantics.
L000266 
L000267 ## Non-goals
L000268 
L000269 This decision does not define:
L000270 
L000271 * universal workflow termination;
L000272 * universal region or branch completion;
L000273 * cancellation;
L000274 * failure propagation;
L000275 * timeout behavior;
L000276 * retry behavior;
L000277 * preemption;
L000278 * recovery;
L000279 * a scheduler algorithm;
L000280 * scheduler priority;
L000281 * weak or strong fairness formulas;
L000282 * runtime occurrence identifiers;
L000283 * UUIDs, counters, tokens, or handles;
L000284 * Rust types;
L000285 * process or thread topology;
L000286 * persistence;
L000287 * TLA+ state variables or actions;
L000288 * a concrete completion/yield protocol for the main agent.

L000026 # ADR-037: Require eventual advance of continuously enabled orchestration progress
L000027 
L000028 ## Context
L000029 
L000030 ADR-036 established `TL-INV-042` as TURNLOCK's occurrence-scoped conditional
L000031 orchestration-progress invariant.
L000032 
L000033 The intended product distinction was:
L000034 
L000035 ```text
L000036 execution-resource completion
L000037 is not universally guaranteed
L000038 
L000039 but
L000040 
L000041 once a TURNLOCK-owned progression occurrence
L000042 is continuously eligible and applicable,
L000043 TURNLOCK must eventually advance that occurrence
L000044 ```
L000045 
L000046 ADR-036 correctly rejected universal completion guarantees and correctly made
L000047 the progress obligation occurrence-scoped.
L000048 
L000049 However, one part of its accepted wording stated that TURNLOCK must not
L000050 indefinitely fail to advance an eligible occurrence:
L000051 
L000052 ```text
L000053 solely because TURNLOCK's own scheduling
L000054 keeps selecting other progression
L000055 ```
L000056 
L000057 That causal qualification is too narrow.
L000058 
L000059 It leaves open a behavior in which the occurrence remains continuously eligible
L000060 and applicable forever while TURNLOCK advances no competing occurrence and
L000061 simply leaves the occurrence unadvanced forever.
L000062 
L000063 That behavior does not satisfy the intended orchestration-engine progress
L000064 contract.
L000065 
L000066 This ADR amends ADR-036 only at that boundary.
L000067 
L000068 ## Discovery classification
L000069 
L000070 ### Decision-required, resolved — remove the causal qualification from conditional progress
L000071 
L000072 ADR-036's accepted wording does not uniquely prohibit indefinite inactivity when
L000073 no competing progression is selected.
L000074 
L000075 The accepted corrected decision is:
L000076 
L000077 ```text
L000078 for every particular TURNLOCK-owned progression occurrence P:
L000079 
L000080 if P is eligible,
L000081 and P remains continuously eligible,
L000082 and P remains applicable under the governing workflow semantics,
L000083 
L000084 TURNLOCK MUST eventually advance P
L000085 ```
L000086 
L000087 The obligation does not depend on why progression has not yet occurred.
L000088 
L000089 In particular:
L000090 
L000091 ```text
L000092 P continuously eligible and applicable
L000093 +
L000094 other occurrences repeatedly progress
L000095 +
L000096 P never progresses
L000097 ```
L000098 
L000099 is non-conforming.
L000100 
L000101 And:
L000102 
L000103 ```text
L000104 P continuously eligible and applicable
L000105 +
L000106 TURNLOCK performs no competing progression
L000107 +
L000108 P never progresses
L000109 ```
L000110 
L000111 is also non-conforming.
L000112 
L000113 No competing occurrence, scheduler preference, or other causal explanation is a
L000114 premise of the liveness obligation.
L000115 
L000116 ### Preserved scope — no universal completion guarantee
L000117 
L000118 This amendment does not require the event, agent, external operation, workflow,
L000119 branch, or other execution resource that would create an eligible continuation
L000120 to eventually complete.
L000121 
L000122 The obligation begins only after the applicable TURNLOCK-owned progression
L000123 occurrence is eligible.
L000124 
L000125 It therefore does not convert TURNLOCK into a universal termination guarantee.
L000126 
L000127 ### Preserved scope — applicability may cease
L000128 
L000129 The obligation applies while the particular occurrence remains continuously
L000130 eligible and applicable.
L000131 
L000132 If governing workflow semantics legitimately make that occurrence no longer
L000133 eligible or applicable before it advances, this ADR introduces no independent
L000134 requirement that the occurrence still execute.
L000135 
L000136 This ADR does not define the semantics that might cause eligibility or
L000137 applicability to cease.
L000138 
L000139 ### Preserved scope — no crash, failure, or durability semantics
L000140 
L000141 This amendment does not define failure, cancellation, timeout, retry,
L000142 preemption, crash recovery, durability, persistence, process lifetime, machine
L000143 failure, or resource-exhaustion semantics.
L000144 
L000145 It does not define whether or how an occurrence remains eligible across such an
L000146 event.
L000147 
L000148 Those questions remain governed separately or intentionally unspecified.
L000149 
L000150 ### Formal-modeling choice remains downstream
L000151 
L000152 This amendment does not select a TLA+ occurrence representation or a fairness
L000153 formula.
L000154 
L000155 Issue #3 remains responsible for representing the accepted semantic obligation
L000156 in the formal model.
L000157 
L000158 Issue #1 remains responsible for the property-level verification/evidence
L000159 metamodel.
L000160 
L000161 ## Decision
L000162 
L000163 ADR-036 is amended as follows.
L000164 
L000165 For every particular TURNLOCK-owned progression occurrence:
L000166 
L000167 ```text
L000168 eligible
L000169 AND continuously remains eligible
L000170 AND continuously remains applicable under the governing workflow semantics
L000171 ```
L000172 
L000173 TURNLOCK MUST eventually advance that same occurrence.
L000174 
L000175 The obligation is occurrence-scoped.
L000176 
L000177 Progress of another occurrence does not discharge it.
L000178 
L000179 No competing progression is required for the obligation to exist.
L000180 
L000181 No causal classification of the delay is required.
L000182 
L000183 A behavior in which the occurrence remains continuously eligible and applicable
L000184 indefinitely but is never advanced is non-conforming, including a behavior in
L000185 which TURNLOCK performs no other progression.
L000186 
L000187 The causal qualifier from ADR-036:
L000188 
L000189 ```text
L000190 solely because TURNLOCK's own scheduling
L000191 continues to select other progression
L000192 ```
L000193 
L000194 does not govern the corrected product contract.
L000195 
L000196 The corrected obligation is:
L000197 
L000198 ```text
L000199 continuously eligible and applicable
L000200 → eventual advance of that occurrence
L000201 ```
L000202 
L000203 ## Invariant consequence
L000204 
L000205 No new invariant identity is introduced.
L000206 
L000207 `TL-INV-042 — Conditional orchestration-progress invariant` remains the stable
L000208 invariant identity.
L000209 
L000210 Its normative meaning is amended to require eventual advance of each particular
L000211 TURNLOCK-owned progression occurrence that remains continuously eligible and
L000212 applicable.
L000213 
L000214 `TL-INV-042` remains a liveness invariant.
L000215 
L000216 No change is made to the identity or classification of:
L000217 
L000218 ```text
L000219 TL-INV-004
L000220 TL-INV-008
L000221 TL-INV-018
L000222 TL-INV-027
L000223 ```
L000224 
L000225 ## Formal-traceability consequence
L000226 
L000227 `formal/verification.yaml` must add ADR-037 as governing authority for
L000228 `TL-INV-042`.
L000229 
L000230 The manifest must state explicitly that:
L000231 
L000232 ```text
L000233 continuously enabled and applicable occurrence
L000234 → eventual advance of that occurrence
L000235 ```
L000236 
L000237 and that no competing progress or scheduler-choice premise is required.
L000238 
L000239 No TLA+ property identifier, action, state variable, occurrence identity,
L000240 fairness formula, or TLC configuration is introduced by this ADR.
L000241 
L000242 ## Consequences
L000243 
L000244 * TURNLOCK cannot conform by indefinitely leaving continuously eligible and
L000245   applicable orchestration progression unadvanced.
L000246 * The obligation applies whether TURNLOCK is progressing other work or no other
L000247   work.
L000248 * Conformance does not require determining why an occurrence was delayed.
L000249 * Execution-resource completion remains distinct from engine progress.
L000250 * Universal workflow, region, invocation, or branch termination remains

L000033 # ADR-041: Establish TURNLOCK formal assurance architecture
L000034 
L000035 ## Context
L000036 
L000037 TURNLOCK has reached semantic closure far enough that executable formalization can
L000038 now be used to challenge the current semantic fixed point.
L000039 
L000040 ADR-015 already established that normative prose remains product authority, that
L000041 formalization should begin early, that formal traceability must be
L000042 machine-readable, that focused checks do not replace integrated behavioral
L000043 exploration, and that successful checker execution evidence is distinct from
L000044 planned formal coverage.
L000045 
L000046 Subsequent semantic work exposed a missing architectural layer in the original
L000047 direct shape:
L000048 
L000049 ```text
L000050 TL-INV
L000051   ↓
L000052 planned TLA+ property
L000053   ↓
L000054 TLC configuration
L000055   ↓
L000056 TLC result
L000057 ```
L000058 
L000059 That shape conflates normative provenance, assurance decomposition, mathematical
L000060 semantics, backend-specific realization, semantic correspondence review,
L000061 verification configuration, and verification evidence.
L000062 
L000063 TURNLOCK also requires the non-mechanical semantic boundaries in that chain to
L000064 be challenged adversarially rather than treated as implicit trust steps.
L000065 
L000066 At the same time, ADR-040 requires future abstraction extractability without
L000067 prematurely introducing a generic TURNLOCK, software-problem-solving, or SCOPE
L000068 IR.
L000069 
L000070 ## Discovery classification
L000071 
L000072 ```text
L000073 decision-required, resolved
L000074 ```
L000075 
L000076 The current normative product semantics do not themselves determine how formal
L000077 assurance artifacts, formal semantic authority, hostile review, projections,
L000078 verification mechanisms, or readiness gates must be organized.
L000079 
L000080 This ADR establishes that architecture without adding product behavior.
L000081 
L000082 ## Decision
L000083 
L000084 ### Product authority remains normative
L000085 
L000086 TURNLOCK product meaning remains owned by:
L000087 
L000088 ```text
L000089 docs/specification/turnlock-spec.md
L000090 +
L000091 accepted TURNLOCK ADRs
L000092 ```
L000093 
L000094 A formal representation MAY become canonical for formal semantics in a declared
L000095 formalized domain, but MUST NOT thereby become normative product authority.
L000096 
L000097 Formal models, assurance manifests, checkers, evidence records, Issues,
L000098 implementations, hostile reviewers, and harnesses MUST NOT resolve missing or
L000099 conflicting product semantics implicitly.
L000100 
L000101 Authority flows downward through the assurance system. Discoveries may flow
L000102 upward, but authority does not.
L000103 
L000104 ### TURNLOCK requires canonical formal semantics
L000105 
L000106 TURNLOCK SHALL maintain one canonical formal semantic representation for each
L000107 formally modeled semantic domain.
L000108 
L000109 For the current operational state/transition domain, the initial canonical
L000110 formal representation SHALL be the integrated TLA+ semantics.
L000111 
L000112 Conceptually:
L000113 
L000114 ```text
L000115 normative TURNLOCK semantics
L000116           ↓
L000117 semantic formalization
L000118           ↓
L000119 canonical formal semantics
L000120 (initially integrated TLA+)
L000121 ```
L000122 
L000123 `canonical` means the governed current formal-semantic baseline for the declared
L000124 domain and scope. It does not mean `normative`.
L000125 
L000126 No distinct backend-neutral TURNLOCK Formal IR is introduced by this decision.
L000127 
L000128 A future TURNLOCK-specific Formal IR requires a separate architectural decision
L000129 and is justified only when multiple current consumers require the same formal
L000130 semantics, or when a mechanically governed intermediate representation provides
L000131 a concrete assurance benefit greater than its additional translation,
L000132 projection, and common-mode trust surface.
L000133 
L000134 Any such future IR MUST be derived from demonstrated TURNLOCK needs and
L000135 formalization pressure rather than from speculative generalization.
L000136 
L000137 ### Required assurance claims are a separate assurance layer
L000138 
L000139 Normative invariants MUST NOT map directly to backend properties as the only
L000140 assurance decomposition.
L000141 
L000142 TURNLOCK SHALL maintain stable required assurance claims.
L000143 
L000144 A required assurance claim is the smallest evidentially coherent proposition
L000145 whose establishment is necessary to support a declared portion of accepted
L000146 TURNLOCK semantics.
L000147 
L000148 Required assurance claims:
L000149 
L000150 * record normative provenance;
L000151 * record assurance intent;
L000152 * may have more than one normative source;
L000153 * may divide one invariant into multiple evidentially distinct obligations;
L000154 * do not define TURNLOCK state variables, transitions, or execution semantics;
L000155 * do not form a second canonical formal-semantic IR.
L000156 
L000157 Claims whose purpose exists only because of a particular formal modeling
L000158 representation are supporting model properties, not automatically required
L000159 assurance claims.
L000160 
L000161 ### Assurance modality is distinct from assurance domain
L000162 
L000163 For behavioral formal assurance, the minimum logical modalities are:
L000164 
L000165 ```text
L000166 safety
L000167 reachability
L000168 liveness
L000169 ```
L000170 
L000171 Safety expresses universal preservation or exclusion.
L000172 
L000173 Reachability expresses positive possibility, capability, representability, or
L000174 existence.
L000175 
L000176 Liveness expresses eventual progression under an explicit premise.
L000177 
L000178 Conformance, architecture, semantic quality, developer experience, coverage, and
L000179 semantic correspondence are separate assurance dimensions and MUST NOT be
L000180 encoded by growing a compound logical-modality enum.
L000181 
L000182 ### Verification mechanism selection is obligation-first
L000183 
L000184 The required order is:
L000185 
L000186 ```text
L000187 required assurance claim
L000188       ↓
L000189 verification obligation
L000190       ↓
L000191 required assurance strength
L000192       ↓
L000193 verification mechanism
L000194 ```
L000195 
L000196 Backend choice MUST NOT define the assurance obligation retroactively.
L000197 
L000198 TLA+ is the initial canonical formal language for the current operational
L000199 state/transition domain.
L000200 
L000201 TLC is the initial justified bounded model-checking mechanism for integrated
L000202 state-space exploration, safety, reachability, and liveness.
L000203 
L000204 Additional checkers, deductive proof, Alloy, SMT, proof assistants,
L000205 model-based conformance, or other mechanisms require a concrete assurance need.
L000206 
L000207 Multiple mechanisms over the same formal semantics provide checker diversity.
L000208 
L000209 An independently authored formalization may provide semantic-interpretation
L000210 diversity.
L000211 
L000212 Those assurance functions MUST NOT be conflated.
L000213 
L000214 ### Formalization is not projection
L000215 
L000216 The relation:
L000217 
L000218 ```text
L000219 normative natural-language semantics
L000220             ↓
L000221 formal representation
L000222 ```
L000223 
L000224 is semantic formalization.
L000225 
L000226 A formal semantic projection exists only between formal semantic
L000227 representations.
L000228 
L000229 Every formal semantic projection MUST declare:
L000230 
L000231 * source representation;
L000232 * target representation;
L000233 * semantic domain;
L000234 * observations or claims for which preservation is asserted;
L000235 * assumptions;
L000236 * direction and limits of evidence transfer.
L000237 
L000238 Projection soundness is claim-relative or observation-relative.
L000239 
L000240 A global label such as `equivalent`, `over-approximation`, or
L000241 `under-approximation` MUST NOT be used beyond the observations for which the
L000242 relation is justified.
L000243 
L000244 For safety, a sound over-approximation may support lifting absence-of-
L000245 counterexample evidence while producing spurious target counterexamples.
L000246 
L000247 For positive reachability, a sound under-approximation may provide source-valid
L000248 witnesses while providing insufficient universal safety coverage.
L000249 
L000250 Liveness requires an explicit preservation argument for the relevant infinite
L000251 behavior, enabledness, stuttering, occurrence, scheduler, and fairness semantics.
L000252 Projection direction alone does not establish liveness soundness.
L000253 
L000254 The following relations are distinct:
L000255 
L000256 ```text
L000257 TL-INV → assurance claim
L000258 = assurance decomposition
L000259 
L000260 normative semantics → canonical formal semantics
L000261 = formalization
L000262 
L000263 canonical formal semantics → restricted checker configuration
L000264 = verification restriction / instantiation
L000265 
L000266 formal representation → derived formal representation
L000267 = formal semantic projection
L000268 
L000269 normative semantics → independently authored second formal model
L000270 = independent formalization
L000271 
L000272 canonical repository state → generated documentation
L000273 = repository projection
L000274 
L000275 formal model + configuration → checker result
L000276 = verification execution
L000277 ```
L000278 
L000279 Normative coverage, formal projection relation, finite checker bounds, and
L000280 evidence strength are orthogonal.
L000281 
L000282 ### Interacting operational semantics require integrated representation
L000283 
L000284 All formally modeled TURNLOCK semantics whose meanings can interact within one
L000285 valid execution MUST be jointly representable and exercisable in at least one
L000286 coherent behavioral model.
L000287 
L000288 The initial integrated TLA+ semantics is the integration backplane for the
L000289 operational domain.
L000290 
L000291 Focused verification MAY restrict constants, initial states, domains, bounds,
L000292 selected properties, or mechanisms where the restriction preserves the relevant
L000293 meaning.
L000294 
L000295 Focused verification MUST NOT redefine independent mini-semantics that can drift
L000296 from the integrated canonical semantics.
L000297 
L000298 An integrated model MAY be physically modular. Integration is semantic, not a
L000299 requirement for one monolithic file.
L000300 
L000301 Claims outside the behavioral state-machine domain may use other assurance
L000302 mechanisms but MUST remain connected through the common assurance graph.
L000303 
L000304 The governing rule is:
L000305 
L000306 ```text
L000307 integrate everything that semantically composes;
L000308 connect everything else through explicit assurance relations
L000309 ```
L000310 
L000311 ### Non-mechanical semantic boundaries require hostile review
L000312 
L000313 A non-mechanically-proven semantic correspondence MUST NOT be treated as a
L000314 silent trust step.
L000315 
L000316 Material semantic boundaries SHALL be subjected to explicit hostile review,
L000317 including where applicable:
L000318 
L000319 ```text
L000320 normative semantics → candidate canonical formal semantics
L000321 TL-INV → required assurance claims
L000322 required assurance claim ↔ backend property
L000323 formal projection preservation contract
L000324 verification-profile adequacy
L000325 evidence interpretation
L000326 ```
L000327 
L000328 The current hostile-review mechanism requires multiple independent frontier LLM
L000329 reviewers.
L000330 
L000331 Review is adversarial falsification, not majority voting.
L000332 
L000333 Reviewers must attempt to find:
L000334 
L000335 * semantic strengthening;
L000336 * semantic weakening;
L000337 * omitted valid behavior;
L000338 * invented behavior;
L000339 * collapsed normative distinctions;
L000340 * invented formal distinctions;
L000341 * hidden assumptions;
L000342 * wrong quantification;
L000343 * wrong occurrence scope;
L000344 * modality mismatch;
L000345 * vacuity;
L000346 * incomplete assurance coverage;
L000347 * alternative incompatible interpretations still permitted by authority;
L000348 * cross-feature interaction failure;
L000349 * incorrect evidence lifting.
L000350 
L000351 A material objection survives because its argument or counterexample survives
L000352 review, regardless of reviewer majority.
L000353 
L000354 A valid minority objection blocks acceptance until it is resolved or refuted.
L000355 
L000356 Hostile-review evidence MUST be durable and inspectable.
L000357 
L000358 The evidence MUST identify the exact reviewed artifacts, reviewers/models,
L000359 review protocol, findings, dispositions, and re-review relationship.
L000360 
L000361 Hostile review does not convert natural-language semantic correspondence into
L000362 mathematical proof.
L000363 
L000364 The strongest valid conclusion is bounded reviewed semantic correspondence under
L000365 the executed review protocol.
L000366 
L000367 ### `formal/verification.yaml` owns the formal-assurance graph
L000368 
L000369 `formal/verification.yaml` SHALL be the canonical machine-readable
L000370 formal-assurance and traceability graph.
L000371 
L000372 It SHALL own:
L000373 
L000374 * normative provenance;
L000375 * required assurance claims;
L000376 * assurance domains;
L000377 * behavioral modalities where applicable;
L000378 * formal coverage;
L000379 * residual assurance;
L000380 * formal-semantic domain bindings;
L000381 * required review classes;
L000382 * future backend realizations;
L000383 * required verification-profile relations;
L000384 * evidence contracts;
L000385 * reverse traceability.
L000386 
L000387 It MUST NOT define:
L000388 
L000389 * TURNLOCK product semantics;
L000390 * the canonical formal semantics themselves;
L000391 * a backend-neutral semantic IR;
L000392 * verification results;
L000393 * hostile-review results.
L000394 
L000395 Facts mechanically derivable from repository artifacts or evidence SHOULD be
L000396 derived rather than independently maintained as mutable status.
L000397 
L000398 In particular, existence of artifacts, binding resolution, current review
L000399 coverage, passing checker evidence, and current readiness state SHOULD be
L000400 derived where practical.
L000401 
L000402 Coverage and current evidence state are distinct.
L000403 
L000404 A partial formalization MUST retain explicit residual assurance rather than
L000405 allowing a checked subset to appear as complete invariant assurance.
L000406 
L000407 The upper assurance graph MUST remain sufficiently backend-independent that a
L000408 future separately justified canonical Formal IR could replace TLA+ as the
L000409 canonical semantic source without replacing stable normative provenance or
L000410 required assurance claims.
L000411 
L000412 ### Discoveries route by earliest unresolved cause
L000413 
L000414 A discovery is routed according to the earliest incorrect or underdetermined
L000415 link in the authority-and-assurance chain, not according to the tool that
L000416 detected it.
L000417 
L000418 If current normative authority does not uniquely determine behavior that a lower
L000419 layer would have to choose, the discovery is `decision-required` and belongs to
L000420 Product Semantics.
L000421 
L000422 If authoritative sources conflict or a derivation depends on an unstated
L000423 semantic assumption, the discovery is
L000424 `authority-conflict-or-uncertain`.
L000425 
L000426 Formal Architecture, Formal Verification, hostile review, implementation, and
L000427 conformance mechanisms MUST NOT resolve those cases implicitly.
L000428 
L000429 When normative authority is sufficient, the defect is corrected at the lowest
L000430 responsible downstream layer, including formalization, assurance decomposition,
L000431 claim/property correspondence, projection, verification configuration,
L000432 evidence integrity, implementation, or conformance.
L000433 
L000434 A downstream repair MUST NOT close a finding while a surviving upstream cause
L000435 can still explain it.
L000436 
L000437 A property established in a formal model does not become normative merely
L000438 because a checker establishes it.
L000439 
L000440 Promotion into normative TURNLOCK meaning requires either complete derivation
L000441 from existing authority or an explicit Product Semantics decision.
L000442 
L000443 ### Formal readiness is staged
L000444 
L000445 TURNLOCK SHALL distinguish three readiness gates.
L000446 
L000447 #### Gate A — Formal-Architecture-Ready
L000448 
L000449 Gate A authorizes creation of a candidate executable formal model.
L000450 
L000451 It does not declare that model semantically correct, canonical, or verified.
L000452 
L000453 Gate A requires:
L000454 
L000455 * accepted formal-assurance architecture;
L000456 * valid assurance metamodel;
L000457 * assurance coverage for every current `TL-INV-*`;
L000458 * required claims and modalities for the candidate operational domain;
L000459 * explicit residual assurance for partial coverage;
L000460 * explicit assurance domains for non-formal obligations;
L000461 * explicit intended operational semantic scope;
L000462 * interaction closure or justified non-distorting exclusions;
L000463 * no unresolved product decision that the candidate model would otherwise have
L000464   to choose;
L000465 * hostile-review protocol;
L000466 * discovery routing;
L000467 * repository integrity.
L000468 
L000469 Gate A does not require checker evidence.
L000470 
L000471 #### Gate B — Canonical-Formal-Semantics-Ready
L000472 
L000473 Gate B promotes an exact candidate formal artifact/version to the current
L000474 canonical formal semantics for its declared scope.
L000475 
L000476 Gate B requires:
L000477 
L000478 * hostile semantic review of the exact candidate;
L000479 * strengthening/weakening/omission/invention attacks;
L000480 * alternative-interpretation attacks;
L000481 * compositional attacks;
L000482 * disposition of every material finding;
L000483 * re-review after material changes;
L000484 * no surviving unresolved material semantic finding;
L000485 * non-vacuity or semantic-adequacy witnesses for represented mechanisms.
L000486 
L000487 Only Gate B authorizes the word `canonical` for that candidate revision.
L000488 
L000489 `canonical` still does not mean `normative`.
L000490 
L000491 #### Gate C — Formal-Verification-Ready
L000492 
L000493 Gate C authorizes checker executions to support assurance claims.
L000494 
L000495 Gate C requires:
L000496 
L000497 * actual backend property bindings;
L000498 * hostile claim/property correspondence review;
L000499 * adequate verification profiles;
L000500 * modality-appropriate safety/reachability/liveness treatment;
L000501 * explicit assumptions and finite bounds;
L000502 * exact artifact identity;
L000503 * mechanism-specific evidence contracts;
L000504 * evidence-lifting rules bounded by correspondence, coverage, projection,
L000505   assumptions, and run scope.
L000506 
L000507 The following states MUST remain distinct:
L000508 
L000509 ```text
L000510 candidate model exists
L000511         !=
L000512 candidate accepted as canonical formal semantics
L000513         !=
L000514 backend property mechanically checked
L000515         !=
L000516 required assurance claim supported
L000517         !=
L000518 TL-INV fully assured
L000519 ```
L000520 
L000521 ## Relationship to ADR-015
L000522 
L000523 This ADR amends ADR-015.
L000524 
L000525 ADR-015 remains authoritative for:
L000526 
L000527 * normative prose remaining product authority;
L000528 * early formalization as discovery and verification pressure;
L000529 * stable invariant identity;
L000530 * machine-readable traceability;
L000531 * separation of intended coverage from executed evidence;
L000532 * retention of integrated exploration in addition to focused checks.
L000533 
L000534 This ADR replaces ADR-015's overly direct effective assurance shape:
L000535 
L000536 ```text
L000537 TL-INV → TLA+ property → TLC configuration → TLC evidence
L000538 ```
L000539 
L000540 with an explicit architecture containing required assurance claims, canonical
L000541 formal semantics, hostile semantic review, typed evidence, and staged readiness.
L000542 
L000543 ADR-015's historical body is not edited.
L000544 
L000545 ## Relationship to ADR-040
L000546 
L000547 This ADR confirms ADR-040.
L000548 
L000549 The initial canonical formal semantics is TURNLOCK-specific integrated TLA+.
L000550 
L000551 No generic TURNLOCK IR, software-problem-solving IR, SCOPE IR, universal
L000552 problem graph, or universal cognition vocabulary is introduced.
L000553 
L000554 A future abstraction must be earned from demonstrated recurring structure.
L000555 
L000556 ## Invariant consequence
L000557 
L000558 No new `TL-INV-*` identity is introduced.
L000559 
L000560 No existing invariant is amended.

1. For every relevant armed Execution E, its only possible mutation of R is a single guarded, atomic CAS(R,P,T), without unconditional fallback, implicit multi-ref update, force-like bypass, other ref mutation, or replay; effects relevant beyond R are explicitly excluded by an independently accepted scoped dependency contract, or closure fails.
2. Exact identities: P != T and P is a strict ancestor of T; expected-old binds the exact predecessor commit, not just a tree, path, inferred Git configuration, or symbolic remote.
3. The observed R(t0) is exactly T by commit and tree SHA; t0 represents an actual trusted remote I/O occurrence with a positive observation/ordering contract, not just a reused content-addressed value.
4. Effective repository/ref, writer/capability, authoritative-ref governance binding, Git transport and protection are consistent for the same operation. Remote protection prevents non-fast-forward and deletion by all ordinary writers in the declared threat model, and continues to hold for subsequent relevant actions. An administrator or provider bypass is outside the existing proto-ring threat model and must not be silently assumed away if included in the targeted support claim.
5. All effect-capable historical armed Executions related to I are considered, INCLUDING prior uncertain Executions progression-superseded for ordinary campaign control. Restricting to M2.unresolvedExecutions alone is insufficient. Each is bound to exactly the qualified effect set; a later successor attempt cannot conceal an older in-flight operation.

Given R(t0)=T, P strictly precedes T, and all later authority transitions preserve T as ancestor-or-equal, R cannot become P in the declared threat model. An as-yet-unapplied CAS(P,T) by any covered E therefore cannot take effect on R after t0. This proves the absence of **future ref mutation by those executions**, not their historical outcome, global external side-effect absence, future ref equality with T, or perpetual governance integrity.

A proof that does not establish any assumption above returns NOT-ESTABLISHED; it is NEVER coerced to success, PNE, PC, or non-application.

## 4. Distinct state satisfaction obligation

Independently require a qualified observation of the exact T and exact binding to I, the currently applicable candidate and GateAQualification, the target's authoritative repository identity, its ref, the prepared successor projection, all required exact evidence, and a valid publication obligation. Tree-only equality or an ancestor/descendant X != T does not satisfy the first v1 lane.

Two distinct things must be represented: (a) EffectClosure(E, R, t0), and (b) PublicationStateSatisfied(I, T, t0). One does not imply the other. The full progression precondition is the conjunction plus current M2 admission predicates and complete covered-Execution closure.

This admits both histories H1 (E applied P→T; response lost) and H2 (another permitted writer applied identical T; E did not), without asserting which history occurred. The same proof must fail if the observation is fabricated, source identities do not match, a historical E may mutate by another route, or the remote protection/writer qualification cannot be established.

## 5. Candidate M2 authority transition (NOT ACCEPTED API)

Conceptual operation: AdmitPublicationStateSatisfactionV1. Proposed durable fact: PublicationProgressionClosureRef (names are provisional; no types are published or approved by this note).

In ONE authoritative StateRevision, gated by existing ownership-generation and expected-StateRevision fencing, M2 must:
- validate current I/WorkItem/current qualified candidate/current publication obligation, nonterminal semantic progression and lack of incompatible publication confirmation;
- validate trusted M7-B-provided effect-closure and state-satisfaction evidence for the COMPLETE covered-Execution set (including prior superseded effects);
- validate exactly scoped M8-B recovery-blocker disposition, and reject any other outstanding causal condition that would be disguised as resolved;
- atomically admit the immutable progression-closure fact, the exact newly distinguished publication-confirmation provenance, the published-view identity, one satisfaction disposition for the exact publication obligation, and disposition of **only** permitted exact pending recovery blocker(s);
- validate complete resulting M2 state before commit, or commit nothing.

The confirmation identity remains logically one per exact PublicationIntent, with no duplicate or incompatible confirmation. Provenance must explicitly distinguish direct-execution, pre-Arm already-current, and the proposed post-Arm state-satisfaction lane. Never manufacture a terminal Execution fact to reuse an existing route.

Following admission, covered E remain immutable, historically outcome-unknown, and ineligible for further campaign-effect authorization or active recovery; M2 snapshot derives this from the new explicit closure fact, NOT an invented terminal recovery resolution or an operator-replacement ExecutionProgressionSupersessionRef. No successor Execution is created. Current GI-65 and M2 unresolved reconstruction need explicit versioned amendment; GI-83's prohibition on the after-Arm already-current shortcut is preserved; GI-75/GI-82's no-unsafe-new-intent protection is not weakened.

M6 post-publication validation still occurs after confirmation. GATE-A-READY still requires all existing qualification, exact published-view, passing validation, no outstanding obligations/blockers, and terminality prerequisites. Neither this closure nor M2 publication confirmation alone can emit READY.

## 6. M8 and M1 interface

M8-A retains ownership of historical Execution reconciliation; do NOT add state satisfaction as a fake M8-A terminal result. The M7-B recovery port retains conservative pending for T under the current contract until the separate lane is accepted. M8-B alone qualifies the exact pending-policy-exhausted recovery blocker disposition from an accepted proof candidate; M2 admits it atomically. No arbitrary removal of unrelated blockers.

For v1, eligible closure may dispose zero or the exact applicable pending-policy-exhausted blocker(s), as supported by the accepted M8-B binding. No-recovery-capability, already terminal executor-domain indeterminacy/UNRESOLVABLE and incompatible terminal execution facts are OUT OF SCOPE for this first lane. Preserve historical blockers and dispositions. Fix missing/X reobservation classification separately.

M1 tests the new **read-only** state-satisfaction lane during the existing prior-session recovery barrier, before historical M8 polling for the eligible publication. If not positively established, fall back to the existing M8 recovery/blocking contract with no re-dispatch. No current six-observation schedule is silently replaced or claimed useful for this new lane.

## 7. Observation time and post-READY restrictions

The proposed publication claim is evidence of exact state **observed at t0**. It is NOT an assertion that R still equals T at M2's later SQLite commit or at every subsequent wall-clock moment. If another permitted writer advances T→V after t0, the no-future-P→T proof remains valid, but current exact equality with T need not. Any stronger atomic remote-and-SQLite/currentness guarantee requires a separately accepted mechanism and proof. The accepted Gate A readiness/validation scope must be reconciled explicitly with this observation-bound interpretation; no hidden clock/time freshness heuristic is permitted.

Crash cases: before M2 admission, reconstruct/revalidate rather than presuming admission; during M2 transaction all-or-none; after admitted confirmation, reconstruct from immutable M2 history and resume M6 without publication replay; after M6 before READY, resume terminal admission; after READY, no further campaign-state mutation. A late direct result for E never creates another confirmation or changes progression; optional out-of-band audit material is not retroactive M2 execution truth or a promise of post-READY storage.

## 8. Mandatory counterexamples / hostile review matrix

H1: E applied T, response lost; T observed → eligible if and only if all positive proof obligations hold, historical outcome remains UNKNOWN.
H2: third party installed exactly T, E did not; same observed state and same permissible progression conclusion; NEVER assign E success.
H3: E still in flight when T observed → prove its exact old-tip CAS cannot succeed subsequently; no retry.
H4: P still observed → no closure, possible E effect remains.
H5: X different from T, even if descendant of P → first lane must not satisfy I; classify read-only continuability independently.
H6: missing ref / unavailable read → no fabricated proof; evaluate governance faults and reobservation separately.
H7: T observed without qualified actual I/O receipt or with stale/reused observation → refuse.
H8: writer has protection bypass, ref protection not qualified, or target identity mismatched → refuse.
H9: historical superseded E1 and live E2 both armed → require positive coverage of BOTH effect sets; never drop E1 because it vanished from unresolvedExecutions.
H10: T→V after qualified observation, before M2 admission → test exact observation-bound semantics and old-tip effect closure; no claim R=T at admission.
H11: direct applied/not-applied and pre-Arm already-current → exact existing routes preserved, no new lane.
H12: pending blocker, unrelated blocker, terminal UNRESOLVABLE, crash and late E result → test disposition boundaries, restart invariants, no second push and no post-READY M2 mutation.
H13: E can cause another relevant external effect despite CAS ref failure → REFUSE closure until those effects are positively handled.
H14: explicit counterexample to remote monotonicity (authorized bypass returns to P) → closure proof is INVALID under that threat model, not a mere warning.
H15: no valid new proof arises during repeated M8 polling → never turn elapsed time/identical observations into PC, PNE, or READY.

## 9. Accepted-authority and implementation gates

This proposal DOES NOT unilaterally ratify a controller semantic change. Before acceptance:
1. Complete the upstream source-to-necessity and publication-as-readiness trace required by #78, and determine whether an accepted ADR amendment is necessary.
2. Run a NEW independent, adversarial, source-pinned review of this precise candidate against NIB-S, M7-B, M8-A/B, M2 mutation/snapshot, M1, proto-ring ARM, and relevant accepted ADRs. Prior PR #80 review predates the corrected NIB-S/M7-B; prior DeepSeek #87 review attempts did not complete. Do not count this author's reasoning or those failed attempts as independent qualification. Preserve every finding, exact cited source, challenged assumption, model/transport identity and receipt; source drift requires a new review identity.
3. Architect must adjudicate every material finding and settle all unresolved authority conflicts (including I36, missing/X) through the appropriate owner, without treating issue comments as technical authority.
4. After ratification, revise and synchronize NIB-S, M7-B, M8-B, M2 mutation/snapshot/persistence, M1 and consumed version pins; make the future NIB-T cases exact. Respect native #87/#90 work dependency and #32/#33 distinct reviews.
5. Qualify Git DC + effective target/writer/observation/monotonicity through #88/#89/#91; no real protected main-ref testing or GREEN before qualified evidence.
6. Only then revisit whether six M8 observations and the 31-second backoff are justified; avoid changing policy based merely on the new architectural candidate.

**Current disposition:** D1 remains LOCKED decision-required; all proposed new types, transition and tests are candidate design only. #87 remains OPEN. Nothing here is Gate A formal proof, hostile-review evidence, a revised NIB, a TURNLOCK Product Intent change or source-code implementation.
