## Architect-side adversarial pre-review — proposal v0.1.0 (NOT independent reviewer evidence)

**Frozen target:** [GA-PUBLICATION-STATE-SATISFACTION-ADJUDICATION-v0.1.0](https://github.com/fanilosendrison/turnlock-rust/issues/87#issuecomment-6254606404), comment 6254606404, UTF-8 body SHA-256 `df6c51ada37e9ca65e4ccb2924b4db9a9cd2ca3fe8226022f36c204a8a3df429` (17,371 bytes). Repository baseline `61e9dc36c4cff133be4437f4898a20a0d2f800f6`.

**Evidence status:** author-side falsification/contract confrontation only; **NO external independent reviewer executed**, no second-model coverage, no accepted adjudication or NIB decision. This note preserves new candidate findings rather than claiming Issue closure, authority, Gate A evidence or GREEN.

### PFR-01 — Same-session lost publication response has no specified state-satisfaction branch

**Category:** unspecified-behavior / material liveness. Proposed §6 tests state satisfaction only in `M1`'s "existing prior-session recovery barrier" before M8. But current [M1 §18.3, L781–794](https://github.com/fanilosendrison/turnlock-rust/blob/61e9dc36c4cff133be4437f4898a20a0d2f800f6/docs/formal/nib-m-gate-a-orchestrator.md#L781-L794) routes *same-session* uncertain `publish_conditionally` immediately into M8. Under [M7-B §23.1, L1052–1079](https://github.com/fanilosendrison/turnlock-rust/blob/61e9dc36c4cff133be4437f4898a20a0d2f800f6/docs/formal/nib-m-gate-a-repository-control-publication-remote-recovery.md#L1052-L1079), observing T still yields pending. Therefore H1 may still exhaust M8 and create an OAR before the proposed new lane ever runs; no guaranteed in-run progression. **Review demand:** explicitly place the new observational admission attempt in both current-session uncertainty handling and restart, preserving one-CAS/no-replay and source-owned authority.

### PFR-02 — Operator replacement before recovery can hide the original armed effect and strand an unarmed successor

**Category:** concrete liveness counterexample. Current [M1 resume §7.2, L245–255](https://github.com/fanilosendrison/turnlock-rust/blob/61e9dc36c4cff133be4437f4898a20a0d2f800f6/docs/formal/nib-m-gate-a-orchestrator.md#L245-L255) admits an operator-resolution effect **before** the recovery barrier. Current [M2 mutation §15, L1999–2111](https://github.com/fanilosendrison/turnlock-rust/blob/61e9dc36c4cff133be4437f4898a20a0d2f800f6/docs/formal/nib-m-gate-a-campaign-state-mutation-execution.md#L1999-L2111) creates a successor `E2`, progression-superseding uncertain `E1`. Current [M2 snapshot §6, L764–794](https://github.com/fanilosendrison/turnlock-rust/blob/61e9dc36c4cff133be4437f4898a20a0d2f800f6/docs/formal/nib-m-gate-a-campaign-state-snapshot-integrity.md#L764-L794) removes superseded `E1` from `unresolvedExecutions`; newly authorized, unarmed `E2` is not unresolved either. M1's recovery barrier is fed exactly that list ([M1 §8, L276–285](https://github.com/fanilosendrison/turnlock-rust/blob/61e9dc36c4cff133be4437f4898a20a0d2f800f6/docs/formal/nib-m-gate-a-orchestrator.md#L276-L285)). Thus a T observation and complete safety proof might never be attempted; ordinary pre-Arm `E2` against old P is stale ([M7-B §15, L676–709](https://github.com/fanilosendrison/turnlock-rust/blob/61e9dc36c4cff133be4437f4898a20a0d2f800f6/docs/formal/nib-m-gate-a-repository-control-publication-remote-recovery.md#L676-L709)). **Review demand:** define admission with historical superseded E1 + current unarmed E2, and choose explicit ordering/semantics of operator-resolution ingestion versus state-satisfaction observation. No reinterpretation of operator supersession as effect proof.

### PFR-03 — The complete effect-risk set is not an accepted exact M2 projection

**Category:** evidence/authority gap. Proposed §3 says every relevant armed E, including already superseded executions, must be considered. But current M2 snapshot's active recovery projection deliberately removes those executions ([§6, L764–794](https://github.com/fanilosendrison/turnlock-rust/blob/61e9dc36c4cff133be4437f4898a20a0d2f800f6/docs/formal/nib-m-gate-a-campaign-state-snapshot-integrity.md#L764-L794)). The proposal provides no exact candidate-selection rule, ordinal/intent scope, immutable history accessor, completeness witness or identity for *all effect-capable* E. An implementer could mistakenly treat the current unresolved list as complete. **Review demand:** define an exact M2-owned authoritative history query for the closed relevant effect set, separately identifying (a) armed unknown, (b) already terminal proven safe, (c) progression-superseded unknown, (d) authorized but unarmed executions; prove each is accounted for and no excluded E can still change R. Add H9 + operator-resolution-before-recovery adversarial cases.

### PFR-04 — Exact proposal bytes are not currently ingestible as a first-class Review Lab Git source

**Category:** review-evidence acquisition blocker, not a demonstrated product flaw. The proposal itself is a mutable GitHub issue comment rather than a blob in `turnlock-rust@61e9dc36`. The [Review Lab PR #3](https://github.com/fanilosendrison/turnlock-review-lab/pull/3) pinned pilot `review_sources.py` admits only Git-commit source files under fixed program identities; its Codex/DeepSeek validators bind source-line citations to those Git snapshots. Running an existing `issue78-pr80` pilot unmodified would **not** review this decision subject or validate citations to the proposed new clauses. **Review demand:** in a disposable Review Lab scratch copy, create a *new* source- and comment-hash-bound program identity; seal exact proposal UTF-8 bytes from comment ID 6254606404 into both packet source manifests with independently checked SHA, physical lines and quotes; preserve all original complete Git source blobs at exact pinned baseline. Never mutate Review Lab PR #3, do not silently truncate, and never call reused model receipts or previous failed DeepSeek executions an independent review.

### Known upstream constraints still active (not new findings)

- M2's [I36](https://github.com/fanilosendrison/turnlock-rust/blob/61e9dc36c4cff133be4437f4898a20a0d2f800f6/docs/formal/nib-m-gate-a-campaign-state-snapshot-integrity.md#L1619-L1624) contradicts its existing `already-current` branch; defer authority reconciliation to #90.
- M7-B's missing/X `unknown` classification and safe read-only reobservation mismatch remains for #87 with #88/#91.
- The future monotonicity and effect-set safety argument is conditional on a *qualified* actual writer, CAS, remote observation-ordering semantics, and declared proto-ring threat model; #88/#89/#91 cannot be bypassed with observed target bytes.

**Disposition:** PFR-01/PFR-02 are counterexamples to completeness of the v0.1.0 progression routing; PFR-03 is a required exact history/effect-set closure obligation; PFR-04 blocks honest claims of independent review by the unmodified Review Lab pilot. None of these is accepted authority without separate architect adjudication. Retain #87 open, preserve original v0.1.0 review subject unchanged, and require a new independently executed source-pinned review before ratification.

# Proposed architecture adjudication v0.2.0 — Gate A post-Arm state-oriented publication satisfaction

**Decision subject:** `GA-PUBLICATION-STATE-SATISFACTION-ADJUDICATION-v0.2.0`  
**Status:** `PROPOSED / LOCKED / SOURCE-PINNED REVIEW REQUIRED`. This is an architect-authored *controller construction decision candidate*, not an accepted ADR, NIB, Git Dependency Contract, verified safety theorem, implementation instruction, full hostile review, or Gate A evidence.  
**Exact Turnlock-Rust source:** `61e9dc36c4cff133be4437f4898a20a0d2f800f6`. Relevant proto-ring ARM contract: `dc8e04c758fb40867dc7ad23f019843413fc4a1b`.  
**Predecessor decision subject:** [v0.1.0, comment 6254606404](https://github.com/fanilosendrison/turnlock-rust/issues/87#issuecomment-6254606404) (17,371 UTF-8 bytes; SHA-256 `df6c51ada37e9ca65e4ccb2924b4db9a9cd2ca3fe8226022f36c204a8a3df429`).  
**Review input:** User-supplied Issue #87 execution report: ONE Codex architecture packet with 22 physically anchored, UNADJUDICATED hypotheses; Codex authority capacity failure, DeepSeek architecture network failure, DeepSeek authority incomplete. Neither two-model review nor complete two-packet review exists. Author-side triage below is NOT an independent reviewer result.  
**Work routing:** primary #87; upstream publication/readiness authority #78, publication target/writer #88, observation occurrence/pre-Arm #89, cross-module synchronization #90, qualified Git DC #91, future NIB-T #32 and full-pack hostile review #33. No status or dependency graph change authorized by this proposal.

## 1. What is selected, and what remains locked

**Selected for adversarial review (not yet accepted):** post-Arm publication may satisfy the *exact existing PublicationIntent I* based on a qualified observed external target state and a separate proof that all relevant already-armed publication Executions have no remaining capacity to alter the authorized ref in the declared threat model, WITHOUT attributing the historical effect to any one Execution. The existing direct-execution and pre-Arm already-current confirmation routes remain disjoint.

Independent propositions (none aliases another):

```text
HistoricalOutcome(E) = unknown | positively-proven terminal
ObservedState(R,t0) = exact T | other
ResidualRefEffectClosed(E,R,t0) = positively established | NOT_ESTABLISHED
PublicationObligationSatisfied(I) = admitted by M2 | not admitted
```

`ObservedState=exact T` never implies `PROVEN-COMPLETED(E)`, `PROVEN-NOT-EXECUTED(E)`, `PublicationNonApplicationRef`, or even `ResidualRefEffectClosed(E)` on its own. An evidence-only progression cut is NOT an Execution terminal result and is NOT `ExecutionProgressionSupersessionRef` (that existing form requires an operator and successor Execution).

**First realization scope:** one current applicable I for one exact authoritative ref, strict P≠T fast-forward, one qualified observed *exact* T (commit SHA AND tree SHA), and a complete positively established ref-effect closure. No state-equivalent descendant X, no `already-current` reuse after Arm, no second CAS, no generic repository-policy implementation inside Turnlock.

**Locked external-outcome question:** source NIB-S §29/§31 currently requires a publication confirmation and bound post-publication validation for runner `GATE-A-READY`; upstream accepted ADR-041 and ADR-045 do not independently prove that historical operation authorship is required, nor that any historical observation of T always suffices for *current* repository readiness. #78 must adjudicate this scope explicitly before acceptance. An Issue comment is not normative authority; a changing historical assumption about the remote must never be smuggled into an ADR or TLC result.

## 2. Exact M2-owned historical risk-set selection (fixes F002/F003/F004)

Introduce a **candidate read-side coherent-revision projection**, `LoadPublicationEffectHistoryView(I)`, owned solely by M2 snapshot/history, not by M8 or M7. It is a proposal; no such API is currently accepted. It must be reconstructed inside ONE M2 read transaction at an exact StateRevision V and must include exact current I, its co-admitted WorkItem W(I), candidate/qualification, publication obligation, prior/current publication-intent chain for the SAME exact ref, every historical W(I) Execution and its chronological creation basis, Arm (if any), direct terminal admission, recovery resolution, pending evidence, progression supersession, nonapplication fact and outstanding blocker identities. A per-Execution series of unrelated snapshots is not a coherent replacement.

Deterministic `riskSet(I,V)`: enumerate **all** historical Executions of W(I), never only `unresolvedExecutions`, in ascending `attemptOrdinal` (tie is integrity failure). Independently reject a previously applicable publication intent on the same ref if its earlier armed Executions lack the exact safe disposition already required by GI-82/I62. Reject inconsistent or ambiguous WorkItem, ref or intent binding. Categorize every E in W(I), using positive authoritative history, as exactly one of:

* `NOT_ARMED`: no Arm fact. Cannot have initiated this ref mutation; must remain unarmable upon atomic satisfaction of O, including current authorized-but-unarmed replacement E2. Do not omit it from the history view.
* `POSITIVE_SAFE_TERMINAL`: exact terminal `PROVEN-NOT-EXECUTED` or authoritative direct `PublicationNonApplicationRef` for that E. It already supplies a distinct positive safe-effect disposition; retain original provenance.
* `ARMED_HISTORICALLY_UNKNOWN`: durable Arm, no directly admitted terminal effect truth, no terminal recovery resolution, with or without pending witness or an `ExecutionProgressionSupersessionRef`. **Every such E is in the closure-risk set**, including E1 superseded by operator-authorized E2. Require a complete exact guarded-mutation proof for EACH.
* `OTHER_TERMINAL_OR_CONFLICT`: captured/direct or recovered applied result awaiting ordinary publication qualification; terminal technical failure not proven non-applying; terminal `UNRESOLVABLE`; incompatible/contradictory history or an already-confirmed intent. **Do not admit this first state-satisfaction lane**: preserve existing direct/recovery/operator pathways or fail integrity as appropriate.

Require at least one `ARMED_HISTORICALLY_UNKNOWN` and require no `OTHER_TERMINAL_OR_CONFLICT` position. Positive-safe past attempts may coexist with a still-unknown E; a direct known outcome for the current attempt never gets silently converted into unknown. A current authorized-but-unarmed E2 is permitted only when the earlier unknown E1 is covered; its future Arm is atomically prevented by satisfying O and the existing M2 Arm guard requiring an outstanding obligation.

The projection must retain every included E identity, exact status, source revision, evidence, Arm binding and original operation (no reconstructed Git meaning from `ExecutionId`). Compute `riskSetDigest` from one M0-canonical typed projection ordered exactly as above; retain V and the immutable projection ArtifactRef as evidence. Reconstruct it identically after crash. An omitted armed E, a wrong alternate CAS, a different publication target or a non-coherent source revision invalidates the proposal.

`riskSet` is a finite, **run-local authorized-effect enumeration**, not an assertion that the runner owns every other repository writer or every other run. External writers and protection bypass belong to the declared trust/environment model. If the external environment violates that model, refuse the closure claim in that support profile.

## 3. Positive read-occurrence causality (fixes F005 and F007)

A content-addressed `GateAPublicationTargetObservationV1` can have identical bytes across reads and does **not** prove a fresh post-Arm I/O occurrence. The candidate must require a new typed, single-use **M2-scoped observation attempt Q**, conceptually `BeginPublicationStateObservationAttempt(I,V,riskSetDigest)`, committed after the relevant durable Arms and before external read. Q binds I, W, R, every covered E, current candidate/qualification, expected target T, effective ownership generation and the exact coherent M2 risk-set revision. It authorizes READ-ONLY evidence acquisition, not publication. An unconsumed older Q is superseded by the newest authorized Q for the same I; after a crash, a fresh Q is needed before a new read.

The selected Git DC must return one qualified **actual remote read occurrence receipt** for Q, with exact request/response identity and verified provider/ref binding, plus a positive exact-T target observation. A local nonce, timestamp, cached data, byte equality or SHA-256 alone is not a remote-read witness. It must attest a read that can be ordered after Q and for which the returned authoritative-ref value is valid at a defined remote observation linearization point t0; if such read semantics cannot be qualified, the lane is UNSUPPORTED/NOT_ESTABLISHED. A provider need not offer a cryptographic timestamp if a separately qualified trusted transport occurrence contract establishes the actual I/O and ordering; name that trust explicitly.

M2's final state-satisfaction admission verifies Q is current, single-use, not superseded, tied to the exact same history/projection/ownership, and that NO later Armed Execution or state revision invalidated its scope. It consumes Q atomically. Stale Q/changed history requires a new attempt and qualified read; no time-window heuristic. Opening Q may be permitted despite its exact recoverable pending blocker because it is read-only; doing so neither disposes nor ignores that blocker.

The concrete schema/version and trust boundary must be ratified with #89/#91. This section is an **obligation**, not a claim that these facilities already exist.

## 4. Residual-effect closure theorem and its limits (F013/F014/F015)

Let P be the strict predecessor of T; `P ≺ T`. Each included historically unknown E is bound to one and ONLY one authorized ref mutation `atomic-CAS(R,P,T)` (no unconditional fallback, ref deletion, multi-target mutation, retry, hidden alternate ref, or force-like bypass). The effective writer/transport and target are independently qualified (#88/#91). At the trusted remote-read linearization point t0: `R(t0)=T` exactly.

The shared proto-ring ARM contract plus the effective consumer/provider binding must guarantee *for the entire relevant future-effect interval in the declared threat model* that accepted ordinary-writer updates of R cannot perform non-fast-forward transitions or deletion. Under this **environmental guarantee**, all later R states have T as ancestor-or-equal, hence cannot equal strict ancestor P, hence any future `CAS(P,T)` by a covered E fails. This proves only the **absence of a future mutation of R by those E** after t0; it does NOT prove historical execution attribution, current R=T at an arbitrary later time, or safety of unrelated external effects.

The lifetime monotonicity assumption is a declared **environmental support guarantee**, not a finite fact proved forever by a single ruleset GET, an imagined lease or a poll. Provider/admin bypass, protection reconfiguration and destructive rewrite remain excluded by the existing proto-ring ARM threat model; if the desired product support claim includes them, this proof is insufficient and the case must be rejected or separately supported. Never fabricate a durable protection lease from a snapshot.

Only the effect scope that can invalidate the *Gate A publication obligation* may be declared closed. If the selected transport can produce any additional effect that could alter the authoritative ref, invalidate the evidence or compromise the publication assertion, it must be positively included and proven inert or the closure MUST fail. No global absence of webhook, deployment, telemetry or other unrelated downstream effect is asserted. Relevance itself requires a closed owning-executor/dependency contract, not agent judgment at runtime.

A missing qualified CAS, writer binding, occurrence receipt, environmental guarantee, complete risk set, or bounded effect scope means `NOT_ESTABLISHED`. It is never a synthetic terminal recovery, `PNE`, `PC`, or `not-applied`.

## 5. Distinct M7-B candidate producer (fixes F022)

Add a **separate observational producer** after construction acceptance, conceptually:

```text
qualify_publication_state_satisfaction({
  observationAttemptQ,
  exactCoherentRiskView,
  exactTransportObservationReceipt,
  exactM2BoundIntentCandidateQualification,
  qualifiedGovernanceAndWriterAndCASProfile
}) -> one of:
    ESTABLISHED {
      riskSetEvidence,
      effectClosureEvidence,
      stateSatisfactionEvidence,
      observationOccurrenceEvidence,
      exactPositiveBasisArtifacts
    }
    NOT_ESTABLISHED { boundedReason, exactAvailableEvidence }
    DEPENDENCY_OR_INTEGRITY_FAILURE
```

`NOT_ESTABLISHED` neither modifies authoritative state nor claims the publication failed; only the existing M8 recovery/operational route then applies. The two proof dimensions are always separately typed. It never invokes `conditionalUpdatePublicationTarget`, returns `CapturedExecutionResult`, constructs a new historical `ExecutionRecoveryObservation.kind=terminal`, or clears a blocker. * the singleton `[B_pending(E_current).blockerId]`, after exact verification of runId, W, E, obligation ID, blocker cause, currentness and linkage to the admitted closure proof.

Prior operator-disposed E1 blockers remain historical and MUST NOT be disposed again. If an unrelated producer blocker or another outstanding recovery-causal blocker exists, preserve it; if its causal condition is incompatible with the proposed closure, reject the closure rather than silently override it. Terminal `UNRESOLVABLE`, `no-recovery-capability` and `executor-domain-indeterminacy` cases are outside this lane.

1. I/W/O/C/qualification are the exact currently projected applicable identities; P≠T; current run nonterminal; O outstanding and not previously disposed; no prior confirmation for I.

Consequence: E1 might be superseded and E2 authorized/unarmed; §2/§7 explicitly support this case.

```text
reload coherent M2 publication-effect history (includes superseded E1)
if candidate scope applies and no direct/terminal conflicting lane is authoritative:

    if positive: M8-B validate optional blocker disposition;

```

The satisfaction attempt is required (a) immediately after same-session M7 uncertainty admission and before its normal M8 path, (b) after resume ownership + optional operator-resolution ingestion, even if `unresolvedExecutions=[]`, (c) before Arm of any authorized-unarmed publication E2, and (d) following a completed finite M8 repository-pending episode **before** committing a pending-exhaustion blocker/OAR, with one fresh qualified read. Existing `resume-reconciliation` likewise re-enters these gates. At most one new read-only satisfaction probe is initiated per distinct M1 triggering decision/state revision; no infinite automatic recheck loop from `NOT_ESTABLISHED`. Existing six-read M8 policy and 31-second deliberate wait budget are unchanged in this candidate; a later policy revision may optimize them after the new evidence path is accepted.

If T appears only transiently during M8's intermediate polling and no qualified exact-T observation survives the final satisfaction probe, the v1 lane may still block; universal liveness is NOT claimed. If T remains at final probe, the new path can complete. Do not mine M8's generic trace and silently reinterpret historical execution completion. A future optimized shared observation feed requires its own explicit versioned contract.

`t0` is the linearization point of the positive remote read. **Selected v0.2 candidate external assertion:** runner `GATE-A-READY` witnesses an exact qualified candidate T that was observed as published authority at a qualified observation point, together with its bound isolated representation and passing post-publication validation. It does not continuously monitor the mutable ref and does not promise it never advanced to V. No hidden distributed transaction or timestamp freshness window is claimed. If upstream #78 determines that READY MUST assert present-time current repository authority (rather than a bounded verified publication occurrence), this candidate is **NOT sufficient** and must remain locked until a new remote/M2 coordination requirement is decided. This is a **decision gate**, not a proof derived from ADR-041/045.

M6 keeps its exact `PublishedRepositoryViewRef` validation and cannot promote a mutable path or an unbound current ref to assurance. If T→V makes the currently designated repository Gate A readiness false under accepted authority, do not hide that conflict behind the historical observation: it must be explicitly resolved by #78 before publishing this candidate as accepted construction authority.

## 10. Crash, replay, anti-resurrection, terminality

* Crash before Q: no authorization inferred from stale observation; run normal fresh derivation.
* Crash after Q before remote read/closure: Q remains historical; generate fresh Q to retry READ-ONLY observation. Never reuse a receipt as new occurrence.

* Crash during M2 commit: closure, provenance, confirmation, obligation and blocker disposition are all admitted in one revision or none.

* Crash after passing M6 before terminal readiness: re-derive from exact retained evidence and admit READY once.
* Crash after READY: no M2 mutation; READ-only history/audit permitted under existing authority.
* Old E1 result arrives after operator supersession or intent closure: reject progression-bearing M2 mutation; no second confirmation, no historical reclassification, no resurrection of active recovery. Preserve optional evidence outside campaign progression only if independently authorized.

One surviving material counterexample blocks approval. An empty finding set is not proof of correspondence or implementation readiness.

## 12. Disposition of 22 scoped Codex architecture hypotheses

Review completeness: only one validated Codex architecture packet. The authority packet and a distinct-provider completed review are still missing. These proposed resolutions require a NEW review identity and source-pinned packet set, not retry or relabeling of the three failed prior attempts.

# #78 — Proposed architect disposition: exact meaning and temporal scope of runner GATE-A-READY

**Disposition identity:** `GA-RUNNER-READY-SEMANTIC-BOUNDARY-v0.1.0`  
**Status:** `ARCHITECT SELECTION / REPOSITORY RATIFICATION PENDING`. This is a proposed **controller construction/outcome interpretation**, not an accepted ADR, modification of ADR-041/045, NIB-S or Product Intent, formal verification result, runtime qualification or permission to enter GREEN.  
**Exact Turnlock-Rust baseline:** `61e9dc36c4cff133be4437f4898a20a0d2f800f6`.  
**Corresponding architectural recovery proposal:** #87 [post-Arm state satisfaction v0.2.0](https://github.com/fanilosendrison/turnlock-rust/issues/87#issuecomment-6261289248).  
**Primary owner of this publication-versus-readiness decision:** #78; the recovery transition belongs to #87. No WorkItem, Issue/Project state, PR, branch, governing ADR or NIB is changed by this comment.

## 1. Authority trace — three different propositions

**Formal Gate A / Formal-Architecture-Ready** is governed by [ADR-041 Gate A](https://github.com/fanilosendrison/turnlock-rust/blob/61e9dc36c4cff133be4437f4898a20a0d2f800f6/docs/adr/adr-041-establish-turnlock-formal-assurance-architecture.md#L443-L469): authority to author a candidate formal model conditional on current assurance architecture, claims/coverage, hostile review, discovery routing and repository integrity. Its successful evaluation is a *derived verdict over current governed repository evidence*, not a fact conferred by a prior runner result. ADR-041 does **not** expressly require this particular campaign process to publish Git or identify which actor advanced the remote ref.

**GateAQualification** is the controller's mechanical qualification of an exact immutable CandidateRevision, selected campaigns, exact subject S and protocol P under NIB-S/M6. It is not a claim that this candidate is the current remote repository authority.

**Runner `GATE-A-READY`** is a terminal result of one `GateARun`. [ADR-045 external outcomes](https://github.com/fanilosendrison/turnlock-rust/blob/61e9dc36c4cff133be4437f4898a20a0d2f800f6/docs/adr/adr-045-bind-gate-a-campaigns-to-versioned-review-protocol-and-derived-evidence.md#L541-L552) establishes exactly `GATE-A-READY`, `DECISION-REQUIRED`, `OPERATOR-ACTION-REQUIRED`, but does not itself select a Git publication algorithm. [NIB-S §29](https://github.com/fanilosendrison/turnlock-rust/blob/61e9dc36c4cff133be4437f4898a20a0d2f800f6/docs/formal/nib-s-gate-a-campaign-runner.md#L8314-L8329), [§31](https://github.com/fanilosendrison/turnlock-rust/blob/61e9dc36c4cff133be4437f4898a20a0d2f800f6/docs/formal/nib-s-gate-a-campaign-runner.md#L8594-L8627), GI-40 and [M2 ready admission](https://github.com/fanilosendrison/turnlock-rust/blob/61e9dc36c4cff133be4437f4898a20a0d2f800f6/docs/formal/nib-m-gate-a-campaign-state-mutation-execution.md#L2777-L2797) select a stronger **end-to-end runner v1 completion policy**: exact candidate qualified, its authorized representation confirmed as published, and the bound immutable published representation mechanically validated. This is a controller realization choice, not a newly discovered TURNLOCK product invariant. The [published M7/proto-ring responsibility audit §4](https://github.com/fanilosendrison/turnlock-rust/blob/61e9dc36c4cff133be4437f4898a20a0d2f800f6/docs/formal/gate-a-m7-proto-ring-responsibility-audit.md#L77-L110) records exactly this distinction.

**Traceability result:** publication-before-**runner**-READY is an explicit stronger v1 construction policy; remote publication by the campaign engine itself is **not uniquely derived** from ADR-041 or ADR-045. Do NOT silently claim otherwise. The review/qualification engine may be separated from a qualified publisher in a future realization, while preserving the exact end-to-end runner result. `GateAQualification`, proto-ring `Repository Integrity PASS`, formal Gate A of the currently governed repository, and terminal runner `GATE-A-READY` are not interchangeable.

## 2. Selected candidate meaning of runner GATE-A-READY

Select **exact-artifact, observation-bound run completion**, not a continuous mutable-ref-currentness assertion.

For one `GateARun` on exact target ref R and exact publication intent I with successor commit/tree T, terminal `GATE-A-READY` asserts that immutable authoritative run history proves all of:
1. The exact CandidateRevision C and its permitted review/qualification evidence were valid for the exact applicable semantic subject S and review protocol P, and a GateAQualification was admitted for C.
2. Exact T is the authorized immutable Git representation of C for I, including commit SHA, tree SHA, target identity, ancestry evidence and material identity.
3. A qualified **positive remote observation occurrence** establishes that the designated authoritative ref R **equaled exact T at a particular qualified observation linearization point `t_pub`**. This must be genuinely observed; content-addressed bytes alone are not an I/O occurrence.
4. An exact PublishedRepositoryViewRef for T was reconstructed/materialized and passed M6 post-publication validation; its passing fact is durably bound to the same C, qualification, confirmation, R and T.
5. M2 admitted the unique exact publication confirmation with the exact publication-obligation satisfaction and the passing validation, no outstanding obligations/blockers and no semantic terminal prohibition, before its terminal Gate A ready fact; no new campaign mutation follows READY.

The causal order must hold: qualification of C; publication/observation witness `t_pub`; positive validation of the immutable published T; M2 terminal-ready admission. These are logical causal relations, **not** timestamps that create an artificial freshness window or an atomic GitHub/SQLite distributed transaction.

**Non-assertions (mandatory):**
- Runner READY does NOT mean that R still equals T when M2 commits READY, when the CLI returns, or when a consumer later reads the result.
- Runner READY does NOT mean the currently governed repository is still Formal-Architecture-Ready after subsequent repository changes. That predicate must be freshly derived from its current repository authority/evidence, respecting current S/P and all other relevant repository conditions.
- Runner READY does NOT establish perpetual provider protection, pre-publication Authoritative State Admission, future repository correctness, correctness of the candidate executable formal model, or formal checker evidence.
- Runner READY does NOT assert that a particular armed Execution E historically performed the mutation, unless separate independent E-specific terminal proof exists.

The accepted existing `GateAReadyResult` already binds runId, candidate, semantic subject, protocol, exact qualification and `PublicationConfirmationRef`. New provenance must make the observation time **logical occurrence identity** and producer branch unambiguous within the authoritative proof history, never add a mutable "open-now/current-ref" boolean to the terminal fact.

## 3. Concrete temporal counterexample: T then V

```text
time t_pub: remote R == T; T matches exact qualified C
time t_val: isolated bound PublishedRepositoryViewRef(T) passes M6
time t_ready: M2 commits runner GATE-A-READY for that run
meanwhile: another ordinary writer may have advanced R: T → V
```

Under the selected meaning, runner READY still truthfully attests the exact **T publication occurrence + subsequent immutable validation**; it NEVER certifies the present-time repository contents V. A user or downstream system seeking **current formal Gate A readiness** must re-evaluate the canonical current-repository assurance check for V and its actual current S/P/governance evidence. In particular, if V invalidates current Gate A, the prior T-bound runner result does **not** grant readiness to V.

There is no universal "R equals T at M2 commit" guarantee from an earlier Git read. Adding more reads, including a last-moment read, cannot supply perpetual currentness or an atomic GitHub/SQLite cut. If accepted upstream authority instead requires exact live equality at the emission moment, this candidate is **not admissible** without an explicitly new coordination/transactional contract and corresponding capability assessment. Do not label inability to supply that stronger contract as a successful validation.

## 4. Historical actor neutrality and uncertain execution

A publication obligation under this selected **state-oriented** completion meaning concerns exact authorized target-state satisfaction and proof closure of all remaining relevant effect risks, **not attribution of the historical Git ref mutation to E**. Thus two histories are treated alike for the state proposition:
- H1: E executes atomic guarded P→T, response lost, qualified ref observation sees T.
- H2: E does not perform P→T, a different eligible writer publishes exact T, qualified ref observation sees T.

A target-T observation **alone** cannot establish E's historical terminal outcome, remove a potentially-effectful E, or satisfy the post-Arm case by bypassing M8/M2/GI-65. Both histories require independently qualified risk-closure proof for all relevant armed E (including superseded ones), exact target/authority verification, and a new explicit M2 progression-only admission boundary as proposed in #87. `HistoricalOutcome(E)` stays UNKNOWN absent positive independent E-specific proof. Do not produce synthetic `CapturedExecutionResult`, `PROVEN-COMPLETED`, `PROVEN-NOT-EXECUTED`, `PublicationNonApplicationRef` or `ExecutionProgressionSupersessionRef` for convenience.

The existing **pre-Arm already-current** route (P=T, zero E) already confirms an exact state without an armed mutation. It is supporting precedent for state-oriented obligation satisfaction, **not** authorization to reuse this shortcut after Arm (GI-79/GI-83 remain in force).

## 5. Component authority and provider scope

- **Current repository Formal Gate A:** current governed repository artifacts plus existing formal-assurance authority and accepted Python/assurance mechanisms; a historical runner result never replaces its verdict.
- **M2:** sole durable authority for the runner's immutable facts, qualification/confirmation admission and terminal readiness; must reject duplicate/stale/conflicting admissions.
- **M7-B/Git DC:** exact Git target/observation/publication transport proofs; not authority to invent a terminal E outcome or declare runner READY.
- **M6:** mechanical validation of exact candidate/published view; not Git effect or campaign terminal decision-maker.
- **M8:** owns recovery classifications and its own operational-blocker obligations; may not recast state equality into historical E completion.
- **M1:** deterministic orchestration only, loads M2 authority, does not decide publication truth.
- **proto-ring:** provider for applicable generic repository-governance guarantees (including externally enforced ordinary-writer authoritative-ref monotonicity), not publisher of Turnlock-specific qualification truth. Its ARM guarantee does not imply exact-old CAS, pre-publication state admission, absence of all bypasses or perpetual live currentness.

Retain the M7-A/M7-B end-to-end v1 construction arrangement as a **bounded chosen realization** compatible with the existing #78 audit, not as a product theorem that the cognitive review engine intrinsically owns Git. No unqualified Ruu/proto-ring publishing delegation and no competing generic Turnlock repository governor. The exact Git Dependency Contract and protected provider/credential conformance are still absent; do not claim the selected realization has been successfully run against authoritative main.

## 6. Alternatives and explicit rejection rationale

1. **Candidate-only runner GATE-A-READY:** REJECT for current v1, because it falsely equates GateAQualification with confirmed repository publication; would silently weaken NIB-S §29–31 and GI-40.
2. **Always-current remote GATE-A-READY:** REJECT as the *meaning of the existing terminal run result*, since a result cannot remain true of an indefinitely mutable ref without ongoing surveillance/revocation and a new externally synchronized authority model. Current repository Formal Gate A is a separate predicate evaluated against actual current evidence.
3. **Exact remote equality at the instant of M2 commit:** NOT established by current mechanisms. A fresh remote read alone is not an atomic cross-system guarantee; selecting this stronger promise would require a separately accepted contract and support proof.
4. **E-specific historical authorship as a prerequisite for publication obligation:** REJECT as a new mandatory claim absent accepted upstream authority, because H2 and pre-Arm already-current demonstrate why *exact published-state existence* and *historical actor attribution* must be separate; do not weaken residual-effect safety to reach this conclusion.
5. **Exactly published + validated immutable T, at qualified observation/validation points:** SELECT as the proposed scoped v1 runner outcome interpretation, retaining all originally accepted safety, qualification, blocker and history requirements.

## 7. Routing, required authority, and non-goals

This is an **architect-selected decision candidate**, not completed issue/ADR ratification. The remaining semantic acceptance choice for the *runner outcome interpretation* must be routed through the repository's accepted controller construction decision process, preferably an explicit accepted construction ADR if the existing authority is deemed insufficient, **before** rewriting NIB-S/M2/M7 or approving #87's state-satisfaction lane. It does **not** change TURNLOCK runtime Product Intent or require a new `TL-INV` by default; should a true upstream normative consequence be demonstrated, route it to Product Semantics rather than hiding it inside NIB.

This comment only addresses the **publication necessity / READY meaning / temporal scope** strand of #78. It does NOT close the entire Issue's 23-primitive, source/owner, Git transport, GitHub provider, repository-governance, NIB coherence, independent review or GREEN gates. The v0.2.0 proposal in #87 remains unaccepted until its own unresolved Q/WorkItem/M8/direct-outcome/UNRESOLVABLE/late-audit decisions and construction conformance are closed.

**No Git ref mutation, source modification, Issue status/dependency change, accepted ADR, NIB change, reviewer evidence or terminal-ready fact is created by this record.**

This is NOT an accepted ADR, NIB-S/NIB-M amendment, completed Git Dependency Contract, live GitHub qualification, proof of an external read that actually happened, Issue #87 progression admission, C9 qualification, or authorization for GREEN.  
**Pinned analysis baseline:** `fanilosendrison/turnlock-rust@ec52ebc62d4d9584e16c7e6bbb26ccb4f466135d`; accepted [ADR-057](https://github.com/fanilosendrison/turnlock-rust/blob/ec52ebc62d4d9584e16c7e6bbb26ccb4f466135d/docs/adr/adr-057-define-gate-a-runner-ready-as-observation-bound-publication.md), NIB-S 13.0.3, M2 mutation/snapshot 9.1.0/8.1.0 and M7-B 2.0.1 remain unmodified.  
**Owning work:** #91 for the Git dependency and conformance trust boundary; #88 for authoritative target/effective principal binding; #87 for post-Arm progression-only closure; #89 for distinct pre-Arm Arm-admission freshness. No issue state or Project mutation.

## 1. Exact choice: qualified transport as I/O fact producer, not independent cryptographic notarization

For the first supported Gate A controller realization, the Git DC adapter operating in an explicitly qualified, controlled execution environment is a declared **trusted computing base (TCB)** component ONLY for facts concerning its actual Git I/O calls, their admitted exact destination/ref, and its observed responses. M2 is the sole authoritative writer; M7-B derives Git-domain consequences from qualified transport results; neither arbitrary artifact bytes nor an M1/LLM assertion gain independent Git authority.

An immutable `GateAPublicationTargetObservationV1` is a **value**, not a real-I/O occurrence. Identical observation bytes may result from distinct legitimate reads. A nonce, timestamp, receipt SHA, locally emitted signature or M2 StateRevision is NOT by itself proof that the remote was contacted. A lying or compromised component capable of manufacturing all purported event data cannot be detected from those bytes alone. This decision therefore does **not** claim independence from the qualified adapter, provider compromise protection, or universal cryptographic remote attestation.

**Selected sufficient trust model:** verify and qualify the adapter's code/runtime/connection/result behavior and enforce a protected internal producer-to-M2 admission path, then let its narrowly scoped factual attestation support a positive occurrence witness. Every implementation/conformance claim beyond this remains to be proven. There is no newly authorized repository-governance engine, signer service, persistent observation database, or GitHub attestation API assumed by this candidate.

## 2. The distinct propositions that must NOT be conflated

```text
ValueObservation(R) = T
    !=
QualifiedActualRemoteIOOccurred(call)
    !=
QualifiedAuthoritativeRefValueAtObservationPoint(R,t_obs) = T
    !=
HistoricalExecutionOutcome(E)
    !=
ResidualExternalEffectClosure(I)
    !=
M2AdmittedPublicationSatisfaction(I)
```

A successful `git ls-remote` or provider ref-read response, without additional qualification, need not establish that the command contacted the consumer-designated authoritative endpoint, that no ambient rewriting/proxy/cache changed its meaning, or that the returned value is coherently attributable to the exact authoritative ref at an admissible observation point. Git ref reads ordinarily return commit OIDs; exact tree identity must be independently checked against the retained immutable commit/projection, not invented as a field returned by the read transport.

For ADR-057, the first implementation must positively establish an actual read occurrence after the controlling M2 contextual read AND an authoritative `R=T` witness at a provider-justified observation/linearization point `t_obs`. A cached or potentially stale response whose provider guarantee does not establish that claim is `NOT_ESTABLISHED`. Rechecking an opaque cached value is never a replacement for a qualified I/O occurrence. A provider API's existence and a one-time local test do not establish a general consistency guarantee.

After `t_obs`, the required **residual effect theorem** separately consumes the qualified applicable monotonic ordinary-writer protection/environmental guarantee for the relevant future-effect interval. A finite protection GET is NOT a proof of perpetual enforcement. Administrator disable/bypass or provider compromise are outside the current proto-ring ARM threat model; if the controller's support promise is expanded to cover them, this theorem needs a different contract. The selected Git DC is not allowed to equate a declared threat-model assumption with a newly observed immutable Git fact.

## 3. Minimal post-Arm evidence flow — no separate durable observation-attempt Q for #87

The proposed #87 read-only preparation/admission sequence is:

```text
M2 obtains ONE coherent read-side history view S at
    (RunId, StateRevision r, WriteAuthority generation g, I, W, O,
     complete historical effect-capable Execution set K, exact R, P, T)
    |
    | direct trusted invocation after S
    v
M7-B invokes qualified Git DC adapter to perform actual READ-ONLY I/O
    on the exact authority-bound repository/ref R;
    adapter returns qualified read-occurrence provenance + result R=T
    and exact qualified provider consistency/support evidence
    |
    v
M7-B derives publication state/effect-closure proof,
    preserving every still-unknown historical E outcome
    |
    v
M2 accepts or rejects a SINGLE atomic I-scoped closure/confirmation/
    obligation/blocker-disposition mutation conditional on
    current StateRevision == r, current ownership == g,
    exact coherent historical K unchanged,
    positive occurrence + effect proof,
    no conflicting admitted direct/terminal result or blocker
```

**Read-side S is not an authoritative occurrence creation.** No extra StateRevision is required merely to initiate a #87 observation. A sealed but unadmitted artifact is not M2 authority. On crash before the closure commit, discard its progression role and obtain a fresh M2 read context and qualified remote I/O on resume; NEVER replay the publication CAS. On crash after the closure commit, reconstruct the unique accepted fact and its exact proof from authoritative M2 history.

**Critical qualification boundary:** M2 cannot derive from an untrusted JSON/ArtifactRef alone that the adapter executed a read after S. The allowed producer-to-consumer route must be directly controlled and sufficiently integrity-protected within the chosen TCB; an arbitrary caller-supplied receipt is NOT acceptable merely because it has the right shape/hash/bindings. Its chosen exact API, receipt/media schema, internal invocation capability, identity linkage, command/binary pin, isolation and conformance tests belong to #91. Any local invocation token/correlation ID is only binding material, not independent remote-I/O proof.

Under conditional admission, a concurrently armed E2 or an ownership change after S invalidates the basis, because M2 checks its exact current revision/generation and rechecks the entire risk set. External Git state itself is NOT fenced by M2; external consistency, CAS enforcement and monotonicity are separate qualified dependencies. An E1 historically superseded by an operator remains included in K if it could still cause the relevant external effect.

A valid already-admitted I-scoped closure is unique; a duplicate evidence submission cannot create another confirmation or obligation disposition. The same immutable witness never represents a *new* read occurrence. Cross-context replay, wrong target, wrong I/K/r/g, unqualified provider identity, corrupt transcript, unknown consistency, and incomplete effect coverage all fail closed. No `PROVEN-COMPLETED(E)`, `PROVEN-NOT-EXECUTED(E)`, direct `CapturedExecutionResult`, `PublicationNonApplicationRef`, or synthetic operator supersession is created.

## 4. Provisional minimum Git DC producer obligations

Before #87 is admissible in any supported profile, #91/#88 MUST establish:

1. Exact executable/provider capability, version, object-format and transport invocation policy, configuration/URL rewrite/remote/refspec/credential-helper behavior, controlled environment, no implicit multi-target or alternate read source.
2. Positively verified consumer-authoritative repo/ref and reader/writer identity binding, independent of bare endpoint-string similarity and without credentials in durable artifacts. A read-only already-current path must not require mutation credentials.
3. One actual remote read operation with bounded request/response identity, qualified authenticated transport provenance, one unambiguous exact target ref and positively parsed Git OID. No inference of tree SHA from an OID-only ref response.
4. A positively qualified provider consistency rule sufficient to establish the actual authoritative R=T state at a justified observation point. Local command success, no-cache options, or a content hash alone are insufficient.
5. A controlled causal call edge from the exact S context to that transport operation, and trustworthy admission provenance preventing untrusted receipt injection, substitution and context/cross-run replay. No proposal to infer this from a locally invented nonce.
6. Exact protected ordinary-writer monotonicity/effective principal constraints, and a separate qualified atomic expected-old `CAS(R,P,T)` implementation with no hidden alternate effect, silent retry, force-like bypass or unconditional fallback.
7. Structured positive/read-unknown/failure classes. Network timeout, unavailable, stale/ambiguous, unqualified consistency, and malformed or absent provenance must never be promoted to an accepted state satisfaction or historical E outcome.
8. Isolated reproducible negative/positive transport tests and GitHub provider tests using disposable non-authoritative refs/repos only, addressing the Q01–Q18 matrix. Unsupported test cases remain explicit `UNDETERMINED`.

This is **not** a declaration that a particular Git CLI command, GitHub REST endpoint, GraphQL mutation, TLS result, helper, installed binary or credential architecture already meets the requirements. #91 must justify the selected realization under the exact no-force-publication constraints already in NIB-S.

## 5. Negative cases mandatory for hostile conformance

* Correctly shaped R=T JSON generated without any remote I/O -> REJECT.
* Same Git observation bytes from two genuinely distinct reads -> same VALUE, separate admitted OBSERVATION OCCURRENCES only when each is positively qualified.
* New receipt constructed from a prior read and relabeled with current revision -> REJECT.
* A source that reads a fork, mirror, redirected endpoint or wrong ref -> REJECT even if its OID matches T.
* A stale/cached result with no qualified authoritative consistency claim -> NOT_ESTABLISHED, no inferred t_obs.
* Read succeeds but provider response is lost/corrupt -> NOT_ESTABLISHED; never claim remote state.
* Read succeeds, M2 subsequently arms E2 or authority generation changes -> proposed admission rejected as stale, without external CAS.
* Direct terminal applied/not-applied result was already admitted -> preserve existing direct branch, no state-lane relabeling.
* Observed T then ordinary writer fast-forwards to V -> historical T witness may remain valid under ADR-057 and qualified monotonicity; do not imply current R=T or current formal Gate A readiness for V.
* Crash before M2 closure -> no accepted authoritative witness; repeat READ-ONLY step from new context, never replay mutation.
* Misbehaving qualified adapter could forge its own attestation -> explicit TCB compromise assumption; NOT an independently cryptographically falsifiable remote fact.
* No qualified Git DC/provider consistency / environmental contract -> feature UNSUPPORTED / NOT_ESTABLISHED, not an operator-invented proof.

## 6. Boundaries and routing

**#87:** keep `PublicationProgressionClosureRef` as an I-scoped candidate, not E terminal outcome. Its M2/M8/WorkItem/blocker admission, GI-54/GI-65 conflict and UNRESOLVABLE treatment remain open. Avoid creating a new #87 durable observation-Q lifecycle unless a surviving falsifying counterexample requires it.

**#89:** remains a separate OPEN pre-Arm authorization contract. It may reuse the same qualified transport-occurrence mechanism, but this note does NOT remove its candidate `BeginPreArmAttempt(E)` Q, waive pre-Arm freshness/non-replay, or ratify a Q-free Arm algorithm. Any change requires #89's own decision and mandatory NIB synchronization.

**#88:** authoritative remote target and effective writer/reader binding remains independent of Git data values.

**#91:** owner of exact Git DC code/transport conformance and producer-fact trust boundary. No NIB-T/RED/GREEN from a proposed receipt schema.

**Selected candidate statement:** trust and independently qualify a narrow Git I/O adapter; do not demand universal independent cryptographic attestation by GitHub. Use only positive producer/authority/occurrence/causal proof; do not equate an immutable observation value with an actual read. No current evidence demonstrates the full claim. **The construction decision and its provider-specific realization still require explicit acceptance and hostile review before any NIB or implementation consumes it.**

# Issue #91 — Exact candidate contract for QualifiedRemoteRefObservationV1

**Decision subject:** `GA-QUALIFIED-REMOTE-REF-OBSERVATION-v0.2.0`  
**Status:** `ARCHITECT-SELECTED CANDIDATE / NOT RATIFIED / NOT QUALIFIED`. Source-pinned implementation-construction design, NOT an accepted ADR/NIB/DC, production implementation, provider consistency proof, formal model-check evidence, approved #87 mutation, or GREEN authorization.  
**Turnlock source:** `fanilosendrison/turnlock-rust@ec52ebc62d4d9584e16c7e6bbb26ccb4f466135d`. Governing accepted [ADR-057](https://github.com/fanilosendrison/turnlock-rust/blob/ec52ebc62d4d9584e16c7e6bbb26ccb4f466135d/docs/adr/adr-057-define-gate-a-runner-ready-as-observation-bound-publication.md).  
**Predecessor:** [#91 architect trust-boundary candidate v0.1.0](https://github.com/fanilosendrison/turnlock-rust/issues/91#issuecomment-6267198688).  
**Other owners:** #88 authoritative repository/ref and effective read/write principals; #89 separate pre-Arm admission; #87 post-Arm progression closure; #90 M0/M1/M2/M7/M8 interface synchronization; #91 actual complete 23-primitive DC and provider qualification. No issue, Project, repository or NIB state is changed here.

## 1. Trust statement; no invented independent attestation

The first supported Gate A profile trusts a **specifically qualified, isolated, controlled Git DC adapter** for the factual occurrence and interpretation of the I/O that it executes. M7-B uses its qualified result to assert Git-domain state; M2 alone owns durable admission. Neither a well-formed `ArtifactRef`, a SHA-256, a nonce, a timestamp, an M2 StateRevision nor a local signature proves independently that GitHub was contacted. A compromised/laughing adapter able to fabricate the contents and provenance of all receipts is outside the selected TCB correctness guarantee; this architecture does NOT promise independent cryptographic proof against a dishonest adapter.

Qualify the trusted production chain **before** any such read result may be used: actual executable/runtime/backend and config; exact effective endpoint/repository/ref and server identity; allowed reader identity, credential mode and protected channel; response semantics; producer-to-admission channel; and required remote consistency. The current bare-Git local script and GitHub REST/Git reference API documentation do NOT themselves establish GitHub production consistency/transport conformance. On absent/undetermined positive evidence, this state-satisfaction lane is UNSUPPORTED / NOT_ESTABLISHED.

## 2. Distinguish data values, live producer authority, and durable history

Three objects have different authorities:

* **Existing** `GateAPublicationTargetObservationV1`: M7-B content-addressed value `{target,state}`. Two actual remote reads may produce byte-identical value artifacts. This value proves neither remote-read occurrence nor ordering.
* **NEW candidate** `QualifiedRemoteRefObservationV1`: an immutable secret-free **qualified occurrence witness** for an exact *actually executed* remote ref observation and exact M2 context, backed by the selected transport's bound, verified actual operation result and the provider consistency/conformance contract. It remains a non-authoritative artifact until consumed by a lawful M2 mutation. An observation of any state other than exact T does not qualify #87 satisfaction.
* **NEW runtime-only admission capability**: unforgeable-to-untrusted-callers, process/session-scoped, non-serializable and single-use private M2/M7/DC evidence that this exact witness arose through the currently authorized call chain **after** the exact M2 contextual read. A JSON/ArtifactRef without this live capability is never enough for *first* admission. A successful M2 commit records that verification as durable authoritative history, not the transient capability itself.

The runtime capability is NOT an authoritative creation/consumption record, new `Q`, nonce-as-proof, new StateRevision, cross-process token or global publication lock. Its actual safe construction and M2 API extension require explicit #90 construction synchronization. An implementation where arbitrary callers can submit a fabricated ArtifactRef and have M2 infer a trusted I/O occurrence is NON-CONFORMING, regardless of correct hashes.

## 3. Minimal versioned public witness schema (candidate)

Exactly one new **persistable witness type** is required above the existing value observation. The context is nested, not another persisted authority object. Proposed contract:

```ts
interface QualifiedRemoteRefObservationV1 {
  readonly schema: "gate-a-qualified-remote-ref-observation.v1";
  readonly purpose: "post-arm-publication-state-satisfaction";

  readonly context: {
    readonly runId: GateARunId;
    readonly stateRevision: StateRevision;
    readonly ownershipGeneration: OwnershipGeneration;
    readonly publicationIntentId: PublicationIntentId;
    readonly publicationWorkItemId: WorkItemId;
    readonly publicationObligationId: ObligationId;
  };

  readonly target: RepositoryPublicationTargetRef;
  readonly targetObservation: ArtifactRef;

  readonly occurrence: {
    readonly invocationId: string;
    readonly verifiedIoReceipt: ArtifactRef;
    readonly producerQualification: ArtifactRef;
    readonly authoritativeTargetBinding: ArtifactRef;
    readonly readerCapabilityBinding: ArtifactRef;
    readonly providerConsistencyQualification: ArtifactRef;
  };
}
```

**No `ExecutionId`, actor-of-CAS claim, outcome classification, WallClock timestamp, ephemeral process path, credential, API secret, `success` boolean or WorkItem-satisfied flag** is added to this witness.

`context` is obtained by a **single coherent M2 read** from authoritative history with current (r,g), one exact currently applicable I and its unique co-admitted W and O. M2 additionally constructs its COMPLETE run-local relevant armed-Execution set K (including superseded/terminal-UNRESOLVABLE history); **K is NOT derived from active `unresolvedExecutions`**. K need not be redundantly serialized in this read witness: the exact closure admission must reconstruct and compare K under unchanged r/g and seal the complete risk-set projection/digest in the separate I-scoped closure evidence. The target and exact successor T are obtained from the immutable I at the same read revision, never from input untrusted to M2.

`targetObservation` points to the existing exact M7-B `GateAPublicationTargetObservationV1` schema. For positive #87 admission, it MUST decode to one `present` value at the exact `target`, with `authority` equal to the authorized successor in I by **commit SHA and tree SHA**. The actual remote ref reply usually advertises a Git commit OID; the tree identity must be derived and verified from the retained exact immutable commit/object materialization, not attributed to GitHub's ref reply. The witness MUST bind the remote-response OID to that observed commit ID and the exact local validated object format.

`invocationId` is an opaque, collision-rejected **per-actual-invocation discriminator issued inside the qualified DC execution**. A duplicate or mismatched ID for accepted occurrence evidence is invalid. Its randomness, timestamp, signature or uniqueness do not constitute the I/O proof. Two real reads under unchanged (r,g,I) MAY create distinct invocation IDs and witnesses while referring to the same `targetObservation` ArtifactRef.

`verifiedIoReceipt` is a separately sealed exact, secret-free typed adapter execution transcript, cryptographically bound to its surrounding witness and occurrence ID, containing at minimum (as versioned fields in the DC's own exact receipt schema): transport/backend/build profile, actual executed command or API operation identity, effective authority-bound destination/ref, exact request class, positive completion/response grammar, parsed raw ref-OID/result class, positive permitted network/server-read path and safe invocation-to-response causality. It MAY contain bounded safe transcript-derived hashes; do not persist auth headers, tokens, passwords, unrestricted stderr, mutable temp paths or raw secrets. A purported receipt constructed without an actual accepted I/O return is not qualified. An exit status alone is insufficient.

The four qualification/binding `ArtifactRef` members name IMMUTABLE, separately positively qualified, exact-effective profiles: (i) trusted DC runtime/producer profile; (ii) consumer-authoritative repo/ref equivalence proof (not mere endpoint-text equality); (iii) effective reader/server identity and credential/capability mode; (iv) provider response consistency semantics sufficient to assert the authoritative ref's exact value at some `t_obs` **during** the actual post-context read. They MUST refer to accepted qualified versions for that execution, not generic placeholders or future Issue text. A public unauthenticated read may be supported if server authentication, authoritative-repo identity, positive response and consistency are separately qualified; it need not borrow the mutating writer credential.

`QualifiedRemoteRefObservationV1` and nested refs use M0 `CanonicalRunnerJsonBytesV1` and the existing `CampaignArtifactStore` media-type/integrity contract for sealing. The Git DC adapter MUST NOT itself write M2 campaign authority or infer NIB-S runner READY.

## 4. Runtime-only causal admission capability (the missing anti-forgery edge)

A serializable witness cannot assert its own trustworthy production. Therefore the **first** M2 admission of the witness MUST additionally consume a valid *live* producer-admission capability from a protected internal channel. This is an architectural **runtime authority boundary**, not a second persistent witness type.

The capability must be produced ONLY by the M2-controlled context-read + qualified M7-B/DC actual-I/O invocation path; bind exact (run,r,g,I,W,O,target,witness ArtifactRef,DC invocationId); be unavailable to externally supplied ArtifactRefs or arbitrary user/coding-agent-provided JSON; be unexportable as JSON/disk artifact; and be invalidated upon use, process/session termination, lost ownership, changed StateRevision or wrong call/context. It MUST NOT be synthesizeable by the M7 result serializer or an untrusted runner caller merely by copying context fields. Exactly one legal first-admission attempt may consume a live capability; after a stale/invalid admission request, no replay of the same live capability to gain new authority.

No particular physical in-process handle, private closure, callback or hidden runtime brand is selected here. The accepting NIB-M/M2 interface under #90 MUST select an enforceable realization without exposing a generic forgery route. The current public M2 `CommitAuthoritativeMutationRequest` transports a `mutation: AuthoritativeMutationRef` and does NOT currently provide this producer-origin control; adding only fields to the referenced JSON is NOT sufficient.

After successful M2 admission, the immutable witness plus the unique M2 mutation and its validated provenance are reconstructible after crash. Reconstructions verify the original **admission record** and exact sealed evidence; they do not claim to replay the vanished runtime capability or independently prove that a past process was honest.

If the process crashes **before** admission, any sealed but unadmitted receipt remains non-authoritative, and resume must acquire a fresh M2 read context and perform a NEW real read. The old receipt cannot be admitted under a new context even when bytes, revision and observation value happen to be identical.

## 5. Acceptance procedure and race ordering (v0.2 candidate, #87 admission not yet accepted)

```text
1. M2 read one internally coherent (r,g,I,W,O,K,target,P,T) snapshot.
   M2 returns one protected, live read-context capability to trusted caller.
2. Trusted M7-B calls the qualified DC exactly once for actual read-only
   ref observation, directly after step 1, with the exact same context.
3. DC returns verified actual I/O result/receipt under its accepted
   target/reader/producer/consistency profile. M7-B binds the existing
   target-value artifact and one QualifiedRemoteRefObservationV1.
4. M7-B derives only a *candidate* exact-T observation plus separate
   residual-effect closure evidence. No E outcome/terminal is inferred.
5. In the same protected authorized call chain, M2 receives the sealed
   artifacts AND consumes the live verified producer-admission capability.
6. Inside ONE M2 atomic state mutation, M2 checks:
   - exact active run, owner g, latest revision r;
   - exact projected I/W/O/C/qualification/target/T;
   - recomputed complete historical risk set K;
   - qualified producer/target/reader/consistency and actual-I/O receipt;
   - effective real-I/O call after the supplied M2 read context;
   - all residual-effect proof/monotonicity/bounded-scope prerequisites;
   - no earlier positive direct/terminal conflicting admission;
   - only legal exactly bound existing blocker dispositions;
   - uniqueness of I closure, confirmation and O disposition;
   - no introduced Arm/supersession/direct result since contextual read.
7. Atomically append, as a future separately RATIFIED #87 M2 transition:
   one I-scoped closure + confirmation/provenance + satisfied O +
   exact approved blocker dispositions. Otherwise commit NOTHING.
8. M6 post-publication validates the bound immutable T view;
   M2 may later admit terminal runner READY under ADR-057 and GI-40.
```

A valid `R=T` value never suffices without full residual-effect proof. A stale local r or g invalidates a prospective admission. A new Arm after the read increments StateRevision and is detected. Git changes are not under the local SQLite transaction; ADR-057 permits T→V after the qualified T observation only under the separately qualified applicable remote monotonicity/environment assumption. The read witness makes NO present-time equality promise at M2 commit.

The existence or replay of one witness does not create a second `PublicationConfirmationRef`, disposition of O, closure, WorkItem success or Execution outcome. After O is atomically satisfied, M2's normal authorization/Arm preconditions must prohibit further publication dispatch from that W. All still-unknown historical E facts remain immutable. GI-54, GI-65, M8 blocker semantics, historical UNRESOLVABLE and WorkItem satisfaction **are not amended by this #91 record**; #87 must choose and synchronize their new lawful progression rules.

## 6. Strict read-result classification and Git-specific parsing

Only a **positive, qualified, exact-ref and exact OID** read can produce an eligible present-state witness. Other outcomes:

* `present-other` (P, X, V, unexpected OID): positive value read MAY be recorded but is NOT state satisfaction for exact T. M7/M8 retains its existing appropriate domain path; no E historical conclusion.
* `missing`: no T witness. Lack of a visible ref may mean absent or inaccessible depending on the API/permissions, so a *positive absent* interpretation requires its own qualified visibility/authority guarantee; otherwise mark unavailable.
* `unavailable`: transport error, timeout, no successful valid complete response, provider/consistency not established -> no positive qualified witness; no assumed `PROVEN-NOT-EXECUTED`, `not-applied`, state satisfaction or mutation retry.
* `integrity/dependency failure`: wrong target, unauthorized producer, schema/call-capability mismatch, malformed/ambiguous response, spoofed read, wrong transport environment, false ref binding, unsupported format -> fail the invocation through existing integrity/dependency error handling; never silently downgrade to pending or normal OAR.

For a future qualified Git CLI `ls-remote` realization, exact full-name parsing is mandatory even if the command supplied a ref pattern: git-ls-remote patterns are globs that may match the tails of ref names, and without `--exit-code`, status 0 does not by itself say any ref matched. Do not accept `--get-url` as a remote read: it resolves a URL without contacting the remote. The command or API selection is NOT ratified by this comment; the future DC must pin actual command/API semantics and supported Git/object formats. GitHub REST `GET /git/ref/{ref}` documents returned Git OID/ref fields but does not alone attest the exact consistency/linearization guarantee demanded above. ETag/304 or a previously cached ref value without a new qualified full positive state observation cannot replace the claim.

## 7. Required independent conformance attack matrix

**Offline/unit/negative**, fully controlled runtime:
T01 forged canonical `R=T` JSON and correct SHA, no actual DC invocation -> REJECT.  
T02 a real sealed value with no live protected admission capability -> REJECT.  
T03 attempt to synthesize capability from context fields or an M1/caller-provided object -> REJECT.  
T04 old receipt copied to new request with same r/g/I, but no new trusted call -> REJECT; old occurrence MUST NOT be relabeled.  
T05 two real qualified reads with equal target value bytes -> two distinct exact invocation identities, one value ArtifactRef MAY be equal.  
T06 wrong Run/I/W/O/target/revision/generation/purpose -> REJECT without M2 mutation.  
T07 E2 Arm or direct terminal outcome admitted between read and closure -> local revision mismatch; fail closed and do not admit.  
T08 ownership transfer without new StateRevision -> generation mismatch; fail closed.  
T09 crash after M2 read but before Git response -> no witness, no mutation; new read after resume.  
T10 crash after qualified Git response but before M2 commit -> unadmitted evidence not authoritative or replayable; new read after resume.  
T11 crash after M2 atomic commit -> unique closure/provenance reconstructible without new I/O, no second O disposition.  
T12 same logical I and duplicate/distinct witness submissions -> one closure at most; no different-bytes same logical ID overwrite.  
T13 tampered/out-of-order/duplicate/truncated/ref-pattern false-match Git output -> reject positive exact ref.  
T14 success exit with empty ref list, `ls-remote --get-url`, wrong branch/symref/peeled-tag, unsupported hash format -> never positive T.  
T15 stdout/stderr containing adversarial text, secrets, binary/NUL, credential-bearing URL -> reject or safely classify, never leak credentials.  
T16 fake Git executable, ambient `insteadOf` rewrite, remote helper, mirror/fork, proxy/SSH command or credential helper substitution -> reject target/producer/reader qualification.  
T17 fabricated/simulated completed I/O transcript with valid media/hash but no trusted producer-origin capability -> REJECT.  
T18 exact T in an unqualified cache/replica/stale HTTP response or a bare `304 Not Modified` -> NOT_ESTABLISHED, not `t_obs`.  
T19 read R=T with local object tree different from I's exact successor -> reject; server ref OID alone does not supply tree SHA.  
T20 qualified read R=T, then legitimate protected T→V before M2 admission -> eligible historical T witness only if all other proof obligations hold; never assert current R=T or readiness of V.  
T21 H1 E published T / H2 other writer published T -> same state witness, no E terminal truth.  
T22 attempted side-effect from read itself or hidden ref mutation -> nonconforming; recovery observations must be read-only.  
T23 provider protection/admin bypass, alternate CAS, incomplete E history or unqualified future monotonicity -> no residual-effect closure, even with perfect read witness.  
T24 `UNRESOLVABLE` and pending-policy-exhausted blockers -> no implicit disposition; only future exact #87/M8-B+M2 contract may dispose.  
T25 consumer-authoritative repo/ref binding mismatch or read under a different read principal than attested -> REJECT.  
T26 provider unavailable or network error after request starts -> no positive state witness; normal uncertainty/integrity distinction must remain correct.

**Positive integration:** exact ref read and same-content repeat against disposable local bare Git fixture, plus provider-specific external disposable non-authoritative GitHub repo/ref/profile under controlled credentials; verify actual effect-free invocation, parsing, target binding, no-cache/consistency behavior and conformance. Verify all Q01–Q18 #91 obligations separately. A finite test or `git ls-remote` syntax doc does NOT mathematically prove future provider consistency or ordinary-writer protection. Persist exact provenance and list unestablished environmental assumptions and version/identity pins as `UNDETERMINED`.

Every negative case must leave `PublicationProgressionClosureRef`, `PublicationConfirmationRef`, obligation disposition, new Arm and M8 historical outcomes unchanged unless a separate already-authorized mutation independently occurred. No test mutates the actual authoritative `refs/heads/main`.

## 8. Explicit open qualification and ratification gates

**Closed at proposal level:** trust model (qualified Git DC as factual I/O TCB), separation of existing target value from new positive occurrence witness, minimal persisted witness shape, protected non-serializable transient admission capability in place of durable #87 Q, fail-closed parsing/admission cases, crash rules and falsifiable test matrix.

**Still UNQUALIFIED / LOCKED:**
- exact Git CLI/API invocation/profile, provider/ref read-consistency guarantee, effective endpoint/reader/server trust and negative-case evidence (#88/#91);
- actual concrete private/runtime admission-capability interface and M2/M7-B cross-module integration (#90);
- valid complete historical E risk-set construction, qualified guarded `CAS(P,T)` effect closure, environmental monotonicity proof, GI-54/M8 and blocker disposition, direct vs unknown vs UNRESOLVABLE case matrix, post-Arm M2 mutation/WorkItem semantics (#87);
- pre-Arm Q lifecycle or optional Q-free replacement, which #89 alone decides;
- accepted ADR/NIB ratification and independent hostile construction review; NIB-T, RED/GREEN and actual Gate A evidence.

**No normative or source edit:** this candidate is NOT itself an admissible typed producer proof in the active DC (which is absent), and must not be used to pretend #87 is closed.
