The following is architect-side source confrontation, NOT independent ratification. Raw private scratch receipts are not independently verified by this comment.  
**Owners:** #87 progression closure and M8 causal routing; #88 exact target/effective principal and consumer governance; #89 pre-Arm freshness; #90 cross-module versioned construction; #91 Git DC/occurrence/CAS conformance; #32 NIB-T; #33 full-pack review. No issue or Project state mutation authorized here.

## 1. Selection, core theorem and scope

The principle is unchanged from v0.3.1 and accepted ADR-057:

```text
Confirmed exact state of I
  != proven historical actor/Execution outcome E

A positively qualified state observation plus complete positive residual-
effect safety and correct M2 admission MAY satisfy I without deciding
whether any given historically unknown E performed its original CAS.
```

Initial profile, no widening: exactly one currently applicable `PublicationIntent I` for qualified C, its exactly one `Obligation O` and `WorkItem W`, one consumer-authoritative ref `R`, strict positively proven fast-forward `P≺T`, one genuinely qualified actual remote observation of `R=T` at `t_obs`, the complete M2 historical risk set K including superseded armed E, only genuinely qualified `CAS(R,P,T)` effects, positive environmental protection assumptions, and no conflicting admitted direct applied/result route. An eligible mixed history may include unknown Armed E1 and separately positively direct non-applying E2 with exact `PublicationNonApplicationRef`; E2 is not recast as unknown. At least one relevant Armed E must still have unknown historical effect for the special lane. If none is unknown, use only existing direct/new-intent/pre-Arm already-current routes.

Preserve full recorded E Arm, outcome, operator supersession, M8 `pending` and lawful historical terminal classification; do not invent `PROVEN-COMPLETED`, `PROVEN-NOT-EXECUTED`, `PublicationNonApplicationRef`, generic `WorkItemSatisfied`, a successor Execution, or pre-Arm `already-current` after an Arm.

New proposed I-scoped fact remains uniquely `PublicationProgressionClosureRefV1` at `deriveId("publication-progression-closure.v1", publicationIntentId)`. It is an immutable reference to exact I/W/O/C/qualification/R/P/T, verified complete M2 historical effect projection, #91 qualified actual I/O occurrence witness, positive per-E bounded-effect proof and provider/protection/consumer-governance qualification. It is not E's terminal outcome or a durable Q. No unadmitted candidate artifact reserves an authoritative closure ID.

**F-01 from v0.3.0 remains settled:** once this mutation produces a `PublicationConfirmationRef` and O satisfied for I, it **does not** authorize another same-run I2. Existing no-prior-confirmation and single-O-terminal-disposition restrictions remain; after M6 post-publication `passed=false`, follow its exact OAR with `resolutionContracts=[]`, no self-invented same-run repair/new intent. A distinct later GateARun derives its own independent current-repository authority. Runner READY is observation-bound to historical T, never a perpetually-current R=T assertion.

## 2. F008 — CLOSED mechanical blocker eligibility, no "independent vs contradictory" judgment

**Replace v0.3.1 §6's special rule allowing closure in the presence of an unspecified unrelated but "non-contradictory" blocker.** That rule required a semantic choice absent from M2/M8-B and is REJECTED for this first realization.

Let `B` be the COMPLETE set of currently outstanding run-local `CampaignBlocker` from ONE verified M2 coherent read, not an arbitrary subset supplied by M1/M7/M8. Partition using only accepted exact closed type tags and positive immutable OAR/recovery-causal source bindings:

- `B_semantic`: every semantic blocker.
- `B_other`: every operational blocker that is not an exact eligible **pending-policy-exhausted recovery-causal blocker** attached to an Armed, historically unknown E of the SAME exact I/W/O in K, with valid source identity and retained `ReconciliationPendingRef`.
- `B_pending(I,K)`: ALL AND ONLY outstanding recovery-causal pending-policy-exhausted blocker IDs meeting that complete exact identity chain.

Selected positive closure gate:

```text
semanticProgressionTerminal == false
AND B_semantic == empty
AND B_other == empty
AND every B in B_pending(I,K) is fully validated by M8-B
AND proposedBlockerIdsToDispose
    == ALL B_pending(I,K), deterministic ordered IDs
```

`B_pending(I,K)` may be empty if no pending exhaustion blocker has been admitted; the exact unknown Armed E still belongs to K and needs its positive guard proof. If ANY producer-occurrence blocker, wrong-intent blocker, different-E blocker, `UNRESOLVABLE` blocker, semantic blocker, unknown/invalid cause or identity-inconsistent blocker exists, this first-version state lane is **INELIGIBLE** and MAY NOT be proposed or admitted, even if someone might describe the blocker in natural language as "unrelated". Do not reinterpret or dispose any of them. Return the existing applicable M8/operator/semantic decision route; an integrity-invalid retained blocker fails integrity, not normal OAR.

M8-B owns a NEW **pure**, separately typed `validatePublicationStateClosurePendingDispositionV1` boundary: consume the exact M2-supplied ordered outstanding operational blocker/OAR projection, exact I/W/O and K unknown E identity set and proof reference; check OAR/ref/Execution/basis binding under its existing recovery-causal identity rules and return exactly the sorted complete list of eligible pending blockerIds or an explicit `INELIGIBLE`/integrity rejection. M8-B MUST NOT query Git, interpret an E historical outcome, invoke M8-A recovery, consume a producer occurrence blocker or mutate M2.

M2 owns exact history coverage and currentness: inside ONE atomic mutation it reconstructs ALL authoritative blocker and disposition history, verifies the M8-B pure result matches current B exactly and that no old disposed blocker is re-disposed. It does not choose causes based on prose. There is NO new generic "commit facts despite unrelated blocker" allowance. Once closure atomically disposes all eligible B, **zero outstanding CampaignBlockers** must remain as a postcondition, before M1 may proceed to M6. This stricter admission costs possible liveness when another independent blocker is present; it deliberately closes F008 without extra semantics.

The ONLY newly proposed causal disposition reason in the initial profile is `publication-residual-effect-risk-closed` for the exact `pending-policy-exhausted` recovery blocker, not `PROVEN-COMPLETED`, `PROVEN-NOT-EXECUTED`, an OperatorResolutionEnvelope, or a successor `ExecutionProgressionSupersessionRef`. Its original pending evidence and OAR remain historical and immutable. M8-B/M2 §16 require explicit accepted versioned amendment; no existing matrix entry already authorizes it.

## 3. F017 — precisely bounded residual-effect theorem and governance retirement fence

**Withdraw v0.3.1's unbounded phrase "old CAS permanently unable to mutate R" without specifying the lifetime of authority and its governance protection.** The accepted proto-ring Authoritative Ref Monotonicity contract (pinned `dc8e04c758fb40867dc7ad23f019843413fc4a1b`) guarantees protected ordinary-writer fast-forward and non-deletion **while R remains designated authoritative**. It expressly does NOT define lawful retirement or migration; an admin changing/bypassing protection is outside its selected threat model. No local ruleset GET proves endless future enforcement.

Let `t0` be the qualified actual authoritative remote `R=T` observation point. Let `D_R(t)` be consumer-authoritative designation of exact R, `ARM_R(t)` the qualified enforced monotonicity/non-deletion for ordinary relevant writers and `PotentialEffect(E,t)` the possibility of a not-yet-quiescent E's original guarded external operation affecting R.

Within a protected authority interval `[t0,t_exit)` for which `D_R ∧ ARM_R` holds:

```text
R(t0) = exact T
P strictly ancestor of T
All modeled E write only atomic CAS(R,P,T), with no fallback
Every intervening ordinary writer update of R monotonic

=> for every t in [t0,t_exit):
      R(t) != P
      => no covered old E can succeed at CAS(R,P,T)
```

**A permanently admitted I-scoped progression closure must also declare and positively qualify its *governance-continuity assumption* across any subsequent retirement or migration:** before `D_R ∧ ARM_R` ceases, the owning consumer must have a separately accepted lawful transition/fence that ensures no covered historic E still has an effective mutation capability on that ref, OR establishes an independently sufficient permanent non-revival guard for that exact old P-bound operation and any later re-designation. Examples of future realizations include **positively proven irreversible effect-capability revocation**, a qualified transport lifetime/dispatch fencing contract that proves all old mutations cannot subsequently apply, or a consumer-governance ref-retirement protocol ensuring later ordinary authority can never reactivate P while any old E might affect it. These are examples of proof obligations, NOT available capabilities or a selected implementation.

Formally the closure's modeled promise is conditional on:

```text
GoverningSupportProfile(I,R,K) asserts:
  - exact protected R designation/monotonicity for all periods
    when an old E effect remains possible and relevant; and
  - any retirement/migration/re-designation preserves safety by an
    independently accepted fence before protection/authority is removed.
```

If this obligation cannot be established for a deployment, **post-Arm state satisfaction is UNSUPPORTED / NOT_ESTABLISHED**. Do not replace it by a finite timestamp/window heuristic, an imaginary lease, or an assertion that a ref will never be retired. Nor may M2 automatically revoke historical E effects when READY is reached; that is no executor-outcome proof. A future observer seeking current repository Formal Gate A readiness must always evaluate current repository state; historical runner READY for T remains immutable under ADR-057.

The I-scoped closure is intentionally **not** a blanket theorem about external behavior on a voluntarily retired/unprotected ref, and cannot be carried as proof for a new designation without its own qualified governance transition. The lifetime assumption and its scope must be explicit in any formal model and environment conformance record. The issue owning consumer target/governance selection is #88; #91 owns selected Git/DC/transport/actual writer qualification. Neither currently supplies a complete retirement fence. This is a **new explicit support-profile gate**, not silently absorbed into proto-ring.

## 4. F025 — exact owner of the domain theorem: M7-B pure producer/validator, M2 covers history

Introduce the candidate versioned M7-B **pure**, domain-owning validation responsibility:

```ts
validate_publication_residual_effect_closure_v1({
  intent: PublicationIntentRef,
  exactHistoryProjection: ArtifactRef,
  qualifiedObservation: ArtifactRef,
  perExecutionOperationProfiles: readonly ArtifactRef[],
  effectiveGitDcQualification: ArtifactRef,
  protectedAuthorityBinding: ArtifactRef,
  governanceContinuityProfile: ArtifactRef
}) -> 
  | { kind: "established";
      qualification: PublicationResidualEffectQualificationRefV1; }
  | { kind: "not-established"; reason: closedReason; }
  | { kind: "invalid-proof-or-dependency"; reason: closedReason; }
```

**Owner split (closed):**

**M2 snapshot/history** provides a single coherent read-only exact `(run, r, ownership g, I, W, O, C, qualification, K, all blocker and disposition history)` with every W historical E, Arm, creation basis, direct/recovered result, PNA, pending, terminal UNRESOLVABLE, operator supersession and the exact historical prior-intent chain. It computes exact authorized identity/fullness/projection/digest and rejects missing/inconsistent E. `unresolvedExecutions` alone is insufficient. M2 does NOT interpret Git command content, force flags, provider protections or CAS semantics.

**M7-B** receives M2's exact complete immutable projection as untrusted request input for domain validation; it verifies each E's exact M7-B publication WorkItem operation/Arm/dispatch/recovery capability binding to I's R/P/T, qualifies the effective DC transport's **one and only one potentially relevant atomic guarded mutation** `CAS(R,P,T)` per originally Armed E with no alternate/replay/bypass/other potentially invalidating effect, and verifies the qualified exact actual Git occurrence and monotonic/environmental support-profile references. It constructs/validates one deterministic `PublicationResidualEffectQualificationRefV1` containing:
- exact I/R/P/T and original qualified C/qualification linkage;
- exact bound `QualifiedRemoteRefObservationV1` occurrence witness from #91 (not just `GateAPublicationTargetObservationV1` content bytes);
- exact canonical `effectHistoryProjection` reference and hash/digest;
- ordered per-E positive effect-scope/guard evidence entries for EVERY historically unknown Armed E;
- positive applicable Git DC CAS and effective-principal/target profiles;
- exact proto-ring ARM and **separate consumer-governance continuity/retirement fence support profile**;
- scope-constrained conclusion `old-cas-ref-effect-excluded-under-accepted-governance-lifetime-assumption`, NOT E historical outcome truth.

The schema is a proposal for versioned M0/NIB-M closure, not a license to invent untyped proof facts. M7-B may read sealed artifacts through accepted M0 `CampaignArtifactStore` verification; it performs **no new remote read, Git mutation, SQL write, historical classification or M2 history enumeration** in this PURE validation.

**M2 final admission** independently reconstructs complete current K, checks exact r/g, exact full projection/ordered identities and every required M7-B proof binding, and calls/consumes the accepted **pure M7-B validator** (or an explicitly equivalent qualified typed pure validator) against the exact supplied immutable artifacts. It requires `established` and matching qualified conclusion before committing its own I-scoped facts. M2 may verify that K is exhaustively covered and accepted qualifications are current; it does NOT re-decide whether Git guarantees are semantically adequate. An arbitrary client-provided `kind=established` object without the accepted validator's exact positive result and protected #91 live trusted producer origin is inadmissible. A missing positive proof yields `NOT_ESTABLISHED`; structural contradiction/provider invalidity yields the owning dependency/integrity failure, not a fabricated normal recovery result.

M8-B independently handles only the pure pending-blocker causal-disposition decision from §2. M8-A retains sole Execution recovery classifier authority. M1 merely sequences; M6 validates immutable published T after confirmation. There is exactly ONE M2 durable mutation authority.

## 5. F011/F012 — exact historical UNRESOLVABLE eligibility; repair conflicting M7-B source rule

Current NIB-S common recovery contract requires `RecoveryIndeterminacyRef` to positively prove that the executor's available recovery mechanism **cannot** establish terminal outcome, valid PNE OR a valid safe-reobservation continuability fact. Lack of a convenient historical-operation lookup alone is insufficient. The selected M7-B v2.0.1 has a non-null read-only target reconciliation capability for every Armed conditional publication E. Its §23 returns `pending` with positive safe read-only continuability for T and P and even when remote observation is unavailable. But its `missing/X` branch returns `unknown` merely because historical-operation lookup is unsupported. That evidence does NOT establish absence of continued safe read-only target observation; it contradicts the higher-level positive-exhaustion predicate.

**Architect-selected correction candidate for selected v1 M7-B profile:**

```text
qualified target = T -> existing pending + safe reobservation
qualified target = P -> existing pending + safe reobservation
qualified target = X -> pending + safe reobservation
qualified target = missing -> pending + safe reobservation
target temporarily unavailable -> existing pending + safe reobservation
```

The last three branches require EXACT positive proof that the bound reconciliation operation remains purely observational and may lawfully be called again, **not** that it will eventually produce a terminal answer. An invalid/malformed/authority-binding failure is an integrity/dependency error, never a synthetic pending. If the accepted DC cannot positively establish safe continuability for an exceptional case, neither `pending` nor `unknown` may be invented: return the appropriate dependency/operational failure as separately specified at its owning layer, without treating lack of visibility as conclusive executor-domain exhaustion.

# Issue #87 — F017 adversarial adjudication: scope residual-effect closure to the continuous authoritative-ref epoch

**Decision candidate:** `GA-F017-AUTHORITY-EPOCH-SCOPED-RESIDUAL-SAFETY-v0.1.0`.  
**Status:** `ARCHITECT-SIDE COUNTEREXAMPLE ADJUDICATION / PROPOSED CORRECTION / NOT RATIFIED`. This comment does not edit the frozen [#87 v0.3.2](https://github.com/fanilosendrison/turnlock-rust/issues/87#issuecomment-6270746979); it proposes a precisely bounded replacement for that proposal's §3 retirement-fencing admission gate and related references in §§4/6/7/9/10. It is NOT an accepted ADR/NIB, Git DC qualification, runtime guarantee, new ref governance service or formal-model proof.  
**Source baseline:** `fanilosendrison/turnlock-rust@ec52ebc62d4d9584e16c7e6bbb26ccb4f466135d`. Accepted ADR-057 blob `f03c37ce05e370e27d25e83d95192e27b9872f08`. Proto-ring ARM pin `dc8e04c758fb40867dc7ad23f019843413fc4a1b`.  
**Owners:** #87 historic I-scoped post-Arm progression; #88 consumer exact ref/governance binding; #91 external protected writer, guarded mutation and remote observation DC; #90 versioned NIB synchronization. A future consumer-governance **retirement/re-designation** decision is separate and has no accepted realization in this record.

## 1. Accepted authority versus v0.3.2's extra assumption

ADR-057 §Decision 2–4 says runner `GATE-A-READY` is an immutable historical attestation of (i) exact qualified C, (ii) exact T observed at an identifiable genuine remote occurrence when R was the designated authority, (iii) M2 publication confirmation/O disposition, (iv) passing M6 validation of immutable T, and (v) normal terminal guards. It explicitly does NOT mean `R=T` at terminal commit or any future time, and does NOT confer current-repository Formal Gate A readiness.

The pinned proto-ring Authoritative Ref Monotonicity contract enforces non-fast-forward/non-deletion against ordinary writers **while R remains designated authoritative**. The consumer owns ref designation; the contract expressly does not define retirement or migration, and excludes protection-admin changes/bypass, provider compromise and destructive admin rewrite from its threat model. The local consumer binding names GitHub `fanilosendrison/turnlock-rust`, `refs/heads/main` and ruleset `24106121`, but a single current ruleset read is not future immutability evidence.

v0.3.2 correctly bounded its local stale-CAS proof to continuous designation/protection, **then added a materially stronger admission gate**: before any post-Arm I closure, positively qualify future retirement/migration/re-designation fencing across all possible later ref histories. Neither ADR-057 nor proto-ring ARM currently requires a past completed runner to prove the safety of hypothetical *future new authority designation* decisions. This global gate over-constrains the selected historical terminal outcome, and could require proving quiescence or permanent credential revocation for E whose historical result is deliberately still UNKNOWN.

**Architect selection candidate:** REMOVE that global future-retirement fence as a prerequisite for #87's I-scoped closure, subject to the exact, narrower run/authority-epoch assumptions in §§2–4. Do NOT replace it by a claim that an old physical Git mutation is forever impossible. This is a proposed scope correction, not an excuse to weaken observed-I/O, protected-CAS or current-epoch monotonicity qualifications.

## 2. Exact two-epoch counterexecution

```text
Epoch A (same continuously designated/protected R):
  t0: third party or E publishes exact T from P
  t1: actual qualified read proves R = T
  t2: complete old E CAS(P,T) risk set proven unable to mutate R
      WHILE THIS AUTHORITY EPOCH CONTINUES
  t3: M2 confirms exact I and admits O satisfied; M6 validates T
  t4: runner returns historic GATE-A-READY for T

Retirement (a separate later consumer governance action):
  t5: R ceases to be designated authoritative; epoch A ends
  t6: R is legitimately reset/recreated at P outside former ARM scope

Epoch B (potential NEW independent designation of the same ref name):
  t7: if the new authority accepts R=P with no old-attempt admission fence,
      a delayed original E CAS(R,P,T) may now succeed
      despite each epoch separately enforcing ordinary-writer fast-forward
```

At t7, **the STRONG global claim** `never again can old E succeed on this physical ref` is FALSE. The **historical claim** `R was authoritatively observed as exact T at t1 and immutable T passed M6` remains TRUE. Epoch B admission is unsafe if it inherits Epoch A's residual-safety proof or fails to screen dormant old attempts; that is a **new-authority admission defect**, not retroactive invalidity of Epoch A's exact I confirmation or ADR-057 terminal fact.

Another allowed trace: after t5, old E could succeed on the **undesignated** physical ref if it is recreated at P. This must NOT be described as proof of physical termination or impossibility of any future effect. It is outside the narrower claim that old E cannot mutate the continuously designated/protected *authoritative ref* for I.

The same issue can arise if an authority epoch ends **during** a still-running GateARun. Such mid-run retirement/re-designation is NOT an accepted supported transition in the first selected profile and must not be hidden behind an immutable M2 publicationTarget field; that field proves the run's fixed target identity, not perpetual external designation or provider protection.

## 3. Minimal formally bounded claim

Define `epoch(I,R,t_obs)` as the **maximal continuous interval of the SAME consumer-authority designation of R with qualified ordinary-writer ARM enforcement that contains the actual qualified observation t_obs**. This is conceptual model scope, NOT an existing persisted GitHub epoch ID, mutable lease, clock freshness window, new Git primitive or M2 StateRevision.

Let `P≺T` be independently proven strict Git ancestry, `K` the complete historical Armed risk set, `OnlyGuardedCAS(K,R,P,T)` positive and exact, and `R(t_obs)=T` positively established by accepted #91 actual Git I/O/provenance/consistency.

Then under the declared environmental ARM guarantee *for this continuous authority epoch*:

```text
for every t >= t_obs WITHIN epoch(I,R,t_obs):
    tip(R,t) is T or a descendant of T
    therefore tip(R,t) != P
    therefore no old E in K can successfully CAS(R,P,T) at t
```

This is a conditional **authority-epoch-scoped noninterference safety theorem**. It asserts neither `TerminalOutcomeKnown(E)` nor permanent physical E quiescence. A finite GitHub ruleset GET does not establish the temporal assumption; provider/consumer support qualification must clearly state the model of environment under which it holds. Admin bypass/reconfiguration and provider compromise remain excluded by the accepted ARM threat model, not silently “proved impossible”.

The prospective durable `PublicationProgressionClosureRefV1` records an immutable fact that **the effect risk was proven closed for this exact I and its continuous designated authority epoch under the qualified environmental support model**. Its fact is not revoked by later retirement, but its asserted applicability **is not transferable** to a different/refreshed epoch, different I, new authoritatively designated repository/ref, or future current-repository readiness verdict. The proof is historical and scope-indexed, not a promise of all-time physical non-execution.

## 4. Minimal supported v1 environment, without a future-governance service

For the initial Gate A run realization, select a narrower support profile: from the positive `R=T` publication witness through M2's I admission, bound M6 validation and terminal result (or blocking OAR), **the exact target remains within the same uninterrupted consumer-authority designation and ordinary-writer ARM enforcement regime**. A deliberate authority-ref retirement/migration/re-designation while this run is active is UNSUPPORTED unless a future separately accepted contract defines safe cutover. This is an explicit **environmental assumption/support restriction**, not a runtime claim that M2 can detect future admin behavior or a proof supplied by a finite protection observation.

The selected in-run profile must still qualify, at the actual I observation/admission boundary:
- exact R target and consumer binding, actual reader/principal and ref occurrence/consistency (#88/#91);
- accepted ordinary-writer monotonicity/non-deletion and non-bypass effective publication identity under the pinned ARM threat model;
- exactly bounded `CAS(R,P,T)`, positive no-alternate-effect/no-replay/no-fallback transport contract for EVERY relevant old E;
- complete coherent M2 historical K and protected actual M7-B positive proof;
- precise inability of E to affect R **while the designated authority epoch persists**;
- no silently supported in-run legitimate retirement/cutover, contrary external ref support or alternate mutable-ref path.

If these positive current-epoch premises cannot be qualified, state closure remains `NOT_ESTABLISHED`. The additional hypothetical **post-READY future retirement fencing** of v0.3.2 is not a current admission prerequisite. Normal in-run Git ref T→V ordinary fast-forward is supported and does not invalidate ADR-057 T-bound historical result.

For a ref deliberately retired AFTER the run terminal result, the old completed runner may not promise physical E quiescence or own the next governance decision. A later new authority designation MUST independently establish its own admissible predecessor/current state and effect-fencing if it would re-enable an old guarded P-bound mutation. That **future new designation gate** is a separate consumer-governance design obligation WHEN such operations are selected; it is neither an existing proto-ring ARM feature nor a current #87 I-closure success condition. This record does NOT invent a new governance API, new persistent epoch field or future migration implementation now.

## 5. Why the stronger future gate is not mechanically dischargeable from present Git data

Given an old Arm with lost E response and no qualified E-specific historical operation query, no finite wait, terminal run result, R=T read or present ruleset status establishes that E's already-dispatched request has physically settled or can never arrive. A future ref retirement that allows P as tip may make its exact expected-old CAS applicable again. Revoking a credential after the request was sent is not automatically proof that all previously in-flight remote operations are impossible.

Therefore v0.3.2's demanded **irreversible effect-capability revocation/future retirement fencing positively established now** is an additional powerful assurance goal with no accepted mechanism, not a necessary logical consequence of ADR-057's historical publication claim. If that stronger “no physical old mutation under ANY later ref governance” property is desired, it must be explicitly adopted at its owning higher authority and qualified with stronger transport/capability/epoch design, rather than hidden as a required field of the current M7-B validator.

## 6. Exact v0.3.2 proposed edits, and unchanged protections

**Proposed replacement of §3:** `Residual-effect proof is authority-epoch scoped. Guarded old CAS cannot mutate R after t_obs while R remains continuously designated and protected. The first supported run forbids in-run retirement/migration/re-designation. Future ref re-designation must establish its own safe authority admission; no old closure is reusable across epochs.`

**Proposed replacement of §4 M7-B pure validator obligation:** replace `governanceContinuityProfile` with a **scoped, accepted current-run authority/ARM support qualification** (one positive provider/consumer profile, not a magical permanently valid future retirement lease). The validator MUST expose exact proof scope/lifetime premises. Its result is NOT global `old-cas-impossible-forever`; it is `old-cas-noninterference-within-qualified-authority-epoch`.

**Proposed replacement of §6 M2 guard:** require qualified applicable continuous-authority/run support profile (and all original E completeness, actual read, CAS and blocker guards). Do NOT require a positively already-implemented future retirement fence before admitting I's historical publication confirmation.

**Proposed replacement of §7/#91 qualification language:** the absence of a future retirement/migration protocol is **not an intrinsic current-epoch blocker for #87**. #88 still owns current exact authority designation; #91 still owns actual I/O, CAS semantics, non-bypass effect/principal, and current support profile conformance. Neither profile can claim provider admin immutability.

**Keep v0.3.2 unchanged elsewhere:** F008 closed ALL-and-ONLY pending-policy-exhausted blocker gate, F025 M7-B positive pure residual-effect validator/M2 exhaustive historical set split, pending rather than unjustified `UNRESOLVABLE` for M7-B missing/X where safe reobservation remains, mixed E1 unknown/E2 direct PNA, no new durable #87 Q, unique atomic I closure+confirmation+O disposition, no I2 after confirmation, positive rematerialized immutable T for M6, original late outcome limitations and direct-result priority.

* `E2`: epoch A ends only AFTER historical GateARun READY; ref resets to P, old CAS might physically succeed while retired; past READY remains true, permanent physical-inertness is not asserted.

## 3. F017 — exact authority-epoch-scoped residual-effect theorem, WITHOUT permanent future-retirement fencing

**Adjudication:** v0.3.2 correctly noticed that proto-ring Authoritative Ref Monotonicity (ARM), pinned to `dc8e04c758fb40867dc7ad23f019843413fc4a1b`, is NOT perpetual. That stronger future-governance requirement is NOT derived from accepted ADR-057, which attests **actual historical publication of exact T, then passing immutable T validation**, not perpetual live ref equality or physical termination of E. **Formal scoped claim.** Let `epoch(I,R,t_obs)` denote the continuous interval that includes the qualified actual remote observation `R(t_obs)=T` and during which the SAME exact ref R remains designated authoritative by the consumer and subject to a qualified externally enforced ordinary-writer ARM/no-deletion regime. Intentional ref retirement/migration/re-designation or protection-regime cutover while such a GateARun is still nonterminal is **UNSUPPORTED** without a distinct accepted cutover/resumption contract. This is an explicitly declared environmental assumption/support restriction; it is not mechanically established by one ruleset GET, M2 revision, ref read, arbitrary credential claim or a documentary promise. If a real mid-run epoch break occurs, old closure cannot silently support further continuation to READY; absent a separate accepted recovery/transition contract, fail closed instead of inferring continuity from immutable `GateARun.publicationTarget`.

**Current qualification still mandatory:** #88/#91 must positively establish the correct consumer-designated R, actual reader and provider-consistency-bound remote I/O occurrence, the effective non-bypass ordinary publication principal, the guarded CAS effect boundary and applicable externally enforced ARM environment *for the supported current epoch*. **Strict boundary:** the new M7-B producer/validator and M2 closure admission must require ONLY the qualified current-epoch support profile and complete actual effect proof, not a future all-time E revocation, all-time Git protection guarantee, or unimplemented permanent retirement fence.     physically terminated or globally incapable of future effects
```text
AFTER closure:
    M6 read-only validates immutable T; historical READY may be admitted
    without a claim that R is still current or physically guarded forever
ANY future epoch-B ref designation:
    MUST independently examine still-effect-capable old E and enforce
    its own new-authority safety barrier
```

A run with an outstanding/uncertain publication obligation (including one blocked in OAR before closure) retains its effect-risk pin across crash/resume, perhaps indefinitely. A run whose exact I was lawfully confirmed and O satisfied MAY be nonterminal for M6 or its OAR while the old-run historical outcome remains valid. The normal `M2` obligation guard/GI-74 still prohibits new original-W Arm after satisfaction. This narrows the amount of concurrency blocking rather than weakening the old-epoch guarded-CAS proof.

**No choice between full-run and effect-risk-only pin has yet been ratified in active NIBs**. v0.3.3 currently states the stricter no-cutover-while-nonterminal environmental support profile. This note demonstrates that it is *stronger than the ADR-057 historical attestation itself*; choosing the narrower candidate requires an explicit successor #87 adjudication/review.

## 4. Exploratory TLC results (not provider proofs)

New runnable local files: `GateAAuthorityContinuity.tla`, `TwoRunEpochPins.tla`, `TwoRunEffectRiskPins.tla`, the prior bounded `GateARefEpoch.tla`, nine explicit TLC configs, full traces, SHA-256 inventory. A private user-facing conversation bundle contains the exact source and outputs; this GitHub comment does NOT itself attach the source bytes. TLC 2.19 / OpenJDK 21 / one worker / seed 20261019.

| Bounded toy configuration | TLC | Distinct states | Claim tested |
|---|---|---:|---|
| `coord_only` | PASS | 10 | One run, shared gated retirement, no bypass |
| `coord_bypass` | counterexample | 5 | Binding edit bypasses a conceptual gate |
| `recheck_race` | counterexample | 17 | Independent recheck followed by cutover then READY |
| `two_runs_guarded` | PASS | 20 | Two resumable runs share a durable pin/cutover authority |
| `two_runs_ungated` | counterexample | 8 | Normal binding edit bypasses global pin |
| `effect_risk_only` | PASS | 83 | Pin through O satisfaction; historical validation/READY later may be allowed |
| `effect_risk_unchecked` | counterexample | 8 | Ungated binding edit breaks epoch while E effect is outstanding |
| `effect_risk_stronger` | counterexample | 21 | Strong no-cutover-until-READY fails after lawful O closure/release |
| `historical_ready_midrun` | PASS | 126 | Prior #87 toy model's *historical* READY invariants hold despite permitted mid-run retirement |

These tests enumerate only finite **abstract** state machines. They do not supply the actual coordinated consumer-governance control plane, prove provider response consistency, cover multiple unknown Armed E/CAS races, or validate real M2 transaction code. The positive tests are conditional on the absence of an ungated authority-change action. The historical-ready toy explicitly lacks NIB-S's full predicates, and does not prove the current controller can legally resume after a cutover.

## 5. Precise qualification and routing

**Present fact:** the current GitHub ruleset is active with `deletion` and `non_fast_forward`; the repo has the consumer binding and accepted proto-ring ARM pin; the M2 persistence brief declares **one shared** authoritative `campaign-state.sqlite` for all GateARuns in the domain. None of these observations qualifies a protected, serialized change-of-designation boundary or shows that an ordinary governing-file fast-forward is ineffective during an active run.

**Design gate:** choose an ACCEPTED support scope: (A) static non-cutover environment with all external designation-changing operations genuinely forbidden for supported actors; (B) full-run globally coordinated pins; or (C) the *recommended minimal, ADR-057-consistent effect-risk-only pin*. B and C require a narrow shared admission-vs-cutover mutual-exclusion contract and an externally enforced **single** designated-governance update path. Otherwise their TLC no-break invariant is only assumed, not mechanically guaranteed. A also requires independently justified exclusion/enforcement of normal binding-file updates, not merely policy prose.

Until the owning #88 governance/conformance authority and #90 M2 integration accept/qualify such enforcement, the statement `NoAuthorityEpochBreakWhileNonterminalRun` must be marked **UNPROVEN AS A REAL PROVIDER GUARANTEE**. Do not silently promote a documentary binding, successful GET, or recheck into an eternal witness. Use explicit `NOT_ESTABLISHED` for unsupported conditions.

Any later #87 construction-version revision must keep the old E attribution UNKNOWN, retained immutable T publication evidence, exact guarded CAS proof under the correctly bounded epoch, no Q durability invented, one-commit closure/O/blocker admission and independence of future epoch-B admissibility. Never weaken already accepted ADR-057, product intent or proto-ring ARM by stealth.

**No files, ADRs, NIBs, Git refs, Issue/Project statuses, provider credentials, live publication or GREEN have been modified by this comment.**

value.body:
## Problem

`formal/verification.yaml` currently uses `Invariant.kind` to describe the broad normative nature of each TURNLOCK invariant (for example `safety`, `safety+liveness`, `reachability`, `conformance`, `dx`, or `architecture`). That classification is useful, but it is not precise enough to describe what TLC must establish for each individual TLA+ property.

One normative invariant can map to multiple formal properties with different proof obligations. The motivating interpretation for `TL-INV-004` is:

- `HandoffPreservesContinuation`: a safety obligation;
- `HandoffCanResume`: a liveness obligation whose successful check would depend on explicit fairness assumptions.

However, the current normative text for `TL-INV-004` requires a valid control path and preservation of the ability to resume; it does not yet state universal eventual resumption. This mismatch is itself evidence that property names and invariant-level `kind` are insufficient. The migration must review semantic correspondence rather than silently strengthening capability/reachability language into liveness. If universal progress is desired but cannot be derived from current authority, route that as a separate product decision.

`TL-INV-005`'s `MultipleHandoffsRepresentable` expresses a clearer capability/reachability obligation: at least one valid behavior must demonstrate repeated handoff. It must not be encoded or reported as the universal temporal claim `<> (handoffCount >= 2)`, because a valid execution in which the user never invokes TURNLOCK does not violate repeatable-handoff semantics.

The same reachability/capability distinction likely applies to planned properties such as `MixedBranchTypesCanCoexist`, `IndependentAgentCanBeWorkflowDeclared`, and `RequiredCoreFormsComposable`.

Without property-level obligation semantics, the manifest, TLC result evidence, checker, and generated mapping can conflate:

- a bounded search that found no safety counterexample;
- a liveness check that found no violating behavior in a declared finite configuration under recorded fairness assumptions;
- a positive reachability witness.

That ambiguity could permit an invalid `checked` claim once the executable model is introduced.

## Evidence and provenance

Inspected on `main` at revision `eb21af5c56736775d8410c32c29ead18f245b873`:

- `formal/verification.yaml` is schema version 2. It contains 33 planned TLA+ properties, but each property currently records only `name` and `status`; `kind` exists only at invariant level.
- `formal/tlc-result.schema.json` is schema version 1. It records one run-level `outcome`, a string list of `checked_properties`, invariant IDs, finite bounds, and optional run-level `fairness_assumptions`, but no property-level obligation or evidence result.
- `scripts/check-formal-traceability.py` checks manifest/reference consistency and requires a passing run mentioning an invariant and its required configs before invariant-level `checked`. It does not establish an exact per-property match for obligation class/mode, fairness, witness evidence, or the revision governed by the claim. It currently checks that the result schema parses as JSON rather than validating run records against its full JSON Schema contract.
- `scripts/render-formal-mapping.py` renders invariant `kind` and a flattened list of property names, but no property-level obligation class, verification mode, fairness profile, or property status.
- `docs/formal/invariant-mapping.md` is mechanically generated and reverse-maps property names to invariant IDs, but cannot expose the missing distinctions.
- No executable `formal/Turnlock.tla`, TLC configuration, or passing run evidence exists. Every current formal property remains planned/not yet modeled.

ADR-015 already requires safety and liveness to remain distinct, requires matching run evidence for `checked`, and separates manifest intent from TLC evidence. The current data model is not yet expressive enough to enforce those requirements per property or to represent reachability witnesses without ambiguity.

## Current authoritative boundary

The central distinction is:

```text
Invariant.kind
= nature of the normative TURNLOCK requirement

TLA property obligation
= nature of the obligation that the model checker must establish
```

The concepts are related, but they are not equivalent. A normative `safety+liveness` invariant may map to separate safety and liveness properties, each with its own verification mode and evidence requirements.

## Discovery classification

**Primary: C — Formal modeling choice.** The metamodel, evidence, and checking mechanics define how accepted semantics are represented and validated; they create no product semantics.

The classification of an individual property may be **A — Derived semantic requirement** only when it follows from current authority without an unstated assumption. If reclassification exposes a genuine semantic ambiguity, record it explicitly as a separate **B — New product or semantic decision** instead of choosing silently in this task.

ADR-015 and the normative specification remain authoritative. Because accepted ADR bodies are immutable, any decision that genuinely amends ADR-015 must be recorded through a later ADR rather than by editing ADR-015.

## Open questions

1. What smallest property-level obligation vocabulary distinguishes safety, liveness, and positive reachability without duplicating invariant-level `kind`?
2. How must mixed invariants split into independently checkable properties and evidence?
3. What property-level fairness metadata is required, and how is its absence validated?
4. What exact evidence proves a witness obligation versus absence of a counterexample?
5. How are revision, configuration, property, invariant, and outcome matched so stale or run-level-only evidence cannot justify `checked`?

## Alternatives

- **Keep run-level evidence only:** rejected because one run-level outcome cannot prove heterogeneous property obligations precisely.
- **Infer obligation from invariant `kind` or property names:** rejected because mixed invariants and capability-oriented names are ambiguous.
- **Use explicit atomic property obligations and class-specific evidence:** preferred, with exact schema names left to the implementation of this C-class metamodel.

## Required outcome

Evolve the formal-verification metamodel before introducing the executable `Turnlock.tla` model so the repository can distinguish:

1. the invariant's normative nature;
2. each TLA+ property's formal obligation class;
3. the verification mode used to establish that obligation;
4. any fairness semantics required by that property;
5. the class-specific TLC evidence required for a valid `checked` claim.

The initial obligation classes should be deliberately small—conceptually `safety`, `liveness`, and `reachability`. Candidate verification modes include `invariant`, `temporal-property`, and `witness`. These spellings and the exact YAML shape are proposals, not pre-approved schema names; the implementation may choose clearer names if it preserves the distinctions and validation rules below.

## Scope

### 1. Evolve `formal/verification.yaml`

Keep `kind` at invariant level as the normative classification. Add an obligation classification to every formally applicable TLA+ property, conceptually similar to:

```yaml
properties:
  - name: HandoffPreservesContinuation
    status: planned
    obligation:
      class: safety
      mode: temporal-property

  - name: HandoffCanResume
    status: planned
    obligation:
      class: liveness
      mode: temporal-property
      fairness_profile: main-agent-region-completion
```

and:

```yaml
properties:
  - name: MultipleHandoffsRepresentable
    status: planned
    obligation:
      class: reachability
      mode: witness
```

Define and validate the allowed class/mode combinations. Also define how property-level `planned`, `modeled`, `checked`, and blocked/unresolved states aggregate to the existing invariant-level formalization/verification status so mixed-property invariants cannot be overstated.

Liveness obligations must be able to reference explicit fairness profiles or equivalent declared assumptions. Do **not** force a concrete fairness choice for a property that is still planned/not yet modeled. The metamodel may represent fairness as unresolved at that stage, but it must make an implicit or unknown fairness basis invalid for `checked`.

### 2. Evolve `formal/tlc-result.schema.json`

Replace or augment the ambiguous run-level property list with property-level results that bind at least:

- property name;
- obligation class;
- verification mode;
- class-appropriate outcome;
- fairness profile and/or exact assumptions when applicable;
- witness/evidence metadata when applicable;
- the run identity required by ADR-015 (revision, module, config, TLC version, finite bounds) and by the current manifest policy (including timestamps).

The result contract must distinguish:

- no counterexample found for a safety obligation within the declared finite state space;
- no violating behavior found for a temporal/liveness obligation in the declared finite model/configuration under explicit recorded fairness assumptions;
- discovery of a reachability witness.

A reachability witness must not be reportable as universal temporal verification, and a witness alone must not satisfy a safety obligation. Define the schema-version migration and compatibility policy explicitly.

### 3. Strengthen formal traceability validation

Update `scripts/check-formal-traceability.py` and its automated test coverage so the checker validates the new metamodel and result records, including their JSON Schema contract.

At minimum, enforce:

```text
liveness + checked
→ explicit, resolved fairness semantics matching the result evidence

reachability + checked
→ corresponding positive witness evidence

safety + checked
→ class-appropriate no-counterexample evidence; witness-only evidence is insufficient

checked
→ exact match for property, obligation class/mode, expected config,
  and the revision governed by the claim
```

Preserve the ability to record planned/not-yet-modeled liveness properties before fairness details are resolved. Define a deterministic policy for revision matching rather than accepting any passing result that merely mentions the invariant ID.

Add positive and negative fixtures/tests covering mismatched class/mode, missing fairness, missing witness, witness-only safety evidence, wrong property/config/revision, malformed result schema, and valid planned entries with unresolved fairness.

### 4. Evolve the generated mapping

Update `scripts/render-formal-mapping.py` so `docs/formal/invariant-mapping.md` exposes, without becoming a second source of truth:

- invariant `kind`;
- TLA+ property name;
- obligation class;
- verification mode;
- fairness profile/state when applicable;
- property verification state (`planned`, `modeled`, `checked`, or the final equivalent vocabulary).

Retain mechanical generation, freshness checking, and reverse traceability from each TLA+ property to affected invariant IDs.

### 5. Synchronize formal-governance documentation and validation entry points

Update `docs/formal/README.md` and `formal/README.md` to explain the property-level obligation/evidence contract, status aggregation, fairness readiness, witness semantics, and schema compatibility policy without duplicating the manifest or result schema as a second authority.

Add a stable, documented command for the new metamodel/result-evidence tests and run it from `.github/workflows/repository-integrity.yml`. Keep the repository's documented local validation sequence synchronized with that command.

### 6. Reclassify every existing planned property

Perform a complete migration of all 33 currently planned properties. For each property, record:

```text
obligation class: safety | liveness | reachability
verification mode: invariant | temporal-property | witness | another explicitly justified mode
```

At minimum:

- classify `HandoffPreservesContinuation` as a safety obligation unless semantic-correspondence review finds a conflict;
- explicitly resolve or block `HandoffCanResume`: do not infer universal liveness solely from its name or `TL-INV-004`'s composite `kind`; if it is ultimately a liveness property, fairness is required before `checked`;
- classify `MultipleHandoffsRepresentable` as a reachability/capability witness, not universal eventuality;
- evaluate `MixedBranchTypesCanCoexist`, `IndependentAgentCanBeWorkflowDeclared`, and `RequiredCoreFormsComposable` explicitly as likely witness obligations rather than inferring their class from `Invariant.kind`.

If a property cannot be classified without a new product decision, mark that classification explicitly blocked/unresolved with rationale and route the semantic decision separately. Do not omit the property or choose a convenient class silently.

<details>
<summary>Current planned property inventory (33)</summary>

- `TL-INV-001`: `DeclaredControlFlowOnly`
- `TL-INV-002`: `EngineDoesNotInventTopology`
- `TL-INV-003`: `MechanicalExecutionNotAgentMediated`
- `TL-INV-004`: `HandoffPreservesContinuation`, `HandoffCanResume`
- `TL-INV-005`: `MultipleHandoffsRepresentable`
- `TL-INV-006`: `EnclosingWorkflowPreservedDuringMainAgentRegion`
- `TL-INV-007`: `ResumePositionWellDefined`
- `TL-INV-008`: `StructuredReturnPath`, `InvocationEventuallyReturnsUnderFairness`
- `TL-INV-009`: `MainAgentLineagePreserved`
- `TL-INV-010`: `WorkflowStateExistsOutsideAgentState`
- `TL-INV-012`: `ExecutionFormsRemainDistinct`
- `TL-INV-013`: `AgentCannotAdvanceUndeclaredGlobalControl`
- `TL-INV-014`: `MainLineageNotForkedByHandoff`
- `TL-INV-016`: `WorkflowInvocationAvailableWheneverMainOwnsControl`
- `TL-INV-017`: `NestedInvocationSuspendsCaller`, `CallerStackWellFormed`
- `TL-INV-018`: `ReturnToImmediateCaller`, `CorrectCallerEventuallyResumesUnderFairness`
- `TL-INV-019`: `NestedInvocationCannotRewriteOuterContinuation`
- `TL-INV-024`: `MixedBranchTypesCanCoexist`, `MixedBranchSemanticsPreserved`
- `TL-INV-025`: `IndependentAgentCanBeWorkflowDeclared`, `IndependentAgentHasDistinctLineage`
- `TL-INV-026`: `IndependentAgentContextIsExplicitlyDeclared`
- `TL-INV-027`: `NoPrematureJoin`, `BranchCompletesAtMostOnce`, `JoinEventuallyReleasesUnderFairness`
- `TL-INV-028`: `RawLLMIsBoundedLeaf`, `RawLLMDoesNotCreateAgentLoop`
- `TL-INV-030`: `ProbabilisticLeafCannotOwnGlobalControl`
- `TL-INV-031`: `RequiredCoreFormsComposable`

</details>

## Sequencing requirements

- Complete this metamodel migration before introducing the executable `formal/Turnlock.tla` and real TLC result claims.
- Concrete main-agent completion semantics and final fairness assumptions are not prerequisites for classifying planned obligations; unresolved fairness may remain explicit until modeling makes it decidable.
- Any newly exposed semantic ambiguity is a separately governed decision and must not be resolved opportunistically here.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `formal/verification.yaml` (or an accompanying validated schema/contract) distinguishes invariant `kind` from property-level obligation class and verification mode.
- [ ] The initial obligation vocabulary covers safety, liveness, and reachability, with validated class/mode combinations.
- [ ] All 33 existing planned TLA+ properties are explicitly reclassified, or carry an explicit blocked/unresolved classification with rationale where a new semantic decision is genuinely required.
- [ ] Liveness properties can reference explicit fairness profiles/assumptions, while planned/not-yet-modeled entries may keep fairness explicitly unresolved.
- [ ] No liveness property can become `checked` with implicit, absent, unknown, or evidence-mismatched fairness semantics.
- [ ] Reachability/capability obligations are represented and evidenced as positive witnesses, not as universal temporal eventualities.
- [ ] The TLC result schema records property-level obligation class, mode, outcome, and class-specific evidence, while preserving concrete run identity and finite bounds.
- [ ] The checker rejects `checked` claims whose evidence mismatches the property's name, class, mode, expected config, governed revision, fairness requirements, or witness requirements.
- [ ] The checker validates result artifacts against the updated JSON Schema, not only for parseability and selected top-level fields.
- [ ] Automated positive/negative coverage demonstrates the rejection rules for safety, liveness, and reachability evidence through a stable documented test command executed by repository-integrity CI.
- [ ] `docs/formal/README.md`, `formal/README.md`, the CI workflow, and the documented local validation sequence are synchronized with the new contract and test entry point.
- [ ] The generated invariant mapping shows invariant kind separately from every property's obligation class, verification mode, fairness state/profile, and verification state.
- [ ] Reverse traceability and generated-file freshness remain mechanical and valid.
- [ ] No property or invariant is promoted from `planned`/`not-yet-modeled` to `modeled` or `checked` solely because of this migration.
- [ ] No normative TURNLOCK semantic choice is introduced silently; ambiguities requiring product decisions are explicitly reported and separately routed.
- [ ] Existing repository integrity validation and CI remain green.

## Validation

Run the repository-required sequence after regenerating the mapping:

```bash
.venv/bin/python scripts/render-formal-mapping.py
.venv/bin/python scripts/tests/test-adr-metadata.py
.venv/bin/python scripts/adr-metadata.py check
.venv/bin/python scripts/check-formal-traceability.py
git diff --check
```

Also run the stable metamodel/result-evidence test command introduced and documented by this work, and inspect the generated mapping diff against `formal/verification.yaml`.

## Non-goals

- Writing the executable `formal/Turnlock.tla` model.
- Resolving product questions found by the recent consistency audit.
- Defining the concrete completion protocol for a main-agent region.
- Selecting the final fairness assumptions of the future model.
- Directly modifying accepted ADR-015; any genuine amendment requires a later ADR and separate semantic authorization.
- Implementing Rust, Cargo, runtime, API, packaging, or release behavior.
- Claiming that any invariant is already formally verified.
- Changing the normative meaning or identity of any `TL-INV-*` invariant as part of reclassification.

## Authoritative references

- [`formal/verification.yaml`](https://github.com/fanilosendrison/turnlock-rust/blob/main/formal/verification.yaml)
- [`formal/tlc-result.schema.json`](https://github.com/fanilosendrison/turnlock-rust/blob/main/formal/tlc-result.schema.json)
- [`scripts/check-formal-traceability.py`](https://github.com/fanilosendrison/turnlock-rust/blob/main/scripts/check-formal-traceability.py)
- [`scripts/render-formal-mapping.py`](https://github.com/fanilosendrison/turnlock-rust/blob/main/scripts/render-formal-mapping.py)
- [`docs/formal/invariant-mapping.md`](https://github.com/fanilosendrison/turnlock-rust/blob/main/docs/formal/invariant-mapping.md)
- [`docs/formal/README.md`](https://github.com/fanilosendrison/turnlock-rust/blob/main/docs/formal/README.md)
- [`formal/README.md`](https://github.com/fanilosendrison/turnlock-rust/blob/main/formal/README.md)
- [ADR-015](https://github.com/fanilosendrison/turnlock-rust/blob/main/docs/adr/adr-015-evolve-the-normative-and-formal-specifications-together.md)
- [TURNLOCK normative specification §9](https://github.com/fanilosendrison/turnlock-rust/blob/main/docs/specification/turnlock-spec.md#9-formal-specification-governance)
- [TURNLOCK Discovery Classification Protocol](https://github.com/fanilosendrison/turnlock-rust/blob/main/docs/repository-governance/turnlock-rust-discovery-classification.md)

value.body:
## Problem

The current normative sources do not uniquely determine what liveness TURNLOCK promises for several planned formal properties. Property names such as `HandoffCanResume`, `InvocationEventuallyReturnsUnderFairness`, `CorrectCallerEventuallyResumesUnderFairness`, and `JoinEventuallyReleasesUnderFairness` may conflate:

1. capability or reachability;
2. engine progress after a completion or return-ready condition has already been satisfied;
3. universal eventual completion of a region, workflow, or branch set.

These are observably different product obligations. Their meaning must be derived from current authority or decided explicitly before the Formal Verification phase encodes them.

This issue now owns only the Specification-phase semantic audit. The downstream formal representation was split into #3.

## Evidence and provenance

Inspected on `main` at revision `eb21af5c56736775d8410c32c29ead18f245b873`:

- `formal/verification.yaml` associates four `safety+liveness` invariants with planned liveness-oriented property names:
  - `TL-INV-004` → `HandoffCanResume`;
  - `TL-INV-008` → `InvocationEventuallyReturnsUnderFairness`;
  - `TL-INV-018` → `CorrectCallerEventuallyResumesUnderFairness`;
  - `TL-INV-027` → `JoinEventuallyReleasesUnderFairness`.
- `TL-INV-004` requires a valid handoff/resume path and preservation of the ability to resume; it does not clearly promise that every main-agent region eventually completes.
- `TL-INV-008` requires a structured return path and first-class transitions; normal completion semantics do not by themselves guarantee that every invocation terminates.
- `TL-INV-018` requires a normally completed nested workflow to return to its immediate caller; this does not by itself require every nested workflow to complete.
- `TL-INV-027` requires workflow-owned fan-out/fan-in and continuation, while failure, cancellation, partial-result behavior, and lifecycle limits remain open.
- The concrete completion or yield protocol for a main-agent region remains unspecified.
- No executable TLA+ model or successful TLC evidence currently exists. Planned property names are not executable formulas or verified claims.

A nesting scenario also exposes an occurrence-scope requirement: if a progress promise concerns one particular region, invocation, caller, or join, progress by another occurrence cannot satisfy that promise. Whether a universal progress promise exists in the first place remains a product question.

## Discovery classification

**Primary: B — New product or semantic decision.** Current authority does not uniquely determine whether each affected concept promises capability/reachability, conditional engine progress, or universal eventual completion. Any genuinely open promise must pass through an explicit product decision and normally a later ADR.

**Per-property alternative: A — Derived semantic requirement.** An individual obligation may instead be classified A only when a complete derivation from accepted specification text and ADRs shows that it adds no new product choice. The audit must retain that derivation and a failure/counterexample. Occurrence identities and fairness formulas used later in TLA+ remain **C — formal modeling choices**; runtime IDs or schedulers would be **D — implementation mechanisms**.

## Current authoritative boundary

Keep these layers separate:

```text
semantic obligation
= what TURNLOCK promises for a particular occurrence

formal-modeling choice
= how TLA+ identifies and checks that occurrence

implementation choice
= any runtime identifier, field, token, or mechanism
```

The normative specification and accepted ADRs own product meaning. An Issue, property name, fairness device, or convenient TLA+ formula cannot create or strengthen that meaning.

Classify a property-level semantic conclusion as derived only when current authority necessarily entails it. If multiple behaviors remain compatible with current authority, the question is `decision-required` and must be resolved through the repository's ADR process before normative promotion. Accepted ADR bodies remain immutable; amendments require a later ADR.

## Semantic questions

1. Does each affected source require only a valid progress path, conditional engine progress after an external completion condition, or universal eventual completion?
2. What exact region, invocation, caller continuation, or join occurrence owns each promise?
3. Which actor controls the enabling condition, and which actor is responsible only after it becomes enabled?
4. Which environmental progress assumptions are product semantics rather than formal-model conveniences?
5. Does any current property name overstate authority and therefore need to be split or renamed downstream?

## Alternatives

- **Treat every `Eventually` name as universal liveness:** rejected because planned names are not product authority.
- **Collapse all four into reachability:** rejected unless each normative derivation proves that capability is the complete promise.
- **Audit and classify each atomic obligation separately:** required; retain capability, conditional liveness, or universal liveness only when supported or explicitly decided.

## Required outcome

Determine the weakest authoritative progress obligation, if any, for every affected concept. Distinguish at least:

### Capability or reachability

```text
a valid behavior can return control to the enclosing workflow or caller
```

### Conditional engine liveness

```text
if the relevant completion or return-ready condition is satisfied,
TURNLOCK eventually advances the corresponding continuation
```

### Universal eventual completion

```text
every normally completable region, workflow, or branch set eventually completes
```

Do not select universal liveness merely because a planned property name contains `Eventually` or because a future model checker needs a temporal formula.

## Scope

1. Audit every current planned property associated with `safety+liveness`, including:
   - `HandoffCanResume`;
   - `InvocationEventuallyReturnsUnderFairness`;
   - `CorrectCallerEventuallyResumesUnderFairness`;
   - `JoinEventuallyReleasesUnderFairness`.
2. For each candidate obligation, record:
   - normative source and derivation;
   - triggering condition;
   - exact occurrence or subject;
   - expected event;
   - actor responsible for progress;
   - whether the obligation is capability/reachability, conditional liveness, or universal liveness;
   - any environmental or fairness premise required by the semantic claim.
3. Classify each atomic conclusion through the repository discovery protocol as derived, decision-required, or uncertain.
4. Route every genuine product choice through a later ADR and synchronize the normative specification, decision history, formal traceability, and generated artifacts as repository governance requires.
5. Produce an authoritative, traceable handoff for #3 without choosing a TLA+ representation or runtime mechanism here.

## Sequencing requirements

- This semantic audit does not require the property-level verification
  metamodel produced by #1 and may proceed in parallel with it.
- The occurrence-scoped formalization in #3 consumes the authoritative liveness
  outcome of this audit as its semantic input.
- Complete the authoritative semantic work before any downstream formal
  representation selects occurrence-scoped fairness profiles.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] Every affected property has been audited individually against its controlling specification sections and accepted ADRs.
- [x] Capability/reachability, conditional engine liveness, and universal eventual completion are not conflated.
- [x] Every claimed obligation identifies its trigger, exact occurrence, expected event, responsible actor, and required premise.
- [x] Every semantic conclusion has an explicit discovery disposition and complete authority trace.
- [x] No property name, TLA+ convenience, fairness assumption, or anticipated TLC result is treated as product authority.
- [x] Every behavior not uniquely determined by current authority is resolved through an accepted later ADR or remains explicitly blocked.
- [x] Accepted ADR bodies remain unchanged.
- [x] Every accepted semantic change is synchronized across the normative specification, decision history, formal traceability, and generated artifacts as required by repository governance.
- [x] The semantic handoff this Issue produces is complete enough for the
      downstream occurrence-scoped formalization to consume without guessing
      product meaning.

value.title: Specification: define TURNLOCK liveness guarantees and occurrence scope

value.body:
## Problem

TURNLOCK's retained liveness obligations must be represented so that progress by one region, invocation, continuation, or join cannot discharge the obligation owned by another occurrence.

A global fairness clause over an unparameterized action type can be satisfied by repeated progress in nested or unrelated occurrences while one particular outer occurrence starves. Once the product-level liveness guarantees are resolved, the formal representation therefore needs occurrence-scoped subjects and explicit fairness semantics.

This work was split from #2 so product meaning is decided in the Specification phase rather than being embedded in a formal-modeling task.

## Evidence and provenance

Split from #2 after inspection of `main` at revision `eb21af5c56736775d8410c32c29ead18f245b873`.

Current planned properties requiring liveness-specific formal treatment include:

- `HandoffCanResume`;
- `InvocationEventuallyReturnsUnderFairness`;
- `CorrectCallerEventuallyResumesUnderFairness`;
- `JoinEventuallyReleasesUnderFairness`.

`formal/verification.yaml` currently provides no occurrence-scoped fairness profile, trigger predicate, responsible actor, or weak-versus-strong fairness selection for these planned properties. No executable TLA+ model or successful TLC evidence currently exists.

## Discovery classification

**C — Formal modeling choice.** Occurrence-scoped subjects, parameterized actions, fairness profiles, and model-only identities represent semantics accepted or derived by #2 using the verification metamodel from #1. They must not become normative product promises or concrete runtime mechanisms. Any semantic ambiguity discovered here is routed back as **B**, never resolved for TLC convenience.

## Current authoritative boundary

- The normative specification and accepted ADRs own TURNLOCK product meaning.
- #2 owns the semantic audit and any required product decision or normative amendment.
- #1 owns the property-level obligation, verification-mode, fairness, and evidence metamodel.
- This issue owns only the downstream formal representation of accepted or fully derived semantics.

An abstract occurrence identity, parameterized action, caller-stack element, branch-set identity, or similar structure is a formal-modeling choice. It does not require a runtime UUID, counter, token, Rust field, or public API.

## Formal questions

1. What model-only subject uniquely owns each live obligation, and what is its lifetime/equality rule?
2. Which action must be parameterized so progress for occurrence `Y` cannot satisfy occurrence `X`?
3. When is the relevant action continuously enabled, intermittently enabled, or controlled by an external actor?
4. Does the accepted semantic promise require `WF`, `SF`, no fairness, or an explicitly named environmental premise?
5. How must result evidence identify the property and fairness profile accepted by #1?

## Alternatives

- **Global fairness over an unparameterized action type:** rejected because unrelated occurrences can mask starvation.
- **Occurrence-scoped parameterized actions/subjects:** preferred when required by the accepted property semantics.
- **Omit the liveness property:** required whenever #2 leaves its product meaning unresolved; do not invent fairness to retain a planned name.

## Required outcome

Represent each retained liveness obligation with a precise trigger, occurrence-scoped subject, expected event, responsible actor, and explicit fairness basis, using the metamodel established by #1 and the authoritative semantic outcome of #2.

The representation must prevent progress for occurrence `Y` from satisfying an obligation for occurrence `X` and must not strengthen product semantics merely to make a temporal property expressible or checkable.

## Scope

1. Consume the accepted or fully derived semantic outcomes of #2.
2. Use the property-level metamodel established by #1.
3. For every retained liveness property, represent:
   - the triggering condition;
   - the exact occurrence or activation that owns the obligation;
   - the expected event;
   - the actor whose progress is assumed;
   - the fairness scope and strength, including a per-property justification of `WF`, `SF`, no fairness, or another precisely defined assumption.
4. Define any model-only occurrence identity with stable lifetime, equality or reuse semantics, and protection against aliasing between concurrently live obligations.
5. Update the formal traceability manifest, generated mapping, and formal-governance documentation as required by the accepted metamodel.
6. Keep unresolved semantic questions explicitly blocked rather than selecting a convenient formal interpretation.

## Required semantic inputs

- The property-level obligation and evidence metamodel established by #1.
- The authoritative liveness outcome resolved or routed by #2.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Every retained liveness property from #2 has a formal representation traceable to its authoritative semantic source.
- [ ] Each represented obligation identifies its trigger, exact occurrence, expected event, responsible actor, and fairness basis.
- [ ] Progress by another occurrence cannot satisfy the represented obligation.
- [ ] `WF`, `SF`, no fairness, or another assumption is justified per property from its enabledness behavior and authority boundary.
- [ ] No fairness assumption is introduced solely to make a future TLC check pass.
- [ ] Every model-only identity is documented as an abstraction and does not create an implementation or API requirement.
- [ ] Unresolved product decisions remain blocked and are not encoded as accepted semantics.
- [ ] The generated invariant mapping remains mechanically derived and fresh.
- [ ] No property or invariant is promoted to `modeled` or `checked` without the executable model and matching evidence required by repository governance.
- [ ] Existing repository integrity validation remains green.

## Validation

After any repository change, run the repository-required sequence, including regeneration of the formal mapping:

```bash
.venv/bin/python scripts/render-formal-mapping.py
.venv/bin/python scripts/tests/test-adr-metadata.py
.venv/bin/python scripts/adr-metadata.py check
.venv/bin/python scripts/check-formal-traceability.py
git diff --check
```

Also run any stable metamodel or result-evidence test command introduced by #1.

## Non-goals

- Deciding what liveness TURNLOCK promises.
- Amending product semantics without an accepted ADR and synchronized normative artifacts.
- Selecting a concrete runtime identity mechanism.
- Implementing Rust, Cargo, runtime, API, packaging, or release behavior.
- Claiming successful formal verification.
- Writing the complete executable TLA+ model as part of this issue unless separately authorized by an accepted repository decision and scope.

## Authoritative references
