value.body:
## Problem

TURNLOCK's accepted product intent supports iterative refinement from actual execution behavior, and ADR-019 allows an explicitly responsible actor outside TURNLOCK core policy to evaluate executions and author a refined workflow. Reliable empirical optimization may eventually require that differences between executions be evaluated under conditions that make the comparison credible for the property being optimized.

Current authority does not decide whether the first runtime architecture must preserve enough provenance about relevant governing conditions to keep that future capability possible.

The risk is not merely that an old execution may lack a convenient metric. Some early architecture choices could irreversibly erase which conditions governed an execution, for example if:

```text
an active execution silently follows whichever workflow artifact exists later

effective model or execution-resource configuration is not distinguishable

effective input or context provenance is lost

important external dependencies remain invisible at TURNLOCK's boundary

execution conditions are mixed with outputs without provenance

execution facts are retained without correspondence to the conditions
under which they occurred
```

If future reliable optimization depends on comparisons whose validity is relative to those conditions, information discarded during execution may not be reconstructable later.

This Issue asks whether that risk creates a **present product-intent obligation**. It does not assert that it does.

## Product motivation

The product hypothesis to examine is:

```text
future reliable workflow optimization
        ↓
credible evaluation of differences
        ↓
property-relative execution comparability
        ↓
knowledge or control of relevant determinants
        ↓
possible present constraints on what TURNLOCK must distinguish,
preserve, expose, or avoid irreversibly discarding
```

A potentially useful framing is:

```text
reproducibility of relevant conditions
        ↓
property-relative comparability
        ↓
credible evaluation
        ↓
reliable optimization
```

This framing does **not** imply reproducible outputs, identical traces, deterministic scheduling, deterministic agents, or a current comparison contract. It is a question about architectural readiness for externally owned evaluation and optimization, not ownership of that policy.

## Discovery statement

### Statement

Current authority does not determine whether TURNLOCK must preserve sufficient provenance about execution-governing conditions from its first runtime architecture so that future property-relative comparability, sufficient reproducibility, and reliable workflow optimization are not made irreversibly impossible.

### Source and evidence

The discovery arose while examining the future empirical evaluation and optimization ambition retained in `docs/vision/future-workflow-run-evaluation.md` against ADR-018's accepted minimum execution truth and ADR-019's accepted policy boundary. The vision note identifies possible determinants, property-relative comparability, reproducibility profiles, and execution evidence, but explicitly has no normative authority.

### Existing authority

The current normative specification and accepted ADRs establish that:

- ADR-018 and `TL-INV-033` require every **completed** workflow execution to expose enough actual TURNLOCK-visible behavior for practical understanding, evaluation, and iterative refinement;
- that minimum concerns what actually happened at TURNLOCK's semantic boundary and does not by itself imply a `Run`, `RunSpec`, workflow revision identity, replay, cross-run comparability, reproducibility level, experiment framework, or automatic optimization;
- ADR-019 and `TL-INV-034` keep evaluation objectives, metrics, superiority relations, experiment policy, and optimization policy outside TURNLOCK core;
- workflow-owned control permits probabilistic, nondeterministic, externally dependent, and event-driven results without promising identical outputs, paths, schedules, or traces;
- ADR-020 and `TL-INV-026` use **context provenance** for the narrower accepted rule governing the initial cognitive context of workflow-declared independent agents; they do not establish a general execution-condition provenance concept; and
- the specification explicitly leaves replay, cross-run comparability, reproducibility profiles, execution proofs, workflow-definition binding, detailed inspection facts, and retention open.

Issue #12 is closed and its outcome is authoritative only through accepted ADR-019 and the synchronized normative specification. Its Issue text remains work/provenance history, not product authority.

No current authority conflict is identified.

### Semantic disposition

**B — `decision-required`**

Primary layer: **product / semantic intent**.

Repository layer mapping:

- `normative-contract`;
- `decision-history`;
- conditional downstream `architecture-or-implementation` and `integration-or-conformance` consequences if an obligation is accepted;
- possible `formal-model-or-analysis` consequences only after product intent is resolved and formal applicability is separately assessed; and
- `repository-governance-or-documentation` for this Issue as the durable work/provenance record.

This is not A / `derived-from-existing-authority`. ADR-018 requires sufficient inspectability of actual TURNLOCK-visible behavior after completed execution, but explicitly declines to derive cross-run comparability, reproducibility, workflow revision identity, replay, or a stronger execution record. ADR-019 establishes who does not own optimization policy, not which execution conditions must remain knowable to that external actor.

At least these architectures remain compatible with current authority:

1. expose only the accepted minimum execution truth and allow old executions to be unusable for later comparison profiles;
2. semantically distinguish some governing conditions without requiring post-run persistence;
3. support capture or later exposure of selected conditions without a universal comparability guarantee;
4. retain a stronger core execution record; or
5. provide stronger guarantees only through explicit profiles or layers.

Choosing among them would add or select product meaning that current authority does not uniquely entail.

### Related discoveries or consequences

- Issue #4 owns workflow-definition binding for active invocations. Its eventual decision may determine whether the governing definition can be known, but it does not settle the broader determinant/provenance question here.
- ADR-018 and Issue #13 own minimum completed-execution inspectability. This Issue must not broaden #13's scope or silently equate execution truth with governing-condition provenance.
- ADR-019 resolves policy ownership and remains unchanged.
- Any accepted obligation may later create separately classified specification, ADR, invariant, formalization, architecture, conformance, privacy, or retention work.

### Required authority

An explicit product decision through a new accepted ADR. If it changes normative product meaning, synchronize the normative specification and every actually affected traceability or generated artifact under repository governance. This Issue records the question and its provenance; creating or closing it does not accept an answer.

### Next action

Adjudicate whether future optimization readiness creates a present TURNLOCK obligation, select the weakest justified semantic boundary, and only then classify invariant, formal, architecture, implementation, and conformance consequences separately.

## Why this is architectural now even though the features are future

Replay, experiment management, comparison APIs, and optimization algorithms can be added later. Provenance that was never semantically distinguished or was irreversibly discarded during execution may not be recoverable later.

The timing question is therefore narrower than feature timing:

> Must v1 avoid architecture choices that destroy information needed for credible future comparison, even if v1 exposes no replay, comparison, reproducibility, experiment, or optimization feature?

A positive answer could constrain the runtime's semantic boundaries without requiring any specific persistence or telemetry mechanism. A negative answer could legitimately accept that future profiles offer weaker guarantees for historical executions. Current authority permits both answers.

## Important conceptual distinctions

### Reproducibility is not identical output

Future comparison may be statistically valid or valid relative to a property even when LLMs, agents, external dependencies, schedules, outputs, and traces vary.

This Issue must not assume:

```text
same inputs → same output
same invocation → identical trace
deterministic scheduling
deterministic agents
```

The relevant question may concern reproducibility or knowledge of selected conditions, not reproduction of every result.

### Comparability is property-relative

The decision must examine whether a comparison should have the form:

```text
Are executions E1 and E2 comparable for property P?
```

rather than claiming that two executions are globally comparable. Determinants relevant to control-path conformance may differ from those relevant to quality, latency, cost, retrieval performance, or model behavior.

### Provenance is not persistence

These obligations are distinct and must not be collapsed:

```text
TURNLOCK semantically distinguishes or knows a fact
TURNLOCK makes a fact exposable
TURNLOCK captures a fact
TURNLOCK persists a fact
TURNLOCK retains a fact indefinitely
```

A present readiness obligation might require none, some, or all of these. The Issue presupposes no level.

### Architecture readiness is not replay

Avoiding irreversible information loss does not itself require replay semantics, a snapshot system, a canonical execution object, or reconstruction of an execution.

### Governing conditions are not execution outcomes

ADR-018 principally asks enough about:

```text
what happened?
```

This Issue asks whether future credible comparison may additionally require enough about:

```text
under which relevant governing conditions did it happen?
```

The questions can overlap, but one must not be derived from or merged into the other without explicit reasoning and authority.

### Provenance terminology is not yet canonical

`execution-condition provenance`, `causal provenance`, `reproducibility readiness`, and `comparability readiness` are candidate descriptions only. The normative terminology registry currently defines `execution inspectability` and uses narrower `context provenance` for independent-agent initial context. Resolution must evaluate terminology against that registry and must not create a canonical term merely by using it in this Issue.

## Relationship to existing work

### Issue #4 — workflow-definition binding

#4 decides which workflow definition governs an active invocation when the source artifact changes, preserving alternatives such as stable binding, live observation, and explicit dynamic mutation. This Issue neither reopens nor decides those alternatives.

The relationship is that knowing which definition governed relevant execution points may be one determinant for some future comparison property. #4 can resolve binding semantics without deciding a general provenance/readiness obligation; this Issue can establish a broader boundary without choosing #4's binding rule.

### ADR-018 / Issue #13 — execution inspectability

ADR-018 and `TL-INV-033` establish minimum completed-execution truth. #13 separately owns the exact minimum fact categories, sufficiency rules, non-completed outcomes, and any availability, retention, access, or privacy obligations needed to apply that accepted invariant.

This Issue introduces a different pressure—possible provenance of relevant governing conditions for future cross-execution evaluation. It must not expand #13, define its fact set, or assume that every governing condition is already part of execution inspectability.

### ADR-019 / resolved Issue #12

ADR-019 keeps evaluation and optimization **policy** outside TURNLOCK core. This Issue does not challenge that boundary.

Even if a provenance/readiness obligation is accepted, TURNLOCK core would not thereby define:

```text
what "better" means
objective functions
evaluation metrics
superiority relations
optimizer policy
```

The question is only whether the runtime must preserve certain execution conditions so that an explicitly responsible external actor or ordinary authored workflow can later evaluate or optimize credibly.

## Candidate determinant categories

The decision should evaluate, without automatically requiring, categories such as:

- governing workflow definition or revision;
- explicit inputs;
- effective execution-resource or model configuration;
- context provenance where TURNLOCK controls it;
- relevant policies or configuration;
- runtime-visible environment facts;
- observations of relevant external dependencies; and
- concurrency or scheduling facts when they affect property `P`.

For each category, distinguish:

1. facts TURNLOCK controls;
2. facts TURNLOCK can observe but does not control;
3. facts an adapter or execution resource may expose;
4. facts intrinsically outside TURNLOCK's observation or control; and
5. facts whose collection would create unacceptable privacy, security, cost, or coupling.

No category is accepted merely because it appears above.

## Candidate product boundaries / alternatives

### Alternative A — no present obligation

TURNLOCK provides only the currently accepted execution inspectability minimum. Future comparison or reproducibility profiles define their own requirements, even if historical executions cannot satisfy them.

### Alternative B — forward-compatible semantic provenance

TURNLOCK provides no replay or comparability contract, but core semantics require selected TURNLOCK-visible governing conditions to remain distinguished or capturable so future capabilities are not structurally precluded.

### Alternative C — stronger core execution record

TURNLOCK accepts a stronger universal obligation to make enough relevant governing conditions reconstructable for specified future classes of comparison. The decision would still need to define scope without prematurely selecting a record schema or storage mechanism.

### Alternative D — profiled or layered guarantees

The universal core remains weak while explicit workflow or execution profiles require additional provenance or reproducibility levels. The decision must state whether the core still owes any readiness floor needed to implement such profiles later.

### Alternative E — another explicitly bounded contract

A different boundary may be accepted if it states the minimum observable obligation, the information-loss trade-off, and why it neither imports optimization policy into core nor pre-decides implementation mechanisms.

These alternatives are open. Creating this Issue selects none of them.

## Decision questions

1. Is future workflow optimizability a sufficiently durable product objective to constrain the runtime architecture now?
2. Is there a general obligation not to irreversibly destroy TURNLOCK-visible information needed for future property-relative comparability?
3. What does `relevant determinant` mean at TURNLOCK's semantic boundary, and who identifies relevance to property `P`?
4. Which candidate determinant categories may matter without becoming universally required?
5. Which information can TURNLOCK reasonably control, observe, distinguish, or expose, and which is intrinsically outside its boundary?
6. Must comparability always be stated relative to a property `P` rather than globally?
7. Would any accepted provenance obligation require only semantic distinction, run-time availability, capture capability, post-execution exposure, minimum persistence, or another level?
8. Would an obligation apply only to completed executions or also to failed, cancelled, and interrupted executions?
9. Which v1 architecture choices, if any, must be prohibited because they would make the capability impossible to add later?
10. Which decisions can safely be deferred without irreversible information loss?
11. Which candidate terminology best fits the existing normative vocabulary without creating a premature canonical term?
12. After product intent is resolved, is the consequence a new invariant, a clarification of an existing invariant, or only a non-normative architecture decision?
13. How should privacy, security, cost, and unavailable external facts bound any obligation without silently nullifying it?

## Required authority and synchronization

Resolution requires a new ADR-level product decision. The decision must identify whether it:

- changes or clarifies the normative contract;
- amends the effect of ADR-018 or leaves it independent;
- introduces a distinct invariant only after the repository's invariant-admission test;
- affects `formal/verification.yaml` only where formal applicability is established;
- creates downstream architecture, implementation, integration, conformance, privacy, or retention work; and
- requires updates to non-normative future-work notes solely to keep their stated baseline accurate.

No TLA+ state, identifier, action, property, fairness premise, or bound may be introduced solely because it is convenient for representing this question.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A new ADR explicitly selects and justifies a product boundary equivalent to Alternative A, B, C, D, E, or a clearly stated refinement.
- [ ] The decision states whether future optimizability creates any present obligation and why that conclusion follows from accepted product intent rather than implementation preference.
- [ ] The decision states whether comparability is property-relative and how determinant relevance is assigned without importing evaluation policy into TURNLOCK core.
- [ ] The decision distinguishes semantic knowledge, exposability, capture, persistence, and indefinite retention.
- [ ] The decision distinguishes reproducibility of relevant conditions from deterministic or identical outputs, schedules, and traces.
- [ ] The decision identifies what TURNLOCK can and cannot reasonably control or observe.
- [ ] The decision evaluates the candidate determinant categories without automatically making all of them required.
- [ ] The decision addresses completed, failed, cancelled, and interrupted executions explicitly or records independently scoped follow-up decisions.
- [ ] The decision identifies any v1 choices that must be avoided now and which capabilities can safely be deferred.
- [ ] The decision evaluates candidate terminology against the normative terminology registry without treating Issue wording as canonical.
- [ ] The relationship to ADR-018, ADR-019, #4, #12, and #13 is explicit, with no silent reopening or scope transfer.
- [ ] The decision explicitly confirms that it does not establish replay, a `RunSpec`, identical-output reproducibility, universal persistence, workflow hashing, repository snapshots, or TURNLOCK-owned optimization policy unless one of those is independently proposed, classified, and accepted.
- [ ] Only after product intent is resolved, invariant admission and formal applicability are classified separately.
- [ ] Any accepted semantic change is synchronized across the normative specification, decision history, formal traceability, and generated projections actually affected.
- [ ] Repository-required generation and validation pass for every eventual repository change.

## Dependencies / coordination

- **Coordination with #4:** its binding decision may supply or constrain one candidate determinant. Neither Issue should decide the other's broader scope.
- **Coordination with #13:** preserve #13's minimum-inspectability scope. If either decision creates genuine overlap, record the exact derived dependency instead of assuming one now.
- **Resolved provenance #12:** ADR-019, not #12's Issue text, controls the evaluation/optimization-policy boundary.
- **ADR-018:** accepted baseline for completed-execution inspectability; it does not currently entail the obligation investigated here.
- No parent, sub-issue, blocked-by, or blocking relationship is currently asserted. Reassess native relationships only if adjudication exposes a concrete prerequisite.

Because this is an open product-semantic decision, it belongs in `Status: Backlog`, `Phase: Specification`, `Kind: Finding`, `Priority: P0` under the current Engineering Project profile. These fields govern work only and accept no product semantics.

## Non-goals

Creating or resolving the question as currently scoped does not decide or require:

- identical-output reproducibility;
- deterministic LLM or agent behavior;
- deterministic concurrency or scheduling;
- replay semantics;
- a `Run`, `RunSpec`, `RunProof`, or event schema;
- run IDs or activation IDs as a concrete public API;
- UUIDs, hashes, Git SHAs, or content addressing;
- repository or filesystem snapshots;
- full agent conversation capture;
- private reasoning capture;
- recording every tool call;
- a storage backend;
- retention duration;
- telemetry architecture, including OpenTelemetry;
- an experiment framework;
- evaluation metrics;
- objective functions;
- optimizer algorithms;
- automatic workflow mutation;
- TURNLOCK-owned optimization policy; or
- TLA+ modeling structures introduced solely for convenience.

It also does not assert that all relevant determinants can be known, controlled, captured, persisted, or retained.

## Validation for the eventual decision

- Re-read then-current normative authority and accepted ADRs.
- Revalidate live outcomes and relationships for #4, #12, and #13.
- Apply discovery classification separately to the product decision and each downstream mechanism or formal consequence.
- Confirm that normative wording states the weakest accepted obligation and does not encode a storage, identifier, hashing, snapshot, telemetry, or replay mechanism.
- Run the complete repository generation and validation sequence required by `AGENTS.md` for any eventual repository changes.
- Confirm that no formal-verification claim is made without scope-bound evidence.

## Authoritative and non-normative references

### Authoritative

- [TURNLOCK normative specification](https://github.com/fanilosendrison/turnlock-rust/blob/main/docs/specification/turnlock-spec.md)
- [ADR-018 — require completed workflow execution inspectability](https://github.com/fanilosendrison/turnlock-rust/blob/main/docs/adr/adr-018-require-completed-workflow-execution-inspectability.md)
- [ADR-019 — keep evaluation and optimization policy outside TURNLOCK core](https://github.com/fanilosendrison/turnlock-rust/blob/main/docs/adr/adr-019-keep-evaluation-and-optimization-policy-outside-turnlock-core.md)
- [ADR-020 — define independent-agent context provenance](https://github.com/fanilosendrison/turnlock-rust/blob/main/docs/adr/adr-020-define-independent-agent-context-provenance.md)
- [`formal/verification.yaml`](https://github.com/fanilosendrison/turnlock-rust/blob/main/formal/verification.yaml) — intended traceability only, not verification evidence
- [Turnlock-Rust discovery-classification profile](https://github.com/fanilosendrison/turnlock-rust/blob/main/docs/repository-governance/turnlock-rust-discovery-classification.md)

### Work/provenance and non-normative context

- [Issue #4 — workflow-definition binding](https://github.com/fanilosendrison/turnlock-rust/issues/4) — open work record; no accepted semantics
- [Issue #12 — evaluation/optimization ownership](https://github.com/fanilosendrison/turnlock-rust/issues/12) — closed provenance; resolved by ADR-019
- [Issue #13 — minimum completed-execution inspectability semantics](https://github.com/fanilosendrison/turnlock-rust/issues/13) — open work record; no new authority
- [Future workflow run-evaluation design space](https://github.com/fanilosendrison/turnlock-rust/blob/main/docs/vision/future-workflow-run-evaluation.md) — explicitly non-normative
value.title: Product intent: decide whether TURNLOCK must preserve execution-condition provenance for future comparability and optimization

value.body:
## Problem

ADR-024 and `TL-INV-036` now require effective execution conditions that TURNLOCK selects, binds, explicitly supplies, or resolves to remain semantically distinguished, attributable to the execution scopes they govern, and exposable or capturable at TURNLOCK's semantic boundary.

Current authority does not determine what a consumer must actually be able to obtain at that boundary when the underlying effective condition is sensitive, confidential, non-disclosable, unavailable for direct exposure, or unsafe to reveal.

For an ordinary condition, direct exposure may appear straightforward:

```text
model = model-X
temperature = 0.2
```

For protected conditions, direct value disclosure may be impermissible:

```text
credential
secret configuration
private context
authorization material
sensitive environment value
provider-internal configuration
other protected execution condition
```

ADR-024 prohibits keeping the attribution only in inaccessible transient state, but it does not state whether conformance requires the exact value, a semantically sufficient representation, evidence about identity or difference, a known-but-non-disclosable state, or another boundary contract. Selecting among those possibilities changes the observable meaning of `exposable or capturable`; it is not merely a serialization, UI, or security-library choice.

This Issue asks:

> **What must be available at TURNLOCK's semantic boundary for effective execution-condition provenance to satisfy `TL-INV-036` when the governing condition's value is sensitive, non-disclosable, unavailable for direct exposure, or unsafe to reveal?**

Creating this Issue accepts no answer.

## Discovery statement

### Statement

Current authority does not uniquely determine the minimum consumer-visible semantic information required to satisfy `TL-INV-036` when TURNLOCK knows or resolves an effective governing condition but direct disclosure of its underlying value is constrained.

### Source and evidence

The discovery follows from applying ADR-024's accepted exposure/capture boundary to protected conditions. ADR-024 deliberately separates semantic distinction, attribution, exposability, capture, persistence, and retention, and rejects concrete representation mechanisms. It establishes that attribution cannot remain only inaccessible transient adapter state, while leaving the detailed disclosure and evidence semantics unstated.

### Existing authority

Current authority establishes that:

- ADR-024 and `TL-INV-036` require effective conditions TURNLOCK selects, binds, explicitly supplies, or resolves to remain attributable to governed execution scopes and exposable or capturable at an execution boundary;
- ADR-024 does not require TURNLOCK itself to capture, persist, or retain that information, and selects no identifier, event, storage, hashing, snapshot, telemetry, or UI mechanism;
- conditions outside TURNLOCK's observation or control may remain unavailable or unknown;
- `unknown` must not be represented as `known-equal` or as evidence of no relevant difference;
- ADR-019 and `TL-INV-034` keep evaluation objectives, determinant relevance, comparison judgments, superiority relations, and optimization policy outside TURNLOCK core;
- ADR-018 and `TL-INV-033` separately require sufficient actual completed-execution behavior to remain inspectable; and
- Issue #13 owns the detailed minimum execution-inspectability contract, including fact sufficiency and possible availability, retention, access, privacy, and non-completed-outcome semantics.

No current authoritative source defines whether `TL-INV-036` requires exact-value disclosure, which non-value representation is sufficient, whether any authorized consumer must be able to obtain one, or whether known-but-protected may satisfy the boundary with existence-only provenance.

No authority conflict is identified.

### Semantic disposition

**B — `decision-required`**

Primary layer: **product / semantic intent** mapped to `normative-contract`.

Affected or potentially affected repository layers:

- `normative-contract`;
- `decision-history`;
- `integration-or-conformance` for adapters and execution resources that can or cannot expose protected conditions;
- `architecture-or-implementation` only for later replaceable realization mechanisms;
- security and privacy consequences within the applicable semantic, conformance, and policy boundaries;
- possible `formal-model-or-analysis` consequences only if independently applicable after the product decision; and
- `repository-governance-or-documentation` for this Issue as a work/provenance record.

This is not A / `derived-from-existing-authority`. ADR-024 requires a real exposure/capture boundary but intentionally does not define a representation, disclosure level, equality evidence, authorization model, or capture payload. At least the following observable contracts remain compatible with its current wording:

1. exact effective-value exposure is required;
2. a non-value semantic representation can suffice;
3. exposing only known-but-non-disclosable status can suffice;
4. disclosure guarantees are layered or profiled; or
5. another bounded contract distinguishes protected provenance from both plaintext disclosure and unknown.

These choices provide materially different security, privacy, auditability, and future-comparison capabilities. Selecting one would add or clarify product semantics not uniquely entailed today.

### Related discoveries or consequences

- ADR-024 / `TL-INV-036` remain accepted and are not reopened.
- Issue #13 may share access, privacy, and availability concerns, but it governs execution inspectability under `TL-INV-033`, not effective-condition provenance under `TL-INV-036`.
- Future comparability or reproducibility contracts may require stronger equality/difference evidence, but they remain separate decisions.
- Concrete protection, representation, storage, and access-control mechanisms remain separately classifiable.

### Required authority

An explicit ADR-level product decision is required before any disclosure/evidence minimum is claimed as TURNLOCK semantics. If accepted product meaning changes or clarifies `TL-INV-036`, synchronize the normative specification, decision history, formal traceability, terminology, and generated projections actually affected. Apply the invariant-admission test only after the product decision; this Issue creates no invariant.

### Next action

Adjudicate the weakest mechanism-independent semantic information that must be available at the boundary for protected effective conditions, while preserving ADR-024, ADR-019, honest unknown semantics, and independently owned security/privacy policy.

## Why this is a product-semantic question

The question is not how bytes are encrypted, identifiers are generated, values are redacted, or widgets display secrets. It determines whether an implementation can claim meaningful effective execution-condition provenance when the consumer receives:

```text
the exact value
vs
an identity-bearing representation
vs
some equality/difference evidence
vs
known-but-non-disclosable status
vs
no usable representation
```

Those alternatives change the observable product contract. An implementation that knows a condition but never allows any authorized consumer to obtain any exploitable representation may satisfy a nominal reading of "provenance exists" while defeating ADR-024's prohibition on inaccessible transient attribution. Conversely, requiring plaintext values universally could make conformance incompatible with legitimate confidentiality and least-disclosure requirements.

The decision must adjudicate, rather than presuppose, the following alternatives:

```text
exact-value exposure is required for boundary conformance
vs
meaningful provenance can be preserved without exact-value exposure
```

Regardless of that choice, security or privacy must not become permission to erase or misrepresent a governing relationship. Whether, and if so how, meaningful provenance can be preserved without disclosing the underlying value remains open.

## Sensitive-condition motivating examples

The decision should analyze examples such as:

```text
provider credential selected for a resource
secret workflow configuration
private context explicitly supplied by workflow semantics
authorization material governing an operation
sensitive environment value resolved by TURNLOCK
provider-internal effective configuration surfaced to an adapter
```

For each example, distinguish without pre-accepting a taxonomy:

```text
unknown to TURNLOCK
known to TURNLOCK but protected from disclosure
known to TURNLOCK and safely disclosable
known or observable through an adapter but not selected/resolved by TURNLOCK
```

The universal scope of ADR-024 remains conditions TURNLOCK selects, binds, explicitly supplies, or resolves. This Issue does not automatically extend `TL-INV-036` to every condition merely observable by an adapter or resource.

## Important conceptual distinctions

The eventual decision must keep all of the following distinct.

### Condition existence

```text
a condition governed execution scope S
```

### Condition identity

```text
which effective condition or condition instance governed S?
```

### Condition value

```text
what was the exact underlying value?
```

### Condition origin or resolution provenance

```text
where did the condition come from or how was it resolved?
```

### Equality or difference evidence

```text
can a consumer establish that two executions used the same
or different relevant condition?
```

### Consumer-visible representation

```text
what information is actually available at TURNLOCK's semantic boundary?
```

### Authorization

```text
which consumer may access which part of that representation?
```

`TL-INV-036` must not be presumed to require all these levels. The decision must state which minimum, if any, belongs to effective execution-condition provenance and which levels remain separate.

Additional distinctions and non-assumptions to preserve:

```text
provenance does not currently entail plaintext disclosure
security or privacy != permission to discard provenance
known-but-protected != unknown
provenance representation != cross-run comparability proof
condition identity != condition value
capture != persistence or retention
equality evidence != evaluator judgment about relevance to property P
```

## Relationship to ADR-024 / TL-INV-036

This Issue does not reopen the accepted provenance floor. The following remain fixed:

```text
TURNLOCK-selected/bound/explicitly-supplied/resolved effective conditions
must remain attributable to the execution scopes they govern

attribution must not exist only in inaccessible transient state

an execution-boundary means of exposure or capture must exist
```

The only open question here is:

```text
what semantic information must that boundary make available
for the obligation to remain meaningful under disclosure constraints?
```

A future decision must neither weaken ADR-024 into nominal hidden provenance nor strengthen it silently into universal disclosure of underlying values.

ADR-024's distinction between unknown and known attribution also remains accepted. This Issue may need to distinguish `known-but-protected` from `unknown-to-TURNLOCK`, but listing that candidate state does not accept it as canonical terminology or required semantics.

## Relationship to Issue #13

Issue #13 owns the detailed execution-inspectability contract under ADR-018 / `TL-INV-033`:

```text
actual execution behavior
minimum fact sufficiency
completed/non-completed outcome inspection
availability
retention
access
privacy
```

This discovery concerns a different normative object under ADR-024 / `TL-INV-036`:

```text
effective governing-condition attribution
and the consumer-visible meaning of its exposure/capture boundary
```

The two may share access, privacy, and availability concerns, but shared concerns do not merge their obligations. This Issue must determine whether:

1. disclosure/capture semantics remain an independent product decision;
2. specific access, privacy, or availability consequences should later be coordinated with #13; or
3. a narrowly identified sub-question becomes derivable from #13 after #13 is resolved.

No scope is transferred to #13 now, and no native dependency is asserted without a concrete blocking relationship.

## Relationship to future comparability and reproducibility

A future comparison contract may ask what evidence establishes that two executions used the same or different condition for property `P`. This Issue does not answer that question.

It may determine whether the provenance boundary must preserve enough semantic information for a future actor to attempt such an assessment. It must not define:

```text
which conditions matter to P
an equality algorithm
a comparison proof
whether two executions are comparable
reproducibility levels
replay semantics
```

ADR-019 remains controlling: the responsible external evaluator selects property `P`, decides determinant relevance, and judges whether available evidence supports comparison or superiority.

## Candidate alternatives

### Alternative A — exact-value exposure required

Effective execution-condition provenance is fully satisfied only if the exact effective value can be captured at the semantic boundary. This preserves maximal direct information but may conflict with confidentiality, least disclosure, provider restrictions, or security obligations.

This Issue does not accept the alternative.

### Alternative B — semantic representation sufficient

A semantically sufficient representation may satisfy provenance without exposing the raw value. The decision would still need to define the minimum meaning of that representation without choosing its encoding or mechanism.

This Issue does not accept the alternative.

### Alternative C — known-but-non-disclosable state

TURNLOCK may preserve attribution while exposing only that a known protected condition governed the scope. The underlying value remains inaccessible. The decision would need to determine whether this is meaningful provenance, when it is sufficient, and how it differs from unknown.

This Issue does not accept the alternative.

### Alternative D — layered or profiled disclosure

Core semantics establish a minimum representation while profiles, integrations, or authorized contexts offer stronger disclosure or evidence. The decision must still define the universal floor and cannot use layering to make `TL-INV-036` nominal.

This Issue does not accept the alternative.

### Alternative E — another bounded semantic contract

Another contract may be accepted if it simultaneously preserves effective-condition provenance meaning, security/privacy, mechanism independence, and future comparability readiness without defining implementation machinery.

No alternative is selected by creating this Issue.

## Decision questions

1. What does `exposable or capturable` mean under `TL-INV-036`?
2. Must the effective value itself be exposable, or can a semantically sufficient representation satisfy provenance?
3. Can `TL-INV-036` be satisfied when TURNLOCK knows the effective value but deliberately does not disclose it?
4. If so, what minimum information must remain available—for example existence, identity, origin, an opaque reference, equality/difference evidence, or classification as known-but-non-disclosable?
5. Does the ability to establish that two executions used the same condition belong to `TL-INV-036`, or only to a future comparability contract?
6. Must non-disclosure be represented differently from absence of knowledge?
7. For a sensitive condition, does capture mean capturing the value, a reference, evidence, only the attribution's existence, or another semantic object?
8. Which responsibilities belong to core semantics, access control, privacy policy, secret management, adapter conformance, persistence, or higher-level tooling?
9. Is an implementation conforming if it knows a condition but never allows any authorized consumer to obtain an exploitable representation of its attribution?
10. How can a security contract avoid converting `known-but-protected` into semantically misleading `unknown`?
11. Should disclosure protections be universal or specific to condition categories, integrations, capabilities, or profiles?
12. Does resolution require a new invariant, clarification of `TL-INV-036`, only a conformance contract, or multiple separately classified decisions?
13. Who or what counts as an authorized consumer at this semantic boundary, and is that itself a separate access-policy decision?
14. What minimum must remain mechanism-independent so that provider or harness limitations are reported as capability/conformance facts rather than silently weakening provenance?

## Required authority and synchronization

Resolution requires a new accepted ADR-level product decision unless a complete derivation from then-current authority is established during adjudication. The resolution must:

- preserve ADR-024's accepted attribution and exposure/capture floor;
- preserve ADR-019's external evaluation/optimization-policy boundary;
- preserve `unknown != known-equal`;
- identify whether it clarifies `TL-INV-036`, entails a distinct invariant, or creates only a conformance boundary;
- apply the repository invariant-admission test before creating any new `TL-INV-*` identity;
- assess formal applicability separately from product meaning;
- synchronize the normative specification, ADR history, formal traceability, terminology, and generated projections only where actually affected; and
- keep representation, protection, storage, and UI mechanisms replaceable unless independently required.

This Issue is a work/provenance record. It does not accept product semantics, amend ADR-024, or provide verification evidence.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A new ADR or complete authority derivation selects and justifies one mechanism-independent semantic boundary equivalent to Alternative A, B, C, D, E, or a clearly stated refinement.
- [ ] The decision defines the minimum consumer-visible meaning of `exposable or capturable` for sensitive or non-disclosable effective conditions.
- [ ] Condition existence, identity, value, origin/resolution provenance, equality/difference evidence, consumer-visible representation, and authorization are explicitly distinguished.
- [ ] The decision states whether and how known-but-protected differs from unknown-to-TURNLOCK without reopening `unknown != known-equal`.
- [ ] The decision explicitly states whether exact-value exposure is required and, if not, what makes non-value provenance meaningful; it never treats security/privacy as permission to discard or misrepresent an attribution.
- [ ] The decision states whether any authorized consumer must be able to obtain an exploitable representation and separates that semantic rule from access-policy mechanisms.
- [ ] The decision states whether equality/difference capability belongs to provenance, future comparability, a stronger profile, or another separately classified contract.
- [ ] ADR-024 / `TL-INV-036` remain in force and are neither weakened nor silently expanded into universal exact-value disclosure.
- [ ] ADR-019 / `TL-INV-034` remain in force; TURNLOCK does not select determinant relevance, judge comparability, or own evaluation/optimization policy.
- [ ] The relationship to #13 is explicitly resolved without automatically merging scopes.
- [ ] No hashing, identity, encryption, redaction, storage, telemetry, event, UI, or provider mechanism is made normative without a separate derivation.
- [ ] Any invariant consequence passes the repository admission test; no candidate automatically receives a new stable identity.
- [ ] Formal applicability is assessed separately, and no modeling structure becomes product semantics.
- [ ] Every accepted semantic change is synchronized across all actually affected authoritative, traceability, terminology, and generated artifacts.
- [ ] The complete repository generation and validation sequence passes for any eventual repository change.

## Dependencies / coordination

- **Authority baseline:** ADR-024 and `TL-INV-036`.
- **Policy boundary:** ADR-019 and `TL-INV-034`.
- **Coordination with #13:** shared access/privacy/availability concerns, distinct normative objects; no scope transfer or blocking relationship is asserted.
- **Coordination with #4:** only if workflow-definition disclosure constraints become a concrete instance after #4 selects the effective-definition binding semantics. This Issue does not decide binding.
- **Future work:** comparability, reproducibility, replay, canonical run models, and stronger evidence profiles remain independently decidable.
- No parent, sub-issue, blocked-by, or blocking relationship is currently established.

Under the current Engineering Project profile, this open product-semantic decision is classified `Status: Backlog`, `Phase: Specification`, `Kind: Finding`, `Priority: P0`. Priority protects the authority boundary; it does not accept an alternative or assert that another Issue is blocked.

## Non-goals

Creating or resolving this Issue as currently scoped does not decide or require:

- a hashing algorithm;
- content addressing;
- a UUID strategy;
- an opaque-ID format;
- an encryption algorithm;
- a secret store;
- key management;
- an ACL or RBAC model;
- a provider credential model;
- a telemetry backend;
- an event schema;
- a canonical `Run`, `RunSpec`, or `RunProof`;
- replay;
- a cross-run comparison algorithm or contract;
- a reproducibility profile;
- an equality algorithm;
- an optimizer;
- a storage backend;
- a retention duration;
- a UI representation;
- a redaction syntax;
- a logging format;
- OpenTelemetry;
- full context capture;
- private reasoning capture; or
- universal disclosure of secret values.

It also does not authorize treating a protected but TURNLOCK-known condition as unknown, prove that any representation establishes cross-run equality, or extend the universal provenance floor to all adapter-observable conditions.

## Validation for the eventual decision

- Re-read then-current normative authority, accepted ADRs, and live related Issues.
- Apply discovery classification separately to the product decision, access/privacy policy, adapter capability, representation mechanism, persistence mechanism, and any formal consequence.
- Confirm that the accepted wording defines the weakest sufficient observable contract without selecting a cryptographic, identifier, storage, telemetry, redaction, or UI mechanism.
- Run the complete repository generation and validation sequence from `AGENTS.md` for every eventual repository change.
- Confirm that no formal-verification claim is made without scope-bound evidence.

## Authoritative references

### Product authority

- [TURNLOCK normative specification](https://github.com/fanilosendrison/turnlock-rust/blob/main/docs/specification/turnlock-spec.md), especially §§0.13B–0.13D, 2.9–2.10, 3.31–3.34, 4, 5.15–5.17, 6, and 7
- [ADR-018 — Require completed workflow execution inspectability](https://github.com/fanilosendrison/turnlock-rust/blob/main/docs/adr/adr-018-require-completed-workflow-execution-inspectability.md)
- [ADR-019 — Keep evaluation and optimization policy outside TURNLOCK core](https://github.com/fanilosendrison/turnlock-rust/blob/main/docs/adr/adr-019-keep-evaluation-and-optimization-policy-outside-turnlock-core.md)
- [ADR-024 — Preserve effective execution-condition provenance](https://github.com/fanilosendrison/turnlock-rust/blob/main/docs/adr/adr-024-preserve-effective-execution-condition-provenance.md)
- [Turnlock-Rust discovery-classification profile](https://github.com/fanilosendrison/turnlock-rust/blob/main/docs/repository-governance/turnlock-rust-discovery-classification.md)

### Work/provenance and non-normative context

- [Issue #4 — workflow-definition binding](https://github.com/fanilosendrison/turnlock-rust/issues/4) — open coordination only
- [Issue #13 — minimum completed-execution inspectability semantics](https://github.com/fanilosendrison/turnlock-rust/issues/13) — open, distinct normative object
