value.title: Specification: define disclosure and capture semantics for effective execution-condition provenance

value.body:
## Problem

ADR-024 and `TL-INV-036` require every effective execution condition that TURNLOCK selects, binds, explicitly supplies, or resolves to remain semantically distinguished, attributable to the execution scope it governs, and exposable or capturable at TURNLOCK's semantic boundary. ADR-025 further requires TURNLOCK-known condition-specific provenance not to be irreversibly substituted away before or during the required semantic-boundary capture opportunity, while leaving post-opportunity availability, persistence, and retention separately governed.

The phrase `required semantic-boundary capture opportunity` now carries a material temporal responsibility: before or during it, TURNLOCK cannot lose required provenance; after it, the current contract does not require continued availability. Current authority does not yet define what makes that opportunity sufficient rather than nominal.

In particular, it does not uniquely determine:

```text
when the opportunity begins or ends
what makes it genuinely usable
whether it must be externally accessible at the time
whether an instantaneous but genuinely realizable semantic-boundary opportunity can suffice
whether a conforming capture consumer can be connected or configured
what happens when no consumer is attached or authorized
whether availability must survive to a scope, invocation, or handoff boundary
when TURNLOCK may legitimately discard the provenance
```

This Issue asks:

> **What constitutes a sufficient semantic-boundary capture opportunity for `TL-INV-036`, and when may TURNLOCK cease to make effective execution-condition provenance capturable without violating that invariant?**

A complementary formulation is:

> **What minimum temporal and accessibility semantics make `capturable` a real TURNLOCK boundary contract rather than a transient internal implementation fact?**

Creating this Issue accepts no answer.

## Discovery statement

### Statement

Current authority requires effective execution-condition provenance to be capturable at TURNLOCK's semantic boundary but does not uniquely determine the minimum temporal and accessibility contract that makes the required capture opportunity real and usable before TURNLOCK may discard that provenance.

### Source and evidence

This discovery was exposed by auditing the resolution of Issue #16 through accepted ADR-025 and the synchronized normative specification. ADR-025 introduces the required boundary capture opportunity as the line between prohibited pre-opportunity provenance loss and separately governed post-opportunity availability, persistence, and retention. Neither ADR-024, ADR-025, `TL-INV-036`, nor the current specification defines the opportunity's beginning, end, usability, consumer realizability, delivery semantics, or discard boundary.

### Existing authority

Current authority establishes that:

- ADR-024 / `TL-INV-036` require effective conditions TURNLOCK selects, binds, explicitly supplies, or resolves to remain semantically distinguished, scope-attributable, and exposable or capturable at TURNLOCK's semantic boundary;
- the attribution cannot exist only as hidden transient adapter state or require reconstruction from later mutable state, human recollection, or agent recollection;
- ADR-025 requires a TURNLOCK-known protected condition to retain condition-specific provenance through the required boundary capture opportunity without requiring exact-value disclosure;
- consumer-visible disclosure differs from underlying provenance capture capability;
- later failure, cancellation, or interruption does not make an already-real governing relationship semantically nonexistent;
- ADR-018 / `TL-INV-033` separately govern minimum completed-execution inspectability;
- ADR-019 / `TL-INV-034` keep evaluation and optimization policy outside TURNLOCK core; and
- persistence, retention, authorization, cross-run identity, equality/difference evidence, replay, comparability, reproducibility, and concrete capture mechanisms remain unselected.

No authority conflict is identified. The missing boundary is not uniquely derivable from the current wording.

### Semantic disposition

**B — `decision-required`**

Primary layer: **product / semantic intent**, mapped to `normative-contract`.

Affected or potentially affected layers:

- `normative-contract`;
- `decision-history`;
- `integration-or-conformance`, because a runtime, adapter, or harness must eventually demonstrate a real boundary capability;
- `formal-model-or-analysis` only for an independently justified abstract temporal consequence after the product decision;
- `architecture-or-implementation` only for later replaceable realization mechanisms; and
- `repository-governance-or-documentation` for this Issue as a work/provenance record.

This is not `derived-from-existing-authority`. Current authority requires a real means of capture and rejects inaccessible transient provenance, but several observably different temporal contracts remain compatible with it: instantaneous boundary availability, availability through a realizable capture path, scope-bounded availability, invocation/lifecycle-bounded availability, profiled guarantees above a core floor, or another bounded contract. Selecting among them adds or clarifies product semantics.

### Related discoveries or consequences

- ADR-024, ADR-025, and `TL-INV-036` remain accepted and are not reopened.
- Issue #13 owns detailed execution-inspectability semantics under `TL-INV-033`; its availability, retention, access, privacy, and non-completed-outcome work may overlap but does not automatically own this provenance-specific pre-persistence boundary.
- Persistence, retention, authorization/privacy, delivery acknowledgment, adapter mechanics, and any formal abstraction remain separately classifiable.
- Concrete push/pull, callback/event, channel, queue, stream, buffer, log, storage, or transport choices are replaceable mechanisms, not answers supplied by this Issue.

### Required authority

Resolution probably requires a new accepted ADR-level semantic decision unless future analysis establishes a complete derivation from then-current authority. Only after that decision may the repository determine specification synchronization, invariant admission, formal applicability, conformance consequences, and implementation consequences.

### Next action

Adjudicate the weakest mechanism-independent temporal and accessibility contract that makes `capturable` falsifiable without silently requiring persistence, retention, successful delivery, or consumer acknowledgment.

## Why the ambiguity is product-semantic

The question determines when TURNLOCK has fulfilled an externally meaningful provenance obligation and may allow required information to become unavailable. That changes observable conformance, even if future implementations realize the boundary with different callbacks, events, channels, or other mechanisms.

A representation that exists only as inaccessible transient internal state is already excluded by ADR-024 and `TL-INV-036`; it is not an open candidate. What remains open is whether an opportunity that is instantaneous at the semantic boundary but genuinely realizable can suffice. A contract requiring TURNLOCK to retain provenance until a consumer successfully reads and acknowledges it would instead silently introduce persistence, backpressure, storage, and consumer-lifecycle semantics not accepted by ADR-024 or ADR-025.

The future decision must identify the minimum mechanism-independent contract between the already-accepted boundary requirement and that over-strong extreme. Implementation machinery cannot decide that product boundary by accident.

## Pathological nominal-capture example

```text
TURNLOCK knows condition C at time t

C governs scope S

runtime creates a condition-specific representation at time t

"capture opportunity" =
an instantaneous, inaccessible internal transition

t + epsilon:
representation discarded
```

A weak literal reading could claim:

```text
the representation existed during a boundary opportunity
therefore TL-INV-036 was satisfied
```

Yet no conforming consumer or integration ever had a realizable way to capture the provenance. Current authority rejects provenance kept only in inaccessible transient adapter state, but it does not yet define the temporal/accessibility test that distinguishes a real opportunity from this nominal one.

The opposite inference is also unauthorized: the example does not establish that TURNLOCK must retain the representation until actual receipt or acknowledgment.

## Important conceptual distinctions

### Capture opportunity is not persistence

```text
capture opportunity
→ minimum boundary contract through which another layer can acquire provenance

possible later persistence
→ whether acquired provenance survives after that boundary
```

The question is whether there was a genuine usable opportunity before discard, not how long provenance must be stored after execution.

### Capture opportunity is not retention

No wall-clock duration, timeout, process-lifetime rule, or retention period is implied. This Issue does not choose `one second`, `until process exit`, `30 days`, or any other duration.

### Capture opportunity is not disclosure

ADR-025 permits different consumer-visible views and does not universally require exact-value disclosure. A condition may remain `known and protected` during a conforming opportunity.

### Capture opportunity is not authorization policy

```text
a semantic capture path exists
!=
which consumer may use it
```

The eventual decision may identify an interaction with authorization, but this Issue selects no identity, role, tenant, ACL, RBAC, or capability model.

### Capture opportunity is not UI or log visibility

A conforming contract need not require CLI output, a log file, dashboard, event viewer, telemetry, or an ordinary inspection surface.

### Capture opportunity is not successful delivery

Making provenance genuinely capturable may differ from guaranteeing receipt. This Issue does not presume that a receiver must exist, remain available, accept delivery, or acknowledge it.

### Capture opportunity, persistence, and retention are separate responsibilities

```text
CAPTURE OPPORTUNITY
minimum boundary contract needed so another layer can acquire provenance

PERSISTENCE
whether acquired provenance survives after that boundary

RETENTION
how long persisted provenance remains available
```

### Capture opportunity is not future comparability

This Issue protects the reality of the opportunity to acquire the provenance defined by ADR-024 and ADR-025. It does not establish cross-run correlation, equality evidence, comparison APIs, determinant relevance to property `P`, reproducibility, or what a future evaluator can prove.

## Candidate dimensions to analyze

The eventual decision must analyze these dimensions separately without treating the examples as accepted semantics.

### Temporal availability

When must provenance be capturable—for example, at condition resolution, before the governed scope begins, while it is active, at scope completion, at invocation completion, or through another explicit semantic boundary?

### Consumer realizability

Must a conforming integration or consumer be capable of being connected or configured so it can receive the information at the relevant semantic time?

### Delivery semantics

Does an opportunity require only that TURNLOCK offer or emit the information, or must delivery or acknowledgment occur? No acknowledgment requirement is presumed.

### Consumer absence

What follows when no consumer exists, none is attached, the consumer is unavailable, or no consumer is authorized? Consumer absence must not be presumed either to discharge TURNLOCK automatically or to impose indefinite retention.

### Loss before observation

At what semantic event may the representation legitimately become unavailable without violating `TL-INV-036`?

### Failures

How does the opportunity apply when an invocation fails, is cancelled, or is interrupted after a condition governed part of execution? ADR-024 already preserves the semantic existence of the relationship; this Issue does not decide the complete failure lifecycle.

### Occurrence granularity

Must an opportunity exist for each governing-condition occurrence, or may occurrences be aggregated while still preserving the condition-specific and scope-attribution semantics accepted by ADR-025?

## Relationship to ADR-024

ADR-024 remains fully accepted. It decides:

```text
TURNLOCK-known effective-condition provenance
must reach an exposable or capturable semantic boundary
```

This Issue does not ask whether that boundary exists and does not reopen the provenance floor. It asks what makes the temporal opportunity at that already-required boundary sufficient.

## Relationship to ADR-025

ADR-025 remains fully accepted. It decides that exact-value disclosure is not universally required and that protection or redaction cannot irreversibly collapse TURNLOCK-known condition-specific provenance before or during the required boundary capture opportunity. It also keeps post-opportunity persistence and retention separate.

This discovery is revealed by that exact formulation: `required semantic-boundary capture opportunity` now determines when provenance loss changes from prohibited to potentially permissible, but the term is not yet sufficiently bounded. This Issue does not modify or reinterpret ADR-025.

## Relationship to TL-INV-036

`TL-INV-036` remains accepted. The reasonable starting hypothesis is that this discovery may clarify the satisfaction condition for `capturable at TURNLOCK's semantic boundary`, which `TL-INV-036` already owns. The eventual decision must nevertheless apply the repository invariant-admission test and determine whether it only clarifies `TL-INV-036` or establishes a sufficiently independent obligation for another invariant. This Issue creates, modifies, or reserves no `TL-INV-*` identity.

## Relationship to Issue #13

Issue #13 owns the detailed execution-inspectability contract under ADR-018 / `TL-INV-033`, including fact sufficiency, completed and non-completed outcomes, availability, retention, access, and privacy.

This discovery concerns a distinct normative object:

```text
minimum temporal/accessibility semantics required
for TL-INV-036 provenance capture to be real
before persistence or retention begins
```

The subjects can interact, especially around availability, access, privacy, and failed outcomes, but they are not automatically identical. A future resolution of either Issue may create a complete derivation or concrete coordination requirement for the other. No scope transfer or native blocked-by relationship is asserted now.

## Relationship to persistence and retention

The decision must preserve this boundary:

```text
real opportunity to acquire provenance
!=
post-boundary survival of acquired provenance
!=
duration of later availability
```

It may identify interactions among them, but it must not merge them by default or turn the capture floor into a mandatory persistent event queue.

## Candidate alternatives

No alternative is selected by creating this Issue.

### Alternative A — instantaneous boundary availability

A conforming representation exists at the relevant semantic boundary when the effective condition becomes governing for its execution scope, with no further temporal obligation. Analyze whether such an instantaneous but genuinely realizable opportunity can suffice.

### Alternative B — realizable capture boundary

TURNLOCK makes the representation available through a boundary that a conforming integration or consumer can effectively use at the semantically defined time. No post-boundary persistence is required. The meaning of `effectively use` remains open.

### Alternative C — scope-bounded availability

The representation remains capturable during a semantic interval tied to the governed scope, up to a future-selected scope boundary. This Issue selects no such boundary.

### Alternative D — invocation/lifecycle-bounded availability

The minimum interval is tied to a broader invocation or terminal-outcome lifecycle. This stronger option has material consequences and is not derived automatically.

### Alternative E — profile/layer-dependent capture guarantees

Core semantics define a non-nominal minimum, while profiles or integrations define stronger opportunities. A profile cannot make the core obligation nominal.

### Alternative F — another bounded semantic contract

Another mechanism-independent contract may be accepted if it makes `capturable` falsifiable without implying persistence by default, requiring consumer acknowledgment without authority, or selecting implementation machinery.

## Decision questions

1. What exactly constitutes a conforming `semantic-boundary capture opportunity`?
2. May an opportunity be instantaneous?
3. What minimum property makes a boundary genuinely realizable, given that a representation existing only in inaccessible transient internal state is already excluded?
4. Must a conforming implementation permit a capture consumer to be configured or attached before the information is lost?
5. Does an opportunity require only an emission/offer capability, or effective delivery or acknowledgment?
6. Does the absence of an active consumer change TURNLOCK's obligation?
7. Does the absence of an authorized consumer change the semantic obligation, or only access policy?
8. What event authorizes TURNLOCK to make the representation unavailable—for example after emission, scope start, scope end, invocation completion, or another semantic boundary?
9. Should the contract be expressed as an interval, event/handoff, capability available during an occurrence, or another abstraction?
10. How does the contract apply to conditions governing scopes that fail, are cancelled, or are interrupted?
11. Must a capture opportunity exist for every governing-condition occurrence, or may occurrences be aggregated?
12. Which responsibilities belong to core semantics, conformance, an adapter or harness, persistence, authorization/privacy, and implementation?
13. May a future layer choose not to capture the information without making the runtime non-conformant, provided a real opportunity exists?
14. Does the decision only clarify `TL-INV-036`, or create an independent obligation?
15. How can the contract be falsifiable without requiring TURNLOCK to guarantee successful delivery?
16. Which conditions make an opportunity realizable without selecting push versus pull, synchronous versus asynchronous delivery, or any concrete transport?

## Required authority

Resolution probably requires a new ADR-level product decision unless a complete derivation from then-current accepted authority is established. The decision must preserve ADR-024 and ADR-025, identify the weakest sufficient semantic boundary, and keep mechanisms replaceable.

Only after the product decision may the repository determine separately:

```text
normative specification synchronization
whether TL-INV-036 is clarified
whether a new invariant is independently justified
formal applicability
conformance consequences
architecture or implementation consequences
```

This Issue is a durable work/provenance record. It accepts no product semantics and provides no formal-verification evidence.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] A new accepted ADR-level decision, or a complete derivation from then-current authority, selects and justifies one mechanism-independent contract equivalent to Alternative A, B, C, D, E, F, or a clearly stated refinement.
- [x] The decision defines what makes a semantic-boundary capture opportunity sufficient and falsifiable.
- [x] The decision identifies when TURNLOCK may allow provenance to become unavailable without silently selecting a wall-clock retention duration.
- [x] The decision preserves the already-accepted rule that inaccessible transient internal state does not satisfy the required capture boundary, and separately decides whether an instantaneous but genuinely realizable semantic-boundary capture opportunity can suffice.
- [x] Consumer realizability, offer/emission, delivery, acknowledgment, active-consumer absence, authorized-consumer absence, and loss before observation are distinguished.
- [x] Capture opportunity remains distinct from persistence, retention, disclosure, authorization, UI/log visibility, and successful delivery.
- [x] Known-and-protected provenance remains distinct from unknown, without requiring universal exact-value disclosure.
- [x] Conditions governing failed, cancelled, or interrupted scopes are addressed only to the extent required by the capture-opportunity contract; the complete terminal-outcome lifecycle remains separately governed.
- [x] Per-occurrence and aggregation semantics are explicitly assessed without weakening ADR-025's condition-specific and scope-attribution floor.
- [x] ADR-024's provenance floor and ADR-025's protected-representation floor remain fully in force.
- [x] The relationship to Issue #13 is resolved explicitly without automatic scope merger or dependency.
- [x] No persistence backend, retention duration, delivery acknowledgment, event queue, API, transport, or other implementation mechanism is made normative without independent authority.
- [x] Any invariant consequence passes the repository invariant-admission test; this Issue creates no invariant automatically.
- [x] Formal applicability is assessed separately, with no concrete API, consumer, authorization, buffering, storage, or network semantics invented in TLA+.
- [x] Every accepted semantic change is synchronized across the authoritative, traceability, terminology, and generated artifacts actually affected.
- [x] The complete repository generation and validation sequence passes for every eventual repository change.

## Dependencies / coordination

- **Authority baseline:** ADR-024, ADR-025, and `TL-INV-036`.
- **Policy boundary:** ADR-019 and `TL-INV-034` remain controlling for evaluation and optimization.
- **Coordination with #13:** possible overlap in temporal availability, access/privacy, and failed outcomes; distinct normative objects; no native dependency currently demonstrated.
- **Historical provenance:** #15 was resolved by ADR-024; #16 was resolved by ADR-025. Neither closed Issue is product authority.
- **Future persistence/retention:** separate responsibilities that may consume captured provenance but do not define this boundary automatically.
- **Future comparability/reproducibility:** separate contracts; this Issue establishes no evidence sufficiency for property `P`.
- No parent, sub-issue, blocked-by, or blocking relationship is currently established.

Under the current Turnlock-Rust Engineering profile, this open product-semantic ambiguity belongs in `Status: Backlog`, `Phase: Specification`, `Kind: Finding`, `Priority: P0`. `P0` protects the `TL-INV-036` conformance boundary; it is not an implementation urgency claim and accepts no alternative.

## Non-goals

Creating or resolving this Issue as currently scoped does not decide or require:

- a persistence backend;
- a retention duration;
- a database;
- a durable event log;
- a canonical event schema;
- OpenTelemetry;
- a callback API;
- a subscription API;
- a streaming protocol;
- an acknowledgment protocol;
- retry semantics;
- backpressure;
- a buffer size;
- queue semantics;
- exact timestamps;
- a wall-clock duration;
- a timeout;
- polling;
- filesystem storage;
- network transport;
- crash durability;
- a `Run`, `RunSpec`, or `RunProof`;
- a UUID;
- a hash or cryptographic representation;
- encryption;
- ACL or RBAC;
- authorized-consumer identity;
- a user interface;
- CLI output;
- logging;
- replay;
- a reproducibility profile;
- a comparison contract; or
- an optimizer.

It also does not decide that provenance must always remain available until workflow completion, that TURNLOCK must block until a consumer acknowledges receipt, that successful delivery is universally required, or that push, pull, callback, event, synchronous, asynchronous, channel, queue, stream, observer, subscriber, socket, or IPC is the required mechanism.

## Formal-model boundary

No TLA+ semantics or traceability change is authorized by this Issue. A future product decision might justify an abstract relation such as:

```text
provenance becomes capturable
→ provenance is not lost before an abstract capture boundary
```

That possibility accepts no formula, property, state variable, action, fairness premise, configuration, or invariant. Actual API accessibility, delivery, consumer authorization, buffering, storage, crash behavior, and network availability must not be invented in the formal model.

## Validation expectations for eventual resolution

- Re-read then-current normative authority, accepted ADRs, related live Issues, and repository governance.
- Apply discovery classification separately to the product decision, authorization/privacy policy, persistence/retention policy, adapter or harness capability, delivery semantics, implementation mechanism, and formal consequence.
- Confirm that the accepted wording defines the weakest sufficient observable contract and makes nominal inaccessible capture non-conforming only to the extent actually decided.
- Confirm that no successful-delivery, acknowledgment, persistence, retention, event, buffering, transport, or UI mechanism is implied without explicit authority.
- Apply the invariant-admission test only after product meaning is accepted.
- Run the complete repository generation and validation sequence in `AGENTS.md` for every eventual repository change.
- Make no formal-verification claim without scope-bound evidence.

## Authoritative references

### Product authority

- [TURNLOCK normative specification](https://github.com/fanilosendrison/turnlock-rust/blob/main/docs/specification/turnlock-spec.md), especially §§0.13B–0.13D, 2.9–2.10, 3.31–3.34, 4, 5.15–5.17, 6, 7, and 9
- [ADR-018 — Require completed workflow execution inspectability](https://github.com/fanilosendrison/turnlock-rust/blob/main/docs/adr/adr-018-require-completed-workflow-execution-inspectability.md)
- [ADR-019 — Keep evaluation and optimization policy outside TURNLOCK core](https://github.com/fanilosendrison/turnlock-rust/blob/main/docs/adr/adr-019-keep-evaluation-and-optimization-policy-outside-turnlock-core.md)
- [ADR-024 — Preserve effective execution-condition provenance](https://github.com/fanilosendrison/turnlock-rust/blob/main/docs/adr/adr-024-preserve-effective-execution-condition-provenance.md)
- [ADR-025 — Preserve condition-specific provenance without requiring protected-value disclosure](https://github.com/fanilosendrison/turnlock-rust/blob/main/docs/adr/adr-025-preserve-condition-specific-provenance-without-requiring-protected-value-disclosure.md)
- [`formal/verification.yaml`](https://github.com/fanilosendrison/turnlock-rust/blob/main/formal/verification.yaml) — intended traceability only, not verification evidence
- [Turnlock-Rust discovery-classification profile](https://github.com/fanilosendrison/turnlock-rust/blob/main/docs/repository-governance/turnlock-rust-discovery-classification.md)

### Work/provenance and non-normative context

- [Issue #13 — minimum completed-execution inspectability semantics](https://github.com/fanilosendrison/turnlock-rust/issues/13) — open coordination; no scope transfer
- [Issue #15 — effective execution-condition provenance](https://github.com/fanilosendrison/turnlock-rust/issues/15) — closed historical provenance; resolved by ADR-024
- [Issue #16 — protected provenance disclosure/capture](https://github.com/fanilosendrison/turnlock-rust/issues/16) — closed historical provenance; resolved by ADR-025
- [Future workflow run-evaluation design space](https://github.com/fanilosendrison/turnlock-rust/blob/main/docs/vision/future-workflow-run-evaluation.md) — explicitly non-normative
value.title: Specification: define the semantic-boundary capture opportunity for effective execution-condition provenance

value.body:
## Problem

TURNLOCK orchestrates declared workflow execution inside a surrounding
execution environment. The accepted corpus did not previously state where
TURNLOCK's semantic authority ends and the environment's authority begins, nor
whether participating in an execution region confers any authority over the
workflow artifact whose definition governs that region.

That gap was exposed while resolving the workflow-definition binding semantics
recorded in ADR-027 and clarified by ADR-028. The original framing of this
Issue asked for a general TURNLOCK authority model: ex-ante grants, runtime
grant/revoke, an authority-source hierarchy, and a workflow-authorship
permission system. That framing is rejected. TURNLOCK core is not the owner of
general permissions over local resources.

The real problem is narrower and must remain precise:

```text
local execution capabilities and local effects
!=
TURNLOCK orchestration authority
```

An execution resource may possess a filesystem or tool capability that lets it
edit a repository file, including a workflow source artifact. Such an edit is a
local action under the surrounding environment. It must never be interpreted as
a mutation of the orchestration program governing an invocation that has
already been accepted and remains active.

## Accepted resolution

The following resolution is accepted product semantics. It resolves this Issue
and is recorded by ADR-029 plus synchronized normative and formal traceability
artifacts.

### 1. TURNLOCK governs orchestration, not general environment permissions

TURNLOCK core does not define and must not invent a general permission system
over the local actions of execution resources. In particular, TURNLOCK core
does not define, for the mere purpose of protecting its own workflows:

- ACL/RBAC;
- filesystem permissions;
- path-based permissions;
- tool allowlists;
- capability tokens;
- sandboxing;
- container permissions;
- TURNLOCK artifact-specific read/write rules;
- a generic local grant/revoke authority system;
- a special "meta-workflow" semantic class;
- a privileged class reserved to official TURNLOCK workflows.

Those responsibilities belong to the surrounding execution environment, harness,
sandbox, or user-controlled environment unless a later, explicit, distinct
product decision introduces a specific TURNLOCK capability.

```text
TURNLOCK orchestration authority
!=
general operational authority over the surrounding environment

filesystem/tool capability
does not imply
TURNLOCK orchestration authority
```

The inverse boundary is equally explicit:

```text
ordinary source file          -> no implicit TURNLOCK permission needed
TURNLOCK workflow source file -> no implicit TURNLOCK prohibition added
```

If the environment of an execution resource permits modifying a repository file,
TURNLOCK core does not add a second permission that treats a workflow file as
specially forbidden.

### 2. Execution resources may modify workflows when their environment permits it

An execution resource — including the main agent, but the boundary is not a
main-agent-specific exception — may perform the local actions its environment
permits, including:

- inspecting a workflow;
- proposing a modification;
- creating a workflow;
- modifying another workflow;
- modifying the workflow whose definition governs the currently active
  invocation;
- deleting or moving an artifact when the environment authorizes it;
- producing a new version of a workflow;
- performing workflow authoring as part of an ordinary
  evaluator/optimizer/meta-workflow.

TURNLOCK must not attempt to infer a workflow's "intent" to decide whether it
may modify workflows. No rule of the following shape exists in TURNLOCK core:

```text
if workflow purpose == "modify workflows"
then allow workflow modification
```

No equivalent semantic flag exists, such as `meta_workflow = true` or
`workflow_authorship_permission`. A workflow that orchestrates a coding agent
performing workflow authoring remains an ordinary workflow.

### 3. Local action versus governing orchestration

```text
local agency / local effects
!=
TURNLOCK global orchestration authority
```

A local action, however powerful, never implicitly becomes a modification of
the orchestration governing the current invocation:

```text
artifact A = D1

accept invocation I of A
→ governingDefinition(I) = D1

during I:
execution resource edits artifact A
A becomes D2

required result:
I continues under D1
```

Never `I switches to D2`. The source-artifact modification is a local
authoring action, not a mutation of the governing definition. It may become
visible to a future invocation under that future invocation's normal resolution
semantics.

### 4. Self-authoring is permitted; self-replanning / self-rebinding is not

The situation must not be described as "self-modifying active workflow",
because that wording conflates two different operations:

```text
source-artifact self-authoring
    MAY occur if the surrounding environment permits it

active invocation self-rebinding
    MUST NOT occur

active invocation self-replanning
    MUST NOT occur
```

```text
A/D1 running
→ execution resource edits artifact A into D2
→ current invocation remains governed by D1
→ invocation ends
→ a later invocation of A may bind to D2
```

The recursive/nested case is also coherent:

```text
I1 executes A/D1
→ edits source artifact A into D2
→ later, according to D1's already-declared semantics, invokes A again
→ new invocation I2 is independently accepted
→ I2 determines its own governing definition
→ I2 may therefore bind to D2
```

This is not replanning of `I1`. `I1` remains governed by `D1`. No special rule
forbids modifying the currently governing source workflow while other workflows
remain editable.

### 5. Governing orchestration is immutable for an accepted invocation

This decision reinforces and makes explicit the contract already carried by
ADR-027, ADR-028, and `TL-INV-037`:

```text
Accepted(I)
→ one governing workflow definition D

while I remains active
→ D remains the governing definition
→ the orchestration envelope authorized by D cannot be replaced,
   rebound, rewritten, or replanned
```

The immutable object is the **orchestration envelope / governing
orchestration**, not every runtime result. A definition may declare branches,
conditions, iteration, runtime inputs, results-dependent choices, event-driven
behavior, bounded delegation to an agent, nested workflow invocation, and other
executable workflow semantics:

```text
D declares:
if X -> A
else -> B
```

`X` may be determined during execution. What is immutable is that `D` authorizes
that decision structure. A runtime result may select a possibility already
declared by `D`; it cannot create a new global possibility that `D` does not
authorize.

The existing distinction is preserved:

```text
workflow-owned control
!=
computational/output/path determinism
```

This Issue does not claim that a run is totally deterministic. The contract
concerns immutability of the governing orchestration and authorization of global
transitions.

### 6. Active replanning / rebinding is outside and contrary to the current product contract

Active replanning, active rebinding, and replacement of the governing workflow
definition of an accepted invocation are **not** supported. This capability is
contrary to the current TURNLOCK product contract.

This is not an unresolved future feature of this Issue, not a roadmap item, not
an expected capability, not an extension to prepare, not a transition to
reserve, and not an obligation of forward compatibility.

ADR-028 already establishes that the current model contains no
active-definition-mutation transition, no authorization guard for one, and no
placeholder for one. That remains required.

If a hypothetical future proposal wanted to introduce such behavior, it would
be an explicit modification of the governing product semantics, requiring a new
decision that amends, supersedes, or reconciles the current invariants.

### 7. The same boundary applies to every execution resource

The boundary is general:

```text
execution resource performs local action
→ local effect may occur according to its environment

BUT

local effect
↛ implicit change of the current invocation's governing orchestration
```

No asymmetric policy is decided here, such as "the main agent may edit workflows
and independent agents may not", or the reverse. Concrete capabilities of each
harness or execution form may differ, but that difference belongs to the
capability/conformance/environment layer, not to a new general TURNLOCK
permission rule.

### 8. Exact non-conformance condition

TURNLOCK non-conformance is **not**:

```text
an execution resource edited a TURNLOCK workflow file
```

Non-conformance is, for example:

```text
an ordinary local edit changed the governing definition
of an already accepted active invocation

a local agent action introduced an undeclared global transition
into the current invocation

the runtime treated local filesystem/tool capability
as authority to replace or replan the current global orchestration
```

```text
workflow source edit
!=
TURNLOCK orchestration mutation
```

TURNLOCK must guarantee the second boundary, not arbitrarily prevent the first.

### 9. Consequences for evaluation and optimization

ADR-019 is preserved. An evaluator, optimizer, coding agent, higher-level
system, or ordinary TURNLOCK workflow may analyze an execution and produce or
refine a workflow `W'`. No privileged optimizer and no privileged official
meta-workflow exists in TURNLOCK core.

```text
W
→ execute
→ inspectable execution truth
→ external/user/workflow evaluation or optimization
→ possible authoring/refinement of W'
→ later TURNLOCK invocation may execute W'
```

A workflow refinement remains authorship. It never becomes implicit replanning
of an invocation that is already active.

## Required distinctions

```text
filesystem/tool capability
!=
TURNLOCK orchestration authority

workflow-artifact edit
!=
active governing-definition mutation

workflow authorship
!=
runtime orchestration authority

source self-authoring
!=
active self-replanning

runtime choice authorized by governing definition
!=
changing the governing definition

future invocation binding
!=
rebinding the current invocation
```

## Examples

### A. Edit another workflow

```text
A/D1 running
→ agent edits B/E1 into B/E2
→ A/D1 remains unchanged
→ a future invocation of B may resolve to E2
```

### B. Edit own source artifact

```text
A/D1 running
→ agent edits A into D2
→ the current invocation remains A/D1
→ a later invocation may use D2
```

### C. Recursive or new invocation

```text
A/D1 running
→ source A becomes D2
→ D1 later invokes A according to already-declared semantics
→ the new invocation independently resolves and binds
→ the new invocation may use D2
→ the outer invocation remains D1
```

## Explicit non-goals / outside TURNLOCK core

- filesystem sandboxing;
- OS permissions;
- container permissions;
- ACL/RBAC;
- path permissions;
- tool allowlists;
- generic capability tokens;
- a generic runtime grant/revoke model;
- meta-workflow classification;
- official-workflow privilege;
- optimizer privilege;
- intent inference for whether a workflow "is allowed" to author workflows.

## Active replanning

Active replanning and active rebinding are **not** unresolved future features of
this Issue. The current product contract does not support them. They are
contrary to `TL-INV-037` and ADR-028 under current semantics, and no model
transition, authorization guard, or placeholder for them may be introduced.

## Classification

```text
Discovery disposition: decision-required, resolved by the accepted product
  directive recorded in this Issue body and in the resulting accepted ADR
Primary layer: product-semantic responsibility boundary
Repository mapping: normative-contract + decision-history
  + formal-model-or-analysis + repository-governance-or-documentation
```

The responsibility boundary between local execution capabilities and TURNLOCK
orchestration authority is a product-semantic responsibility boundary decided
here. Concrete sandbox and harness mechanisms are implementation, conformance,
and environment concerns. Consequences already imposed by `TL-INV-037` are
derived from existing authority rather than redecided.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] Local execution capability and TURNLOCK orchestration authority are
      separated normatively, and the boundary states that TURNLOCK core defines
      no general repository/filesystem/tool authorization for execution
      resources.
- [x] Responsibility for restricting local access and local actions is
      explicitly assigned to the surrounding execution environment unless a
      separately accepted TURNLOCK semantic defines otherwise.
- [x] Workflow authoring by an execution resource is permitted when the
      environment allows it and produces no effect on the governing definition
      or declared global progression of an already accepted active invocation.
- [x] Source-artifact self-authoring and active self-replanning/self-rebinding
      are explicitly distinguished, and active replanning/rebinding is recorded
      as absent from and contrary to the current product contract rather than as
      a reserved future feature.
- [x] The same general boundary applies to every execution resource, with no
      main-agent/independent-agent asymmetry decided in this Issue.
- [x] The conformance condition identifies a changed governing definition of an
      accepted active invocation, or a local action that introduces an
      undeclared global transition, as non-conformant; a workflow-file edit by
      itself is not non-conformance.
- [x] The decision is recorded in a new accepted ADR without editing any
      accepted ADR body.
- [x] The normative specification is synchronized, and no new `TL-INV-*`
      identity is created unless the existing invariant-admission rules and an
      independent universal obligation require one.
- [x] Formal traceability is synchronized only to the extent required;
      `TL-INV-037` remains `planned` / `not-yet-modeled`, and no replanning or
      rebinding transition, state variable, authorization guard, or placeholder
      is introduced.
- [x] Generated ADR and formal projections are regenerated from their canonical
      sources.
- [x] Repository-required validation remains green.

## Validation

For any resulting repository change, regenerate affected projections and run:

```bash
.venv/bin/python scripts/adr-metadata.py render
.venv/bin/python scripts/render-formal-mapping.py
.venv/bin/python scripts/tests/test-adr-metadata.py
.venv/bin/python scripts/tests/test-normative-terminology.py
.venv/bin/python scripts/adr-metadata.py check
.venv/bin/python scripts/check-normative-terminology.py

```

## Authoritative references

- [ADR-001 — make the workflow own orchestration after session entry](https://github.com/fanilosendrison/turnlock-rust/blob/main/docs/adr/adr-001-make-the-workflow-own-orchestration-after-session-entry.md)
- [ADR-007 — main-agent continuity and ordinary interactive agency](https://github.com/fanilosendrison/turnlock-rust/blob/main/docs/adr/adr-007-preserve-main-agent-cognitive-lineage-and-ordinary-interactive-agency.md)
- [ADR-014 — workflow program and TURNLOCK engine](https://github.com/fanilosendrison/turnlock-rust/blob/main/docs/adr/adr-014-define-turnlock-as-the-orchestration-engine-and-the-workflow-as-the-orchestration-program.md)
- [ADR-016 — authorship versus execution authority](https://github.com/fanilosendrison/turnlock-rust/blob/main/docs/adr/adr-016-separate-workflow-authorship-from-runtime-execution-authority.md)

- [ADR-028 — TL-INV-037 forbids governing-definition changes under current semantics](https://github.com/fanilosendrison/turnlock-rust/blob/main/docs/adr/adr-028-clarify-that-tl-inv-037-forbids-governing-definition-changes-under-current-semantics.md)
