value.title: Semantics: separate local execution capabilities from immutable invocation orchestration

value.body:
## Problem

Turnlock-Rust has a clear authority model for product semantics, decision history, formal intent, and verification evidence, but its GitHub Issue corpus does not yet apply the same single-owner discipline to **live work state**.

Several Issue bodies manually reproduce facts whose live authority already exists elsewhere in GitHub, including:

* whether another Issue is open, closed, resolved, or completed;
* whether another Issue currently blocks or is blocked by work;
* parent/sub-issue structure;
* `Status`, `Phase`, `Kind`, and `Priority`;
* readiness tables that require manual synchronization with other Issues;
* cross-Issue checkboxes whose truth changes when another work item changes state.

Those Markdown copies form manually maintained projections of the work graph. They can diverge from the GitHub Issue state, Project fields, and native relationships that actually own the information.

The failure mode is not merely cosmetic. Once stale prose is consumed by a coding agent or reviewer, the repository presents two different descriptions of current work state and requires the consumer to rediscover which one is authoritative.

The repository must adopt the same rule for engineering work state that it already applies to generated ADR and formal projections:

```text
one canonical live owner
→ references or mechanically generated projections

not

one canonical live owner
+
independently maintained Markdown copies
```

The governing principle for Issue bodies is:

```text
Reference, do not mirror.
```

## Discovery snapshot

This section is historical provenance, **not a live work-status view**.

Observed on 2026-09-16, with repository `main` at revision:

```text
8032317acde7c41e87ed7d2e42536fb8f2463f8d
```

Representative examples included:

* #9 maintaining a `Tracked work` table for #1–#8, cross-Issue readiness checkboxes, native relationship assertions, and Project-field assertions inside its body;
* #9 retaining unchecked conditions concerning work that had subsequently been completed, demonstrating actual drift rather than only a theoretical risk;
* #6 reproducing the resolved state of #5 in its authority section, acceptance checklist, and dependency prose even though accepted ADRs own the resulting product meaning and GitHub owns work state;
* #13 describing #4 as the “still-open workflow-definition binding decision” after definition-binding semantics had moved into accepted authority;
* #13 treating the Issue owning evaluation/optimization work as the current semantic authority instead of referring directly to the accepted product boundary;
* #18 reproducing `Status`, `Phase`, `Kind`, and `Priority` as a Markdown `Project classification` block even though those values belong to Turnlock-Rust Engineering.

These examples motivate the governance correction. They must not themselves become another live status inventory.

## Authority model for live work state

Turnlock-Rust must use the following ownership model.

| Information                                       | Canonical owner                        |
| ------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------- |
| Durable work item                                 | GitHub Issue                           |
| Open/closed Issue state                           | GitHub Issue state                     |
| Workflow state                                    | Project `Status`                       |
| Lifecycle classification                          | Project `Phase`                        |
| Work-item classification                          | Project `Kind`                         |
| Scheduling priority                               | Project `Priority`                     |
| Parent/sub-issue structure                        | Native GitHub Issue relationships      |
| Blocking/blocked-by structure                     | Native GitHub dependency relationships |
| Pull Request linkage                              | Native GitHub relationships            |
| Product semantics                                 | `docs/specification/turnlock-spec.md`  |
| Accepted decision history                         | Accepted ADRs                          |
| Intended formal traceability/coverage             | `formal/verification.yaml`             |
| Concrete bounded verification evidence            | `formal/results/`                      |
| Acceptance criteria for the work owned by Issue X | Issue X body                           |

An Issue may reference another Issue, explain why another work product matters, or describe the semantic input it expects.

An Issue body must **not** act as a manually maintained current-state projection of another Issue or of the Project work graph.

## Required governance rules

Update repository governance so the following rules are explicit.

### 1. No duplicated live work state

Issue bodies MUST NOT mirror as current truth:

```text
another Issue's open/closed state
another Issue's completion state
Project Status
Project Phase
Project Kind
Project Priority
parent/sub-issue membership
blocked-by/blocking state
PR relationship state
```

The GitHub object or native relationship that owns the fact remains the single live authority.

### 2. Acceptance checklists are local

A checkbox in Issue X must describe an outcome that can be satisfied by executing Issue X.

Do not use checkboxes such as:

```text
[ ] #4 is resolved
[ ] #7 is complete
[ ] #8 defines ...
[ ] #5 is closed
```

Cross-Issue completion and readiness must be observed from the native work graph.

A local criterion may instead require the Issue's own result to consume, exclude, or remain compatible with the then-current authoritative outcome of related work.

### 3. Native GitHub relationships own the work graph

Use native parent, sub-issue, blocked-by, blocking, and Pull Request relationships for current work relationships.

Issue prose may explain the **semantic reason** an input or sequencing constraint matters, but it must not maintain a second copy of the current relationship state.

For example, prefer a stable statement such as:

```text
The occurrence-scoped formalization consumes the property-level verification
metamodel produced by #1.
```

over a manually maintained state assertion such as:

```text
This Issue is currently blocked by #1.
```

The native dependency relationship owns the latter fact.

### 4. Project fields own live Project classification

`Status`, `Phase`, `Kind`, and `Priority` belong exclusively to Turnlock-Rust Engineering as live classification state.

Do not reproduce a block such as:

```text
Status: Backlog
Phase: Specification
Kind: Finding
Priority: P0
```

inside an Issue body.

Repository governance may require a rationale when a classification deviates from a default, but the rationale must not create a second copy of the current field values.

If a durable explanation of a classification exception is required, record it as historical rationale without making the Issue body another live Project record.

### 5. Accepted authority owns accepted outcomes

When an Issue results in an accepted ADR, normative specification change, formal contract, or other authoritative artifact, open Issue bodies that need the resulting technical meaning should reference that authoritative artifact.

Do not use:

```text
Issue #N is resolved
```

as the technical authority for an accepted product or formal conclusion.

The closed Issue may still be referenced as historical provenance.

### 6. Historical snapshots are allowed only when explicit

Historical observations are legitimate when provenance matters.

They must be explicitly bounded by a date, repository revision, or equivalent immutable context and must be clearly identified as a snapshot rather than current work state.

For example:

```text
Discovery snapshot

Observed on main at revision <sha> on <date>.
This records discovery provenance and is not a live summary of current authority
or Project state.
```

Existing revision-scoped evidence sections are not violations merely because later repository state differs.

### 7. Do not maintain manual work-status dashboards

Do not add manually maintained tables or dashboard sections whose rows are intended to track the current state of multiple Issues.

GitHub Issues, Project fields, and native relationships already provide the live work graph.

If a future use case genuinely requires another projection, it must be separately justified and mechanically generated from canonical live sources, clearly marked as non-authoritative, rather than manually synchronized.

No such generator is required by this Issue.

### 8. Closed Issues are historical records

Do not rewrite closed Issues solely to make their historical bodies conform to this new presentation rule.

Apply the rule prospectively and normalize the currently active Issue corpus.

A closed Issue may be changed only for an independently justified reason, not merely for stylistic cleanup.

## Required repository-governance changes

Update:

```text
docs/repository-governance/turnlock-rust-engineering.md
```

as the detailed owner of this policy.

In particular:

1. add the live-work-state ownership rules above;
2. reconcile the current `Issue requirements` section so it no longer instructs Issue bodies to duplicate a live `Phase` value or mutable prerequisite state;
3. preserve the requirement to populate `Status`, `Phase`, `Kind`, and `Priority` in the Project itself;
4. preserve the requirement to use native GitHub relationships;
5. make clear that explanation of semantic prerequisites is allowed while current dependency state belongs to native GitHub relationships;
6. make clear that a classification rationale does not justify copying the Project field block into Markdown;
7. document the explicit historical-snapshot exception.

Update:

```text
AGENTS.md
```

only as much as necessary to make the operational rule visible to agents.

`AGENTS.md` should contain a concise directive equivalent to:

```text
Treat GitHub Issue state, Turnlock-Rust Engineering fields, and native GitHub
relationships as the single live authority for work state. Reference them from
Issue prose; do not mirror mutable work state in Issue bodies. Apply the
detailed policy in docs/repository-governance/turnlock-rust-engineering.md.
```

Do not duplicate the complete policy into both files.

## Open-Issue normalization scope

As part of implementing this governance Issue, revalidate every Issue that is open at implementation time against the new rule.

The discovery snapshot identified the following concrete normalization targets:

```text
#1
#2
#3
#6
#9
#13
#18
```

Do not assume their state or content is unchanged when implementation begins. Re-read the live Issue before editing it.

The intended normalization for the known targets is already decided as follows.

### #1

Remove any body-level copy of the Project `Phase` field, such as:

```text
Phase: Formal Verification
```

Preserve revision-scoped evidence and stable sequencing requirements.

Do not alter its formal-verification scope.

### #2

Remove or rewrite body prose whose only purpose is to mirror the native blocking relationship with #3.

Preserve the stable semantic fact that downstream occurrence-scoped formalization consumes this Issue's semantic outcome.

Do not change the liveness question or its product authority.

### #3

Remove or rewrite:

```text
Blocked by #1
Blocked by #2
```

as live dependency assertions.

Preserve the stable required-input semantics: this work consumes the verification metamodel produced by #1 and the authoritative liveness outcome produced by #2.

Preserve the native dependency relationships.

### #6

Remove the manually maintained work-state assertion that #5 “is resolved”.

Refer directly to ADR-022 and ADR-023 for the accepted declared-invocation and caller/continuation semantics.

Remove the cross-Issue acceptance checkbox whose predicate is that #5 is resolved.

Rewrite the criterion so it tests only #6's own scope, for example that restricted-placement and transitive-admissibility semantics remain compatible with the accepted declared-invocation authority.

Remove the `Satisfied blocker` prose that mirrors the native dependency state.

Preserve any native GitHub relationship as provenance/work-graph data.

Do not change #6's semantic decision space.

### #9

This is the primary tracker normalization.

Remove the manually maintained `Tracked work` table as a live projection of #1–#8.

Replace it with stable conceptual readiness gates, not rows representing current Issue states.

Rewrite `READY-BEFORE-FIRST-SAFETY-MODEL` so every checkbox is local to #9's readiness result.

In particular, remove checkboxes whose predicate is:

```text
#1 is complete / defines X
#4 is resolved
#5 is resolved
#6 is resolved
#7 provides X
#8 defines X
```

Replace them with local scope criteria such as:

```text
the first-model scope consumes the then-current accepted definition-binding semantics
or explicitly excludes behavior outside its declared state space

the first-model scope identifies every represented invariant/property

the first-model scope contains no liveness formula or fairness assumption

every semantic behavior exercised by the model has accepted authority or an
explicit model-scope exclusion

a separately scoped implementation Issue exists before executable model work begins
```

Remove acceptance criteria whose sole purpose is to assert:

```text
other Issues' open/completed state
parent/sub-issue relationships
blocked-by relationships
Project Status/Phase/Kind/Priority values
```

Preserve those relationships natively in GitHub.

Replace status-sensitive references to previously resolved semantic questions with direct references to the accepted ADR/specification authority where applicable.

Keep #9 as the pre-TLA+ readiness tracker. Do not turn it into an implementation Issue and do not alter the intended safety-only first-model boundary.

### #13

Remove stale current-state wording that treats #4 as the “still-open workflow-definition binding decision”.

Use the then-current accepted definition-binding authority directly, including ADR-027, ADR-028, `TL-INV-037`, and the normative specification as applicable.

Do not make #4 the current semantic authority.

Replace prose that assigns current evaluation/optimization product authority to #12 with the accepted evaluation/optimization boundary, including ADR-019 and `TL-INV-034`, as applicable.

The historical discovery relationship to #4 or #12 may be retained only as clearly historical provenance.

Rewrite dependency/acceptance wording accordingly.

Do not change #13's inspectability decision space.

### #18

Remove the Markdown `Project classification` block containing:

```text
Status
Phase
Kind
Priority
```

The live values remain in Turnlock-Rust Engineering.

Preserve the substantive rationale for why the authority question matters, but do not maintain a duplicate live Project record.

Rewrite status-sensitive dependency prose concerning #4 so it relies on ADR-027/ADR-028 and the accepted governing-definition boundary rather than #4's current work state.

Preserve `Originating work: #4` or equivalent only as explicit historical provenance.

Do not change #18's authority decision space.

## Acceptance criteria

* [ ] `docs/repository-governance/turnlock-rust-engineering.md` explicitly assigns live work-state ownership to GitHub Issue state, Project fields, and native relationships.
* [ ] The governance profile explicitly prohibits Issue bodies from mirroring another Issue's mutable completion/state, Project field values, or native relationship state as current truth.
* [ ] The governance profile defines the local-checklist rule: every acceptance checkbox in Issue X must be satisfiable by work owned by Issue X.
* [ ] The governance profile distinguishes a stable explanation of why another work product matters from a mutable assertion of its current dependency state.
* [ ] The governance profile directs current technical meaning to accepted authoritative artifacts rather than the closed Issue that produced them.
* [ ] The governance profile defines the revision/date-bounded historical-snapshot exception.
* [ ] The governance profile explicitly discourages manually maintained work-status dashboards and requires any future projection to be mechanically derived from canonical live data.
* [ ] The existing Issue requirements no longer require a body-level duplicate of Project `Phase` or other live Project metadata.
* [ ] `AGENTS.md` contains a concise operational pointer to the detailed live-work-state policy without duplicating it.
* [ ] Every Issue open at implementation time is audited against the rule.
* [ ] Known targets #1, #2, #3, #6, #9, #13, and #18 are normalized according to the scope above if they remain open and relevant.
* [ ] #9 no longer contains a manually maintained live work-status table or cross-Issue completion checklist.
* [ ] Native parent/sub-issue, dependency, Project-field, and Pull Request data are preserved as the work graph's live state rather than deleted because their Markdown copies are removed.
* [ ] Revision-scoped or explicitly historical provenance is preserved where useful and cannot reasonably be mistaken for live state.
* [ ] Closed Issues are not rewritten solely for conformance with the new presentation rule.
* [ ] No TURNLOCK product semantic, accepted ADR meaning, `TL-INV-*`, formal-verification claim, runtime contract, API, DSL, or implementation mechanism changes as a consequence of this governance cleanup.
* [ ] No new work-status checker, generator, dashboard, or CI mechanism is introduced by this Issue.
* [ ] Repository-required validation remains green after repository-document changes.
* [ ] A final review confirms that the cleanup reduced duplicated authority rather than merely moving the duplicate information to another manually maintained location.

## Non-goals

This Issue does not:

```text
change TURNLOCK product semantics
change any accepted ADR decision body
add or modify a TL-INV-* product requirement
write the executable TLA+ model
change TLC evidence semantics
change Rust/runtime architecture
change workflow syntax
change evaluation or optimization policy
change authority semantics owned by #18
change composition semantics owned by #6
change inspectability semantics owned by #13
create a work-status dashboard
create a GitHub synchronization bot
create a new checker or generator
rewrite all historical closed Issues
```

This is repository governance and active-work hygiene only.

## Validation

For repository-file changes made when this Issue is implemented, use the then-current validation contract in `AGENTS.md`.

At minimum, under the current contract, validation includes:

```bash
.venv/bin/python scripts/tests/test-adr-metadata.py
.venv/bin/python scripts/tests/test-normative-terminology.py
.venv/bin/python scripts/adr-metadata.py check
.venv/bin/python scripts/check-normative-terminology.py
.venv/bin/python scripts/check-formal-traceability.py
git diff --check
```

Regenerate a derived artifact only if an authoritative source that owns that projection actually changes.

Editing GitHub Issue prose must not cause unrelated normative or generated artifacts to change.

After normalization, inspect the live Project and native Issue relationships to confirm that removing Markdown mirrors did not remove or alter the canonical work graph.

## Relevant references

* `AGENTS.md`
* `docs/repository-governance/turnlock-rust-engineering.md`
* #9 — pre-TLA+ semantic readiness tracker
* #6 — nested composition admissibility
* #13 — minimum completed-execution inspectability semantics
* #18 — ex-ante authority and runtime exercise of agentic authority
* ADR-019 — evaluation/optimization policy boundary
* ADR-022 — workflow-declared invocation
* ADR-023 — caller-context and continuation semantics
* ADR-027 — stable governing workflow definition
* ADR-028 — clarification of `TL-INV-037`
value.title: Repository governance: eliminate duplicated live work state from Issue bodies

value.body:
## Problem

Turnlock-Rust currently assigns `Priority` to each Project Issue, but repository governance does not define a portfolio-level revalidation loop when the work graph changes.

The current Project profile correctly defines:

```text
P0
P1
P2
P3
```

and states that priority controls scheduling.

It also requires every Project Issue to have a `Priority`.

However, the current procedure is effectively local:

```text
new Issue appears
→ assign a Priority to that Issue
```

There is no corresponding mandatory operation:

```text
new information changes the work graph
→ reconsider the Priority of every still-open Issue
```

As a result, an Issue may retain a priority that was reasonable when it was created even after later discoveries materially change:

* the current critical path;
* the blast radius of unresolved work;
* the safety of continuing other agent-driven work;
* which work protects repository authority or traceability;
* which work now blocks current progress;
* or which work can safely wait.

This is particularly important because Turnlock-Rust relies heavily on coding agents consuming GitHub Issues and Project state to decide what work to execute.

A scheduling defect in the Project therefore affects the mechanism used to select subsequent engineering work.

`Priority` must be treated as live portfolio-relative scheduling state, not as a permanent classification assigned once at Issue creation time.

## Observed governance gap

This section records discovery provenance and is not a live Project dashboard.

Observed on 2026-09-16 with repository `main` at:

```text
8032317acde7c41e87ed7d2e42536fb8f2463f8d
```

The repository governance at that revision established all of the following:

```text
Turnlock-Rust Engineering
= authority for work classification, priority, and workflow state

P0
= blocks current progress
  OR protects a critical correctness, authority,
  traceability, or verification invariant

P1
= should be completed in the current phase

P2
= important but non-blocking

P3
= useful retained work that can wait
```

It also stated:

```text
Priority controls scheduling only.
```

But the repository did not define:

```text
when priorities must be recalculated

which Issues participate in that recalculation

how a newly created Issue can change existing Issues' priorities

how autonomous pickup consumes Priority

how ties between Ready work and In Progress work are treated

how portfolio reprioritization remains separate from semantic dependency
```

`AGENTS.md` required every Issue/finding to be revalidated against current authoritative repository sources before implementation, but did not require the Issue's scheduling priority to be revalidated against the current open-work portfolio.

The current `Agent Queue` was declared as a surface containing `Ready` or `In Progress` work, but no repository instruction explicitly required autonomous pickup to choose the highest-priority `Ready` work.

## Scope relationship with #19

This Issue and #19 are related repository-governance corrections but have distinct ownership.

### #19 owns

```text
single ownership of live work state

removal of manually mirrored:
- Issue state
- Project fields
- dependency state
- parent/sub-issue state

local acceptance checklists

historical snapshot rules

elimination of manually maintained work-status projections
```

### This Issue owns

```text
the lifecycle of Priority as live scheduling state

portfolio-wide priority revalidation

events that trigger revalidation

the priority decision procedure

autonomous pickup ordering

the one-time migration of current open Issues to the new policy
```

Do not merge these scopes.

Do not close #19 as a duplicate.

Do not implement #19's Issue-body cleanup as part of this Issue.

Both Issues may modify:

```text
AGENTS.md
docs/repository-governance/turnlock-rust-engineering.md
```

If one is implemented before the other, the later implementation must re-read the current files and integrate its change without reverting or duplicating the earlier governance rule.

No native dependency between the two Issues is required merely because they touch the same governance files.

## Governing principle

Adopt the following scheduling model:

```text
Priority is a live scheduling judgment over the current open-work portfolio.

It is not a permanent classification assigned once when an Issue is created.
```

A material change to the work graph must cause existing open Issues to be reconsidered.

The result of revalidation may be:

```text
Priority unchanged
```

or:

```text
Priority updated
```

Revalidation does NOT mean every Issue must receive a different value.

It means every in-scope open Issue must be deliberately reconsidered against the current portfolio before the scheduling operation is complete.

## Separation of concerns

Keep these concepts distinct.

### Priority

Answers:

```text
How urgently should this work be scheduled relative to other open work?
```

### Status

Answers:

```text
Is this work unready, independently executable, active, under review, or done?
```

### Dependency relationships

Answer:

```text
What work structurally depends on what other work?
```

### Phase

Answers:

```text
Which lifecycle domain owns the immediate deliverable?
```

### Kind

Answers:

```text
What relationship does this work item have to the engineering plan?
```

Do not encode a dependency by changing Priority.

Do not encode Priority by changing Status.

Do not interpret `P0` as automatically `Ready`.

A valid state may be:

```text
Priority: P0
Status: Backlog
```

when the work is critically important but not yet independently executable.

Likewise, a lower-priority Issue may be `Ready`.

Readiness and scheduling importance are separate.

## Priority decision contract

Preserve the existing four Project values:

```text
P0
P1
P2
P3
```

Do not introduce P-1, P4, Critical, Urgent, Severity, rank scores, numeric weights, or another priority field.

Clarify their operational meaning as follows.

### P0

Use `P0` when either branch applies.

#### Current-progress branch

The Issue materially blocks current engineering progress or the current critical path.

#### Protection branch

Continuing normal work before resolving the Issue can materially compromise or amplify risk to:

```text
correctness
authority
traceability
verification integrity
repository work-governance integrity
```

This includes cross-cutting governance failures where later agent-driven work can accumulate invalid, stale, mis-authorized, misleading, or unnecessarily expensive downstream work.

An Issue does not need to block one specific downstream deliverable to qualify for the protection branch.

Preserve the existing rule that an unresolved product/specification semantic `Finding` in `Phase: Specification` defaults to `P0`.

### P1

Use `P1` when the work should be completed during the current phase, but it is safe for other valid current-phase work to continue before it completes.

The key distinction from `P0` is:

```text
P1:
important now,
but continued normal work is still safe

P0:
delay can block progress or compromise protected engineering/governance integrity
```

### P2

Use `P2` for important retained work that does not materially block current progress and does not need to complete in the current phase.

### P3

Use `P3` for useful retained work that may safely wait without meaningful current scheduling cost.

## Priority is portfolio-relative

When assigning or revalidating a Priority, evaluate the Issue against the current portfolio, not only against its own body.

At minimum, inspect:

```text
the Issue's current required outcome

its Status

its Phase

its Kind

native blocked-by / blocking relationships

native parent/sub-issue relationships when relevant

current accepted repository authority

current open semantic decisions

current phase goals

whether the Issue protects a cross-cutting governance or verification mechanism

whether continuing other agent-driven work before resolution amplifies rework or authority risk
```

Do not copy this portfolio state into the Issue body.

Read it from its canonical live owners.

## Mandatory portfolio-revalidation triggers

A full open-Issue Priority revalidation MUST occur after any of the following material events.

### Trigger 1 — durable Issue creation

After creating any new durable Turnlock-Rust Issue and adding it to Turnlock-Rust Engineering:

```text
re-evaluate Priority for every open Project Issue,
including the newly created Issue
```

Issue creation is not operationally complete until this revalidation has happened.

### Trigger 2 — Issue completion, closure, or reopening

When a tracked Issue is completed/closed or reopened, re-evaluate every remaining open Issue because:

```text
critical paths may change
blockers may disappear or return
phase urgency may change
```

### Trigger 3 — native dependency-graph change

When a native blocked-by/blocking relationship is added or removed, re-evaluate all open Project Issues.

### Trigger 4 — authoritative decision changes prerequisites

When an accepted ADR, normative specification change, formal-governance change, or other authoritative repository change:

```text
resolves a prerequisite
creates a prerequisite
changes a work item's critical-path role
changes the risk of continuing downstream work
```

re-evaluate all open Project Issues.

This trigger concerns scheduling consequences only.

It does not make Project Priority semantic authority.

### Trigger 5 — phase transition

When the project's active engineering focus materially transitions between:

```text
Specification
Formal Verification
Implementation
```

re-evaluate the open portfolio because `P1` is explicitly relative to the current phase.

### Trigger 6 — validated cross-cutting governance finding

When a newly validated concern affects the machinery by which multiple other Issues are selected, interpreted, validated, or governed, re-evaluate the open portfolio even if no direct dependency relationship exists.

## Events that do not independently require full reprioritization

Do not trigger a full portfolio pass solely because of:

```text
comment creation
label-only changes
assignee changes
formatting-only Issue-body edits
historical provenance edits
a Priority correction itself
```

unless that operation also reveals one of the material changes above.

This prevents recursive reprioritization loops.

## Revalidation algorithm

Implement the procedural algorithm exactly as follows.

### Step 1 — load canonical live work state

Read every open Issue that is a member of Turnlock-Rust Engineering.

For each Issue, read from canonical sources:

```text
Issue open/closed state
Project Status
Project Phase
Project Kind
Project Priority
native dependencies
native parent/sub-issue relationships when relevant
```

Do not derive live Project values from Markdown bodies.

### Step 2 — refresh authoritative repository context

Read the current authority necessary to understand prerequisites and phase-critical work.

At minimum use:

```text
AGENTS.md
docs/repository-governance/turnlock-rust-engineering.md
docs/repository-governance/turnlock-rust-discovery-classification.md
current accepted ADR/spec/formal authority referenced by affected Issues
```

Do not reinterpret product semantics while performing scheduling.

### Step 3 — evaluate every open Issue

Apply the existing/default semantic-Finding rule plus the P0/P1/P2/P3 decision contract above.

For each Issue ask, in order:

```text
1. Does an existing repository default force P0?
   Example:
   unresolved Specification semantic Finding.

2. Does it currently block critical progress?

3. Would normal continued work before resolution materially risk
   correctness, authority, traceability, verification integrity,
   or work-governance integrity?

4. If neither P0 branch applies, must it complete in the current phase?

5. If not, is it important retained non-blocking work?

6. Otherwise it is P3.
```

This is the complete decision tree.

Do not invent an additional scoring model.

### Step 4 — compare with live Priority

For each open Issue:

```text
computed Priority == live Priority
→ no mutation

computed Priority != live Priority
→ update only the Project Priority field
```

Do not edit the Issue body merely to record the new live value.

Do not create a manually maintained portfolio-priority table.

### Step 5 — verify portfolio consistency

After updates:

* re-read every changed Project item;
* confirm each changed Issue now has the intended Priority;
* confirm no unintended Status, Phase, Kind, relationship, body, or repository mutation occurred.

## Autonomous pickup contract

Clarify the repository rule for agents selecting their own next task.

Autonomous pickup uses `Ready` work only.

`In Progress` work may remain visible in `Agent Queue`, but it is not a new pickup candidate.

Use this selection order:

```text
1. consider only Status = Ready
2. choose the highest Priority:
   P0 before P1
   P1 before P2
   P2 before P3
3. do not select a lower-priority Ready Issue while a higher-priority
   Ready Issue exists, unless the user explicitly selects another item
4. an explicit user selection overrides pickup order for that action only;
   it does not itself rewrite Priority
```

Priority does not create a dependency.

If two Ready Issues have equal Priority:

```text
- obey native dependency ordering when one must precede the other;
- otherwise retain the Project's existing/manual order as the tie-break.
```

Do not invent a second ranking field.

## In-progress work and preemption

Do not make a newly created `P0` automatically interrupt an Issue already marked `In Progress`.

Priority governs scheduling and new pickup.

If a new discovery makes continuation of active work invalid or unsafe, represent the actual condition through the appropriate canonical mechanism:

```text
native dependency
Status change
authority conflict
explicit user direction
```

as permitted by repository governance.

Do not use Priority as an implicit cancellation or preemption mechanism.

## Required repository changes

Implementation of this Issue MUST update:

```text
docs/repository-governance/turnlock-rust-engineering.md
```

as the detailed owner of the policy.

### Required edits to `turnlock-rust-engineering.md`

Make all of the following changes.

#### A. Clarify Priority's nature

Add explicit wording equivalent to:

```text
Priority is live, portfolio-relative scheduling state.

It must be revalidated when material changes to the open work graph or
current engineering context can change relative scheduling urgency.

It is not a permanent classification assigned once at Issue creation.
```

#### B. Preserve and refine P0–P3

Keep the exact Project values:

```text
P0
P1
P2
P3
```

Preserve the existing semantic-Finding P0 default.

Clarify P0/P1 using the safety-of-continuing distinction specified in this Issue.

Do not remove the statement that Priority controls scheduling only.

#### C. Add mandatory revalidation triggers

Add the six trigger classes defined above.

Make durable Issue creation explicitly require a full open-portfolio Priority revalidation.

#### D. Add the exact revalidation procedure

Document:

```text
load live open Project Issues
refresh authoritative context
evaluate all open Issues
update changed Priority fields only
verify no unrelated mutations
```

#### E. Update Issue-creation requirements

Change the repository's durable-work creation procedure so creation is not complete after only assigning fields to the new item.

The procedure must become conceptually:

```text
create Issue
add to Project
populate required fields
establish required native relationships
revalidate Priority across all open Project Issues
verify changed priorities
```

Do not require Issue Markdown to mirror the resulting fields.

#### F. Update autonomous pickup rules

Make `Agent Queue` pickup consume Priority explicitly:

```text
Ready only
highest Priority first
user may explicitly override
```

Keep `Status` and `Priority` independent.

#### G. Preserve native relationships

Do not use Priority as a replacement for blocked-by/blocking or parent/sub-issue relationships.

### Required `AGENTS.md` update

Update:

```text
AGENTS.md
```

only enough to expose the operational rule to coding agents.

Do not duplicate the entire detailed policy.

Add a concise directive equivalent in meaning to:

```text
Treat Project Priority as live portfolio-relative scheduling state.
After a material work-graph change, including creation of a durable Issue,
revalidate Priority across every open Turnlock-Rust Engineering Issue under
docs/repository-governance/turnlock-rust-engineering.md.

For autonomous pickup, select the highest-priority Ready Issue; Priority does
not replace dependencies or readiness.
```

Keep the detailed procedure in the repository-governance profile.

## One-time migration required by implementation

After the governance documents are updated, immediately exercise the new policy once against the live open portfolio.

At implementation time:

1. fetch every open Turnlock-Rust Engineering Issue;
2. ignore historical lists in this Issue as live authority;
3. re-evaluate every open Issue under the new decision tree;
4. update only Priority fields whose value changes;
5. verify all open items.

### Discovery snapshot

At discovery time, before creation of this Issue, the open repository Issue set was:

```text
#1
#2
#3
#6
#9
#13
#18
#19
```

This list is historical only.

The implementing agent MUST query the live Project instead of assuming this remains the complete set.

The newly created Issue itself will also be part of the live open portfolio if still open during migration.

### Required treatment of #19

If #19 is still open and its governance defect remains unresolved at migration time, evaluate it under the P0 protection branch.

The decided interpretation is:

```text
#19 protects work-governance correctness and authority.

While unresolved, continued agent-driven work can create additional stale or
duplicated work-state representations and increase cross-cutting cleanup.

Therefore #19 qualifies for P0 while those conditions remain true.
```

Do not leave this determination to implementation-agent design judgment.

If #19 has already been completed before the migration, do not reopen it merely to change historical priority.

### Other open Issues

Apply the new deterministic decision tree to every other live open Issue.

Do not preserve an old Priority merely because it was previously assigned.

Do not change:

```text
Status
Phase
Kind
dependencies
body
semantic scope
```

unless a separate already-authorized work item owns such a change.

This Issue's one-time migration owns Priority recalculation only.

## Relationship to Project views

Preserve the current intended Project views unless the shared Project tooling provides a supported way to make the existing `Agent Queue` ordering reflect Priority.

At minimum, repository governance MUST define the pickup rule independently of UI sort configuration.

If supported by the existing Project tooling without inventing new infrastructure, configure `Agent Queue` so Priority is visible and higher-priority items are surfaced before lower-priority items.

Do not create a new dashboard, synchronization service, bot, custom ranking field, or generated work-status file.

The governance rule is authoritative for agent behavior even if Project UI sorting capabilities are limited.

## No automation required

Do not add:

```text
GitHub Actions automation
a priority checker
a scheduling bot
a synchronization daemon
a generated priority report
a portfolio database
a second ranking field
```

as part of this Issue.

The immediate requirement is repository governance plus agent procedure.

If repeated procedural failures later justify automation, route that as a separate independently scoped Issue.

## Interaction with #19 implementation

If #19 is implemented first:

* read its final governance changes;
* retain the new single-live-owner rules;
* add this Issue's Priority lifecycle rules without restoring duplicated Project metadata to Issue bodies.

If this Issue is implemented first:

* do not perform #19's Issue-body normalization;
* #19 later applies its own cleanup;
* #19 must preserve this Issue's dynamic Priority rules.

Neither Issue supersedes the other.

## Acceptance criteria

* [ ] `docs/repository-governance/turnlock-rust-engineering.md` explicitly defines Priority as live portfolio-relative scheduling state rather than one-time Issue classification.
* [ ] Existing Project values `P0`, `P1`, `P2`, and `P3` are preserved without adding another ranking field.
* [ ] The distinction between P0 and P1 explicitly includes whether normal work can safely continue before the Issue is resolved.
* [ ] The existing unresolved Specification semantic-Finding default to P0 is preserved.
* [ ] Durable Issue creation explicitly triggers a Priority revalidation of every open Turnlock-Rust Engineering Issue.
* [ ] Issue completion/closure/reopening, dependency-graph changes, authority changes affecting prerequisites, phase transitions, and validated cross-cutting governance findings are documented as revalidation triggers.
* [ ] Non-material metadata changes do not create recursive/full revalidation loops.
* [ ] The governance profile defines the exact full-portfolio revalidation algorithm.
* [ ] Revalidation updates only Priority when only Priority changed.
* [ ] No Issue body is used as a live copy of Project Priority.
* [ ] Priority remains distinct from Status, Phase, Kind, and native dependency relationships.
* [ ] `P0 / Backlog` is explicitly valid when critical work is not independently executable.
* [ ] Autonomous pickup considers `Ready` items only.
* [ ] Autonomous pickup selects `P0` before `P1`, `P1` before `P2`, and `P2` before `P3`.
* [ ] A direct user request may override pickup order for one action without implicitly changing Priority.
* [ ] Equal-priority Ready work respects native dependency order and otherwise retains existing Project ordering rather than introducing another ranking system.
* [ ] A new P0 does not automatically preempt an `In Progress` Issue solely because of Priority.
* [ ] `AGENTS.md` exposes the operational portfolio-revalidation and highest-priority-Ready pickup rule without duplicating the full policy.
* [ ] The live open Project portfolio is re-evaluated once immediately after the policy is introduced.
* [ ] Every open Issue at migration time is inspected, even if its Priority ultimately remains unchanged.
* [ ] #19 is moved to P0 if it is still open with the unresolved cross-cutting live-state governance risk described above.
* [ ] Only changed live Project Priority fields are mutated during the one-time migration.
* [ ] The migration does not change unrelated Issue bodies, Status, Phase, Kind, semantic scope, or native relationships.
* [ ] No TURNLOCK product semantic, accepted ADR decision, `TL-INV-*`, formal property, runtime behavior, API, DSL, or implementation mechanism is changed by this governance work.
* [ ] No priority bot, checker, generated dashboard, synchronization service, or second ranking field is introduced.
* [ ] Repository-required validation remains green.
* [ ] Final verification confirms repository governance, live Project Priority state, and autonomous-pickup policy are mutually consistent.

## Non-goals

This Issue does NOT:

```text
change TURNLOCK product semantics
change accepted ADR bodies
add or modify TL-INV-* requirements
change TLA+ properties
create formal verification evidence
implement Rust
define workflow syntax
change #19's live-state mirroring scope
normalize Issue bodies under #19
replace native dependencies with Priority
make every P0 Ready
automatically preempt In Progress work
introduce numeric priority scoring
introduce severity fields
introduce a second rank field
create a dashboard
create a priority bot
create a GitHub synchronization service
create a repository priority checker
```

This is repository work-management governance only.

## Validation

Implementation must use the then-current mandatory validation contract in `AGENTS.md`.

Under the current repository contract, the required repository checks include:

```bash
python3 -m venv .venv
.venv/bin/python -m pip install --requirement requirements.txt

.venv/bin/python scripts/tests/test-adr-metadata.py
```

Do not regenerate formal or ADR projections unless an authoritative source that owns those projections actually changes.

Changes to:

```text

docs/repository-governance/turnlock-rust-engineering.md
```

must not cause unrelated normative, ADR, or formal artifacts to change.

After the one-time Priority migration, separately verify the live Project state.

Product semantics: make TURNLOCK Core runtime-composable for external execution realizations

value.body:
## Problem

ADR-013 established heterogeneous workflow-owned parallel fan-out/fan-in for mechanical execution, bounded raw-LLM inference, and independent-agent execution, but explicitly left main-agent continuation in a concurrent branch unresolved.

That unresolved boundary now blocks composition-admissibility work because TURNLOCK must know whether a main-agent continuation may participate in workflow-owned concurrency and, if so, how the unique continuing main-agent cognitive lineage behaves when the declared topology contains multiple possible main-agent uses.

The relevant distinction is not whether two main-agent regions happen to execute at the same wall-clock instant. The semantic question is whether the workflow topology permits two independently concurrent, non-causally-ordered continuations of the same main-agent cognitive lineage.

This Issue records an explicit product-owner decision supplied for specification work. The Issue is work/provenance, not normative product authority: the decision becomes repository authority only through the required new accepted ADR and synchronized normative artifacts.

## Existing authority

The resulting decision MUST remain compatible with, and MUST NOT reopen, the following accepted authority:

- ADR-005: a main-agent step is a reversible and repeatable control handoff inside an active workflow.
- ADR-006: ordinary TURNLOCK workflow execution is nested inside the originating main-agent session lifecycle.
- ADR-007: a main-agent step preserves the continuing main-agent cognitive lineage and ordinary interactive coding-agent agency; a fresh or reconstructed agent is not automatically equivalent.
- ADR-008: nested workflow invocation from a main-agent region preserves structured suspension and return to the same immediate caller context.
- ADR-013: heterogeneous workflow-owned parallel fan-out/fan-in is accepted for mechanical, raw-LLM, and independent-agent branches, while main-agent concurrency was intentionally left unresolved.
- ADR-014: TURNLOCK executes declared orchestration and MUST NOT invent undeclared global strategy or rewrite the workflow topology.
- `TL-INV-014`: main-agent cognitive-lineage continuity.
- `TL-INV-024`: heterogeneous parallel composition, currently without authority for main-agent continuation as an ordinary concurrent branch.
- `TL-INV-027`: workflow-owned parallel semantic fan-out/fan-in.
- `TL-INV-030`: every change in global control must remain authorized by workflow semantics.
- `TL-INV-031`: the workflow orchestration surface must remain expressive enough to encode known control structure directly.

Issue #6 owns transitive nested-composition admissibility. It must later consume the authoritative result of this Issue rather than deciding main-agent concurrency itself.

## Discovery classification

### B — product/semantic decision

The following capability was explicitly left open by ADR-013 and therefore requires new product authority:

```text
A main-agent continuation MAY participate as a branch of workflow-owned concurrent execution.
```

This is a new product/semantic decision and MUST be recorded through a new ADR before being treated as normative TURNLOCK behavior.

### A — consequences derived after accepting that decision

Once main-agent participation in workflow-owned concurrency is accepted, the following consequences are required by the existing main-agent-lineage and workflow-owned-control semantics:

```text
one continuing main-agent cognitive lineage
MUST NOT be forked or duplicated across
independently concurrent, non-causally-ordered continuations
```

and:

```text
runtime scheduling order
MUST NOT manufacture semantic causal ordering
that the declared workflow does not provide
```

and:

```text
a main-agent handoff occurring in one parallel branch
MUST NOT implicitly suspend unrelated sibling branches
whose progression remains enabled by the declared topology
```

The implementation or formal mechanism used to establish ordering, co-reachability, mutual exclusion, or admissibility is not selected by this Issue.

## Product-owner decision to encode

The resulting normative decision MUST have all of the following meaning.

### 1. Main-agent continuation is permitted in workflow-owned concurrency

A declared parallel region MAY contain a main-agent continuation alongside other branch types.

For example, this topology is semantically permitted:

```text
parallel
├── mechanical
├── raw LLM
├── independent agent
└── main-agent region
```

The main-agent branch remains semantically a continuation of the existing session main-agent cognitive lineage. It MUST NOT be silently implemented as a fresh independent agent merely because it participates in concurrent workflow topology.

### 2. Main-agent handoff is branch-local

When a main-agent continuation is reached inside one concurrent branch, the handoff suspends only the calling continuation represented by that branch.

It does NOT, merely because the main agent is active, suspend independently active sibling branches permitted by the declared parallel topology.

Conceptually:

```text
parallel
├── mechanical ────────────────>
├── independent agent ─────────>
└── main-agent region ──────>

join
↓
continuation
```

The branches remain governed by the workflow-declared concurrency and join semantics.

Completion of the main-agent branch does not itself complete the parallel region. The workflow may pass the join only according to its declared join semantics.

### 3. One main-agent cognitive lineage is non-forkable

The same continuing main-agent cognitive lineage MUST NOT be forked, duplicated, or shared across two independently concurrent continuations that are not causally ordered by the declared orchestration.

Therefore this topology is not admissible for the same main-agent lineage:

```text
parallel
├── main-agent A
└── main-agent B
```

The problem is not merely simultaneous wall-clock activity. The problem is that the workflow declares neither:

```text
A before B
```

nor:

```text
B before A
```

for the same cognitive lineage.

### 4. Validity is determined by declared causal structure, not scheduler timing

A topology MUST NOT become valid merely because one main-agent use happens to finish before another reaches the main agent during one particular execution.

For example:

```text
parallel
├── main-agent A
└── mechanical
      ↓
      main-agent B
```

cannot be admitted on the reasoning:

```text
"A happened to finish before B requested the main agent,
therefore no conflict occurred."
```

Unless the declared orchestration itself establishes the required ordering or mutual exclusion, the two uses remain unordered possible continuations of the same lineage.

TURNLOCK MUST NOT silently serialize such uses. Hidden serialization would create an observable cognitive causal order not declared by the workflow and would therefore alter workflow meaning.

### 5. Declared causal ordering permits repeated use

Repeated use of the same main-agent lineage is valid when the workflow declares the causal order.

For example:

```text
main-agent A
↓
main-agent B
```

is valid.

Likewise:

```text
parallel
├── main-agent A
└── mechanical
join
↓
main-agent B
```

is valid because the join establishes the relevant order before `B`.

The number of main-agent uses is not itself restricted.

### 6. Established mutual exclusion also permits multiple syntactic uses

Multiple branches MAY syntactically contain a use of the same main-agent lineage when the declared orchestration establishes that those uses cannot both be reached as concurrent continuations.

For example, a structure equivalent in semantics to:

```text
parallel
├── if X:
│     main-agent A
└── if !X:
      main-agent B
```

may be admissible when TURNLOCK can establish from the declared orchestration that the two main-agent uses are mutually exclusive.

The normative rule is NOT:

```text
at most one syntactic main-agent occurrence in a parallel region
```

The normative rule is about co-reachability of unordered continuations of the same cognitive lineage.

How mutual exclusion or co-reachability is represented or established is NOT decided here.

### 7. Fail closed when the required compatibility cannot be established

If a topology potentially exposes the same main-agent lineage to unordered concurrent continuations and TURNLOCK cannot establish sufficient declared ordering or mutual exclusion, the topology/invocation MUST NOT be admitted under full TURNLOCK semantics.

TURNLOCK MUST NOT repair the problem by:

* silently serializing the continuations;
* choosing whichever main-agent use reaches the resource first;
* duplicating or cloning the main-agent cognitive lineage;
* substituting fresh independent agents;
* changing one execution form into another; or
* inventing an undeclared ordering.

### 8. Structured nesting remains valid and is not a fork

Structured nested main-agent use remains valid where call/suspension/return semantics preserve one sequential cognitive lineage.

For example:

```text
main-agent region A
  ↓
  invoke workflow B
      ↓
      main-agent region B
      ↓
  return to main-agent region A
```

does not constitute a concurrent fork of the main-agent lineage.

The relevant structure is sequential suspension and resumption of the same lineage under structured nested invocation.

## Required normative property

The resolution MUST establish a normative obligation equivalent to:

> An admitted TURNLOCK topology MUST NOT permit the same main-agent cognitive lineage to continue through two independently concurrent, non-causally-ordered continuations. Declared causal ordering or established mutual exclusion may permit multiple uses of that lineage. Runtime scheduling order MUST NOT be used to manufacture the required semantic ordering.

The exact final wording may be normalized to repository terminology when the ADR/specification synchronization is performed, but its semantic strength MUST NOT be changed.

The invariant-admission process MUST determine whether this obligation receives a new `TL-INV-*` identity. The current analysis expects a distinct invariant to be justified because existing lineage-continuity and workflow-owned-control invariants do not independently state concurrent non-forkability, but the repository's invariant-admission procedure remains mandatory.

Do NOT reuse or silently repurpose an existing invariant identity.

## Required repository outcome when this Issue is executed

Resolution of this Issue MUST:

1. create a new chronological ADR recording the B-class product decision and its A-class consequences;
2. leave accepted historical ADR bodies unchanged;
3. synchronize the normative specification with the accepted main-agent concurrency semantics;
4. update ADR-013 only through later decision-history relations/projections as permitted by repository governance, not by editing its accepted body;
5. run the repository invariant-admission test for the main-agent-lineage non-forkability obligation;
6. if a new invariant is admitted, allocate a new stable `TL-INV-*` identity rather than modifying the meaning of an existing identity;
7. synchronize `formal/verification.yaml` only to the extent required for intended traceability/formal applicability;
8. regenerate every mechanically derived projection required by repository governance;
9. preserve the distinction between normative semantics and C/D implementation or modeling choices;
10. leave Issue #6 to consume this new authoritative result rather than using #6 itself as authority for main-agent concurrency.

## Explicit non-goals

This Issue MUST NOT decide or introduce:

* a scheduler algorithm;
* a lock, mutex, semaphore, queue, lease, token, actor, or runtime ownership mechanism;
* a concrete `main_agent_id` representation;
* a rule equating session identity with a technical main-agent identifier;
* a static-analysis algorithm;
* arbitrary theorem proving over workflow conditions;
* an effect system;
* a capability lattice;
* a Rust type, trait, enum, API, or data structure;
* DSL syntax;
* process or thread architecture;
* a concrete proof representation for mutual exclusion;
* a concrete co-reachability algorithm;
* sibling session-root invocation policy;
* independent-agent-selected workflow invocation;
* recursive/cyclic workflow-call policy except where examples are needed to preserve already accepted structured nesting semantics;
* failure propagation, retries, cancellation, timeout, crash recovery, or resource-budget semantics;
* repository-authoring conflict or convergence semantics;
* any RUu-specific mechanism;
* active replanning or active rebinding.

In particular, do not turn the product rule into:

```text
at most one active main-agent region globally
```

because runtime simultaneity is not the governing semantic property.

Do not turn it into:

```text
one main-agent step per parallel region
```

because established mutual exclusion can make multiple syntactic occurrences valid.

## Acceptance criteria

* [ ] A new ADR explicitly accepts main-agent continuation as a valid participant in workflow-owned concurrent topology.
* [ ] The ADR/specification preserve main-agent cognitive-lineage semantics from ADR-007 rather than redefining a concurrent main-agent branch as a fresh agent.
* [ ] Main-agent handoff inside a concurrent branch is explicitly branch-local and does not implicitly suspend unrelated sibling branches.
* [ ] Main-agent branch completion is distinguished from completion of the enclosing parallel region/join.
* [ ] The same main-agent cognitive lineage cannot be admitted into two independently concurrent, non-causally-ordered continuations.
* [ ] Runtime scheduling order is explicitly insufficient to manufacture semantic causal ordering.
* [ ] Silent serialization of unordered main-agent uses is prohibited.
* [ ] Silent cloning/forking/substitution of the main-agent lineage is prohibited.
* [ ] Declared causal ordering permits repeated main-agent use.
* [ ] Established declared mutual exclusion may permit multiple syntactic main-agent uses.
* [ ] The semantics do not require TURNLOCK to prove arbitrary program theorems; representation/detection of mutual exclusion remains C/D.
* [ ] When compatibility cannot be established for a potentially conflicting topology, admission fails closed rather than changing workflow meaning.
* [ ] Structured nested suspension/return remains distinguishable from concurrent lineage fork.
* [ ] The invariant-admission test is applied explicitly and any new invariant receives a new stable identity.
* [ ] ADR-013's accepted body is not edited.
* [ ] Issue #6 can consume the resulting accepted authority without itself deciding main-agent concurrency.
* [ ] No scheduler, locking primitive, effect system, static-analysis algorithm, Rust mechanism, DSL syntax, or harness-specific mechanism becomes normative.
* [ ] Required normative, decision-history, formal-traceability, and generated artifacts are synchronized.
* [ ] Repository-required validation passes.

## Semantic examples that the final authority must preserve

### Admissible: one main-agent branch with independent sibling work

```text
parallel
├── mechanical
├── raw LLM
├── independent agent
└── main-agent M
join
↓
continue
```

### Not admissible: unordered fork of the same lineage

```text
parallel
├── main-agent M/A
└── main-agent M/B
```

### Not rescued by accidental runtime order

```text
parallel
├── main-agent M/A
└── mechanical
      ↓
      main-agent M/B
```

The topology does not become valid merely because `M/A` happens to finish first.

### Admissible: explicit causal order

```text
main-agent M/A
↓
main-agent M/B
```

### Admissible: join establishes ordering

```text
parallel
├── main-agent M/A
└── mechanical
join
↓
main-agent M/B
```

### Potentially admissible: established mutual exclusion

```text
parallel
├── if X:
│     main-agent M/A
└── if !X:
      main-agent M/B
```

This is admissible only when the declared semantics allow TURNLOCK to establish that the two uses cannot be concurrent. No specific proof or analysis mechanism is selected here.

### Admissible: structured nested use is sequential, not a fork

```text
main-agent region A
↓
invoke workflow B
  ↓
  main-agent region B
  ↓
return
↓
main-agent region A resumes
```

## Validation when resolving the Issue

For any eventual repository modification performed while resolving this Issue, follow the then-current `AGENTS.md` validation contract.

At the current repository state, this includes creating the required isolated Python environment if absent, rendering affected generated artifacts when their canonical sources change, and running:

```bash
.venv/bin/python scripts/check-repository-integrity.py
```

Do not claim TLA+/TLC verification merely from planned traceability.

## Relevant repository references

* `docs/specification/turnlock-spec.md`
* `docs/adr/adr-005-model-main-agent-steps-as-reversible-repeatable-control-handoffs.md`
* `docs/adr/adr-006-nest-workflow-execution-inside-the-originating-main-agent-session-lifecycle.md`
* `docs/adr/adr-007-preserve-main-agent-cognitive-lineage-and-ordinary-interactive-agency.md`
* ADR-008, the accepted ADR governing nested workflow invocation from main-agent regions
* `docs/adr/adr-013-allow-heterogeneous-parallel-fan-out-across-execution-forms.md`
* `docs/adr/adr-014-define-turnlock-as-the-orchestration-engine-and-the-workflow-as-the-orchestration-program.md`
* `formal/verification.yaml`
* `docs/repository-governance/turnlock-rust-discovery-classification.md`
* Issue #6 — `Semantics: close execution restrictions under nested workflow composition`
