value.title: Semantics: delegate dynamic nested-workflow invocation to independent-agent regions without main-agent reachability

value.body:
## Problem

TURNLOCK defines ordinary workflow execution as a bounded episode inside an originating coding-agent session.

ADR-006 establishes the top-level lifecycle:

```text
main-agent session
↓
workflow
↓
main-agent session resumes
```

ADR-007 establishes that a main-agent handoff preserves the continuing cognitive lineage of that coding-agent session rather than substituting a fresh reconstructed agent.

ADR-008 then generalizes workflow composition through structured nested invocation and immediate-caller return.

Those accepted semantics define a single root workflow episode and arbitrary structured nested composition beneath it, but they do not decide whether the same coding-agent session may simultaneously carry multiple independent session-root TURNLOCK invocations.

The unresolved shape is:

```text
coding-agent session S
↓
session-root invocation A accepted
↓
A remains active

while A is active:

attempt another session-root invocation B
attached to the same session S
```

Without an explicit product decision, several materially different behaviors remain possible:

```text
accept both roots concurrently
reject the second root
silently queue the second root
silently serialize the roots
reinterpret the second root as nested under the first
replace the first root
fork or clone the main-agent lineage
```

None of those alternatives follows uniquely from current accepted authority.

This Issue records an explicit product-owner decision supplied for specification work.

The Issue is work/provenance, not normative product authority: the decision becomes repository authority only through the required new accepted ADR and synchronized normative artifacts.

## Terminology

Use `session-root invocation` for the invocation whose immediate surrounding lifecycle is the coding-agent session itself.

Conceptually:

```text
coding-agent session S
↓
session-root invocation A
```

is distinct from:

```text
session-root invocation A
↓
some authorized execution context
↓
nested invocation B
```

`B` is not another session-root invocation merely because it is another workflow invocation.

Do not use the ambiguous rule:

```text
one workflow per session
```

That rule is NOT accepted and would incorrectly prohibit ordinary nested and concurrent workflow composition.

The decision concerns only:

```text
one active session-root invocation
per coding-agent session
```

## Existing authority

The resulting decision MUST remain compatible with, and MUST NOT reopen, the following accepted authority:

* ADR-005: workflow/main-agent interaction uses reversible control handoffs.
* ADR-006: ordinary TURNLOCK workflow execution is semantically nested inside the lifecycle of the originating main-agent session, and normal root completion returns to that surrounding interaction.
* ADR-007: main-agent continuation preserves the current main-agent cognitive lineage and ordinary interactive coding-agent agency.
* ADR-008: nested workflow invocation uses structured suspension and immediate-caller return; nested invocation is distinct from sibling or top-level workflow concurrency.
* ADR-013: workflow-owned heterogeneous parallel fan-out/fan-in exists for accepted execution forms.
* ADR-014: the workflow program owns declared orchestration and TURNLOCK executes it without inventing undeclared strategy.
* ADR-022 and ADR-023: nested workflow invocation has explicit caller-context and preserved-continuation semantics.
* ADR-027: every accepted invocation independently binds a stable governing workflow definition.
* `TL-INV-014`: main-agent cognitive-lineage continuity.
* `TL-INV-017`–`TL-INV-019`: structured nested invocation, immediate-caller return, and enclosing-orchestration preservation.
* `TL-INV-027`: declared parallel fan-out/fan-in remains workflow-owned.
* `TL-INV-030`: global control transitions must remain authorized by workflow semantics.

Issue #22 owns main-agent participation in workflow-owned concurrency and main-agent lineage non-forkability.

Issue #23 owns recursive/cyclic workflow invocation.

Issue #24 owns explicitly delegated independent-agent-selected nested workflow invocation.

Issue #6 owns transitive nested-composition admissibility.

This Issue MUST NOT reopen those decisions.

## Discovery classification

### B — one active session-root invocation per coding-agent session

The accepted corpus does not currently determine how many independent session-root workflow episodes may remain active simultaneously in one coding-agent session.

The product-owner decision is:

```text
A coding-agent session MAY have
at most one active session-root TURNLOCK invocation.
```

This is a product/semantic decision and requires new accepted ADR authority before becoming normative product meaning.

### B — second same-session root attempt is rejected before acceptance

When a session-root invocation is already active for coding-agent session `S`, a later attempt to create another session-root invocation attached to `S` MUST be rejected before that second invocation is accepted.

Conceptually:

```text
session S
↓
accept root A
↓
A active

attempt root B in S
↓
reject B before acceptance
```

The selected product behavior is rejection.

TURNLOCK MUST NOT silently replace rejection with queueing, serialization, reinterpretation as nesting, lineage cloning, or another undeclared coordination policy.

### A — one coding-agent session carries one continuing main-agent lineage

ADR-006 and ADR-007 already require the root workflow episode to remain embedded in the continuing cognitive lifecycle of the originating main-agent session.

The semantic model is therefore:

```text
coding-agent session S
↓
one continuing main-agent cognitive lineage M(S)
```

This is a semantic continuity property.

It does NOT require any concrete identity representation such as:

```text
main_agent_id == session_id
```

and does not require process identity, UUID equality, PID identity, or any other implementation mechanism.

### A — rejection creates no second invocation

Once the B-class admission boundary above is accepted, rejecting the second root attempt before acceptance entails:

```text
no accepted root B
no B execution episode
no B normal completion event
no B call/return episode
no B root return transition
```

The rejected attempt is not a failed accepted invocation.

No second invocation exists.

### A — rejection does not modify the already-active root

If root `A` is already accepted and a root attempt `B` is rejected:

```text
A accepted and active
B attempted
B rejected before acceptance
```

the rejection of `B` MUST NOT by itself:

```text
cancel A
replace A
pause A
rebind A
rewrite A
complete A
change A's governing definition
consume A's continuation
change A's caller
```

`A` continues according to its own governing semantics.

### A — session-root exclusivity does not prohibit nested composition

The rule:

```text
one active session-root invocation per session
```

does NOT imply:

```text
one active workflow invocation per session
```

Nested invocations remain governed by ordinary structured-composition semantics.

For example:

```text
session S
↓
root A
  ↓
  main-agent region
      ↓
      nested B
          ↓
          nested C
```

does not violate session-root exclusivity.

`B` and `C` are nested invocation occurrences, not additional session roots.

### A — session-root exclusivity does not prohibit workflow-owned concurrency

Native TURNLOCK concurrency inside one root remains distinct from sibling session roots.

For example:

```text
session S
↓
root workflow P
↓
parallel
├── workflow A
└── workflow B
↓
join
```

may be valid under the applicable accepted concurrency and admissibility semantics.

`A` and `B` are branches inside workflow-owned declared topology.

They are not two independent roots attached directly to `S`.

### A — the restriction is per session, not global

The accepted restriction is scoped to one coding-agent session.

Therefore it does NOT establish:

```text
TURNLOCK may have only one root invocation globally
```

Distinct sessions remain semantically independent with respect to this rule.

Conceptually:

```text
session S1
↓
root A

session S2
↓
root B
```

may execute concurrently.

## Product-owner decision to encode

The resulting normative decision MUST have all of the following meaning.

### 1. At most one active session-root invocation per coding-agent session

For any coding-agent session `S`:

```text
active session-root invocation count for S <= 1
```

This is a semantic cardinality rule over root invocation attachment.

It is NOT a limit on:

```text
nested workflow depth
number of workflow invocations in an execution tree
parallel workflow branches inside declared topology
number of independent-agent regions
number of raw LLM regions
number of mechanical branches
number of TURNLOCK sessions globally
```

### 2. The second same-session root attempt is rejected at admission

If:

```text
root A is already active for session S
```

and a new request attempts to establish:

```text
root B attached directly to session S
```

then `B` MUST NOT become an accepted invocation.

Conceptually:

```text
attempt root B
↓
session-root admission check
↓
existing active root for same session?
├── no  → ordinary remaining acceptance rules apply
└── yes → reject B before acceptance
```

This Issue does not define the complete invocation-acceptance algorithm.

It defines only the same-session root cardinality constraint at that boundary.

### 3. Do not defer the conflict until runtime resource contention

TURNLOCK MUST NOT accept two same-session roots and postpone resolution until both later attempt to use the session's main-agent lineage.

This is NOT the selected semantics:

```text
accept root A
accept root B
↓
wait until A and B collide on main agent
↓
decide who wins
```

The second root is rejected before acceptance.

The validity of the second root MUST NOT depend on runtime timing or scheduling accidents.

### 4. Do not silently queue the second root

The following is NOT the selected semantic behavior:

```text
root A active
↓
root B requested
↓
TURNLOCK silently queues B
↓
A ends
↓
TURNLOCK starts B later
```

A request for a second root while the session already has an active root is rejected.

If TURNLOCK ever offers an explicit user-visible or workflow-declared queueing facility, that would require separately defined semantics.

This Issue introduces no such facility.

### 5. Do not silently serialize sibling roots

TURNLOCK MUST NOT transform:

```text
root A requested
root B requested while A active
```

into an undeclared ordering:

```text
A
↓
B
```

merely to avoid root concurrency.

That would invent orchestration not declared by a workflow and not selected by the caller.

### 6. Do not reinterpret the second root as a nested invocation

The following transformation is forbidden:

```text
session S
↓
root A active

external/user attempt root B
↓
TURNLOCK silently treats B
as though A had invoked B
```

A nested invocation has an actual authorized immediate caller context.

A root-admission conflict does not manufacture such a caller.

Therefore:

```text
second root attempt
!=
implicit nested invocation
```

### 7. Do not replace the active root

The second root attempt MUST NOT cause:

```text
A active
↓
B requested
↓
A disappears
↓
B becomes root
```

unless separate explicit semantics later define an intentional replacement/cancellation operation.

No such operation is introduced here.

### 8. Do not clone or fork the session main-agent lineage

TURNLOCK MUST NOT satisfy simultaneous sibling-root attachment by inventing:

```text
session S
├── main-agent lineage M1 for root A
└── cloned main-agent lineage M2 for root B
```

when both are presented as continuation of the same coding-agent session.

ADR-007's main-agent continuity semantics remain authoritative.

A cloned or reconstructed fresh lineage is not automatically the same main-agent continuation.

### 9. Native same-session concurrency remains inside declared workflow topology

If the user requires concurrent TURNLOCK work inside one coding-agent session, the native semantic shape is workflow-owned composition.

For example:

```text
session S
↓
root P
↓
parallel
├── invoke A
└── invoke B
↓
join
```

subject to the applicable accepted composition rules.

The root workflow `P` owns the concurrent topology.

TURNLOCK executes it.

This Issue does NOT require users to use parallelism and does NOT define a specific parallel syntax.

It only distinguishes declared workflow concurrency from independent sibling session roots.

### 10. Nested main-agent invocation remains nested, not a second root

This remains valid:

```text
session S
↓
root A
  ↓
  main-agent region
      ↓
      main agent invokes workflow B
      ↓
      B completes
      ↓
      main-agent region resumes
```

`B` is an ADR-008-style nested invocation.

The session still has one root:

```text
A
```

Nested composition MUST NOT be counted as multiple session-root attachment.

### 11. Different coding-agent sessions may each have an active root

The restriction is local to a single coding-agent session.

This is compatible:

```text
session S1
↓
root A
```

concurrently with:

```text
session S2
↓
root B
```

No global singleton TURNLOCK root is introduced.

### 12. A later root is allowed after the prior root is no longer active

The cardinality rule is:

```text
at most one ACTIVE session-root invocation
per coding-agent session
```

It is NOT:

```text
only one root invocation ever per session
```

Therefore the following lifecycle is permitted:

```text
session S
↓
root A accepted
↓
A eventually leaves the active-root lifecycle
↓
session S resumes ordinary root-entry eligibility
↓
later root B may be attempted
```

This Issue does NOT define the complete meaning of root termination under failure, cancellation, crash, timeout, or recovery.

It only establishes that the exclusion applies while an accepted session-root invocation remains active according to the applicable lifecycle semantics.

### 13. External process concurrency does not override TURNLOCK admission semantics

A user, harness, shell, external launcher, or operating system may technically permit multiple processes or commands to attempt TURNLOCK invocation.

Technical process concurrency does not itself authorize multiple same-session roots.

The distinction is:

```text
technical ability to launch multiple attempts
!=
TURNLOCK authority to accept multiple session roots
```

If a second external attempt targets the same coding-agent session while that session already carries an active root, TURNLOCK's session-root admission rule rejects the second root attempt.

TURNLOCK does not need to prevent the operating system from creating the process that made the attempt.

### 14. A rejected root attempt creates no root lifecycle

When the second same-session root attempt is rejected before acceptance:

```text
no root B invocation exists
```

Therefore it has no:

```text
governing invocation lifetime
normal root completion
root return-to-session transition
nested descendants
active orchestration episode
```

The attempt may produce an observable rejection to its initiator.

This Issue does NOT define the concrete error representation, transport, UI, message, exception, exit code, or retry behavior.

### 15. The active root remains intact after rejection

Given:

```text
session S
↓
root A active

attempt root B
↓
reject B
```

the required state is conceptually:

```text
session S
↓
root A remains active under its original semantics
```

The rejection of `B` does not consume or mutate `A`.

## Required normative property

The resolution MUST establish product meaning equivalent to:

> A coding-agent session may have at most one active session-root TURNLOCK invocation. While such an invocation remains active, an attempt to accept another session-root invocation attached to the same session MUST be rejected before acceptance. TURNLOCK MUST NOT repair the conflict by silently queueing, serializing, nesting, replacing, or cloning the session's main-agent cognitive lineage. Nested invocations and workflow-declared concurrency inside the active root remain governed by their ordinary semantics, and distinct coding-agent sessions may execute independent root invocations concurrently.

The exact final wording may be normalized to canonical repository terminology during ADR/specification synchronization.

Its semantic strength MUST NOT be weakened, broadened, or replaced.

## Invariant-admission requirement

Do NOT pre-decide the identity or number of new `TL-INV-*` invariants.

The resolution MUST explicitly apply the repository invariant-admission procedure.

Evaluate at minimum these aspects separately:

```text
A. session-root cardinality:
one active session-root invocation per coding-agent session
```

```text
B. admission rule:
a second same-session root attempt is rejected before acceptance
```

```text
C. preservation:
rejection does not modify the already-active root
```

```text
D. scope:
nested invocations and workflow-owned concurrency
are not additional session roots
```

```text
E. locality:
the restriction is per coding-agent session,
not global TURNLOCK state
```

The current product analysis expects that session-root cardinality may justify a distinct stable invariant because current accepted invariants do not independently state this universal per-session root constraint.

However, the repository invariant-admission procedure remains authoritative.

Do NOT invent an invariant number in the Issue.

Do NOT:

```text
reuse an existing TL-INV identity for new meaning
silently broaden an existing invariant
rename an existing invariant merely to absorb this rule
```

If a new invariant is admitted when this Issue is later resolved, allocate a new stable identity according to repository governance.

## Required repository outcome when this Issue is executed

Resolution of this Issue MUST:

1. create a new chronological ADR recording the B-class one-active-session-root-per-session decision;
2. record the B-class decision to reject a second same-session root attempt before acceptance;
3. record that silent queueing, serialization, reinterpretation as nesting, root replacement, and main-agent-lineage cloning are not the selected semantics;
4. preserve ADR-006's root workflow lifecycle;
5. preserve ADR-007's main-agent cognitive-lineage continuity;
6. preserve ADR-008/ADR-022/ADR-023 structured nested invocation semantics;
7. distinguish session-root invocation from nested invocation;
8. distinguish sibling session roots from workflow-owned concurrency inside one root;
9. preserve the ability for different coding-agent sessions to carry independent roots concurrently;
10. preserve the ability for a later root to begin after the previous root is no longer active;
11. apply the repository invariant-admission procedure;
12. create a new `TL-INV-*` identity only if justified by that procedure;
13. synchronize the normative specification with the accepted session-root semantics;
14. synchronize `formal/verification.yaml` only to the extent justified by actual intended formal applicability;
15. regenerate all required mechanically derived projections;
16. leave accepted historical ADR bodies unchanged;
17. preserve normative semantics separately from session identity, locking, scheduling, process, API, DSL, and runtime implementation mechanisms.

## Explicit non-goals

This Issue MUST NOT decide or introduce:

* a concrete session identifier;
* a concrete main-agent identifier;
* `main_agent_id == session_id`;
* UUID semantics;
* PID semantics;
* process identity;
* thread identity;
* a session registry design;
* a root registry implementation;
* mutexes;
* locks;
* file locks;
* database locks;
* advisory locks;
* leases;
* fencing tokens;
* semaphores;
* sockets;
* lock servers;
* leader election;
* a queue;
* an implicit root scheduler;
* root priority scheduling;
* root preemption;
* root takeover;
* explicit root replacement semantics;
* cancellation semantics;
* timeout semantics;
* failure propagation;
* crash recovery;
* stale-root recovery;
* distributed coordination;
* multi-process coordination protocol;
* multi-machine coordination protocol;
* persistence;
* replay;
* an invocation API;
* a Rust type, trait, enum, struct, module, or crate;
* DSL syntax;
* a TLA+ state-variable representation;
* a TLC finite bound;
* a concrete formal encoding;
* a harness implementation;
* a slash-command implementation;
* multi-user semantics;
* authentication;
* authorization infrastructure;
* workflow-owned parallel semantics beyond consuming accepted authority;
* main-agent concurrency semantics beyond consuming Issue #22's accepted result when available;
* recursion/cyclic-call semantics beyond consuming Issue #23's accepted result when available;
* independent-agent-selected invocation semantics beyond consuming Issue #24's accepted result when available;
* transitive nested-composition admissibility beyond consuming Issue #6's accepted result when relevant;
* repository-authoring conflict/convergence semantics;
* any RUu-specific mechanism.

In particular, do NOT convert the decision into any of these incorrect rules:

```text
only one TURNLOCK workflow may execute in a session
```

```text
only one TURNLOCK workflow may execute globally
```

```text
nested invocation counts as another root
```

```text
parallel workflow branches count as sibling roots
```

```text
the second root should wait until the first finishes
```

```text
TURNLOCK may silently queue the second root
```

```text
TURNLOCK may silently treat the second root as nested
```

```text
TURNLOCK may clone the session main-agent lineage
```

```text
the session may only invoke one root workflow during its entire lifetime
```

None of those rules has been accepted.

## Acceptance criteria

* [ ] A new accepted ADR explicitly defines `session-root invocation` or an equivalent unambiguous canonical term.
* [ ] The normative semantics establish at most one active session-root invocation per coding-agent session.
* [ ] A second same-session session-root attempt while the first remains active is rejected before acceptance.
* [ ] The decision is expressed as an admission constraint rather than a first-runtime-contention rule.
* [ ] Runtime timing or scheduler order cannot make two same-session roots acceptable.
* [ ] The second root is not silently queued.
* [ ] The second root is not silently serialized after the first.
* [ ] The second root is not silently reinterpreted as a nested invocation.
* [ ] The second root does not replace the active root.
* [ ] TURNLOCK does not clone/fork the session main-agent cognitive lineage to support sibling roots.
* [ ] Rejected root admission creates no accepted second invocation.
* [ ] Rejected root admission does not modify, cancel, rebind, pause, or consume the active root's lifecycle/continuation.
* [ ] Nested invocations are explicitly distinguished from session-root invocations.
* [ ] Multiple nested invocation levels remain compatible with one active session root.
* [ ] Workflow-owned parallelism inside the active root is explicitly distinguished from sibling session-root concurrency.
* [ ] Different coding-agent sessions may independently carry roots concurrently.
* [ ] A later root may be admitted after the previous root is no longer active.
* [ ] No global singleton-root restriction is introduced.
* [ ] Technical ability to launch multiple processes/commands is distinguished from TURNLOCK authority to accept multiple same-session roots.
* [ ] No locking, queueing, process, registry, identity, scheduler, API, DSL, Rust, or TLA+ mechanism becomes normative.
* [ ] Failure/cancellation/crash-recovery semantics remain outside scope.
* [ ] The repository invariant-admission procedure is applied explicitly.
* [ ] Any genuinely new invariant receives a new stable `TL-INV-*` identity.
* [ ] No existing invariant is silently broadened or repurposed.
* [ ] Accepted historical ADR bodies remain unchanged.
* [ ] Required normative, decision-history, formal-traceability, and generated artifacts are synchronized.
* [ ] Repository-required validation passes.

## Semantic examples that the final authority must preserve

### Valid: one active root

```text
session S
↓
root A
```

### Invalid: second same-session root while A remains active

```text
session S
├── root A active
└── attempt root B
```

Required result:

```text
root B rejected before acceptance
root A remains active
```

### Invalid repair: silent queue

```text
session S
↓
root A active
↓
root B requested
↓
queue B
↓
A completes
↓
start B
```

This is NOT ordinary session-root admission semantics.

### Invalid repair: silent nesting

```text
session S
↓
root A active

external root B attempt
↓
TURNLOCK invents:
A → nested B
```

This is forbidden because no authorized caller created that nested relation.

### Invalid repair: cloned main-agent lineage

```text
session S
├── root A ↔ cloned main lineage M1
└── root B ↔ cloned main lineage M2
```

This is not same-session main-agent continuation semantics.

### Valid: nested invocation under one root

```text
session S
↓
root A
  ↓
  main-agent region
      ↓
      nested B
          ↓
          nested C
```

The session still has exactly one root: `A`.

### Valid: workflow-owned concurrency under one root

```text
session S
↓
root P
↓
parallel
├── invoke A
└── invoke B
↓
join
```

subject to applicable accepted concurrency/admissibility semantics.

### Valid: different sessions, independent roots

```text
session S1
↓
root A
```

concurrently with:

```text
session S2
↓
root B
```

### Valid: sequential roots in one session

```text
session S
↓
root A
↓
A no longer active
↓
session resumes root-entry eligibility
↓
root B
```

### Rejection does not damage active root

```text
session S
↓
root A active

attempt root B
↓
reject B

result:
root A remains unchanged and active
```

## Validation when resolving the Issue

For any eventual repository modification performed while resolving this Issue, follow the then-current `AGENTS.md` validation contract.

At the current repository state, this includes creation of the required isolated Python environment if absent, regeneration of affected projections when canonical sources change, and execution of:

```bash
.venv/bin/python scripts/check-repository-integrity.py
```

Do not claim TLA+/TLC verification merely from planned formal traceability.

## Relevant repository references

* `docs/specification/turnlock-spec.md`
* `docs/adr/adr-005-model-main-agent-steps-as-reversible-repeatable-control-handoffs.md`
* `docs/adr/adr-006-nest-workflow-execution-inside-the-originating-main-agent-session-lifecycle.md`
* `docs/adr/adr-007-preserve-main-agent-cognitive-lineage-and-ordinary-interactive-agency.md`
* `docs/adr/adr-008-allow-nested-workflow-invocation-from-main-agent-regions.md`
* `docs/adr/adr-013-allow-heterogeneous-parallel-fan-out-across-execution-forms.md`
* `docs/adr/adr-014-define-turnlock-as-the-orchestration-engine-and-the-workflow-as-the-orchestration-program.md`
* `docs/adr/adr-022-allow-workflow-declared-invocation-with-structured-call-return-semantics.md`
* `docs/adr/adr-023-clarify-caller-context-and-continuation-semantics-across-nested-workflow-invocations.md`
* `formal/verification.yaml`
* `docs/repository-governance/turnlock-rust-discovery-classification.md`
* Issue #6 — `Semantics: close execution restrictions under nested workflow composition`
* Issue #9 — `Formal verification: pre-TLA+ semantic readiness`
* Issue #22 — `Semantics: allow main-agent participation in workflow-owned concurrency without cognitive-lineage fork`
* Issue #23 — `Semantics: permit recursive and cyclic workflow invocation under ordinary invocation semantics`
* Issue #24 — `Semantics: delegate dynamic nested-workflow invocation to independent-agent regions without main-agent reachability`

## Problem

The normative terminology checker validates canonical terminology registry
entries against their declared `term-*` anchors, but it does not validate the
inverse relationship.

A syntactically valid canonical-looking anchor can therefore exist in the
normative specification without any corresponding canonical terminology
registry entry.

Because occurrence discovery is driven by concepts already present in the
registry, the lexical definition following that orphan anchor can also escape
the terminology inventory and the repository-integrity check.

This leaves the reserved `term-*` canonical-anchor namespace structurally open.

## Evidence and provenance

The gap was exposed during the post-resolution audit of Issue #6.

At repository revision:

`5e6db2c9fec98960204d4f203b8b5fe7f91dafc3`

Section 2.8A contained the canonical-looking anchor:

`term-nested-composition-admissibility`

and its lexical definition, but the concept was absent from the canonical
terminology registry and `terminology-inventory.yaml`.

The normative terminology checker and Repository integrity validation still
passed.

The repository content itself was corrected in:

`6c71aaa8272889483a44d5c2852d339ca7a002f5`

by registering the concept and its inventory occurrence.

The generic checker gap remains.

Current checker control flow explains the false negative:

1. `parse_blocks()` discovers `term-*` anchors.
2. `discover_occurrences()` validates anchors only while iterating concepts
   already returned by `parse_registry()`.
3. No check compares all discovered `term-*` anchors against the registry's
   declared canonical-anchor set.
4. `_definition_concepts()` cannot identify the unknown lexical concept because
   its vocabulary is also registry-driven.

## Discovery classification

### Statement

The normative terminology checker does not reject a syntactically valid
`term-*` anchor that is absent from the canonical terminology registry.

### Source and evidence

Historical repository revision `5e6db2c9fec98960204d4f203b8b5fe7f91dafc3`
and current `scripts/check-normative-terminology.py`.

### Existing authority

Section 2 of `docs/specification/turnlock-spec.md` requires every normative
concept receiving a lexical definition to be registered in the canonical
terminology registry and identified by its stable `term-*` anchor.

`AGENTS.md` assigns canonical terminology authority to Section 2 and treats
`terminology-inventory.yaml` as non-authoritative review/fingerprint tracking.

### Semantic disposition

`no-normative-impact`

### Affected layers

- `repository-governance-or-documentation`
- `architecture-or-implementation`

### Related discoveries or consequences

A passing repository-integrity check can otherwise miss a new canonical-looking
lexical definition that bypasses the canonical registry and review inventory.

### Required authority

No product-semantic or ADR decision is required. Existing repository authority
already determines the required structural consistency.

### Next action

Close the `term-*` anchor namespace mechanically against the canonical
terminology registry and add regression tests for both the checker API and the
`--list-occurrences` CLI.

## Current authoritative boundary

This is repository-validation tooling.

It MUST NOT modify TURNLOCK product semantics, accepted ADRs, `TL-INV-*`
invariants, formal-verification traceability, or the current canonical
terminology registry contents.

The fix must enforce existing terminology-governance authority rather than
create new terminology rules.

## Scope

In scope:

- reproduce the current orphan-anchor false negative end-to-end;
- reject every parsed `term-*` anchor that is absent from the canonical
  terminology registry;
- preserve the existing registry-to-anchor validation;
- cover the behavior through independent regression tests;
- ensure `--list-occurrences` also fails on an unregistered canonical anchor;
- preserve the existing behavior for conforming specifications;
- run the complete repository-integrity suite.

Out of scope:

- discovering unknown lexical concepts without an explicit `term-*` anchor;
- changing the canonical terminology registry format;
- changing Section 2 product terminology;
- modifying `terminology-inventory.yaml`;
- changing product semantics or ADRs;
- modifying `formal/verification.yaml`;
- adding dependencies;
- refactoring the checker into new modules;
- changing GitHub Actions membership/order;
- redesigning repository integrity;
- generic Markdown validation.

## Dependencies

None.

This finding does not reopen or invalidate Issue #6. The missing registry entry
that exposed the checker gap has already been corrected in the current
repository authority.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The pre-fix checker false negative is reproduced with the real
  `--list-occurrences` CLI using a specification fixture containing an
  unregistered `term-*` anchor.
- [ ] A regression test proves `check_document()` rejects an unregistered
  canonical `term-*` anchor.
- [ ] A regression test proves `--list-occurrences` exits nonzero and reports
  the same unregistered anchor.
- [ ] The new regression tests are observed RED before production-code
  modification.
- [ ] `discover_occurrences()` rejects every parsed `term-*` anchor absent from
  the canonical registry's anchor set.
- [ ] Existing registered canonical anchors retain their current behavior.
- [ ] The live Turnlock-Rust specification and terminology inventory remain
  unchanged.
- [ ] `scripts/check-normative-terminology.py` and its test file remain within
  the shared 400-line hand-written file limit.
- [ ] The normative terminology tests pass.
- [ ] The live normative terminology check passes.
- [ ] The complete canonical repository-integrity suite passes.
- [ ] GitHub Repository integrity passes on the published Turnlock-Rust SHA.
- [ ] No product semantics, ADR, invariant, formal-verification claim, dependency,
  or public implementation API is changed.

## Validation

Run:

`python3 -m venv .venv`

`.venv/bin/python -m pip install --requirement requirements.txt`

`.venv/bin/python scripts/tests/test-normative-terminology.py`

`.venv/bin/python scripts/check-normative-terminology.py`

`.venv/bin/python scripts/check-repository-integrity.py`

`git diff --check`

and verify the GitHub Actions `Repository integrity` workflow succeeds on the
exact published revision.

## Authoritative references

- `AGENTS.md`
- `docs/specification/turnlock-spec.md`
- `docs/specification/terminology-inventory.yaml`
- `scripts/check-normative-terminology.py`
- `scripts/tests/test-normative-terminology.py`
- `scripts/check-repository-integrity.py`
- `docs/repository-governance/turnlock-rust-engineering.md`
- `docs/repository-governance/turnlock-rust-discovery-classification.md`

value.body:
## Purpose

This Issue is the durable discovery record and execution contract for TURNLOCK's formal-assurance architecture before the first executable formal model is authored.

The underlying architectural discovery has established that the existing direct shape

```text
TL-INV
  ↓
planned TLA+ property
  ↓
TLC configuration
  ↓
TLC result
```

is too compressed to express the assurance boundaries TURNLOCK now requires.

This Issue preserves the detailed conclusions that must be recorded authoritatively in a new ADR and then reflected in the formal-assurance metamodel and repository governance.

The Issue itself does **not** establish TURNLOCK product semantics, does **not** constitute an accepted architecture decision, and does **not** constitute formal-verification evidence.

The immediate deliverable is Formal Architecture over already accepted TURNLOCK semantics. If execution of this work exposes product behavior that current normative authority does not determine, that discovery must be routed to Product Semantics rather than resolved here.

The work owned here ends at readiness to author a candidate executable formal model. It does not author that model.

---

## Problem

TURNLOCK needs formalization not merely to translate existing prose into another notation, but to challenge the current semantic fixed point through executable formal pressure, adversarial semantic review, counterexamples, and explicit assurance accounting.

The repository already has strong foundations:

* normative product meaning remains in `docs/specification/turnlock-spec.md`;
* accepted ADRs preserve decision history and amendments;
* stable `TL-INV-*` identities provide normative traceability;
* ADR-015 requires early formalization, machine-readable traceability, separate run evidence, and integrated behavioral exploration;
* `formal/verification.yaml` records intended formal coverage;
* `formal/results/` is reserved for concrete TLC execution evidence;
* ADR-040 requires future abstraction extractability without prematurely inventing generic TURNLOCK, software-problem-solving, or SCOPE IRs.

However, the current formal-verification shape still conflates several distinct responsibilities:

```text
normative invariant
formal assurance claim
verification obligation
formal semantics
backend property
verification profile
verification evidence
normative coverage conclusion
```

It also treats planned TLA+ property names as the immediate decomposition of normative invariants before an executable canonical model exists.

Before any executable `Turnlock.tla` is introduced, TURNLOCK needs an explicit architecture for those responsibilities.

---

## Architectural conclusions to record authoritatively

The resulting architecture decision MUST preserve the following conclusions.

### 1. Authority is responsibility-specific

TURNLOCK product meaning remains owned by the normative specification and accepted ADRs.

A formal representation may be canonical for formal semantics within a declared formalized domain without becoming normative product authority.

`formal/verification.yaml` or its successor owns formal-assurance intent and traceability, not product semantics and not verification evidence.

Backend result artifacts own only the concrete, scope-bound evidence they identify.

Generated views remain projections of canonical sources and create no independent semantics.

The governing direction is:

```text
authority flows downward

discoveries may flow upward

authority does not flow upward from
model, checker, evidence, implementation,
Issue, reviewer, or harness
```

No lower layer may resolve under-specification or conflict in an upper authoritative layer.

---

### 2. TURNLOCK requires canonical formal semantics, but not a distinct formal IR yet

TURNLOCK requires one canonical formal semantic representation for each formally modeled semantic domain so that the same product semantics are not independently reinterpreted for every assurance artifact.

For the current operational state/transition domain, the minimum justified initial canonical formal representation is the integrated TLA+ model itself.

Conceptually:

```text
normative TURNLOCK semantics
          ↓
reviewed semantic formalization
          ↓
canonical formal semantics
(initially integrated TLA+)
```

`canonical` does not mean `normative`.

The TLA+ representation is canonical only for the current formalized semantic domain and scope.

A distinct backend-neutral TURNLOCK Formal IR is **not** currently justified merely because multiple backends may exist in the future.

A future TURNLOCK-specific Formal IR becomes eligible for separate architectural consideration when multiple current consumers need the same formal semantics, or when a mechanically governed intermediate representation provides a concrete assurance benefit that exceeds its additional translation, projection, and common-mode trust surface.

If such an IR is later introduced, it must be derived from demonstrated TURNLOCK needs and formalization pressure rather than invented as a speculative generic problem-solving representation.

This preserves ADR-040's direction:

```text
TURNLOCK
    ↓ later extraction from demonstrated structure
software problem-solving representation
    ↓ later extraction from broader evidence
SCOPE
```

and not:

```text
speculative generic ontology
    ↓
force TURNLOCK to fit it
```

---

### 3. Required assurance claims are not a second formal semantics

A `TL-INV-*` must not map directly to backend-specific properties as the only assurance abstraction.

TURNLOCK needs explicit required assurance claims.

A required assurance claim is:

> the smallest evidentially coherent proposition whose establishment is necessary to support a declared portion of accepted TURNLOCK semantics.

A required assurance claim records assurance intent and normative provenance.

It does **not** define TURNLOCK's state space, transitions, operational semantics, or executable formal language.

Claims are backend-neutral at the assurance layer, not a backend-neutral formal semantic IR.

Conceptually:

```text
normative invariant
      ↓
required assurance claim
      ↓
verification obligation
```

while independently:

```text
normative semantics
      ↓
canonical formal semantics
```

and then:

```text
required assurance claim
        ↕ reviewed correspondence
backend property interpreted over
canonical formal semantics
```

One invariant may yield zero, one, or multiple required assurance claims.

One claim may have multiple normative sources.

Claims must be evidentially atomic: safety, reachability, and liveness burdens must not be hidden inside one ambiguous property when they require distinct judgments.

Supporting properties introduced solely by a modeling representation are not automatically required assurance claims.

For example, a future `CallerStackWellFormed` property may be a supporting property if a stack is merely a TLA+ representation choice; TURNLOCK does not thereby acquire a normative stack requirement.

---

### 4. Assurance modalities and assurance domains must remain separate

The minimum logical modalities for behavioral formal assurance are:

```text
safety
reachability
liveness
```

Safety captures universal preservation or exclusion.

Reachability captures positive possibility, witness, capability, representability, or existence where the product requires that at least one admissible behavior exists.

Liveness captures eventual-progress obligations under their explicit premises.

Other concepts currently mixed into invariant-level `kind` values are not necessarily additional logical modalities.

Conformance, semantic-quality, DX, architecture, semantic-boundary, coverage, and similar concerns belong to separate dimensions.

Relational assurance must also be represented separately when the concern is correspondence between two artifacts or semantic surfaces, for example:

```text
normative semantics ↔ formal semantics
claim ↔ backend property
formal source ↔ formal projection
formal semantics ↔ implementation or harness
```

The architecture must not encode all of these axes into one compound enum.

---

### 5. Backend selection is obligation-first

The architecture MUST follow:

```text
required assurance claim
      ↓
verification obligation
      ↓
required assurance strength
      ↓
verification mechanism/backend
```

and not:

```text
preferred tool
      ↓
find something to verify with it
```

TLA+ is the initial canonical formal language for the current operational state/transition domain unless a concrete current obligation demonstrates that it cannot faithfully represent the required semantics.

TLC is the initial justified model-checking mechanism for bounded state-space exploration, safety, reachability, liveness, and integrated behavioral interaction.

Additional mechanisms such as another TLA+ checker, deductive proof, Alloy, SMT, a proof assistant, model-based conformance, or another formal method require a concrete present assurance need.

The existence or prestige of a tool is not sufficient justification.

Multiple checkers over one semantic representation provide checker diversity.

An independently authored formalization can provide semantic-interpretation diversity.

Those are distinct assurance functions and must not be conflated.

---

### 6. Formalization, projection, restriction, configuration, and independent formalization are distinct

The translation:

```text
normative natural-language semantics
            ↓
canonical formal semantics
```

is **formalization**, not formal semantic projection.

A formal semantic projection exists only when both source and target are formal semantic representations and the source-to-target semantic relation can be characterized.

A projection contract must identify, for the relevant scope:

* the source representation;
* the target representation;
* the represented semantic domain;
* the observations or claims for which preservation is asserted;
* assumptions required by the relation;
* the direction and limitations of evidence transfer.

Projection relations are claim-relative or observation-relative.

A whole model must not be globally described as `over-approximation`, `under-approximation`, or `equivalent` when that statement is only valid for particular dimensions.

For safety, a sound over-approximation may permit absence-of-counterexample results to lift while producing spurious counterexamples that require concretization.

For positive reachability, a sound under-approximation may provide meaningful witnesses while providing insufficient safety coverage.

Liveness requires explicit preservation of the relevant temporal, enabledness, stuttering, occurrence, scheduler, and fairness semantics. Projection direction alone does not establish liveness preservation.

The following distinctions must remain explicit:

```text
NL → canonical TLA+
= formalization

TL-INV → assurance claim
= assurance decomposition

canonical formal semantics → focused TLC configuration
= verification restriction / instantiation

formal representation → derived formal representation
= formal semantic projection

normative semantics → independently authored second model
= independent formalization

canonical repository state → generated Markdown
= repository projection

model + configuration → checker result
= verification execution
```

Normative coverage, formal abstraction/projection relation, finite verification bounds, and evidence strength are orthogonal axes.

---

### 7. Global integration means semantic interaction closure, not one physical file

All formally modeled TURNLOCK semantic claims whose meanings can interact within one valid execution must be jointly representable and exercisable in at least one coherent behavioral model.

The initial integrated TLA+ semantics acts as the integration backplane for the operational domain.

This requirement exists to detect failures that appear only when individually correct mechanisms interact.

Focused verification configurations may restrict:

* constants;
* initial states;
* domains;
* bounds;
* selected properties;
* explored mechanisms where semantically safe to restrict.

Focused configurations MUST NOT redefine independent mini-semantics that can drift from the integrated canonical model.

`One integrated model` does not require one monolithic TLA+ source file. Modular TLA+ source may compose into one governed integrated semantics.

Claims outside the behavioral state-machine domain may use other assurance mechanisms, but they remain connected through the common assurance/traceability graph.

The rule is:

> Integrate everything that semantically composes; connect everything else through explicit assurance relations.

---

### 8. Non-mechanical semantic boundaries require explicit hostile assurance review

The architecture MUST NOT treat semantic correspondence as an informal one-person trust step.

Every material non-mechanically-proven semantic boundary must be subject to explicit adversarial review, including where applicable:

```text
normative semantics → candidate canonical formal semantics

TL-INV → required assurance claims

required assurance claim ↔ backend property

formal projection preservation contract

verification-profile adequacy

evidence interpretation
```

The intended review mechanism uses multiple independent frontier LLMs as hostile reviewers.

The purpose is not majority voting.

Reviewers must actively attempt to falsify the proposed correspondence, including attacks for:

* semantic strengthening;
* semantic weakening;
* omitted valid behaviors;
* invented behaviors;
* collapsed normative distinctions;
* invented formal distinctions;
* hidden assumptions;
* wrong quantification;
* wrong occurrence scope;
* modality mismatch;
* vacuity;
* alternative incompatible interpretations still compatible with normative authority;
* cross-feature interaction failure;
* incorrect evidence lifting.

A material objection survives because its argument or counterexample is valid, not because a majority agrees.

A minority reviewer with one valid counterexample defeats a majority of unsupported approvals.

Hostile-review evidence must be durable and inspectable.

Review evidence is a distinct evidence class from mechanical checker evidence.

It should be possible to establish for a review campaign:

```text
what exact artifact/version was reviewed
what attack objectives were used
which reviewers/models participated
which findings were produced
how each finding was classified/disposed
whether changed artifacts were re-reviewed
whether any material finding remains unresolved
```

No number of hostile LLM reviews converts natural-language-to-formal correspondence into a mathematical proof.

The correct conclusion is bounded review-based assurance, not `proved equivalence`.

---

### 9. `formal/verification.yaml` becomes the canonical formal-assurance and traceability graph

`formal/verification.yaml` MUST NOT become:

* TURNLOCK product semantics;
* a canonical semantic IR;
* the executable formal model;
* a verification result store;
* a hostile-review result store.

Its responsibility is the machine-readable formal-assurance graph.

Conceptually it must be able to represent:

```text
normative sources
      ↓
required assurance claims
      ↓
verification obligations
      ↓
formal coverage / residual coverage
      ↓
binding to canonical formal semantics
      ↓
required semantic/correspondence review
      ↓
backend realization
      ↓
required verification profiles
      ↓
required evidence contracts
```

It must preserve reverse traceability.

Given a formal property, state variable, action, verification profile, claim, or relevant realization element, tooling must be able to identify affected assurance claims and normative sources where the relation is declared.

The manifest owns intended assurance requirements.

Evidence artifacts own what actually happened.

Mutable facts mechanically derivable from repository artifacts or evidence should be derived rather than independently maintained as manual truth.

In particular, concepts equivalent to:

```text
artifact currently exists
binding currently resolves
required run exists
current evidence passes
current review gate is satisfied
```

should be mechanically derived where practical.

The architecture must avoid independent mutable `checked` truth when the same fact can be derived from validated evidence.

Coverage and status are different:

```text
coverage
= what portion/type of assurance is intended

current status
= what valid evidence currently exists
```

Partial formalization must identify its residual assurance obligation rather than allowing a checked formal subset to appear as full invariant assurance.

The upper assurance structure must remain sufficiently backend-neutral to survive a future change from:

```text
canonical semantics = TLA+
```

to a separately justified:

```text
canonical semantics = TURNLOCK Formal IR
                ↓
             TLA+ projection
```

without replacing stable normative provenance, assurance claims, modalities, or coverage relationships.

---

### 10. Discoveries are routed by earliest unresolved cause, not by detection tool

A discovery found by TLC is not automatically a Formal Verification defect.

A discovery found by a hostile reviewer is not automatically a review defect.

A discovery found during implementation is not automatically an implementation defect.

For every material finding, locate the earliest incorrect or underdetermined link in the authority-and-assurance chain.

Conceptually:

```text
normative authority
      ↓
canonical formalization
      ↓
assurance decomposition
      ↓
claim/property correspondence
      ↓
verification mechanism/profile
      ↓
evidence integrity
      ↓
implementation/conformance
```

If current normative authority does not uniquely determine a product behavior required by the formalization, classify and route it as `decision-required`.

If authoritative sources conflict or the derivation depends on an unstated product assumption, classify and route it as `authority-conflict-or-uncertain`.

Formal Architecture, Formal Verification, hostile reviewers, TLA+, TLC, implementation mechanisms, Issues, and harness capabilities MUST NOT resolve those cases implicitly.

When normative authority is sufficient, fix the lowest responsible downstream layer:

* canonical formalization defect;
* assurance-decomposition defect;
* claim/property correspondence defect;
* projection defect;
* verification mechanism/configuration defect;
* evidence-integrity defect;
* implementation defect;
* conformance defect.

No discovery may be closed through a downstream repair while a surviving upstream finding can still explain it.

A property discovered to hold in the formal model does not become a new normative invariant merely because the model checker established it.

Promotion into normative TURNLOCK semantics requires either:

* a complete derivation from existing normative authority; or
* an explicit product-semantic decision through the existing ADR/specification process.

Formal verification is allowed to refute the current semantic fixed-point hypothesis by exposing ambiguity, inconsistency, missing distinctions, incompatible obligations, or previously hidden semantic consequences.

It is not allowed to resolve those findings by itself.

---

### 11. Readiness is staged into three separate gates

A single `ready before first model` gate is insufficient because semantic hostile review of the candidate model cannot happen before the model exists.

The architecture therefore requires three distinct readiness gates.

#### Gate A — Formal-Architecture-Ready

Passing this gate authorizes authoring a **candidate** executable formal model.

It does not establish that the candidate is semantically correct, canonical, or verified.

Gate A requires at minimum:

* the new Formal Architecture ADR is accepted;
* the formal-assurance metamodel is migrated to the accepted architecture;
* every current `TL-INV-*` has assurance coverage classification;
* every invariant in the intended candidate-model scope has required assurance claims and modalities;
* partial coverage records explicit residual assurance;
* formally out-of-scope obligations identify their assurance domain rather than disappearing;
* the intended operational semantic scope is explicit;
* included semantics are interaction-closed, or exclusions/abstractions are justified as non-distorting for the claims in scope;
* every product choice that the candidate model would otherwise have to decide is already determined by authority or faithfully abstracted over;
* modeling choices that do not create observable product semantics remain free formalization choices;
* hostile-review requirements are defined;
* discovery routing is defined;
* repository validation passes.

Gate A does not require checker evidence because no executable candidate model exists yet.

#### Gate B — Canonical-Formal-Semantics-Ready

Passing this gate promotes an exact candidate artifact/version to the current canonical formal semantics for its declared scope.

Gate B requires:

* hostile semantic review of the exact candidate;
* attacks for strengthening, weakening, omission, invention, hidden assumptions, alternative interpretations, and composition failure;
* disposition of every material finding;
* re-review of every materially changed affected boundary;
* no surviving unresolved material semantic finding;
* integrated compositional review for interacting represented mechanisms;
* non-vacuity or semantic-adequacy witnesses showing that important represented mechanisms are actually exercisable rather than making safety properties true by accidental unreachability.

Only after Gate B may the candidate be treated as the governed current canonical formal-semantic baseline for its declared scope.

`canonical` still does not mean `normative`.

#### Gate C — Formal-Verification-Ready

Passing this gate authorizes verification runs to support assurance claims.

Gate C requires:

* real backend property bindings to required assurance claims;
* hostile correspondence review of claim/property relations;
* verification profiles adequate for the obligations they claim to exercise;
* modality-appropriate treatment of safety, reachability, and liveness;
* explicit finite bounds and assumptions;
* sufficient identity of exact executed model/configuration artifacts;
* valid mechanism-specific evidence schemas/contracts;
* evidence interpretation rules that cannot lift results beyond correspondence, coverage, abstraction, bounds, and assumptions.

The following states must remain conceptually distinct:

```text
candidate model exists
        ≠
candidate accepted as canonical formal semantics
        ≠
backend property mechanically checked
        ≠
required assurance claim supported
        ≠
TL-INV fully assured
```

---

## Consolidated architecture

The resulting architecture is:

```text
                         PRODUCT AUTHORITY
              turnlock-spec.md + accepted ADRs
                              │
               ┌──────────────┴──────────────┐
               │                             │
               │ assurance decomposition     │ semantic formalization
               ▼                             ▼
      REQUIRED ASSURANCE CLAIMS      CANDIDATE FORMAL SEMANTICS
               │                             │
               │                             ▼
               │                    HOSTILE SEMANTIC REVIEW
               │                             │
               │                             ▼
               │                  CANONICAL FORMAL SEMANTICS
               │                  initially integrated TLA+
               │                             │
               │                  ┌──────────┴──────────┐
               │                  │                     │
               │            supporting             backend
               │            properties             properties
               │                                      │
               └──────── correspondence ───────────────┤
                                                      │
                                             hostile correspondence
                                                    review
                                                      │
                                                      ▼
                                           verification profiles
                                                      │
                                                      ▼
                                                   checker
                                                      │
                                                      ▼
                                            mechanical evidence
                                                      │
                                                      ▼
                                         assurance interpretation
                                                      │
                                                      ▼
                                             supported claims
                                                      │
                                                      ▼
                                           normative coverage
```

Hostile semantic-review evidence and mechanical verification evidence are distinct evidence classes.

Assurance strength may be preserved or weakened as evidence is lifted upward.

It must never become stronger than the weakest justified link in the chain.

---

## Relationship to ADR-015 and ADR-040

The resulting architecture MUST be recorded in a new ADR.

The new ADR must:

```text
amend ADR-015
confirm ADR-040
```

ADR-015 remains correct in its fundamental commitments that:

* normative prose remains product authority;
* formalization is an early discovery and verification instrument;
* stable invariant identities matter;
* machine-readable traceability is required;
* intended verification and actual run evidence are distinct;
* focused verification does not replace integrated behavioral exploration.

The new ADR must amend ADR-015's overly direct assurance shape by introducing the explicit assurance, canonical-semantics, hostile-review, and staged-readiness boundaries defined by this Issue.

ADR-040 remains consistent with the architecture because the initial canonical representation is TURNLOCK-specific TLA+ semantics and no speculative generic IR is introduced.

The new ADR must create no new TURNLOCK product semantics and no new `TL-INV-*` identity.

Accepted historical ADR bodies must not be edited.

---

## Required repository migration

After the architecture ADR is accepted, this Issue owns the migration required to reach Gate A.

The migration must cover, at minimum:

### `AGENTS.md`

Update the formal-verification governance so that it reflects:

* normative authority versus canonical formal semantics;
* required assurance claims;
* verification obligations;
* the formal-assurance graph;
* hostile-review requirements;
* semantic discovery routing;
* the distinction between formalization and formal semantic projection;
* integrated semantic requirements;
* the three readiness gates;
* future IR admission without premature genericization.

### `formal/verification.yaml`

Migrate the manifest from direct invariant-to-TLA planning into the accepted formal-assurance metamodel.

The migration must represent, as required by the accepted architecture:

* normative provenance;
* required assurance claims;
* assurance modalities;
* coverage;
* residual assurance for partial coverage;
* current canonical-formal representation metadata;
* backend bindings only when executable identifiers actually exist;
* required hostile-review gates;
* required verification profiles;
* evidence requirements;
* reverse traceability.

Do not turn this YAML into a semantic IR.

Do not encode TURNLOCK state-transition semantics in the manifest.

### Existing planned TLA+ property names

Audit every currently planned TLA+ property name.

Do not automatically preserve those names as future TLA+ identifiers.

For each existing planned name, classify its underlying intent as exactly one of:

```text
required assurance claim candidate
supporting/model-specific property candidate
obsolete or incorrectly placed planning artifact
```

Preserve required normative assurance intent.

Do not preserve a backend identifier merely because it already appears in the manifest.

Do not invent executable TLA+ identifiers before the executable model introduces them.

### `scripts/check-formal-traceability.py`

Evolve validation to the new graph.

Validation must distinguish:

* authored assurance intent;
* referential integrity;
* derived repository facts;
* review evidence;
* mechanical verification evidence.

Where a current lifecycle/status fact can be mechanically derived from real artifacts or evidence, prefer derivation over a second manually maintained mutable truth.

### `scripts/render-formal-mapping.py`

Generate a human-readable view of the new assurance graph, including forward and reverse traceability.

The generated view must not become an independent authority.

### `docs/formal/invariant-mapping.md`

Regenerate this file from the migrated manifest.

Do not hand-edit it.

### `docs/formal/README.md`

Document the new artifact responsibilities and assurance chain.

### `formal/README.md`

Document candidate formal semantics, canonical promotion, verification readiness, and evidence separation.

### Mechanical verification evidence

Keep TLC execution evidence separate from assurance intent.

`formal/tlc-result.schema.json` remains a TLC-specific evidence schema unless the accepted migration requires a versioned strengthening.

The migration must address the current provenance weakness whereby a commit SHA and path alone may be insufficient to bind evidence to the exact executed bytes if the working tree is dirty or otherwise differs from the referenced revision.

The exact mechanism must be documented and validated before Gate C; this Issue must define the contract required by the architecture but does not run TLC.

### Hostile-review evidence

Introduce a durable, inspectable evidence contract for non-mechanical hostile reviews.

Do not mix hostile-review evidence into TLC result records.

Do not invent one universal result schema merely to combine heterogeneous evidence types.

The migration must define where review evidence lives, what identifies the exact reviewed artifact/input, how findings and dispositions are represented, and how re-review is established.

---

## Historical provenance

Earlier work remains useful provenance but is not the architecture authority for this Issue.

### Issue #1

Preserve its core discovery that one normative invariant may require multiple verification obligations with different evidence semantics, including the distinction among safety, reachability/capability, and liveness.

Do not preserve its assumption that the correct architectural layer is directly `TL-INV → TLA+ property`.

Its useful conclusions must be re-expressed through required assurance claims, verification obligations, backend realization, and evidence contracts.

### Issue #3

Preserve its occurrence-scoped liveness insight: progress of one occurrence cannot satisfy an obligation belonging to another occurrence.

Do not treat any earlier proposed TLA+ fairness encoding or identifier as pre-approved backend architecture.

### Issue #9

Preserve its core readiness concern: executable formal modeling must not silently decide unresolved product semantics.

Do not restore its former sequencing assumption that the next milestone is a first safety-only `Turnlock.tla`.

Its readiness concern is replaced architecturally by Gate A, Gate B, and Gate C.

These Issues are historical provenance inputs.

This Issue does not reopen, rewrite, or establish current dependency state for them.

---

## Discovery routing during this work

If migration work exposes a behavior not uniquely determined by current normative authority:

```text
do not choose
do not encode one alternative in the manifest
do not encode one alternative in future TLA+
do not resolve it as a formal-architecture convenience
```

Classify and route it according to the repository discovery protocol.

If current normative authority is contradictory or uncertain, use the existing authority-conflict process.

If the issue is purely an assurance representation, traceability, review, projection, backend, or evidence-contract concern and introduces no product meaning, keep it in Formal Architecture.

No repository migration performed under this Issue may silently introduce a new product requirement.

---

## Required outcome

This Issue is complete only when the repository has an accepted formal-assurance architecture and has been migrated far enough that Gate A — readiness to author a **candidate** formal model — can be satisfied without the future TLA+ author having to invent product semantics or formal-assurance architecture.

The result must make it possible to answer, mechanically where appropriate and reviewably where semantics are involved:

```text
What is the product authority?

What is the current canonical formal-semantic representation?

Which required assurance claims derive from each normative obligation?

What modality and verification obligation does each claim require?

What part of the normative obligation is covered?

What residual assurance remains?

Which backend property realizes each claim once executable bindings exist?

Which hostile reviews are required?

Which verification profiles are required?

What evidence exists?

What exact artifact did that evidence concern?

What conclusion may legitimately be lifted from it?

Which upstream normative obligations are affected by a changed formal construct?

Where must a newly discovered ambiguity or contradiction be routed?
```

---

## Acceptance criteria

* [ ] A new accepted ADR records the complete formal-assurance architecture defined by this Issue.
* [ ] The new ADR amends ADR-015 and confirms ADR-040 without editing either accepted historical ADR body.
* [ ] The architecture preserves the normative specification and accepted ADRs as TURNLOCK product authority.
* [ ] The architecture establishes one canonical formal semantic representation for the operational domain and selects the integrated TLA+ model as the initial representation without introducing a distinct backend-neutral TURNLOCK Formal IR.
* [ ] The architecture defines the admission condition for a future TURNLOCK-specific Formal IR without introducing one.
* [ ] Required assurance claims are represented as assurance decomposition rather than as a second formal semantics.
* [ ] Safety, reachability, and liveness obligations are structurally distinguishable.
* [ ] Relational assurance, conformance, semantic-quality, coverage, and other non-modal dimensions are not collapsed into the logical modality axis.
* [ ] Formalization, formal semantic projection, independent formalization, verification restriction/instantiation, repository projection, and verification execution are explicitly distinguished.
* [ ] Interacting operational semantics are required to remain jointly exercisable in an integrated canonical behavioral model.
* [ ] Hostile semantic review is a first-class assurance mechanism with durable evidence distinct from mechanical checker evidence.
* [ ] Review validity is based on surviving arguments/counterexamples rather than reviewer majority.
* [ ] `formal/verification.yaml` is migrated into the canonical formal-assurance and traceability graph without becoming product semantics, canonical formal semantics, or evidence.
* [ ] Every current `TL-INV-*` has explicit assurance coverage classification.
* [ ] Every invariant within the intended candidate-model domain has required assurance claim coverage and modality classification.
* [ ] Every partial coverage case identifies explicit residual assurance.
* [ ] Formally non-applicable obligations remain visible and identify their assurance domain rather than disappearing from the assurance graph.
* [ ] Existing planned TLA+ property names are audited rather than automatically preserved as executable backend identifiers.
* [ ] Supporting/model-specific properties are distinguishable from product-derived required assurance claims.
* [ ] No executable TLA+ identifier is fabricated before the executable model introduces it.
* [ ] Mutable evidence-derived state is mechanically derived rather than duplicated manually wherever practical.
* [ ] Forward and reverse formal-assurance traceability are mechanically validated.
* [ ] Hostile-review evidence has a durable artifact contract.
* [ ] TLC evidence remains a separate mechanism-specific evidence class.
* [ ] Exact artifact identity/provenance requirements are defined strongly enough that future evidence cannot silently refer to different model/configuration content than was executed.
* [ ] Discovery routing follows the earliest unresolved cause in the authority-and-assurance chain.
* [ ] Downstream repairs cannot close a finding while a surviving upstream explanation remains unresolved.
* [ ] Gate A, Gate B, and Gate C are explicitly defined and mechanically/reviewably enforceable according to their responsibilities.
* [ ] Gate A can be satisfied without any executable `formal/Turnlock.tla` existing.
* [ ] This Issue introduces no executable TURNLOCK formal model.
* [ ] This Issue introduces no product semantics and no new `TL-INV-*` identity.
* [ ] No generic TURNLOCK IR, software-problem-solving IR, SCOPE IR, generic problem graph, or speculative universal problem-solving primitive is introduced.
* [ ] Generated formal documentation is regenerated from canonical machine-readable sources.
* [ ] Repository integrity validation passes after the migration.
* [ ] A final review confirms that the repository is ready to create a separately scoped Formal Verification work item for authoring the candidate canonical TLA+ semantics, but that no such model has been authored by this Issue.

---

## Non-goals

This Issue does not:

* author `formal/Turnlock.tla`;
* run TLC;
* produce a successful verification claim;
* prove any `TL-INV-*`;
* introduce a generic formal IR;
* introduce a software-problem-solving IR;
* introduce SCOPE;
* design universal problem-solving primitives;
* introduce an Alloy model;
* introduce a direct SMT encoding;
* introduce a proof-assistant model;
* introduce Rust implementation artifacts;
* define runtime APIs;
* define workflow DSL syntax;
* define persistence;
* define harness mechanisms;
* weaken TURNLOCK semantics to fit a verifier or harness;
* strengthen TURNLOCK semantics to make a property pass;
* turn finite formal-model bounds into product limits;
* turn formal fairness mechanisms into product semantics;
* treat LLM hostile review as mathematical proof;
* treat an Issue, Project field, checker result, or model convenience as product authority.
