## Problem

The Gate A campaign runner must delegate provider API execution through the
approved M4 cognitive-execution boundary rather than leaving the runtime
surface implicit.

The coding agent must not infer which Pi API surface is allowed, how retries
relate to campaign attempts, which response field is sealed, how provider
identity evidence is captured, or how provider/runtime errors map into runner
behavior.

## Current authoritative boundary

`@earendil-works/pi-ai@0.99.2` is an implementation dependency, not TURNLOCK
product authority and not hostile-review protocol authority.

The selected M4 realization is:

```text
@earendil-works/pi-ai@0.99.2
Pi source commit: 005af57d88ee23b33778f343a9595b32e67ff788
public execution surface: Models.streamSimple(...)
execution wrapper: explicit campaign-owned M4 adapter
runtime floor: Node.js >=22.19.0
```

The adapter may realize accepted campaign mechanics but may not redefine
reviewer independence, attempt qualification, sealing, model identity, retry
admissibility, challenge behavior, recovery classification, or external Gate A
outcomes.

`AgentSession`, Pi coding-agent/subagent loops, Codex CLI, Codex App Server,
and other higher-level harness execution paths are excluded from the M4
boundary.

Provider-reported resolved-identity versus unresolved-alias semantics remain an
unresolved Product Semantics question tracked separately in Issue #47. This
contract must preserve that boundary and must not resolve it from Pi behavior.

## Required identity and call boundary

The Dependency Contract must preserve this exact construction mapping:

```text
runner Execution
→ one protocol attempt
→ one M4 cognitive call
→ exactly one direct Models.streamSimple(...) invocation
→ provider/transport attempt(s) internal to that call
```

For each qualified hostile-review receipt attempt:

```text
receipt.attempts[*].attempt_id = corresponding runner ExecutionId
receipt.attempts[*].call_id = exact M4 cognitive-call identity
call_id != provider response identity
```

The M4 cognitive-call identity identifies the adapter invocation, not the
provider response identity. A provider/transport retry remains internal to the
same M4 cognitive call and does not create a new runner Execution or protocol
attempt. A runner-level retry creates a new runner Execution and protocol
attempt.

The adapter must invoke public `Models.streamSimple(...)` directly once for the
M4 cognitive call. It must not use `AgentSession`, a coding-agent/subagent
loop, Codex CLI, Codex App Server, or another higher-level execution path.

## Scope

Produce the scoped active Pi M4 Dependency Contract for the exact
`@earendil-works/pi-ai@0.99.2` dependency and pinned Pi source revision
consumed by the campaign runner.

The architect must establish at least:

- exact package identity, version, and Pi source revision;
- exact explicit M4 adapter interface and public `Models.streamSimple(...)` surface consumed;
- fresh public `pi-ai` Context construction and execution isolation;
- exact request fields and semantic-input binding;
- explicit transport, `maxRetries`, tool behavior, deferred behavior, and execution-owned `AbortSignal` settings;
- provider-owned request/response evidence capture through `fetch`, `onPayload`, `onResponse`, and `onProviderStreamEvent` without rewriting the semantic request;
- exact provider/model/provider-reported-model evidence semantics and limitations;
- runtime call identity and provider-attempt identity;
- transport-attempt versus campaign protocol-attempt boundary;
- retry ownership and prohibition of hidden agent/coding-agent retries;
- exact provider-semantic textual completion and its relationship to sealed UTF-8 completion bytes;
- timeout, abort, cancellation, and typed error behavior;
- adapter lifecycle, isolation, and credential-injection boundaries;
- operational M4 journal and recovery-evidence obligations;
- provider-specific recovery/reconciliation capability and its conservative mapping into the existing M4/M8 contract;
- invalid usage patterns, including `AgentSession` and higher-level Pi/Codex execution paths;
- known Pi/provider-normalization limitations that the runner must not treat as stronger identity evidence;
- explicit preservation of the unresolved provider-reported identity decision routed to Issue #47.

The contract must be a curated consumer contract, not copied upstream
documentation.

## Exclusions

This Issue does not:

- modify TURNLOCK product semantics or Gate A protocol semantics;
- resolve Issue #47 or select a reviewer-profile `model_version`;
- modify `@earendil-works/pi-ai`, Pi, or any upstream provider integration;
- implement the campaign runner or the M4 adapter;
- store credentials or put secret values in the repository;
- define Gate A semantics from Pi behavior;
- select real reviewer profiles;
- execute provider calls as Gate A evidence;
- use `AgentSession`, a coding-agent/subagent loop, Codex CLI, or Codex App Server as an M4 execution path.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] One active Pi M4 Dependency Contract covers `@earendil-works/pi-ai@0.99.2` and Pi commit `005af57d88ee23b33778f343a9595b32e67ff788`.
- [ ] Every Pi API surface consumed by the accepted M4 boundary is explicit, with public `Models.streamSimple(...)` as the execution surface.
- [ ] The exact runner Execution → protocol attempt → M4 cognitive call → direct `Models.streamSimple(...)` invocation → provider/transport-attempt mapping is explicit.
- [ ] The exact receipt `attempt_id` and `call_id` bindings are explicit, and `call_id` is distinct from provider response identity.
- [ ] The explicit adapter's fresh-context, isolation, request, options, and abort behavior is explicit.
- [ ] Provider-owned request/response and provider-stream evidence capture is explicit and cannot rewrite semantic input.
- [ ] Transport retries and campaign protocol attempts cannot be conflated.
- [ ] The exact completion field and exact UTF-8 sealing boundary are explicit.
- [ ] Model/provider identity evidence and its limitations are explicit without inventing the unresolved-alias resolution rule from Issue #47.
- [ ] Error, timeout, abort, cancellation, lifecycle, recovery, isolation, and configuration behavior required by the runner is explicit.
- [ ] AgentSession and Pi/Codex higher-level loops are explicitly excluded from M4.
- [ ] Credential retrieval is outside durable repository/evidence content.
- [ ] The contract introduces no product or hostile-review semantics.
- [ ] Every material discovery is classified and routed before acceptance.

## Validation

Validate the contract against the current workspace Dependency Contract
convention, the synchronized NIB-S/NIB-M construction boundary, and the actual
`@earendil-works/pi-ai@0.99.2` source/API revision.

Confirm that the contract preserves the existing M4/M8 recovery semantics and
leaves Issue #47 unresolved pending its accepted Product Semantics decision.

## Authoritative references

- synchronized Gate A campaign runner NIB-M set
- `docs/formal/gate-a-campaign-runner-construction-plan.md`
- ADR-042 through ADR-048
- Issue #47 as the separately tracked unresolved provider-reported identity question

value.body:
## Problem

The active Gate A campaign-runner construction authority currently selects `llm-runtime` as the in-process dependency consumed by M4 `cognitive-execution`.

Before the M4 Module Brief and the cognitive-execution Dependency Contract are finalized, a newly relevant implementation possibility must be qualified: Pi can execute isolated child/subagent contexts and can route model execution through Codex/provider integrations.

The existence of a Pi subagent feature is not sufficient evidence that Pi can satisfy M4.

M4 and the accepted hostile-review evidence architecture require a much narrower property:

```text
one runner Execution
→ one protocol attempt
→ one exact LLM call
```

while preserving exact input identity, operational reviewer isolation, provider/model identity evidence, raw completion sealing, retry boundaries, cancellation/failure distinctions, and crash/recovery truth without manufacturing an execution outcome.

The required work is therefore to determine whether Pi exposes a sufficiently low-level, stable, and auditable cognitive-execution primitive to realize the existing M4 contract without hiding facts required by Gate A.

This Issue is a qualification task only. It does not itself replace `llm-runtime`, amend the NIB-S, or accept Pi as a dependency.

## Evidence and provenance

This work originates from campaign-runner construction analysis at repository revision:

```text
fa3bffea8ff8a12e1d271113a1b6fe0dd2143d00
```

At that revision:

- `NIB-S-GATE-A-CAMPAIGN-RUNNER` is active at version `6.0.13`;
- the runner is selected as an isolated strict TypeScript/Node.js ESM application;
- M4 `cognitive-execution` is the sole direct consumer of `llm-runtime`;
- M4 must bind one exact runner `Execution` to one exact cognitive external call and preserve exact executor-domain evidence;
- ADR-049 separates logical cognitive execution, protocol attempt, LLM call, and provider/transport retry identity;
- ADR-042 defines reviewer independence operationally rather than as process or provider inequality;
- hostile-review evidence remains runtime-neutral;
- model identity is `(provider, model, model_version)`;
- exact raw reviewer output must be sealed before interpretation.

The implementation possibility to qualify is specifically a constrained Pi execution path, not the generic proposition that “Pi supports subagents”.

Observed candidate Pi surfaces to investigate include isolated `AgentSession`/child execution, explicit provider/model selection, disabling tools, provider-request observation, provider-stream observation, abort/cancellation, and Codex/provider integration.

Those observed surfaces are investigation inputs only. They are not accepted TURNLOCK construction authority. The qualification must pin and inspect the exact Pi and Codex/provider revisions actually tested.

## Current authoritative boundary

TURNLOCK product semantics remain owned by the normative specification and accepted ADRs.

The active campaign-runner NIB-S remains the current implementation-construction authority unless explicitly revised through the repository's accepted construction process.

This Issue MUST NOT silently change:

```text
TURNLOCK product semantics
Gate A hostile-review protocol semantics
reviewer qualification rules
independence rules
execution-receipt semantics
protocol-attempt semantics
retry admissibility
model-identity rules
raw-output sealing rules
M2 authority
M5 retry authority
M6 validation authority
M8 recovery classification
```

Pi, Codex, Codex App Server, Codex CLI, provider APIs, and any harness-specific mechanism are implementation candidates only. Their capabilities do not create or weaken Gate A semantics.

A successful qualification may justify a later explicit construction-authority change. This Issue does not perform that change.

## Qualification question

Answer exactly this question:

> Can a pinned Pi execution mechanism realize the existing M4 `cognitive-execution` contract such that one runner `Execution` maps to exactly one protocol attempt and exactly one provider LLM call, while exposing sufficient stable evidence to preserve Gate A input identity, reviewer isolation, model identity, raw-output sealing, retry boundaries, cancellation/failure truth, and crash/recovery classification?

The answer must be evidence-based.

A generic “Pi can spawn an independent subagent” result is insufficient.

## Candidate execution shape to test

The primary candidate is now architecturally fixed for this spike as the lowest-level public Pi AI execution surface, not a Pi coding-agent session:

```text
M4 cognitive-execution
    ↓
explicit M4 qualification adapter
    ↓
@earendil-works/pi-ai
    ↓
public Models.streamSimple(...)
    ↓
qualified provider adapter
```

The spike MUST qualify this path first.

It MUST NOT use `AgentSession` as the primary candidate. `AgentSession`, Pi coding/subagent loops, Codex CLI, and Codex App Server may be examined only as explicitly separate comparison candidates after the primary path is characterized.

The primary candidate execution shape is:

```text
fresh pi-ai Context
    ↓
systemPrompt = exact canonical review prompt
messages     = exact canonical review packet input only
tools        = []
    ↓
no AgentSession
no coding-agent resource discovery
no repository browsing
no inherited coding-agent task context
no sibling-reviewer visibility
no steering
no follow-up
no compaction
no agent-loop retry
    ↓
Models.streamSimple(...)
    ↓
explicit provider request options chosen to minimize hidden behavior
    ↓
exactly one provider LLM call
    ↓
provider response/evidence observed
    ↓
exact model completion sealed
    ↓
only then parse / mechanically validate
```

For the `openai-codex` candidate path, the spike MUST attempt the narrowest deterministic transport configuration supported by the pinned version, including:

```text
transport = SSE when the pinned public/provider surface supports selecting it
maxRetries = 0 explicitly, never by relying on a library default
tools/toolChoice configured so no tool continuation can occur
no deferred execution unless the tested backend contract proves it is required and purely observational
one execution-owned AbortSignal
```

The spike MUST instrument the lowest stable surfaces available around the call, including where supported by the pinned Pi version:

```text
onPayload
instrumented fetch / transport boundary
onResponse
onProviderStreamEvent
```

Those hooks are observational for qualification. The M4 adapter MUST NOT rewrite the semantic request through an observation hook.

The spike must prove the exact relationship:

```text
canonical review prompt + packet
→ pi-ai Context
→ final provider request
→ provider response
→ sealed rawContent
```

Do not assume that a normal coding-agent or subagent loop satisfies this shape.

Do not assume that a selected `provider/model` value proves the effective upstream model identity.

Do not assume that a final Pi assistant message is byte-identical to the model-produced raw completion.

Do not assume that cancellation, timeout, missing response, or process death proves non-execution.

Do not assume that the current `Node.js >= 20` construction floor is compatible with the Pi version that ultimately qualifies. Runtime compatibility is a measured construction fact of this spike.

## Required qualification experiments

### 1. Exact request/input fidelity

Demonstrate the exact final provider request generated for one candidate M4 execution.

Prove whether the model receives only the authorized semantic inputs or whether Pi injects any additional material such as:

```text
coding-agent system instructions
tool declarations
AGENTS.md content
workspace context
skills
session history
extension-generated instructions
environment-derived semantic context
implicit follow-up messages
```

The test must establish the exact relationship between:

```text
canonical review prompt
canonical review packet
final provider request
```

Any hidden semantic input that cannot be disabled or made part of the exact reviewed protocol input is a qualification failure.

### 2. One-execution / one-call cardinality

For one synthetic M4 `Execution`, prove the exact count and ordering of provider LLM calls.

Required result:

```text
1 runner Execution
=
1 protocol attempt
=
1 provider LLM call
```

The candidate mechanism must not create a second provider call through:

```text
tool-use continuation
agent-loop continuation
automatic compaction
automatic retry
follow-up handling
steering
implicit summarization
recovery replay
```

If more than one provider LLM call occurs for one candidate M4 protocol attempt, the tested mechanism fails this requirement.

### 3. Provider and effective-model identity evidence

Capture and distinguish at minimum:

```text
reviewer-profile provider
reviewer-profile request_model
actual request payload model
Pi high-level assistant-message model, if present
provider response identity
provider-reported response.model / effective-model field when available
```

For this Issue, Q5 qualifies the Pi/M4 execution mechanism's ability to expose identity evidence faithfully.

It does not independently admit a concrete reviewer profile or decide whether one concrete provider-reported identifier is semantically admissible as a Gate A `model_version`.

The accepted Gate A resolution kinds remain exactly:

```text
provider-reported
pinned-request-model
```

The Pi candidate must preserve enough execution evidence for those accepted rules to be applied downstream without inventing provider truth.

For a provider-reported path, the qualification must establish mechanically that:

```text
the exact request model is observable
the exact final payload model is observable
the provider response identity is observable
the provider-reported model field / exact equivalent is observable when the provider emits it
provider-owned response evidence is captured before Pi high-level normalization can substitute the requested model
the runner does not manufacture model_version from a local arbitrary string
```

For a pinned-request-model path, the qualification must establish mechanically that:

```text
the exact configured request model reaches the provider request
provider-owned execution evidence is preserved
an explicit provider-reported contradiction is not hidden
```

The Pi high-level assistant-message model MUST NOT be substituted for provider-reported evidence when it only reflects the requested model.

A request/response identity contradiction must be preserved as evidence.

The experiments may record whether observed identifiers appear as aliases, snapshots, or other provider naming forms, but this Issue MUST NOT invent a semantic rule for deciding reviewer-profile admissibility that accepted TURNLOCK authority does not already define.

In particular, this Issue does NOT require separate provider documentation classifying every observed provider-reported identifier as immutable as a hard requirement for Pi backend qualification.

If accepted authority does not uniquely determine how to establish that a provider-reported identifier is resolved rather than an unresolved alias:

```text
record and route a decision-required Product Semantics Finding
do not manufacture a resolution rule
do not fail the Pi execution mechanism solely because that separate reviewer-admission rule is under-specified
```

Concrete reviewer-profile admission remains outside this Issue.

The backend qualification question is whether Pi exposes the exact provider-owned evidence required for a later accepted identity-resolution rule to operate.

### 4. Exact raw-output sealing

Gate A requires the exact model-produced `rawContent` bytes, not the HTTP/SSE framing bytes used to transport them.

The candidate definition to qualify is:

```text
rawContent
=
exact provider-semantic finalized textual completion

rawContentBytes
=
UTF-8(rawContent)
```

The M4 qualification adapter MUST perform no transformation between the provider-semantic textual completion and the bytes that are sealed.

Forbidden transformations include:

```text
trim
leading/trailing whitespace cleanup
newline insertion
newline normalization
JSON parse + reserialization
pretty-printing
JSON repair
Unicode NFC/NFD normalization
refusal rewriting
semantic cleanup
finding extraction before sealing
```

Required ordering:

```text
provider textual completion
→ exact rawContent bytes
→ durable write
→ SHA-256 / seal
→ only then parsing / protocol validation / interpretation
```

Where the provider exposes both streaming textual deltas and a terminal textual projection, the spike MUST independently derive both and require byte equality:

```text
UTF-8(exact concatenation of provider textual deltas)
==
UTF-8(provider terminal textual projection)
==
sealed rawContent bytes
```

Any unexplained divergence is an executor-integrity failure for the tested path.

Transport representation differences that decode to the same provider-semantic text do not create different rawContent identities. For example, a provider JSON transport encoding of `"é"` versus `"\\u00e9"` may represent the same textual completion after protocol decoding.

By contrast, semantically similar but byte-distinct Unicode strings MUST remain byte-distinct. Do not normalize:

```text
U+00E9
!=
U+0065 U+0301
```

Test at minimum:

```text
leading whitespace
trailing whitespace
newlines
Unicode composed/decomposed forms
transport JSON escapes
multi-chunk streaming with different chunk boundaries
empty textual completion
protocol-invalid JSON text
large structured output
provider refusal / refusal text
multiple textual content parts if the provider can produce them
```

Chunk boundaries are transport facts and MUST NOT affect rawContent identity.

If a completed model response contains protocol-invalid JSON, seal its exact completed rawContent first. A completed invalid JSON response is not converted into a technical failure merely because parsing fails.

If the provider can return more than one terminal textual content part, the spike MUST determine the provider-owned aggregation semantics. TURNLOCK/M4 MUST NOT invent a separator or aggregation rule merely for convenience.

If exact model-produced completion bytes cannot be defined and reconstructed losslessly from the pinned provider surface, the tested provider path fails Q6.

HTTP framing bytes do not become hostile-review raw output unless some current accepted authority explicitly requires them.

### 5. Retry and transport-attempt visibility

Disable every retry mechanism that can be disabled.

Verify separately:

```text
Pi/agent retry
provider-adapter retry
HTTP/transport retry
protocol retry
```

M4 must not silently perform a fresh protocol attempt.

Any dependency-internal provider/transport retry is admissible only if its existence and count can be represented exactly under the current M4/ADR-049 boundary and later authorized by the Dependency Contract.

Inject or simulate transient failure where possible and prove the resulting call/attempt count.

### 6. Timeout, abort, and cancellation

Exercise:

```text
caller abort before provider request
abort after request initiation
timeout before completion
mid-stream interruption
provider-side technical failure
```

Determine exactly what Pi/provider evidence exists for each case.

Do not classify:

```text
no response
timeout
abort
cancellation
process interruption
```

as `not-executed` without positive executor-owned proof that the exact cognitive-call boundary was never crossed.

### 7. Crash-cut matrix and durable M4 recovery journal

The primary candidate MUST test a narrowly scoped durable write-ahead M4 execution journal.

This journal is operational executor evidence only. It is NOT authoritative GateARun state and does not replace M2.

The candidate minimum state machine is:

```text
PREPARED
    ↓ durable transition before provider transport can become reachable
MAYBE-SENT
    ↓ terminal provider result + exact durable sealing
TERMINAL-CAPTURED
```

A durable `MAYBE-SENT` transition MUST occur before any provider network side effect can become possible.

The adapter MUST NOT use absence of a post-dispatch record as proof that dispatch did not occur.

The spike must establish whether a valid durable `PREPARED` state plus the pinned adapter invariant:

```text
provider transport is unreachable
until PREPARED → MAYBE-SENT is durably committed
```

is sufficient executor-owned positive evidence for a `NonExecutionProofRef`.

Inject process termination at all of these boundaries:

```text
C0 after M2 Arm but while the durable M4 journal still proves PREPARED and before MAYBE-SENT

C1 after MAYBE-SENT is durable and the request may have crossed the provider boundary, but before any terminal provider result is durably captured

C2 during response streaming

C3 after provider terminal completion is observed in process but before exact raw completion / terminal evidence is durably sealed

C4 after exact raw completion and required terminal provider evidence are durably sealed

C5 after construction of the terminal M4 capture but before authoritative M2 disposition
```

For each cut, determine which existing M4/M8 result is justified.

The expected conservative candidate behavior to test is:

```text
C0
→ not-executed only if the durable PREPARED proof and adapter invariant positively prove the cognitive-call boundary was unreachable

C1
→ unknown unless the exact provider backend offers a durable, purely observational recovery capability for this exact request

C2
→ unknown unless the exact provider backend can safely observe the original call without replay
→ partial stream material is operational provenance, not a completed hostile-review raw output

C3
→ unknown if terminal completion existed only in volatile process state and cannot be reconstructed

C4
→ terminal / recovered captured outcome when sealed raw bytes + exact terminal provider evidence are intact and bound to the same Execution

C5
→ terminal / PROVEN-COMPLETED recovery from the same durable terminal evidence; never replay the provider call
```

For a known terminal provider/transport failure with positively established no-completed-response semantics, recovery may return a recovered terminal `technical-failure`. Do not infer that state from timeout, cancellation, disconnect, or missing response alone.

Provider-specific recovery capability MUST be tested separately.

For a ChatGPT/Codex provider path whose pinned contract uses `store:false` or otherwise exposes no durable post-crash response lookup, the adapter MUST NOT invent `pending`. After `MAYBE-SENT`, loss of terminal truth is `unknown` unless another exact provider-owned recovery capability exists.

A `pending` observation is permitted only when another invocation of the exact reconciliation operation is positively proven to be observational and incapable of submitting, resubmitting, or replaying the original cognitive request.

The spike MUST record whether each tested backend supports:

```text
pre-dispatch positive non-execution proof
post-dispatch durable response lookup
safe post-crash observational reconciliation
durable-local terminal recovery
provider response-id recovery
no-recovery-capability / unknown
```

No experiment may manufacture an outcome from absence of evidence.

Lack of provider-side recovery does not by itself disqualify Pi because the active NIB-S permits limited or null recovery capability. It is an operational limitation only if every uncertain path maps conservatively into the existing M4/M8 contract.

### 8. Reviewer isolation

Run at least two concurrent synthetic reviewer executions.

Prove that before each raw output is sealed, a reviewer has no direct or indirect access to:

```text
the sibling reviewer's conversation
the sibling reviewer's raw output
the sibling reviewer's findings
the sibling reviewer's adjudication
parent-agent conversational history not part of the canonical input
shared mutable semantic scratch state
```

No tool access is required for the Gate A reviewer candidate and should remain disabled.

Process-level isolation is not required by current authority. Operational context isolation is required.

### 9. Pi/Codex boundary identification

Explicitly distinguish the following possible mechanisms:

```text
@earendil-works/pi-ai public Models.streamSimple(...)
pi-ai provider adapter
pi-ai openai-codex provider path
Pi AgentSession / coding-agent loop
Pi spawned/subagent execution
Codex CLI
Codex App Server
other Codex harness execution
```

Do not treat them as interchangeable.

The mandatory primary qualification target is:

```text
@earendil-works/pi-ai
→ public Models.streamSimple(...)
→ explicit M4 qualification adapter
→ pinned provider adapter
```

`AgentSession` is NOT the primary candidate because its conversation/session/resource/tool/agent-loop behavior adds mechanisms M4 does not require and would need to neutralize.

A full Codex coding-agent loop is not automatically acceptable merely because it can produce an answer.

Codex CLI, Codex App Server, AgentSession, or other higher-level paths may be recorded only as separate comparison candidates after the primary path is characterized.

The result MUST say precisely which layer owns each fact used by M4:

```text
request construction
authentication plumbing
transport call
call count
provider response id
provider-reported model identity
raw textual completion
abort/cancellation
retry behavior
durable local journal
post-crash provider recovery
```

### 10. Stability, pinning, and runtime compatibility

Record exact immutable identities for every upstream component used by the spike, including as applicable:

```text
Pi repository commit
@earendil-works/pi-ai package version
Pi SDK/public Models surface version
Pi provider-adapter version/commit
Codex/provider integration version/commit
Codex App Server/CLI version if separately tested
Node version
relevant provider API version/surface
provider-owned model-identity authority used for IMMUTABLE / MUTABLE-ALIAS / UNKNOWN classification
```

For each M4-critical observation surface, classify whether it is:

```text
public supported API
public but version-sensitive API
internal API
undocumented implementation detail
```

The spike MUST prefer the public `pi-ai` Models surface as the dependency boundary.

If satisfying Q1-Q13 requires a lower-level provider hook or adapter detail, identify exactly why it is needed and whether an explicit narrow M4 adapter can freeze/expose that fact without depending on unstable hidden behavior.

A mechanism that satisfies semantics only by relying on unstable internals MUST NOT be reported as unconditionally `QUALIFIED`.

Runtime compatibility MUST be measured, not assumed.

The active NIB-S currently selects:

```text
Node.js >= 20
```

The spike MUST record the exact Node engine/runtime requirement of the Pi version that actually qualifies.

If the qualifying Pi version requires a higher Node floor, record that as a construction discovery and identify the later NIB-S synchronization that would be required. Do NOT pin an older Pi version merely to preserve `Node.js >= 20`, and do NOT modify the NIB-S inside this Issue.

## Required spike implementation discipline

The future executor of this Issue must create the qualification harness in an isolated disposable workspace.

Do not add production campaign-runner code.

Do not modify active NIBs during the spike.

Do not modify hostile-review protocol artifacts.

Do not create real Gate A campaign evidence.

Use synthetic non-sensitive prompts and packets sufficient to exercise the mechanics.

Never write provider credentials, access tokens, cookies, authentication headers, user-specific filesystem paths, or secret-bearing payloads into:

```text
the repository
Issue bodies
Issue comments
committed artifacts
durable evidence
logs intended for sharing
```

If live provider access is required, resolve credentials through the authorized local mechanism and redact all secret-bearing material from durable reports.

## Required qualification matrix

Produce one durable result matrix with exactly these requirement rows:

```text
Q1 exact semantic input / no hidden prompt context
Q2 isolated execution context
Q3 exactly one provider LLM call per protocol attempt
Q4 exact provider-call identity
Q5 provider/model identity evidence required by downstream resolution is faithfully exposed
Q6 exact rawContent sealing before interpretation
Q7 no hidden protocol retry
Q8 provider/transport retry count is known or disabled
Q9 timeout/abort/cancellation evidence is exact
Q10 positive non-execution proof is possible only when justified
Q11 uncertain post-dispatch execution is never fabricated into success/failure
Q12 C0-C5 crash cuts map safely through the durable M4 adapter into existing M4/M8 recovery semantics
Q13 sibling reviewer visibility is absent before sealing
Q14 public pi-ai boundary and every required adapter/provider surface are pinned and sufficiently stable
```

Every row MUST contain:

```text
PASS | FAIL | BLOCKED
exact evidence
tested component/version
reproduction command or test identifier
residual limitation
```

Q5 MUST additionally record:

```text
requested model identifier
actual final payload model identifier
provider-reported model identifier / exact equivalent when available
provider response identity
provider-owned evidence surface used
identity contradiction: yes | no
reviewer-profile admissibility: outside this backend qualification when current authority leaves alias-resolution semantics decision-required
```

Q10-Q12 MUST additionally identify the exact durable journal state and provider recovery capability used by each crash case.

No weighted score is permitted.

No majority decision is permitted.

A single failed hard requirement is sufficient to reject the tested candidate as a complete M4 backend.

## Required final classification

The qualification report MUST end with exactly one of:

```text
QUALIFIED
QUALIFIED-WITH-REQUIRED-ADAPTER
NOT-QUALIFIED
INCONCLUSIVE
```

Use them exactly as follows.

### QUALIFIED

Use only if every hard M4 requirement passes directly on a pinned supported Pi surface.

### QUALIFIED-WITH-REQUIRED-ADAPTER

Use only if every semantic/evidence requirement can be satisfied, but a narrowly scoped explicit adapter/wrapper is required to expose or freeze the necessary information.

The report must identify the exact adapter responsibility.

The adapter may expose existing facts. It may not invent provider truth, reinterpret Gate A semantics, or hide additional model calls.

### NOT-QUALIFIED

Use if any hard requirement cannot be satisfied by the tested Pi mechanism, including inability to prove exact input, one-call cardinality, faithful exposure of provider-owned model identity evidence, exact raw completion, retry boundaries, or safe execution/recovery truth.

### INCONCLUSIVE

Use only when the required experiment cannot be completed because an external capability or access prerequisite is unavailable.

Do not convert absence of evidence into qualification.

## Possible downstream consequences

This Issue does not apply any downstream architecture change.

If the final classification is `QUALIFIED` or `QUALIFIED-WITH-REQUIRED-ADAPTER`, the report must identify the exact construction artifacts that would require later architect-controlled synchronization, including at minimum:

```text
NIB-S-GATE-A-CAMPAIGN-RUNNER M4 dependency boundary
M4 Module Brief
the scoped cognitive-execution Dependency Contract
Issue #31 scope/title if llm-runtime is no longer the selected dependency
NIB-T coverage for the selected execution dependency
Node runtime floor if the qualifying Pi version is incompatible with the current NIB-S floor
```

Do not edit those artifacts in this Issue.

The likely architecture to validate, not assume, is:

```text
M4 cognitive-execution
    ↓
explicit M4 qualification adapter
    ↓
@earendil-works/pi-ai
Models.streamSimple(...)
    ↓
qualified provider adapter
```

A positive Pi mechanism result does NOT automatically qualify every provider/model reachable through Pi or admit a concrete Gate A reviewer profile.

Q5 qualifies whether the backend faithfully exposes provider/model identity evidence.

If accepted authority does not uniquely determine how a provider-reported identifier is established to be resolved rather than an unresolved alias, preserve that as a separate `decision-required` Product Semantics Finding.

Do not invent that semantic rule inside this integration qualification.

Do not label the current checker non-conforming solely because it lacks a mechanical rule that accepted authority has not yet uniquely defined.

If the final classification is `NOT-QUALIFIED`, record the exact failed requirement and preserve the current `llm-runtime` selection unchanged.

If the final classification is `INCONCLUSIVE`, record the exact missing prerequisite and do not alter the current construction authority.

## Exclusions

This Issue MUST NOT:

- modify TURNLOCK product semantics;
- introduce or amend any `TL-INV-*`;
- change Gate A protocol semantics;
- alter hostile-review evidence schemas;
- modify the current review protocol bundle;
- select real reviewer profiles;
- execute a real Gate A campaign;
- create Gate A review evidence;
- modify `NIB-S-GATE-A-CAMPAIGN-RUNNER`;
- write the M4 Module Brief;
- write any Dependency Contract;
- implement the campaign runner;
- modify `llm-runtime`;
- modify Pi or Codex upstream;
- accept Pi merely because a demo succeeds;
- treat Codex/App Server/CLI behavior as authority;
- hide a second LLM call behind the word “subagent”;
- weaken recovery semantics to accommodate Pi.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The exact Pi/Codex/provider revisions exercised by the qualification are recorded.
- [ ] The primary candidate is the public `@earendil-works/pi-ai` `Models.streamSimple(...)` path behind an explicit M4 qualification adapter; `AgentSession` is not used as the primary candidate.
- [ ] Q5 proves that requested model, final payload model, provider response identity, and provider-reported model evidence are separately observable where the provider exposes them.
- [ ] Q5 uses provider-owned execution evidence without substituting the requested Pi model for provider-reported evidence and preserves any request/response identity contradiction.
- [ ] Q6 demonstrates exact `UTF-8(rawContent)` sealing with no trim, reserialization, newline insertion, Unicode normalization, or repair.
- [ ] The C0-C5 experiments exercise the candidate durable M4 write-ahead journal and prove that `MAYBE-SENT` is durable before provider transport can become reachable.
- [ ] Provider-specific post-crash recovery capability is recorded; `pending` is never emitted without a positively safe observational recovery operation.
- [ ] The exact Node runtime requirement of the qualifying Pi version is recorded and compared with the current NIB-S `Node.js >= 20` construction floor.
- [ ] The tested Pi execution mechanism is explicitly identified and distinguished from other Pi/Codex execution paths.
- [ ] A fresh isolated no-tools/no-history candidate execution is demonstrated.
- [ ] The exact final provider request is captured and checked for hidden semantic inputs.
- [ ] One candidate M4 protocol attempt is proven to cause exactly one provider LLM call.
- [ ] Automatic agent retry and compaction behavior are disabled or mechanically proven absent.
- [ ] Provider/transport retry behavior and exact attempt count are known.
- [ ] The source of provider/model execution evidence is demonstrated mechanically without inventing a reviewer-profile `model_version` resolution rule that accepted authority does not define.
- [ ] Exact raw completion sealing occurs before parsing or semantic interpretation.
- [ ] Whitespace, Unicode, streaming, invalid JSON, and large-output raw sealing cases are exercised.
- [ ] Abort, timeout, cancellation, and technical-failure cases are exercised.
- [ ] The complete C0-C5 crash-cut matrix is exercised or a specific unavailable cut is reported as `BLOCKED`.
- [ ] No crash path infers `not-executed`, success, technical failure, or `pending` from absence of evidence.
- [ ] At least two concurrent synthetic reviewer executions demonstrate the required pre-sealing isolation.
- [ ] Every M4-critical Pi surface is classified by API stability and pinned identity.
- [ ] The Q1-Q14 qualification matrix is complete.
- [ ] The report ends with exactly one allowed final classification.
- [ ] Any required downstream construction synchronization is identified but not performed.
- [ ] No TURNLOCK repository authority, NIB, ADR, protocol artifact, production code, or real Gate A evidence is modified by the qualification spike.
- [ ] No secret value is persisted in the repository or GitHub work record.

## Validation

Validation must include:

```text
repeatable automated tests for the one-call executor behavior
exact request-capture evidence
provider-event/call-count evidence
raw-byte/hash comparisons
retry/failure injection
abort/cancellation tests

```

The durable report must record the exact commands/tests executed and their results without including credentials or secret-bearing payloads.

A successful demo is not sufficient. Qualification requires the complete Q1-Q14 matrix.

## Authoritative references

## Required outcome

Build and execute a fully deterministic local qualification harness for the primary `pi-ai` M4 candidate defined by Issue #41.

This work validates the M4 adapter mechanics that do not require a live external provider.

It must consume the exact pinned Pi surface selected by the dependency-boundary characterization for this qualification.

If no exact usable pin exists, stop and report this work as blocked. Do not choose another Pi version or another execution mechanism.

## Authority boundary

Use Issue #41 as the complete qualification contract.

Preserve the current TURNLOCK boundaries for:

```text
one runner Execution
one protocol attempt
one provider LLM call
rawContent sealing before interpretation
reviewer isolation
retry separation
abort/cancellation truth
```

Do not create or modify TURNLOCK semantic authority.

## Workspace

Build the harness in a disposable directory outside the Turnlock-Rust repository.

Do not add qualification code to Turnlock-Rust.

Do not add production campaign-runner code.

Use no live provider credentials.

Use a synthetic provider/transport controlled completely by the harness.

## Mandatory harness shape

Exercise exactly this logical path:

```text
synthetic M4 Execution
→ explicit qualification adapter
→ public Models.streamSimple(...)
→ controlled synthetic provider/transport
```

The harness must support exact observation of:

```text
constructed Context
final provider request
provider-call count
transport-attempt count
onPayload observations
fetch/transport observations
onResponse observations
provider stream events
terminal provider response
raw textual deltas
terminal textual projection
sealed rawContent bytes
SHA-256
abort state
retry state
reviewer execution identity
```

Observation hooks must not rewrite the semantic request.

## Required deterministic tests

### Q1 exact semantic input

Prove that the final provider request contains only the explicitly supplied synthetic canonical prompt and packet plus protocol-required provider framing.

Test that no coding-agent/session material appears:

```text
AGENTS.md
workspace context
skills
tool declarations
session history
steering
follow-up
compaction material
parent-agent history
```

### Q2 isolated context

Create two fresh independent contexts.

Prove no mutable semantic state, message history, or sibling output is inherited.

### Q3 one Execution / one provider call

For one synthetic runner Execution, require mechanically:

```text
provider call count == 1
```

No tool continuation, agent continuation, hidden follow-up, compaction, or protocol retry may create another provider call.

### Q6 exact rawContent sealing

Implement and test:

```text
rawContentBytes = UTF-8(exact provider-semantic finalized textual completion)
```

Seal before parsing or interpretation.

The test vectors must include exactly these classes:

```text
leading whitespace
trailing whitespace
embedded newlines
U+00E9
U+0065 U+0301
transport JSON escape representation
one-chunk output
multi-chunk equivalent output
empty textual output
protocol-invalid JSON
large structured JSON output
provider refusal text
multiple textual parts if the pinned provider abstraction permits them
```

Require that equivalent chunk boundaries produce identical rawContent bytes.

Require that Unicode composed/decomposed forms remain byte-distinct.

Require no:

```text
trim
newline insertion
JSON reserialization
pretty printing
JSON repair
Unicode normalization
refusal rewriting
```

Where both delta and terminal projections exist, require:

```text
UTF-8(concatenated textual deltas)
==
UTF-8(terminal textual projection)
==
sealed rawContent bytes
```

### Q7 hidden protocol retry

Disable all controllable retries.

Inject a synthetic failure and prove no fresh protocol attempt is started inside one runner Execution.

### Q8 provider/transport retry accounting

Exercise synthetic transport retry behavior.

Prove the exact transport-attempt count is observable.

If retry is disabled, prove count `1`.

### Q9 abort/cancellation mechanics

Exercise separately:

```text
abort before transport invocation
abort after transport invocation
timeout before completion
mid-stream interruption
known provider-side technical failure
```

Do not map absence of response to non-execution.

### Q13 sibling isolation

Run at least two concurrent synthetic reviewer executions.

Before either raw output is sealed, prove each execution has zero access to the sibling's:

```text
conversation
raw output
findings
adjudication
semantic scratch state
```

### Q14 dependency-surface confirmation

Record exactly which pinned public/version-sensitive/internal surfaces the harness actually exercised.

Do not silently use a different Pi surface from the pinned characterization.

The disposable harness must remain reproducible after its workspace is deleted.

The final Issue report must therefore contain:

```text

SHA-256 of every harness source/config file
exact package lock or exact dependency versions
exact commands
exact environment/runtime versions
complete patch of every harness file against an empty directory
```

The patch must be sufficient for another executor to reconstruct the harness without access to your disposable directory.

```text
PASS | FAIL | BLOCKED

exact command
```

## Recovery model to implement

Implement in the disposable qualification harness exactly this candidate operational journal:

```text
PREPARED
    ↓
MAYBE-SENT
    ↓
TERMINAL-CAPTURED
```

This journal is qualification-harness operational evidence only.

It is not authoritative GateARun state.

It must not emulate or replace M2.

## Durability invariant

The harness must enforce and prove:

```text
provider transport is unreachable
until PREPARED → MAYBE-SENT
has completed its durable write
```

The `MAYBE-SENT` transition must be persisted before any code path capable of reaching the provider transport is invoked.

The durability implementation must include the exact filesystem synchronization required by the selected local journal representation.

Record the exact sequence of:

```text
write
flush
fsync
rename if used
directory fsync if required by the selected atomic-write algorithm
transport invocation
```

Do not use absence of a later journal record as proof that transport was not reached.

## Crash injection mechanism

Use a child process for each crash-cut experiment.

The parent test process must terminate the child at one exact instrumentation barrier.

Do not simulate a crash by ordinary exception handling.

Do not intentionally kill a live external provider request.

Use the controlled synthetic provider/transport for C0-C5 crash injection.

Combine those deterministic adapter results with the already established live provider recovery-capability facts.

## Required crash cuts

Exercise exactly:

### C0

```text

journal == PREPARED
MAYBE-SENT has not been durably committed
provider transport is still unreachable
process terminates
```

```text
not-executed
```

only if the positive proof is mechanically valid.

### C1

```text
MAYBE-SENT durable

no terminal provider result durably captured
process terminates
```

```text
unknown
```

unless the previously qualified live provider capability supplies an exact non-replaying observational recovery mechanism.

```text
process terminates
```

```text
unknown
```

unless exact provider-side observational recovery proves another valid state.

### C3

when terminal truth existed only in volatile process state.

### C4



and not:

```text

AND
```

Never to inference from absence.

value.title: Adjudicate the Issue #41 Q1-Q14 Pi qualification matrix

value.body:
## Problem

Accepted Gate A authority currently defines model identity as:

```text
(provider, model, model_version)
```

For `provider-reported` identity resolution, ADR-045 and the hostile-review protocol documentation require:

```text
qualified attempt provider_model must be non-empty
model_version = qualified attempt provider_model
```

The same authority also prohibits:

```text
model_version = an unresolved alias
```

The accepted authority does not currently define the mechanical evidence or resolution rule that establishes when an exact provider-reported model identifier is resolved rather than an unresolved alias.

This gap was exposed while qualifying the Pi M4 cognitive-execution backend. The integration successfully exposed provider-owned response identity and `response.model` evidence, but a qualification Issue had introduced an additional requirement that every observed identifier be classified as immutable by separate pinned provider documentation. That additional requirement is not currently established by accepted TURNLOCK authority.

This Finding preserves the unresolved semantic question. It does not answer it.

## Current accepted boundary

The following statements remain accepted and must not be weakened:

```text
model identity = (provider, model, model_version)

provider-reported:
  qualified attempt provider_model must be non-empty
  model_version = qualified attempt provider_model

pinned-request-model:
  request_model_is_immutable_version must be true
  model_version = profile.request_model

model_version must not be an arbitrary runner-supplied string
model_version must not be "latest"
model_version must not be an unresolved alias

same (provider, model_version)
=
same effective reviewer identity
```

No Issue, harness, provider implementation, checker behavior, or external documentation becomes semantic authority merely by existing.

## Decision required

The accepted architecture must explicitly determine the resolution rule for `provider-reported` identity.

The decision must answer at minimum:

1. What exact evidence is sufficient to treat a provider-reported model identifier as the resolved `model_version`?
2. Is the provider's execution-time `provider_model` / equivalent response field itself sufficient, and under what contract?
3. If it is not sufficient, what additional resolution evidence is required?
4. How is an unresolved mutable alias distinguished from a resolved effective model identity?
5. What happens when the provider exposes only an alias-like identifier and no stronger version identity?
6. What must a reviewer profile declare, if anything, beyond `identity_resolution.kind = provider-reported`?
7. What evidence must be preserved in the execution receipt / attempt evidence?
8. What exact rule must independent-reviewer counting apply when multiple request aliases produce the same provider-reported effective identity?
9. What mechanical rule, if any, must the checker enforce?
10. Whether provider-owned documentation/catalog metadata is required, optional evidence, or irrelevant must be decided explicitly rather than assumed.

## Provenance

This Finding was exposed by the completed Pi M4 qualification work around:

```text
Issue #41
Issue #44
Issue #46
```

The live Pi experiment demonstrated that the provider response identity and provider-reported model field can be captured separately from the requested model.

That integration fact does not resolve the semantic question in this Finding.

## Required resolution discipline

Classify the final resolution through the accepted ADR process.

Do not:

```text
derive the answer from current checker behavior
derive the answer from Pi behavior
derive the answer from OpenAI documentation alone
infer immutability from model-name syntax
infer immutability from a date suffix
infer immutability from repeated stable observations
weaken the unresolved-alias prohibition merely to accommodate a provider
```

If the accepted decision changes or clarifies existing Gate A semantics, synchronize every owned authority and derived contract required by repository governance.

## Synchronization surface to evaluate

The resolution must determine whether synchronization is required for:

```text
ADR-045 or a later explicit amendment
formal/reviews/README.md
review protocol/profile schemas
execution-receipt / review-evidence schemas
mechanical checker behavior
formal traceability and governed claims
future reviewer-profile admission
```

Do not modify those artifacts as part of merely creating or triaging this Finding.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The accepted decision defines exactly what constitutes a resolved `provider-reported` model identity.
- [ ] The accepted decision defines how unresolved aliases are detected or conservatively handled.
- [ ] The relation between request model, provider-reported model, and `model_version` is unambiguous.
- [ ] Independent-reviewer counting remains unable to inflate diversity through aliases of the same effective identity.
- [ ] The role, if any, of provider-owned documentation or catalogs is explicit.
- [ ] The checker obligation is explicit rather than inferred from its current implementation.
- [ ] Every required normative, ADR, formal, schema, checker, and generated synchronization target is identified.
- [ ] No integration implementation becomes semantic authority.

## Exclusions

This Finding does not:

```text
qualify or disqualify Pi
select a reviewer profile
select a concrete model_version
modify the campaign runner
modify M4
modify the current Dependency Contract selection
execute a provider call
execute Gate A
```

GitHub work state and Project classification remain owned by their canonical GitHub fields and relationships.


## Resolution

Resolved by accepted `ADR-054: Define provider-reported effective model identity resolution` and the synchronized protocol-v6 construction authority.

The accepted resolution defines `provider-reported` through the qualified contract:

```text
provider-owned-canonical-effective-model-identity-v1
```

The provider-reported identity channel must be provider-owned, execution-bound, post-routing, post-alias-resolution, canonical for effective-model identity equality, and opaque to TURNLOCK. For a qualified attempt, the exact channel value is preserved as `provider_model` and becomes `model_version`.

ADR-054 also defines fail-closed behavior when the selected realization cannot establish that capability, preserves the prohibition on fabricated or unresolved aliases, and introduces hostile-review protocol v6 without changing TURNLOCK product semantics or Gate A semantic subject S.

The repository construction authority has been synchronized accordingly, including active NIB-S 9.1.0, M4-A 1.1.0, and the Pi M4 Dependency Contract 1.1.0.

This Finding is therefore complete.

## Problem

The accepted Gate A campaign-runner System Brief selects M4 `cognitive-execution` as the sole system module responsible for bounded external cognitive execution.

M4 contains two independently coherent construction responsibilities:

```text
execution / capture
recovery observation
```

They require different inputs, algorithms, failure handling, and validation boundaries. M4 therefore requires separate Module Brief coverage without changing the system-level module decomposition.

This Issue owns only the execution/capture half of M4.

```text
NIB-S-GATE-A-CAMPAIGN-RUNNER 9.1.0

NIB-M-GATE-A-COGNITIVE-EXECUTION-CAPTURE 1.1.1

DC-PI-M4-GATE-A-COGNITIVE-EXECUTION 1.1.1

```

## Problem

The accepted Gate A campaign-runner System Brief requires M4 `cognitive-execution` to implement the executor-domain recovery boundary for unresolved cognitive Executions.

This responsibility is distinct from initial cognitive execution/capture.

Recovery receives an already armed and unresolved Execution and must only observe or derive exact executor-domain recovery facts. It must never replay the original cognitive request or infer execution truth from absence of evidence.

The coding agent must not infer provider-recovery semantics, positive non-execution proofs, safe re-observation rules, indeterminacy rules, or recovered-terminal behavior during GREEN.

This Issue owns only the recovery-observation half of M4.

## Current authoritative boundary

This Module Brief consumes the active synchronized construction authority:

```text
NIB-S-GATE-A-CAMPAIGN-RUNNER 9.1.0

NIB-M-GATE-A-COGNITIVE-EXECUTION-CAPTURE 1.1.1

DC-PI-M4-GATE-A-COGNITIVE-EXECUTION 1.1.1

NIB-M-GATE-A-COGNITIVE-EXECUTION-RECOVERY-OBSERVATION 1.0.0 active

NIB-M-GATE-A-RECOVERY-OPERATOR-RECONCILIATION 2.0.9

NIB-M-GATE-A-RECOVERY-OPERATOR-BOUNDARY 2.0.9
```

and the accepted hostile-review authority including ADR-042 through ADR-049, ADR-053, ADR-054, and hostile-review protocol v6.

ADR-054 has resolved the provider-reported model-identity semantics previously tracked by Issue #47. M4-B must preserve that accepted authority and must not reinterpret provider identity during recovery.

The system-level module remains exactly:

```text
M4 — cognitive-execution
```

The M4-A / M4-B split is a NIB-M construction decomposition only.

M4-B implements the M4-owned executor-domain side of the existing:

```ts
interface ExecutionRecoveryPort {
  reconcile(
    unresolved: UnresolvedExecutionRecoveryRef
  ): Promise<ExecutionRecoveryObservation>;
}
```

M4-B establishes executor-domain recovery observations.

M8 owns common-envelope validation and recovery classification.

M2 alone admits authoritative campaign-state consequences.

Dependency-specific Pi/provider recovery capabilities remain owned by the scoped Pi M4 Dependency Contract.

For the selected Pi backend, DC 1.1.1 establishes no accepted provider-side post-crash response lookup, no safe read-only provider pending observation, and no provider-call replay. Therefore the initial M4-B realization has no legal `pending` branch. Its reachable local recovery outcomes are derived from the M4-A journal:

```text
valid PREPARED
and no valid MAYBE-SENT
and no valid TERMINAL
→ positive executor-owned non-execution proof
→ not-executed

valid TERMINAL-DURABLE
→ reconstruct exact captured or technical-failure terminal outcome
→ terminal

valid MAYBE-SENT
and no valid TERMINAL-DURABLE
→ provider effect may have crossed the boundary
→ no qualified observational provider recovery exists
→ positive executor-domain indeterminacy
→ unknown
```

M4-B never submits, resubmits, replays, or otherwise re-executes the original cognitive request.

## Required outcome

Produce one active Module Brief:

```text
docs/formal/nib-m-gate-a-cognitive-execution-recovery-observation.md

id:
NIB-M-GATE-A-COGNITIVE-EXECUTION-RECOVERY-OBSERVATION
```

The brief must close the recovery-observation responsibility of M4 sufficiently that GREEN contains no implementation-design discretion.

It must define at minimum:

- exact M4-B responsibility and exclusions;
- exact construction dependencies;
- exact `ExecutionRecoveryPort` implementation boundary;
- validation of the incoming `UnresolvedExecutionRecoveryRef`;
- exact use of the bound `RecoveryCapabilityRef`;
- exact relationship to M4 execution/call identity and durable operational journal evidence;
- exact executor-owned proof-artifact schemas required for cognitive recovery;
- exact positive proof rule for `ExecutionRecoveryObservation.kind = "not-executed"`;
- exact cognitive-call effect boundary whose non-crossing must be proven;
- exact construction and runtime validation of `NonExecutionProofRef`;
- exact terminal recovered-capture behavior;
- exact terminal known no-completed-response technical-failure behavior;
- exact construction and runtime validation of `ReconciliationContinuabilityRef`;
- exact positive conditions required before `kind = "pending"` is legal;
- exact prohibition on replay/resubmit/re-execution during reconciliation;
- exact construction and runtime validation of `RecoveryIndeterminacyRef`;
- exact positive conditions required before `kind = "unknown"` is legal;
- provider/backend recovery capability handling;
- local durable-terminal reconstruction rules;
- provider-response recovery rules where the accepted dependency contract supports them;
- behavior when no trustworthy recovery capability exists;
- crash/restart behavior;
- immutable-artifact evidence requirements;
- evidence ordering and duplicate rules required by the NIB-S envelopes;
- exact dependency-contract requirements consumed from the Pi M4 Dependency Contract;
- implementation/process/integrity failure conditions;
- forbidden behavior.

M4-B must preserve the accepted rule:

```text
absence of evidence != proof of non-execution
```

The following facts alone are never sufficient for `not-executed`, `pending`, `unknown`, or terminal completion:

```text
timeout
cancellation request
process crash
missing response
missing receipt
transport disconnect
elapsed time
failed convenient lookup
absence of provider material
```

M4-B may return `not-executed` only from a positive executor-owned proof that the exact cognitive-call boundary was never crossed.

M4-B may return `pending` only from a positive executor-owned proof that another invocation of the exact reconciliation operation is purely observational and incapable of creating, repeating, replaying, resubmitting, or otherwise re-executing the original cognitive request.

M4-B may return `unknown` only from a positive executor-owned indeterminacy fact establishing that the available recovery mechanism cannot determine a terminal outcome and cannot establish either positive non-execution or safe continued observation.

M4-B never assigns:

```text
PROVEN-NOT-EXECUTED
PROVEN-COMPLETED
UNRESOLVABLE
RECONCILABLE
```

Those are M8-owned classifications.

## M4 decomposition boundary

M4-B and the separately scoped M4-A execution/capture Module Brief together provide complete NIB-M coverage of the single system module:

```text
M4 cognitive-execution
```

M4-B must remain coherent with the exact execution identity, cognitive-call identity, dispatch evidence, recovery capability, journal evidence, and terminal artifacts selected by the M4 execution/capture construction.

Do not introduce a third NIB-M for the Pi adapter.

Dependency-specific provider/Pi recovery facts belong to the separate Pi M4 Dependency Contract.

## Exclusions

This Issue does not:

- perform the initial cognitive request;
- authorize protocol retry;
- replay an uncertain provider call;
- classify recovery for M8;
- write authoritative M2 state;
- implement production code;
- create RED tests;
- create the NIB-T;
- write the Pi M4 Dependency Contract;
- modify the NIB-S;
- modify TURNLOCK Product Semantics;
- modify Gate A hostile-review semantics;
- reinterpret, weaken, or replace ADR-054 provider-reported model-identity semantics;

- [x] `ExecutionRecoveryPort.reconcile(...)` behavior is decisionally complete.

- [x] A negative lookup or missing evidence can never independently establish non-execution.
- [x] Recovered captured completion and recovered terminal technical failure are mechanically distinct.
- [x] `pending` requires positive safe-observation evidence and cannot replay the original request.
- [x] The selected Pi backend cannot produce `pending` unless a future accepted Dependency Contract version establishes a positively safe read-only recovery capability.
- [x] `unknown` requires positive executor-domain indeterminacy evidence.

## Problem

Architectural analysis performed while beginning the M5 `assurance-ledger`
Module Briefs exposed three construction-boundary gaps in the active Gate A
campaign-runner System Brief.

The gaps must be closed before M5 internal algorithms are frozen because
working around them inside an M5 Module Brief would move unresolved
cross-module architecture into implementation.

The first gap concerns assurance evidence materialization.

M5 produces immutable hostile-review and assurance artifacts including execution
receipts, review records, findings, challenges, re-adjudications, and related
provenance. Mechanical Gate A validation, however, operates against one exact
sealed `CandidateRevision`. The current non-C0 candidate construction path is
bound only to an admitted `RepairIntent`, leaving no explicit mechanical path
for assurance artifacts to become part of the exact candidate repository state
that M6 validates and M7 may later publish.

The second gap concerns existing repository campaigns.

`GateAEvaluationContext` currently identifies current and stale-protocol
campaigns through `ReviewCampaignRef`, but M5 must consume their exact immutable
review evidence and finding state without reconstructing the ledger by scanning
mutable repository/workspace state. The cross-module contract therefore needs
an exact immutable campaign-evidence observation boundary.

The third gap concerns operational blockers.

M8-B owns `OperationalBlocker` identity and Operator Action Request
materialization. M5 owns assurance-domain operational causes. The current
construction contract must preserve that ownership split so M5 produces exact
producer-domain cause material and M8-B alone materializes the corresponding
operational blocker.

## Current authoritative boundary

This work is implementation-construction architecture only.

It must preserve:

- TURNLOCK product semantics;
- accepted hostile-review protocol semantics;
- ADR-041 through ADR-049;
- the existing M1-M8 system module boundaries;
- M2 as the sole authoritative campaign-state writer;
- M3 ownership of campaign/currentness selection;
- M5 ownership of assurance-ledger semantics;
- M6 ownership of Python mechanical validation invocation;
- M7 ownership of repository/candidate materialization;
- M8-B ownership of operational-blocker identity and Operator Action Requests;
- the rule that M5 returns explicit cross-module assurance products rather than
  committing authoritative state directly.

No provider, harness, implementation convenience, or NIB-M may create new
product or hostile-review semantics.

## Scope

Close the exact construction gaps exposed by M5 analysis.

The architect must establish a decisional-complete construction contract for:

### Immutable existing-campaign evidence

Define the exact immutable cross-module representation by which the
repository-selected campaigns returned through the campaign-authority boundary
carry or resolve the exact review record and immutable artifact closure required
by M5.

The contract must preserve:

```text
M3
→ selects campaign applicability/currentness

M5
→ interprets exact immutable assurance evidence

no M5 mutable-workspace rescan
```

### Assurance repository projection

Define the exact construction boundary by which M5-produced assurance artifacts
that belong in the Gate A repository representation are projected
mechanically into repository materialization.

The boundary must preserve:

```text
M5
→ determines exact assurance artifacts and exact intended repository placement

M7
→ performs mechanical repository/candidate materialization

M7 does not reinterpret assurance meaning
M5 does not mutate repository state directly
```

The design must support the exact cases required by the accepted pipeline:

```text
assurance-materialization-only successor
repair successor
repair + assurance-materialization successor
```

without fabricating a semantic repair merely to place assurance artifacts in
the candidate repository.

An assurance-only repository projection must not silently alter the semantic
subject it is evidence about.

If exact assurance-only materialization changes the derived semantic subject
when the accepted construction contract requires preservation, that condition
must fail closed as a construction/integrity defect rather than silently
creating a new semantic campaign meaning.

### Candidate provenance

Synchronize the candidate-construction/admission contract so a non-C0 candidate
is not incorrectly assumed to exist only because of `RepairIntent`.

Candidate lineage and provenance must remain exact, append-only, and
reconstructible.

The contract must distinguish the accepted construction provenance needed for:

```text
assurance materialization
repair
repair + assurance materialization
```

while preserving deterministic candidate identity and the existing prohibition
on speculative candidate branching.

### Assurance operational causes

Define the exact M5 non-recovery operational-cause handoff to M8-B.

M5 may own:

```text
assurance-ledger cause schema
assurance-domain cause semantics
cause validation
basis evidence
lawful non-recovery resolution contracts
```

M5 must not own:

```text
OperationalBlocker identity
BlockerId normalization
Operator Action Request bytes
operator-resolution state effects
```

Those remain M8-B responsibilities.

### Synchronization

Synchronize every already-active construction artifact whose accepted contract
is affected by the above changes, including the active System Brief and any
existing M2/M7/M8 Module Brief whose consumed boundary becomes stale.

Synchronize the top-level orchestration pseudocode where required.

Do not create production implementation.

## Exclusions

This Issue does not:

- write the M5-A/B/C/D Module Briefs;
- implement the campaign runner;
- write RED tests or NIB-T;
- create or execute real hostile-review evidence;
- change TURNLOCK product semantics;
- change accepted hostile-review protocol semantics;
- change the M1-M8 module topology;
- give M5 repository mutation authority;
- give M7 assurance-semantic authority;
- give M8 product-semantic authority.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Exact immutable existing-campaign evidence can reach M5 without mutable workspace rescanning.
- [ ] Exact M5-produced repository assurance artifacts have a mechanical M5-to-M7 materialization path.
- [ ] Assurance-only, repair-only, and repair-plus-assurance candidate construction cases are unambiguous.
- [ ] Candidate provenance remains exact and reconstructible.
- [ ] Assurance-only repository materialization cannot silently change the reviewed semantic subject.
- [ ] M5 produces assurance-domain operational causes rather than independently constructing M8-B-owned OperationalBlockers.
- [ ] M8-B remains the sole owner of operational blocker identity and Operator Action Request construction.
- [ ] M2 remains the sole authoritative campaign-state writer.
- [ ] Existing active downstream briefs affected by the changed System Brief boundary are synchronized.
- [ ] Top-level orchestration remains implementable without a coding-agent architecture choice.
- [ ] Every material discovery encountered while closing the boundary is classified and routed under repository governance.
- [ ] No production implementation is added.

## Problem

M5-A construction exposed an underdetermination in the accepted Gate A
hostile-review assurance contract.

Current authority defines:

- a protocol-owned reviewer-profile registry;
- static reviewer-profile qualification;
- evidence-derived reviewer identity;
- effective duplicate identity `(provider, model_version)`;
- `minimum_independent_reviewers`;
- the prohibition on semantic-result model shopping.

It does not uniquely determine:

- which statically qualifying profiles must actually be executed when more
  profiles are eligible than the minimum;
- the order in which profiles are acquired;
- how acquisition expands after qualified executions resolve to duplicate
  effective identities;
- whether operational failure of a selected reviewer permits automatic
  substitution by another profile;
- what happens when all eligible profiles are exhausted while the effective
  independent-reviewer minimum remains unmet.

Choosing these behaviors inside M5-A would silently create hostile-review
assurance semantics in an implementation-construction brief.

## Discovery classification

```text
decision-required
formal-assurance / hostile-review architecture
no TURNLOCK product-semantic impact
```

## Required outcome

Accept one deterministic hostile-review acquisition policy that:

- treats the reviewer registry as eligibility rather than an obligation to
  execute every registered profile;
- acquires only the reviewer executions needed to establish the required
  effective independent-reviewer minimum;
- uses an explicit protocol-owned total profile acquisition order;
- is independent of review content and execution timing;
- expands only after qualified evidence establishes that the effective identity
  target remains unmet;
- preserves every actually executed qualified review even when its effective
  identity is redundant;
- does not use another reviewer profile as an automatic substitute for
  operational retry exhaustion of an already-selected WorkItem;
- routes eligible-pool exhaustion with the minimum still unmet to
  OPERATOR-ACTION-REQUIRED;
- leaves TURNLOCK product semantics and Gate A semantic subject S unchanged.

## Selection and frozen evidence authority


- E6-C: 204 calls, 169.919012s inclusive; 51 actual read paths, all recorded, plus one conservative `docs/adr` membership sentinel in an ambiguous state.

Distinguish proven reachable, conditionally reachable, unproven, and not relevant by construction. Preserve callsite and source-location evidence. Explicitly analyze the four known patch symbols:

```text

_p7_unique_correction_exhaustion_errors
```

**R2 — ADR membership and nonregular inputs.** Distinguish observed file-content hashes from directory-member identity, missing/duplicate/renamed matching ADRs, glob resolution, symlinked path components, unreadable/nonregular files, unresolved paths, and exception/diagnostic behavior. A conservative `docs/adr` recorder sentinel alone must **not** be counted as a usable directory fingerprint.

**R3 — Controlled differential/falsification matrix.** Using **external test code and disposable copies/fixtures only**, execute genuinely independent uncached E6-C evaluations and compare complete ordered errors, exception type/text where stable, and important side effects for these conditions:

1. Pristine same-root repeated evaluation and pristine equal-content distinct roots; compare errors without discarding root-specific diagnostics.

6. Cold versus warm relevant parser/cache/global states under identical files and callables, isolating whether mutation changes E6-C behavior. Capture module-global changes/restoration and avoid observer-caused result changes.
7. Cached-positive and cached-negative counterfactuals: for at least one authentic nonempty diagnostic case and one authentic successful case, demonstrate whether a proposed file-plus-callable key would wrongly reuse a stale result after an unrepresented effective input changes. Do **not** install a production E6-C cache to conduct this test; simulate lookup in the external harness only, with genuine uncached results as oracle.

For every variant retain the exact initial state, one controlled change, actual path/identity observation, whether the changed behavior was genuinely exercised, baseline and variant results, and the safety conclusion. If no effective mutation can be constructed for a required transitive symbol, record `UNEXERCISED` and keep admissibility undetermined; do not fabricate an error or replace an assertion with a tautology.

**R4 — Exact candidate-boundary argument.** Evaluate whether a cache key plus explicit fail-closed guard assembled **solely from already existing repository primitives and observable state** could distinguish every effective E6-C input in the delimited contract. State the minimal necessary identity components, invalidation conditions and required guards *as qualification findings*, not as executable code or authorized architecture. Identify any state the existing primitive cannot represent. Test *necessity* of each proposed component with counterexamples and establish *sufficiency* only with a traceable, independently falsifiable argument, not by a finite green test matrix alone.

**R5 — Evidence integrity and independent falsification review.** Read the #64 DATA and, if accessible, verify the original `/tmp/turnlock-post63-validation-profile/` evidence manifest and key raw observations against the published digest. If those are missing, report the exact evidence gap rather than silently recreating the original profile; continue only with independently grounded source and new observations where the absence does not invalidate the claimed finding. Keep all newly generated scripts, fixtures, logs, witnesses, hashes and analysis strictly under a unique `/tmp/turnlock-e6c-reuse-qualification/` evidence root. Obtain a fresh independent review aimed at falsifying any positive reuse claim and verifying honest unresolved conclusions.

## Verdict semantics

A reviewer can approve an honestly reported `UNDETERMINED` without endorsing a cache. Distinguish review quality from reuse safety.

```text
BOUNDARY_VERDICT=ESTABLISHED | REFUTED | UNDETERMINED
```

- `ESTABLISHED` only when every named and discovered effective dependency class is accounted for, a concrete existing-primitives-only guard/key contract is justified, required negative cases pass, and the independent reviewer accepts the explicit sufficiency argument **for the declared bounded domain**.
- `REFUTED` when a reproducible, relevant counterexample invalidates a specific proposed key/guard boundary; report the counterexample and the affected condition. This verdict does not mean all future E6-C caching is impossible.

Produce an evidence-grounded, source-derived contract boundary and differential counterexamples if one exists.

This is an **implementation-level safety qualification**, not a new-cache or source-fix task. No optimization, E6-C whole-result cache, change to repository or formal authority, or implementation Issue is selected.

## Origin and known evidence

- Issue #65: https://github.com/fanilosendrison/turnlock-rust/issues/65#issuecomment-6191718057
- Issue #64: https://github.com/fanilosendrison/turnlock-rust/issues/64#issuecomment-6181495510
