content.body:
## Problem

TURNLOCK is a runtime for executable orchestration programs, not a collection of
opaque automations that invoke one another as external services. Under ADR-014
the workflow program is the source of declared orchestration topology and
TURNLOCK is the engine that executes it without inventing undeclared strategy.
Composition capabilities such as sequencing, branching/iteration, concurrency,
fan-out/fan-in, nested workflow invocation, and structured return are already
required of that program surface (Section 0.1, Section 0.2, `TL-INV-031`).

The previous framing of this Issue treated "may a workflow declaratively invoke
another workflow?" as an open, exotic product capability. That is the wrong
abstraction level. Invocation composition is a consequence of the workflow being
an orchestration program with already-required expressive power. The real
blocker for the first TLA+ state machine is the missing **structured call/return
semantics** for workflow invocation:

> **What is the structured call/return semantics between TURNLOCK workflows,
> independent of the concrete mechanism used to represent the call?**

Two invocation decision owners are involved, and accepted authority currently
defines only one:

```text
workflow-declared invocation                agent-selected invocation
decision owner = workflow program           decision owner = main agent
executor       = TURNLOCK                   during a main-agent region
```

ADR-008 accepted the agent-selected path: while the main agent owns a
main-agent region it may select workflow B; B executes its own declared
progression; normal completion returns to that same main-agent region. ADR-008
therefore governs a specific decision owner, not a general call/return
primitive.

The corpus simultaneously pressures toward workflow-declared invocation:

- `TL-INV-031` requires the workflow-declared orchestration surface to be
  expressive enough that known control decisions remain executable workflow
  logic rather than being delegated back to an agent for lack of orchestration
  primitives; its composition list includes nested workflow invocation and
  structured return to caller.
- ADR-014 requires TURNLOCK to provide sufficient execution authority to
  realize declared workflow semantics, including nested invocation and
  structured return, without inventing strategy.
- Section 0.1 lists nested workflow invocation among workflow-owned composition
  capabilities; Section 0.2 says regions "may be composed with explicit
  workflow control, including fan-out/fan-in and nested workflows"; Section 2.2
  says a workflow may contain nested workflow invocations.

A topology such as:

```text
workflow A
  → X
  → declared invocation of workflow B
  → Y
```

must not be forced into:

```text
workflow A
  → X
  → handoff to main agent
  → main agent decides to invoke B
  → B
  → ...
```

merely to reproduce an invocation decision the workflow program already
declares. Otherwise a known orchestration decision is pushed back into agent
judgment solely because the invocation primitive is missing, which is exactly
what `TL-INV-031` and ADR-014 exist to prevent.

At the same time, no accepted authority defines the transition for a
workflow-declared invocation, and the canonical terminology of Section 2.8 is
narrower than the composition language above. This Issue must make that tension
visible and resolve it, rather than silently selecting an interpretation.

## Why this blocks the first TLA+ model

The first safety model must represent invocation and return as first-class
transitions. `formal/verification.yaml` already plans properties such as
`StructuredReturnPath`, `NestedInvocationSuspendsCaller`,
`CallerStackWellFormed`, `ReturnToImmediateCaller`,
`CorrectCallerEventuallyResumesUnderFairness`, and
`NestedInvocationCannotRewriteOuterContinuation` for `TL-INV-008` and
`TL-INV-017`–`TL-INV-019`.

To do so abstractly, the model must be able to distinguish at least:

```text
who authorized or selected the invocation     (decision owner)
what execution context is the immediate caller
which continuation is suspended
what workflow invocation is active
where normal completion returns
```

If the model reuses ADR-008's main-agent-selected transition for a
workflow-declared invocation, it misattributes decision ownership: an agent
decision appears where the workflow program owns the decision. If the model adds
a generic declared-invocation transition without accepted semantics, it creates
product meaning inside a model. Neither is acceptable under the discovery
protocol or `TL-INV-031`'s expressive-power obligation.

This Issue also gates the transitive composition/admissibility work in Issue #6
and the corresponding readiness item in Issue #9.

## Existing authority

### Composition and expressive power

- **Section 0.1** lists workflow-owned composition capabilities: "sequencing,
  branching/iteration where declared, concurrency, fan-out/fan-in, nested
  workflow invocation, and structured return to the immediate caller".
- **Section 0.2** says regions "may be composed with explicit workflow control,
  including fan-out/fan-in and nested workflows" and that "when an invocation
  finishes, control returns to its immediate caller".
- **Section 2.2** defines a workflow as an executable user-defined process that
  owns progression and may contain "control-flow/composition operations, and
  nested workflow invocations".
- **Section 5.8 and Section 5.13** require the authoring surface to express
  nested invocation and structured return without harness plumbing, and the
  executable control layer to represent declared topology directly, including
  nested composition.
- **`TL-INV-031`** requires the workflow-declared orchestration surface to be
  expressive enough that known control decisions can remain executable workflow
  logic rather than being delegated back to an agent for lack of orchestration
  primitives; its list includes `nested workflow invocation` and `structured
  return to caller`.
- **ADR-014** separates workflow program (declared orchestration decisions and
  topology) from TURNLOCK (engine executing them) and requires sufficient
  execution authority to realize declared semantics including `nested
  invocation` and `structured return`.

### Invocation, caller, and return

- **Section 2.6** defines an `immediate caller context` as "the execution
  context that invoked a workflow and to which normal completion of that
  workflow returns", with a conceptual `caller stack` that is explicitly "not a
  requirement to implement a literal process stack".
- **Section 2.2A** defines an `execution region` as a workflow-declared semantic
  scope with local execution authority, without requiring any runtime
  representation.
- **`TL-INV-008`** states the universal rule: "Every workflow invocation MUST
  preserve a structured return path: `immediate caller → workflow → immediate
  caller`."
- **Section 0.6 and ADR-006** define the top-level lifecycle: workflow
  completion returns to the immediate invocation context, which for a top-level
  workflow is the surrounding main-agent interaction.
- **Section 0.3A** and ADR-008 define the accepted nested scenario: the main
  agent may invoke another available workflow while it owns a main-agent region;
  the enclosing workflow is suspended and is not replaced or discarded.
- **`TL-INV-016`–`TL-INV-019`** and **ADR-008** define that path's semantics:
  workflow availability during main-agent control; suspension of the immediate
  caller; a distinct callee execution owning its own declared progression;
  immediate-caller return; preservation of the outer workflow's orchestration;
  no assumption of nesting depth one; no required literal stack or representation.
- **Section 2.8** is the canonical definition: "A **nested workflow invocation**
  is a workflow invocation made from a main-agent region while that immediate
  caller context is suspended."

### Workflow-owned control and decision ownership

- **Section 0.8, Section 0.8A, `TL-INV-001`, `TL-INV-002`, and `TL-INV-013`**
  require global progression to be workflow-declared, forbid hidden agent
  orchestration, and forbid the engine from inventing undeclared strategy.
- **ADR-016 and `TL-INV-032`** separate workflow authorship from runtime
  execution authority; TURNLOCK executes the artifact regardless of author
  provenance, and the author does not become the runtime scheduler.

### Declared concurrency

- **ADR-013, `TL-INV-024`, `TL-INV-027`, and Section 5.11** require declared
  parallel branches to execute concurrently under workflow-owned control while
  preserving each branch's semantics; ADR-013 explicitly leaves main-agent
  continuation as an ordinary parallel branch undecided.

### Explicitly open boundaries

- **Section 4** records as intentionally undecided: resource/safety limits on
  nesting depth and how they are surfaced without changing immediate-caller
  return semantics; sibling/top-level workflow concurrency; and other items
  listed as future derivation points. It states that "structured nested
  invocation is already allowed".

### Current formal status

- `formal/verification.yaml` contains intended traceability only. No
  executable `Turnlock.tla` exists, no TLC configuration exists, and no
  invariant is `checked`. Adding formal entries for any outcome of this Issue is
  limited to `planned`/`not-yet-modeled` under ADR-015.

## Discovery classification

Classification uses the shared `engineering-discovery-classification` skill and
`docs/repository-governance/turnlock-rust-discovery-classification.md`. This
Issue records work and provenance; it does not accept product semantics. The
later ADR is the acceptance authority.

### DC-1 — Declared-call composition is pressured by existing authority but blocked by a canonical-definition conflict

**Statement.** A workflow artifact must be able to express an already-known
invocation of another workflow as executable workflow logic, without delegating
the invocation decision to the main agent.

**Candidate A derivation.**

- Derived from: `TL-INV-031`; ADR-014; `TL-INV-001`/`TL-INV-002`; Sections 0.8
  and 0.8A.
- Steps:
  1. `TL-INV-031` requires the workflow-declared orchestration surface to keep
     known control decisions in executable workflow logic.
  2. The decision "invoke workflow B at this point of A's topology" is a known
     control decision.
  3. Without a declared invocation primitive, executing that topology would
     require delegating the invocation decision to the main agent, the only
     other accepted invocation owner.
  4. Delegating a known decision for lack of a primitive is what `TL-INV-031`
     forbids; ADR-014 forbids the engine from inventing the missing transition.
  5. Therefore the workflow-declared orchestration surface must admit a
     declared invocation.
- Why no new choice: the steps negate the only alternative (agent delegation)
  using accepted obligations; they do not select among independent design
  options.
- Failure if omitted: topologies containing known invocations cannot satisfy
  `TL-INV-031`; TURNLOCK either invents the transition or returns a known
  decision to agent judgment.

**Conflict.** Section 2.8 canonically defines `nested workflow invocation` as an
invocation made from a main-agent region, and `TL-INV-017`/ADR-008 define only
that path. Under the Section 2 registry rule, the composition references in
Section 0.1, Section 2.2, and `TL-INV-031` may be read using that narrow
meaning. But then `TL-INV-031`'s listed `nested workflow invocation` item would
refer to an agent-selected capability, not to a capability of the
*workflow-declared orchestration surface* the invariant governs, making the item
incoherent with the invariant's own framing. No accepted decision resolves which
reading governs.

**Disposition:** `authority-conflict-or-uncertain` (blocks the candidate
A derivation; the outcome may resolve it toward A or toward an explicit B
decision).

**Affected layers:** `normative-contract`; `decision-history`;
`formal-model-or-analysis`.

**Next action:** resolve the reading explicitly through the outcome ADR. Do not
silently choose between the narrow and broad readings.

### DC-2 — Actor-neutral structured-return obligations for every admitted invocation

**Statement.** Any admitted workflow invocation preserves `immediate caller
context → workflow → same immediate caller context`; the callee owns its
declared progression and cannot rewrite, replace, or skip the caller's
continuation.

**Derived from:** `TL-INV-008` (unqualified "every workflow invocation");
Section 2.6 (general definition of immediate caller context); Section 2.2;
`TL-INV-001`/`TL-INV-002`; ADR-014.

**Why no new choice:** the structured-return rule already quantifies over every
workflow invocation and does not depend on the selecting actor; the caller is
defined as the context that invoked; the callee's independence follows from the
workflow-program/engine separation.

**Condition:** conditional on the invocation being admitted by DC-1/DC-3 and
Issue #6's admissibility rules.

**Disposition:** `derived-from-existing-authority` (legacy A, conditional).

**Affected layers:** `normative-contract`; `formal-model-or-analysis`.

### DC-3 — The workflow-declared transition and decision-owner factoring are underdetermined

**Statement.** Current authority does not uniquely determine:

- the precise identity of the immediate caller context for a declared
  invocation in declared-topology terms (calling continuation / branch context);
- the suspension scope when other declared contexts are concurrently active;
- whether the agent-selected and workflow-declared paths share one abstract
  invocation/return semantic parameterized by decision owner, or remain two
  semantics that share only abstract obligations;
- whether a declared invocation is admissible in a restricted context such as a
  parallel branch (owned by Issue #6).

**Disposition:** `decision-required` (legacy B). **Locked** until accepted by
the repository ADR process.

**Affected layers:** `normative-contract`; `decision-history`;
`formal-model-or-analysis`.

### DC-4 — Representation and resource-policy choices

**Statement.** Caller-stack/frame representation, TLA+ state variable or action
names, activation identifiers, Rust types, DSL opcodes, process models, and
maximum nesting depth are realization or resource-policy choices, not product
semantics.

**Disposition:** `no-normative-impact` (legacy C/D).

**Affected layers:** `formal-model-or-analysis`; `architecture-or-implementation`.

### Locked `decision-required` items

The following semantic choices must be decided through the accepted ADR process
before this Issue resolves; they must not be selected by the model, the issue,
or implementation convenience:

1. whether workflow-declared invocation is admitted, and the terminology
   reconciliation that follows from the DC-1 conflict;
2. the abstract caller identity and suspension-scope semantics for a declared
   invocation;
3. the accepted or rejected factoring between ADR-008's agent-selected path and
   the workflow-declared path;
4. the admissibility boundary for recursion/cycles and restricted placements
   (coordinated with Issue #6);
5. any new invariant identity, only under the repository's invariant admission
   test.

## Candidate general semantic (to test and establish — not accepted)

The outcome of this Issue is expected to establish, via a later ADR, either the
following candidate semantic or a documented rejection with a
specification-consistent account of nested composition.

For an admitted invocation:

```text
caller context C
  → invokes workflow B
  → C's call continuation is suspended
  → B executes its own declared progression
  → B normally completes
  → control returns to the same caller context C
  → C's declared post-call continuation becomes eligible
```

Candidate obligations for any admitted invocation:

1. **Decision owner.** For a declared invocation, the decision to invoke B
   belongs to the workflow program; TURNLOCK executes it. A known declared
   invocation must not require a main-agent handoff to be selected.
2. **Immediate caller.** `§2.6`'s general definition applies: the immediate
   caller is the execution context that invoked the workflow and to which
   normal completion returns.
3. **Suspended continuation.** The caller's call continuation is suspended
   while the callee is active; the caller's declared post-call continuation is
   the only continuation enabled by normal return.
4. **Callee progression.** The callee owns its own declared progression and may
   use execution forms and invocations already authorized by accepted semantics
   and Issue #6's admissibility rules.
5. **Outer-continuation preservation.** The callee must not rewrite, replace,
   or skip the caller's continuation; the caller's control flow comes only from
   the caller workflow program.
6. **Decision-owner distinction.** Workflow-declared and agent-selected
   invocation must remain distinguishable by decision owner even if they share
   one abstract return semantic.
7. **Engine boundary.** TURNLOCK executes the declared invocation; it does not
   invent the call or the continuation.

Candidate factoring to test (not accepted): one abstract structured
invocation/return semantic — caller context, suspended calling continuation,
callee progression, normal return to the same caller context — parameterized by
the decision owner that selects the callee:

```text
workflow program (declared invocation) | main agent (ADR-008 region)
```

The factoring would preserve ADR-008 as an accepted special case of selection
authority while sharing suspension/return semantics. It must not be treated as
accepted until the ADR process accepts it, and it must not erase the difference
in who selects the callee.

## Concurrency caveat: calling continuation, not whole-workflow suspension

The semantic must not state without justification that "workflow A is
suspended" while B executes. TURNLOCK supports declared fan-out/fan-in and
declared concurrency (`TL-INV-024`, `TL-INV-027`, ADR-013). For example:

```text
workflow A
  fan-out
    ├─ branch X
    │    → declared invocation of B
    │    → X2
    └─ branch Y
         → Y1
         → Y2
```

The correct abstract statement is local: the calling continuation/context that
performed the invocation is suspended. Concurrently active independent contexts
of the same workflow continue according to the declared topology.

The semantics must reason in terms of:

```text
immediate caller context
calling continuation
callee invocation / active progression
normal return target
```

and not in terms of a whole workflow necessarily blocked. Whether a declared
invocation may occur inside a parallel branch or another restricted context is
Issue #6's admissibility question; this Issue must not prejudge it, but its
semantic must not assume unconditional whole-workflow suspension.

No concrete representation is selected here. Names such as `callerContext`,
`calleeActivation`, or `returnContinuation` are illustrative only and are not
product contract.

## Structured nesting versus recursion and cycles

Arbitrary structured nesting:

```text
A → B → C → D
```

is not the same question as recursion or cycles:

```text
A → A
A → B → A
```

Current authority already forbids assuming nesting depth one (`TL-INV-017`,
ADR-008). That does not decide whether TURNLOCK accepts self-recursion, mutual
recursion, or cyclic workflow call graphs.

Scope for this Issue:

- define the call/return semantics of every **admitted** invocation;
- do not decide recursion/cycle admissibility unless accepted authority
  requires it; the transitive admissibility question, including recursive and
  cyclic call graphs, is tracked by Issue #6;
- do not derive a concrete limit such as `max_depth = 32`; any resource/safety
  limit is policy (`§4`, ADR-008) and must preserve caller/return semantics for
  every accepted invocation;
- state the normative property as: for every admitted invocation, the
  caller/return guarantees hold.

## Open questions

1. Does the corpus's expressive-power requirement entail a workflow-declared
   invocation decision owner, or can declared invocation be rejected while
   `TL-INV-031`, Section 0.1, Section 0.2, and ADR-014 remain satisfied? If
   rejected, what exact account explains "known control decisions" for nested
   composition?
2. If admitted, what is the immediate caller context of a declared invocation
   in declared-topology terms, and how is the suspended calling continuation
   identified without selecting a runtime representation?
3. Do the workflow-declared and ADR-008 agent-selected paths share one abstract
   invocation/return semantic parameterized by decision owner, or remain two
   semantics with common abstract obligations?
4. How is suspension expressed so that concurrently declared contexts are
   unaffected, while parallel-placement admissibility remains Issue #6's
   decision?
5. Which canonical terminology must change, and how, if Section 2.8's
   definition is found too narrow relative to the composition language?

## Required outcome

Adopt an accepted decision — recorded in a later ADR, without editing any
accepted ADR body — that does one of the following:

- **Accept** workflow-declared structured invocation as part of workflow
  composition and define the abstract call/return semantics: immediate caller
  context, suspended calling continuation, callee progression, normal return
  target, outer-continuation preservation, and the decision-owner distinction
  from ADR-008; or
- **Reject** declared invocation explicitly and provide a
  specification-consistent account of how the composition and expressive-power
  language is satisfied without it, including the meaning of `TL-INV-031`'s
  `nested workflow invocation` item.

Either outcome must reconcile Section 2.8's canonical definition with the
composition language and determine whether the ADR-008 path becomes an accepted
special case or a distinct path sharing abstract obligations.

Synchronization required by the accepted outcome (only what it actually
affects):

- `docs/specification/turnlock-spec.md`: affected Sections, canonical
  terminology registry, and invariant text. Prefer clarifying existing
  `TL-INV-008`, `TL-INV-016`–`TL-INV-019`, and `TL-INV-031`; mint a new
  `TL-INV-*` identity only under the invariant admission test.
- `docs/specification/terminology-inventory.yaml`: refresh entries and
  fingerprints for any moved definition-like occurrences.
- `docs/adr/`: new ADR; regenerate `docs/adr/index.md` through the ADR metadata
  tool.
- `formal/verification.yaml`: add or update intended mappings only as
  `planned` or `partial`; verification stays `not-yet-modeled`. Regenerate
  `docs/formal/invariant-mapping.md` from the manifest.
- No `formal/Turnlock.tla`, no TLC configuration, and no `checked` claim.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] The Section 2.8 canonical-definition conflict is explicitly resolved by a
  later ADR — either the concept is broadened/clarified or the term is scoped
  and the declared concept is named separately — rather than silently
  interpreted.
- [x] Workflow-declared and agent-selected invocation remain distinguished by
  decision owner even if a shared abstract invocation/return semantic is
  accepted.
- [x] For every admitted invocation, the immediate caller, suspended calling
  continuation, callee progression, and normal return target are defined at an
  implementation-independent level.
- [x] Suspension is not defined as unconditional whole-workflow suspension and
  is consistent with declared concurrent topology (`TL-INV-024`, `TL-INV-027`,
  ADR-013); parallel-placement admissibility remains with Issue #6 and is not
  decided here.
- [x] The semantics cover every admitted invocation; recursion/cycle
  admissibility is either explicitly deferred with its owning authority
  identified or decided with explicit authority; no concrete depth/resource
  limit is made normative.
- [x] Any A-class rule includes a complete derivation chain; every non-derived
  choice is recorded as B and decided through the accepted ADR process.
- [x] The composition/expressive-power language is reconciled whether declared
  invocation is accepted or rejected; `TL-INV-031`'s nested workflow invocation
  item is no longer ambiguous.
- [x] No accepted ADR body is edited; the decision is recorded in a later ADR.
- [x] Normative, terminology, traceability, and generated artifacts are
  synchronized; formal entries are only `planned`/`partial` and
  `not-yet-modeled`; the generated mapping and ADR index are regenerated.
- [x] No TLA+ variable/action name, DSL/API syntax, Rust type, caller-stack or
  frame representation, activation identifier, or process model is made
  normative.
- [x] Independent agents receive no workflow-invocation capability from this
  outcome; ADR-020/ADR-021 and `TL-INV-025`/`TL-INV-026` boundaries remain
  intact.
- [x] Repository-required validation is green, and the Issue and its Project
  item are re-read after every mutation.

## Dependencies

- **Readiness class:** resolve before the first core model whenever the model
  represents workflow-declared invocation; otherwise Issue #9 requires the
  behavior to be explicitly excluded from the model's declared scope.
- **Issue #6** (`Semantics: close execution restrictions under nested workflow
  composition`) depends on this Issue's decision and owns transitive
  composition/placement admissibility, including parallel branches and
  recursive/cyclic call-graph questions.
- **Issue #9** (`Formal verification: pre-TLA+ semantic readiness`) consumes
  this outcome for its safety-model readiness gate.
- No existing Issue owns the structured call/return semantic itself.

## Non-goals

- Deciding Issue #6's placement/admissibility rules (parallel branches,
  restricted contexts, transitive restrictions, recursion/cycle policy).
- Selecting concrete depth, resource, or safety limits.
- Defining failure, cancellation, interruption, timeout, or crash semantics.
- Selecting a TLA+ representation, state-variable names, actions, or
  configurations.
- Selecting workflow DSL syntax, a Rust invocation API, a literal call stack,

content.body:
## Problem

TURNLOCK workflows are developer-readable artifacts that developers and coding agents may edit. A main-agent region also restores ordinary coding-agent agency, which can include repository edits. The current specification does not decide which workflow definition governs an invocation that is already active when its source artifact changes.

```text
invoke workflow W from definition D1

W executes step 1

someone edits the workflow artifact:
D1 → D2

W reaches its next control transition

which topology governs the active invocation?
D1?
D2?
some explicitly mutated runtime definition?
```

Several behaviors remain compatible with the current prose. Encoding any one of them silently in the first state machine would make TLA+ the source of a product decision.

## Why this blocks the first TLA+ model

The first executable model must represent the workflow program as the source of declared topology and determine which transition is next. Without definition-binding semantics, the model cannot state whether the definition associated with an active invocation is stable, live, or explicitly mutable without inventing behavior.

Before the first core safety model, this ambiguity must either be resolved or explicitly excluded from the modeled behavior. The target readiness outcome is a decision rather than a permanent exclusion, because properties such as `DeclaredControlFlowOnly`, `EngineDoesNotInventTopology`, and `AgentCannotAdvanceUndeclaredGlobalControl` depend on knowing what “declared” means for an already-active invocation whenever definition changes are in scope.

## Existing authority

- `TL-INV-001` and ADR-014 make the workflow program the source of declared global orchestration and TURNLOCK the engine that executes it.
- `TL-INV-002` forbids the engine from changing declared topology or substituting undeclared global decisions.
- `TL-INV-013` forbids hidden agent-owned orchestration.
- ADR-009 and `TL-INV-020` require one editable workflow artifact class for developer and coding-agent authorship.
- ADR-016 and `TL-INV-032` separate workflow authorship from runtime execution authority.
- ADR-007 preserves ordinary main-agent agency, so edits during an active workflow cannot be dismissed as impossible.
- The normative specification does not currently define edit visibility for active invocations.

## Discovery classification

**B — New product or semantic decision.**

The Discovery Classification Protocol explicitly lists whether workflow edits become visible to already-running invocations as a B-class question. Stable binding may later support an A-class derived clarification or invariant, but it must not be assumed before the visibility decision is accepted.

```text
TLC/TLA+ needs a fixed transition relation
≠ TURNLOCK already requires snapshot binding
```

Mechanisms such as SHA-256 identifiers, Git revisions, filesystem snapshots, AST copies, databases, copy-on-write structures, or Rust fields are **D — implementation/architectural mechanisms** and are outside this decision.

## Semantic questions

Decide the abstract visibility/version semantics of a workflow definition for an accepted invocation:

1. What definition governs the invocation at acceptance/start?
2. Can ordinary artifact edits change the active invocation's remaining topology?
3. If changes are visible, at what semantic boundary and under what consistency rule?
4. If the definition is stable, how long does that binding last, including nested invocations?
5. Is explicit dynamic mutation a distinct future workflow operation rather than a side effect of editing the source artifact?
6. How does the decision preserve workflow-owned orchestration and prevent the runtime or author from silently inventing topology?
7. Does a nested invocation bind its own callee definition independently from its caller?

## Candidate interpretations / alternatives

### Stable definition binding for the invocation lifetime

An accepted invocation continues against one abstract definition even if its source artifact is edited. This gives a stable meaning to declared topology but does not prescribe how the implementation represents the binding.

### Live observation of artifact changes

An active invocation may observe edits. This requires an explicit semantic rule for when and how new topology becomes authoritative and how partially executed control flow remains coherent.

### Explicit dynamic mutation as a separate semantic operation

Ordinary source edits do not implicitly alter active invocations, but a future explicit workflow semantic could deliberately mutate or replace remaining topology. This is only an alternative to decide, not a primitive approved by this issue.

## Required outcome

Adopt one non-ambiguous abstract definition-binding contract, with rejected alternatives and consequences recorded. The result must let the future TLA+ model determine whether the definition associated with an active invocation can change, without selecting a storage, hashing, snapshotting, or language mechanism.

Record the accepted B-class decision in a new ADR; do not edit an accepted ADR body. Synchronize the normative specification and evaluate existing invariants before proposing any new derived invariant. Any applicable formal property enters `formal/verification.yaml` as `planned`, never `modeled` or `checked` from this decision alone.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] One normative definition-binding/visibility rule is accepted for active invocations.
- [ ] The rule defines the binding lifetime and the semantics of ordinary artifact edits during execution.
- [ ] Stable binding, live observation, and explicit dynamic mutation are evaluated, with rejected alternatives and consequences documented.
- [ ] Nested invocation behavior is addressed without pre-deciding workflow-to-workflow invocation syntax.
- [ ] The decision preserves workflow-owned orchestration and identifies what “declared topology” means for an active invocation.
- [ ] A new ADR records the B-class decision; no accepted ADR body is edited.
- [ ] The normative specification is synchronized.
- [ ] Existing invariants are evaluated to determine whether clarification is sufficient or whether an independently justified derived invariant candidate is needed under the admission test.
- [ ] Any applicable formal property is added to the verification manifest only as `planned`/`not-yet-modeled`, with the generated mapping refreshed.
- [ ] No implementation representation is made normative.
- [ ] Repository-required validation remains green.

## Dependencies

- **Readiness class:** MUST RESOLVE BEFORE FIRST CORE MODEL.
- No semantic prerequisite is currently known. Coordinate any manifest shape with [#1](https://github.com/fanilosendrison/turnlock-rust/issues/1), but do not let metamodel work decide the product semantics.

## Non-goals

- Choosing SHA-256, a Git commit SHA, filesystem/AST snapshots, copy-on-write, a database version, or a Rust field.
- Defining persistence, crash recovery, hot reload, deployment, or packaging.
- Designing a workflow DSL or mutation API.
- Creating a new `TL-INV-*` without the Discovery Classification Protocol and invariant admission test.
- Writing `formal/Turnlock.tla` in this issue.

## Validation

For any resulting repository change, regenerate affected projections and run:

```bash
.venv/bin/python scripts/adr-metadata.py render
.venv/bin/python scripts/render-formal-mapping.py
.venv/bin/python scripts/tests/test-adr-metadata.py
.venv/bin/python scripts/adr-metadata.py check
.venv/bin/python scripts/check-formal-traceability.py
git diff --check
```

## Relevant repository references

- [TURNLOCK normative specification](https://github.com/fanilosendrison/turnlock-rust/blob/main/docs/specification/turnlock-spec.md)
- [ADR-007 — main-agent continuity and ordinary agency](https://github.com/fanilosendrison/turnlock-rust/blob/main/docs/adr/adr-007-preserve-main-agent-cognitive-lineage-and-ordinary-interactive-agency.md)
- [ADR-009 — shared workflow artifact](https://github.com/fanilosendrison/turnlock-rust/blob/main/docs/adr/adr-009-use-the-same-turnlock-primitives-for-developer-and-agent-authored-workflows.md)
- [ADR-014 — workflow program and TURNLOCK engine](https://github.com/fanilosendrison/turnlock-rust/blob/main/docs/adr/adr-014-define-turnlock-as-the-orchestration-engine-and-the-workflow-as-the-orchestration-program.md)
- [ADR-016 — authorship versus execution authority](https://github.com/fanilosendrison/turnlock-rust/blob/main/docs/adr/adr-016-separate-workflow-authorship-from-runtime-execution-authority.md)
- [`formal/verification.yaml`](https://github.com/fanilosendrison/turnlock-rust/blob/main/formal/verification.yaml)
- [TURNLOCK Discovery Classification Protocol](https://github.com/fanilosendrison/turnlock-rust/blob/main/docs/repository-governance/turnlock-rust-discovery-classification.md)

content.body:
## Problem

TURNLOCK's composition rules are not yet closed under nested execution effects. ADR-013 intentionally does not authorize main-agent continuation as an ordinary parallel branch. It also does not currently authorize a workflow invocation as an ordinary parallel branch, so the following topology is a **hypothetical admissibility test**, not accepted syntax or semantics:

```text
parallel
├── mechanical branch
└── workflow B
      └── workflow C
            └── main-agent continuation
```

If a prior decision ever admits workflow invocation in a restricted context such as a parallel branch, a direct-only restriction could be bypassed by transitive behavior. Conversely, excluding workflow calls from that placement is itself an admissibility boundary that must be explicit rather than accidental. The same hazard applies to any already-authorized context where nesting can introduce a restricted execution form transitively.

## Why this blocks the first TLA+ model

The first model must decide which nested invocation transitions are admissible in each modeled context. If it checks only direct branch types, it may accidentally admit main-agent concurrency that the specification explicitly leaves open. If it rejects or serializes transitive effects without authority, it invents policy.

Before the first safety model, the admissibility boundary must be explicit: unsupported placements may be excluded, but the model must not accidentally admit them through an underspecified generic nesting transition.

## Existing authority

- ADR-013 and `TL-INV-024` authorize heterogeneous parallel branches for mechanical, raw-LLM, and independent-agent execution, while leaving main-agent continuation in parallel unresolved.
- ADR-008 defines agent-selected nested invocation and structured immediate-caller return.
- `TL-INV-017`–`TL-INV-019` require nested suspension, correct return, and outer-orchestration preservation.
- `TL-INV-031` requires nested workflow composition and expressive control without prescribing an implementation.
- ADR-014 requires TURNLOCK to execute declared topology without inventing a different one.
- ADR-022 accepts workflow-declared nested invocation, `TL-INV-035` carries the declared-invocation obligation, and ADR-023 clarifies caller-context and continuation semantics.

## Discovery classification

**Primary: B — New product or semantic decision.**

A candidate principle may be **A — Derived semantic requirement**:

```text
a compositional restriction cannot be bypassed merely by nesting
```

That A classification must be demonstrated with a derivation chain from the accepted restriction and composition semantics. The exact behavior when required transitive effects are not admissible—reject, validate earlier, serialize, lift capability, or allow under explicit rules—is not uniquely determined and therefore remains B.

An effect type system, capability lattice/bitmask, static compiler pass, runtime graph walk, or Rust trait design would be **C/D** machinery, not product semantics.

## Semantic questions

1. Which execution contexts impose local restrictions relevant to the first core model?
2. Are those restrictions closed transitively across already-authorized nested invocation paths?
3. In which placements, if any, may a workflow invocation occur inside a parallel branch or another restricted context? Sequential declared invocation does not imply parallel placement.
4. What abstract information about a workflow's possible execution forms is needed to determine admissibility?
5. When a callee may transitively require a disallowed form, is invocation rejected, conditionally admitted, serialized, or handled by another explicit semantic rule?
6. At what semantic point is admissibility determined: artifact acceptance, invocation, region entry, or another boundary?
7. How are recursive/cyclic call graphs treated abstractly without choosing a compiler/runtime algorithm?
8. How do structured return and outer-continuation preservation remain valid when invocation is rejected or not admitted?
9. Which questions must remain excluded from the first safety model rather than settled by convenience?

## Candidate interpretations / alternatives

- **Direct-only admissibility checks:** insufficient when an admitted callee can introduce restricted execution forms transitively.
- **Reject or exclude nested calls in restricted contexts:** valid if explicitly accepted or declared as a first-model scope exclusion.
- **Transitive admissibility contract:** evaluate a callee's possible execution forms against the caller context while leaving representation open.
- **Implicit serialization or capability lifting:** B-class alternatives that require explicit product authority and must not be selected by model convenience.

The analysis may use an implementation-independent relation such as:

```text
RequiredEffects(workflow)
AllowedEffects(execution-context)

RequiredEffects(workflow) ⊆ AllowedEffects(execution-context)
```

or an equivalent semantic abstraction. The issue must not make an “effect system” implementation normative.

## Required scope

Audit compositional closure for the first-model semantics of:

- parallel regions;
- agent-selected nested workflow invocation;
- workflow-declared nested invocation accepted by ADR-022;
- main-agent continuation;
- raw LLM inference;
- independent-agent execution;
- structured return and preservation of the caller's continuation.

Do not grant independent agents a workflow-invocation capability that current authority does not provide. Analyze only already-authorized invocation contexts, including the workflow-declared invocation accepted by ADR-022.

## Required outcome

Define an implementation-independent admissibility contract for nested composition. Local restrictions must have clear transitive meaning, and the first TLA+ model must be able to determine whether a nested invocation transition is admissible without deciding main-agent concurrency itself or selecting a capability/effect implementation.

Where the result is genuinely B, record the accepted decision in a later ADR and synchronize the specification/invariants/manifest. Where a rule is claimed as A, preserve the complete derivation chain required by the Discovery Classification Protocol.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The restricted-placement and transitive-admissibility outcome remains compatible with the accepted declared-invocation authority (ADR-022) and caller/continuation semantics (ADR-023), without re-deciding them.
- [ ] The accepted placement rules state explicitly whether workflow invocation is admissible in a parallel branch or any other restricted context; sequential declared invocation is not treated as sufficient authority.
- [ ] Every local execution-form restriction relevant to the first model has an explicit transitive composition rule or an explicit exclusion from the modeled state space.
- [ ] Composition cannot silently bypass the unresolved status of main-agent concurrency.
- [ ] The future model can determine when each authorized nested invocation is admissible.
- [ ] Agent-selected and workflow-declared invocation contexts remain distinguishable where decision ownership differs.
- [ ] Independent agents receive no new invocation capability without separate normative authority.
- [ ] Structured return and outer-continuation preservation remain defined for admitted invocations.
- [ ] Any A-class rule includes a valid derivation chain; every non-derived policy choice is treated as B.
- [ ] A new ADR is created if a B-class decision requires it; no accepted ADR body is edited.
- [ ] The normative specification, affected invariants, and planned formal traceability are synchronized.
- [ ] No effect type system, capability representation, compiler pass, Rust trait, or runtime algorithm is made normative.
- [ ] No main-agent concurrency feature, sibling workflow concurrency, failure propagation, or resource policy is decided.
- [ ] Repository-required validation remains green.

## Sequencing requirement

- **Readiness class:** MUST RESOLVE BEFORE FIRST CORE MODEL for restricted-placement and transitive admissibility.

## Non-goals

- Deciding whether main-agent continuation should be allowed concurrently.
- Designing a general workflow effect/capability type system.
- Granting workflows or agents new invocation powers beyond accepted semantics.
- Defining failure, cancellation, timeout, resource-budget, or crash-recovery behavior.
- Selecting DSL syntax, Rust traits, bitmasks, static analysis, or runtime validation algorithms.
- Writing `formal/Turnlock.tla` in this issue.

## Validation

For any resulting repository change, regenerate affected projections and run:

```bash
.venv/bin/python scripts/adr-metadata.py render
.venv/bin/python scripts/render-formal-mapping.py
.venv/bin/python scripts/tests/test-adr-metadata.py
.venv/bin/python scripts/adr-metadata.py check
.venv/bin/python scripts/check-formal-traceability.py
git diff --check
```

## Relevant repository references

- [TURNLOCK normative specification](https://github.com/fanilosendrison/turnlock-rust/blob/main/docs/specification/turnlock-spec.md)
- [ADR-008 — nested invocation and immediate-caller return](https://github.com/fanilosendrison/turnlock-rust/blob/main/docs/adr/adr-008-allow-nested-workflow-invocation-from-main-agent-regions.md)
- [ADR-013 — heterogeneous parallel fan-out](https://github.com/fanilosendrison/turnlock-rust/blob/main/docs/adr/adr-013-allow-heterogeneous-parallel-fan-out-across-execution-forms.md)
- [ADR-014 — workflow program and TURNLOCK engine](https://github.com/fanilosendrison/turnlock-rust/blob/main/docs/adr/adr-014-define-turnlock-as-the-orchestration-engine-and-the-workflow-as-the-orchestration-program.md)
- [`formal/verification.yaml`](https://github.com/fanilosendrison/turnlock-rust/blob/main/formal/verification.yaml)

content.body:
## Problem

TURNLOCK repeatedly uses `bounded` in different contexts:

```text
bounded raw LLM inference
bounded independent-agent execution
bounded context
bounded autonomous work
```

The word can refer to materially different properties:

```text
bounded authority
bounded structural region
bounded context
bounded lifecycle
bounded turns/tokens/tool calls/cost/time
or guaranteed termination
```

These meanings must not be conflated in the first model. In particular, a structurally bounded execution region does not automatically imply a concrete resource budget or universal eventual completion.

## Why this blocks the first TLA+ model

The first state machine must represent raw-LLM and independent-agent regions as distinct execution forms with local authority and workflow-owned continuation. If `bounded` is left ambiguous, the model may accidentally assume termination, finite turns, timeouts, or fixed resource limits merely to keep the state space finite.

The model needs the minimum structural semantics required by `RawLLMIsBoundedLeaf`, independent-agent properties, and execution-form distinction while leaving budgets and liveness out of the safety-only scope.

## Existing authority

- ADR-011 and `TL-INV-025` define independent agents as first-class bounded cognitive lineages that perform autonomous multi-turn work and return a result to workflow progression.
- `TL-INV-026` requires task-specific/explicitly scoped context rather than implicit full main-agent lineage inheritance; the manifest marks the formalization partial.
- ADR-012 and `TL-INV-028` define raw LLM inference as a bounded, non-agentic semantic operation distinct from agents and main-agent continuation.
- `TL-INV-012` requires execution forms to remain non-equivalent.
- `TL-INV-030` preserves workflow-owned global control around probabilistic leaves.
- The specification leaves model/provider budgets, context construction, lifecycle limits, failure, cancellation, and timeouts open.

## Discovery classification

**Primary: A — Derived semantic clarification for the minimum structural/authority meaning.**

The following appear derivable and must be verified through a recorded derivation chain:

- raw LLM inference is a non-agentic leaf rather than an autonomous observe/reason/act loop;
- an independent agent is a distinct cognitive lineage with autonomous multi-turn local execution;
- neither form acquires undeclared global workflow authority;
- context may be deliberately scoped;
- workflow progression owns the continuation after the region if/when it completes.

Subproblems such as guaranteed termination or normative maximum turns/tokens/time are **B** if they change product semantics. Concrete counters, timeouts, quotas, provider settings, or runtime budget fields are **D** mechanisms. Finite TLA+ bounds used only for model checking are **C** and must not be promoted into product requirements.

```text
TLC needs finite bounds
≠ TURNLOCK normatively requires that concrete resource limit
```

## Semantic questions

### Raw LLM inference

1. Does `bounded` minimally mean one declared non-agentic inference region with explicit input/context and one result boundary?
2. Which lifecycle distinction prevents it from becoming an autonomous agent loop?
3. Does structural boundedness imply anything about provider retries, latency, tokens, or guaranteed completion? Do not assume that it does.

### Independent-agent execution

1. Does `bounded` minimally constrain authority/task/context while allowing autonomous multi-turn work?
2. What is local to the region, and what global progression authority remains with the workflow?
3. What does “returns a result” mean conditionally if/when the region completes, without claiming universal termination?
4. Which context-scoping guarantee is normative versus left to implementation and conformance?

### Cross-cutting

1. Which meanings belong in the first safety model?
2. Which liveness questions must remain with #2?
3. Which resource and failure semantics remain intentionally abstract/out of scope?

## Candidate interpretations / alternatives

- **Structural/authority boundedness:** the region has an explicit place in the workflow, local execution authority, and a continuation/result boundary; it cannot take undeclared global control.
- **Context boundedness:** selected task context may be scoped independently from the main-agent lineage.
- **Resource boundedness:** explicit numerical/time/cost/tool limits; deferred unless separately decided.
- **Termination boundedness:** universal eventual completion; not implied and must be handled by the liveness/fairness issue.

The final clarification may use different terms if that avoids overloading `bounded`.

## Required outcome

Define the minimum normative meaning of `bounded` separately for raw-LLM and independent-agent regions, and identify which dimensions remain open. The result must let a safety-only TLA+ model represent `Start...`/`Complete...` transitions and authority boundaries without claiming that completion universally occurs or selecting concrete budgets.

Identify the semantic consequences for `RawLLMIsBoundedLeaf`, `IndependentAgentCanBeWorkflowDeclared`, `IndependentAgentHasDistinctLineage`, and `IndependentAgentContextIsExplicitlyDeclared`. Feed those conclusions to #1, which owns property-level metamodel migration and status handling.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `bounded` has an explicit minimum semantic meaning for raw-LLM inference.
- [ ] `bounded` has an explicit, separately stated minimum semantic meaning for independent-agent execution.
- [ ] Raw LLM remains one bounded non-agentic semantic operation with no autonomous observe/reason/act loop or persistent independent lineage.
- [ ] Independent-agent execution may remain autonomous and multi-turn within its declared local region and distinct lineage.
- [ ] Neither form acquires undeclared global workflow authority.
- [ ] Context scoping, structural region boundaries, resource budgets, and termination/liveness are not conflated.
- [ ] No maximum turns, tokens, tool calls, cost, wall-clock time, timeout, cancellation behavior, or provider setting is selected.
- [ ] The clarification does not imply universal completion of raw-LLM or independent-agent regions; liveness/fairness remains coordinated with #2.
- [ ] Finite model-checking bounds are identified as C-class modeling choices rather than product requirements.
- [ ] The future safety model can represent the structural transitions and authority boundaries without inventing resource or liveness semantics.
- [ ] Consequences for `RawLLMIsBoundedLeaf`, `IndependentAgentCanBeWorkflowDeclared`, `IndependentAgentHasDistinctLineage`, and `IndependentAgentContextIsExplicitlyDeclared` are recorded for #1 without duplicating its metamodel migration.
- [ ] The complete A-class derivation records accepted sources, reasoning, why no new product choice is introduced, and a failure/counterexample if the clarification is omitted.
- [ ] Any B-class discovery is routed through a later decision/ADR; no accepted ADR body is edited.
- [ ] Normative/formal traceability and generated projections are synchronized.
- [ ] Repository-required validation remains green.

## Dependencies

- **Feeds [#1](https://github.com/fanilosendrison/turnlock-rust/issues/1):** this semantic clarification is independently executable; #1 consumes its conclusions for affected property classification.
- **Related, not blocking the first safety model:** [#2](https://github.com/fanilosendrison/turnlock-rust/issues/2) owns occurrence-scoped liveness/fairness and the question of universal eventual completion.
- **Readiness class:** MUST RESOLVE BEFORE FIRST CORE MODEL.

## Non-goals

- Selecting concrete resource budgets, timeouts, quotas, retries, failure handling, or cancellation semantics.
- Claiming guaranteed termination for any execution form.
- Resolving activation-scoped liveness/fairness.
- Choosing provider APIs, agent runtimes, context formats, DSL syntax, or Rust fields.
- Treating TLC finite bounds as normative runtime limits.
- Writing `formal/Turnlock.tla` in this issue.

## Validation

For any resulting repository change, regenerate affected projections as applicable and run:

```bash
.venv/bin/python scripts/adr-metadata.py render
.venv/bin/python scripts/render-formal-mapping.py
.venv/bin/python scripts/tests/test-adr-metadata.py
.venv/bin/python scripts/adr-metadata.py check
.venv/bin/python scripts/check-formal-traceability.py
git diff --check
```

## Relevant repository references

- [TURNLOCK normative specification](https://github.com/fanilosendrison/turnlock-rust/blob/main/docs/specification/turnlock-spec.md)
- [ADR-007 — main-agent execution semantics](https://github.com/fanilosendrison/turnlock-rust/blob/main/docs/adr/adr-007-preserve-main-agent-cognitive-lineage-and-ordinary-interactive-agency.md)
- [ADR-011 — independent-agent execution](https://github.com/fanilosendrison/turnlock-rust/blob/main/docs/adr/adr-011-make-independent-agents-first-class-and-support-parallel-fan-out-fan-in.md)

content.body:
## Problem

The normative corpus uses several related but non-equivalent expressions:

```text
deterministic computation
deterministic orchestration
deterministic orchestrator
mechanical execution
workflow-owned control
```

A mechanical step may invoke an external command, wait for an event, read environment state, or produce a result that is not mathematically deterministic. A workflow may also branch on a probabilistic result while still selecting only among authored transitions.

TURNLOCK's central guarantee is primarily that known orchestration decisions are represented by workflow semantics and are not delegated to agent recollection or judgment—not necessarily that equal inputs always produce identical outputs or traces.

## Why this blocks the first TLA+ model

TLA+ specifications naturally contain nondeterminism. If “deterministic” is translated as one enabled successor, deterministic outputs, or deterministic replay, the first model may prove a stronger property than TURNLOCK promises and exclude valid external/probabilistic behavior.

The intended meaning must be clear before formalizing `DeclaredControlFlowOnly`, `EngineDoesNotInventTopology`, `MechanicalExecutionNotAgentMediated`, `AgentCannotAdvanceUndeclaredGlobalControl`, and `ProbabilisticLeafCannotOwnGlobalControl`.

## Existing authority

- `TL-INV-001` and `TL-INV-002` define ownership of declared orchestration decisions and separate the workflow program from engine execution.
- `TL-INV-003` defines mechanical execution as non-agent-mediated and permits a defined non-success outcome.
- `TL-INV-013` rejects hidden agent interpretation/scheduling.
- Specification §0.10D and `TL-INV-030` explicitly state that deterministic orchestration is compatible with probabilistic leaves.
- ADR-012 says deterministic orchestration does not require deterministic leaf computations.
- ADR-014 distinguishes authored topology from runtime execution machinery.
- Some broader phrases such as “deterministic computation/orchestrator” remain capable of a stronger mathematical reading.

## Discovery classification

**A — Derived semantic clarification, subject to a complete derivation check.**

### Derivation chain

1. TURNLOCK's product intent moves known control-flow decisions from agent memory/judgment into executable workflow logic.
2. `TL-INV-003` defines the relevant mechanical boundary by execution authority, not by identical outputs.
3. `TL-INV-001`, `TL-INV-002`, and `TL-INV-013` constrain who may choose global progression.
4. `TL-INV-030` and ADR-012 explicitly permit probabilistic leaves under workflow-owned control.
5. Therefore “deterministic orchestration” cannot generally mean deterministic leaf output or a single mathematically deterministic execution trace without contradicting accepted semantics.

If the terminology audit finds accepted wording that genuinely requires mathematical determinism, stop and reclassify the conflict rather than rewriting it silently. TLA+'s convenience is not authority to weaken or strengthen the promise.

## Semantic questions

1. Which uses of `deterministic` describe control ownership, transition selection, output repeatability, or a truly deterministic computation?
2. What is the minimum normative meaning of `mechanical`?
3. Can a mechanical region wait for or read nondeterministic external state while remaining non-agent-mediated?
4. How should a declared branch over probabilistic input be described without calling its output deterministic?
5. Which terms should be used for workflow-declared topology versus execution-resource behavior?
6. Do any planned TLA+ property names encode an unintended mathematical-determinism claim?

## Candidate interpretations / alternatives

- **Mathematical/output determinism everywhere:** rejected because accepted semantics permit probabilistic leaves and externally varying mechanical results.
- **One-successor deterministic transition relation:** rejected as an unsupported strengthening and an unnecessary restriction on TLA+ nondeterminism.
- **Control-authority terminology:** distinguish workflow-declared/workflow-owned control from output, replay, or trace determinism.

Candidate terminology under the third interpretation:

- **workflow-declared / workflow-owned control:** orchestration choices and topology originate in the workflow artifact.
- **non-agent-mediated / mechanical:** progression follows executable semantics rather than agent recollection or discretionary interpretation.
- **deterministic computation:** reserve for operations whose semantics actually justify mathematical/output determinism, if the term remains useful.
- **probabilistic:** output or local behavior may vary while global transition authority remains declared.

These are candidate consolidations to audit, not a license to rewrite accepted ADR bodies.

## Required outcome

Produce one consistent normative vocabulary that separates control ownership from output/trace determinism and is precise enough to formalize the affected invariants without accidental strengthening. Preserve historical ADR bodies; use a later ADR only if an accepted decision must change rather than merely be consolidated in the normative specification.

Record which planned property names/descriptions #1 must re-evaluate. The actual property-level metamodel migration remains owned by #1, avoiding duplicate implementation scope.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Every normative use of `deterministic`, `mechanical`, `workflow-declared`, `workflow-owned`, `non-agent-mediated`, and `probabilistic` relevant to the first model is inventoried and classified.
- [ ] The A-class derivation is documented, or any conflicting non-derived meaning is explicitly reclassified and escalated.
- [ ] Normative terminology clearly separates control/decision ownership from mathematical output or trace determinism.
- [ ] Mechanical execution is defined without assuming that every external command, event, or result is mathematically deterministic.
- [ ] Declared branching on probabilistic results remains compatible with workflow-owned control.
- [ ] `TL-INV-001`, `002`, `003`, `013`, and `030` can be formalized without guessing which meaning applies.
- [ ] Planned property names/formulations requiring re-evaluation are identified and handed to #1; this issue does not duplicate #1's property-level migration.
- [ ] No new guarantee of identical outputs, deterministic replay, or one-successor state transitions is introduced.
- [ ] No accepted ADR body is edited; any true decision change uses a later ADR.
- [ ] Normative/formal traceability and generated projections are synchronized.
- [ ] Repository-required validation remains green.

## Dependencies

- **Feeds [#1](https://github.com/fanilosendrison/turnlock-rust/issues/1):** this semantic clarification is independently executable; #1 consumes its outcome when classifying affected properties.
- **Readiness class:** MUST RESOLVE BEFORE FIRST CORE MODEL.

## Non-goals

- Requiring deterministic outputs, replay, command results, environment reads, or scheduler ordering.
- Selecting a workflow DSL, evaluator, scheduler, or Rust representation.
- Defining failure, retry, timeout, cancellation, or observability behavior.
- Editing accepted ADR bodies.
- Writing `formal/Turnlock.tla` in this issue.

## Validation

For any resulting repository change, regenerate affected projections as applicable and run:

```bash
.venv/bin/python scripts/adr-metadata.py render
.venv/bin/python scripts/render-formal-mapping.py
.venv/bin/python scripts/tests/test-adr-metadata.py
.venv/bin/python scripts/adr-metadata.py check
.venv/bin/python scripts/check-formal-traceability.py
git diff --check
```

## Relevant repository references

- [TURNLOCK normative specification](https://github.com/fanilosendrison/turnlock-rust/blob/main/docs/specification/turnlock-spec.md)
- [ADR-012 — probabilistic leaves under deterministic orchestration](https://github.com/fanilosendrison/turnlock-rust/blob/main/docs/adr/adr-012-make-bounded-raw-llm-inference-first-class-and-allocate-minimum-sufficient-cognition.md)
- [ADR-014 — workflow program and TURNLOCK engine](https://github.com/fanilosendrison/turnlock-rust/blob/main/docs/adr/adr-014-define-turnlock-as-the-orchestration-engine-and-the-workflow-as-the-orchestration-program.md)
- [Issue #1 — property-level verification obligations](https://github.com/fanilosendrison/turnlock-rust/issues/1)
- [`formal/verification.yaml`](https://github.com/fanilosendrison/turnlock-rust/blob/main/formal/verification.yaml)

content.body:
## Problem

The repository has no executable `formal/Turnlock.tla`, TLC configuration, or successful TLC result evidence. Before the first model is authored, the formal metamodel and several semantic ambiguities must be resolved or explicitly excluded from the model's declared scope.

Without one readiness tracker, work can start from planned property names while silently choosing product behavior for workflow-definition changes, nested invocation, composition admissibility, deterministic terminology, bounded cognition, or liveness.

## Why this matters for the first TLA+ model

The first model should be a deliberately scoped safety model, not an accidental mixture of safety, reachability, universal liveness, implementation mechanisms, and unresolved product choices. This tracker defines the pre-model gate and keeps liveness readiness separate from safety-model readiness.

It does not authorize `formal/Turnlock.tla`; it records when the authoritative prerequisites and explicit exclusions are sufficient for a separately scoped modeling task.

## Existing authority

- The normative specification and accepted ADRs own TURNLOCK product meaning.
- ADR-015 requires normative and formal artifacts to evolve together without treating planned mappings as verification evidence.
- `formal/verification.yaml` currently records planned properties but no executable formulas.
- `formal/tlc-result.schema.json` currently records run-level evidence but does not yet provide the property-level obligation/evidence semantics tracked by #1.
- The Discovery Classification Protocol requires B-class ambiguities to be decided, abstracted over, or explicitly excluded; TLC convenience cannot decide them.
- ADR-022 accepts workflow-declared nested invocation; ADR-023 clarifies caller-context and continuation semantics; `TL-INV-035` carries the declared-invocation obligation.

## Discovery classification

**C — Formal modeling and readiness choice.** The safety-only boundary, explicit exclusions, dependency graph, and readiness checklist govern how accepted semantics are prepared for formal representation. This tracker creates no TURNLOCK product semantics.

The underlying discoveries keep their own classifications:

- property-level formal metamodel and evidence semantics: C (#1);
- product-level liveness meaning: primarily B, with per-property A derivations
  possible (#2);
- occurrence-scoped formal representation: C (#3);
- active-invocation definition visibility and binding: decided by ADR-027,
  ADR-028, and `TL-INV-037`; whether definition edits are modeled remains a
  C-class model-scope choice;
- declared workflow-to-workflow invocation: accepted by ADR-022 and clarified
  by ADR-023; whether the accepted behavior is modeled remains a C-class
  model-scope choice;
- transitive composition admissibility: B with a possible A non-bypass
  principle (#6);
- deterministic-control terminology: A (#7);
- bounded execution-form semantics: primarily A, with B/C/D subproblems kept
  separate (#8).

## Open readiness questions

1. What is the smallest safety-only state space that still exercises TURNLOCK's core authority, handoff, nesting, execution-form, and parallel-join invariants?
2. Which unresolved B-class behaviors must be decided for that state space, and which may be explicitly excluded without weakening a claimed property?
3. Which planned properties are safety, liveness, reachability, or mixed obligations under #1's metamodel?
4. Which occurrence or fairness semantics are deliberately deferred to #2 and #3?
5. What assumptions and exclusions must appear in the future model/configuration documentation so they cannot be mistaken for normative behavior?

## Alternatives

### Model all planned behavior immediately

Rejected as a readiness strategy. It would force unresolved liveness and semantic choices into the first state machine and blur the evidence boundary.

### Wait for every liveness and implementation question

Rejected for the first safety model. #2 and #3 are required before encoding or claiming liveness, but they do not prevent a model whose declared scope is safety-only.

### Begin with an explicit safety-only boundary

Preferred. Resolve the semantic prerequisites exercised by the model, explicitly exclude undecided behavior, and preserve deferred liveness and mechanism questions as tracked work.

## Readiness gates

The first safety model requires the following semantic inputs. Each gate is a
stable condition on the model's declared scope, not a live status of another
work item.

### Verification-metamodel gate

The property-level obligation, verification-mode, fairness, and evidence
metamodel must exist before any property is reported as modeled or checked
(#1).

### Definition-binding gate

The first-model scope must consume the then-current accepted definition-binding
semantics (ADR-027, ADR-028, `TL-INV-037`) or explicitly exclude behavior
outside its declared state space.

### Declared-invocation gate

The first-model scope must either include the declared workflow-to-workflow
invocation behavior accepted by ADR-022 and clarified by ADR-023, including
`TL-INV-035`, or record an explicit C-class model-scope exclusion.

### Composition-admissibility gate

Every restricted context in which nested invocation is admitted must have an
explicit transitive composition rule or an explicit model-scope exclusion
(#6).

### Terminology gate

The model must use terminology that separates workflow-owned or
non-agent-mediated control from output or trace determinism (#7 clarification).

### Bounded-execution gate

The minimum structural and authority meaning of bounded raw-LLM and
independent-agent regions must be defined without implying resource limits or
universal completion (#8 clarification).

### Liveness gate

No liveness formula, fairness assumption, or progress claim may appear in the
model or its configuration until the product-level liveness guarantees and
occurrence scope (#2) and their occurrence-scoped formal representation (#3)
are authoritative.

## Required outcome

Produce a reviewable readiness record for the first safety model that:

1. identifies the exact authoritative semantic subset to model;
2. confirms the obligation and evidence metamodel is available before any
   modeled or checked claim;
3. consumes the authoritative deterministic-terminology and
   bounded-execution-form clarifications;
4. either consumes the accepted definition-binding, declared-invocation, and
   composition-admissibility outcomes or names the corresponding behaviors as
   explicit non-normative exclusions;
5. excludes liveness formulas and fairness assumptions until product-level
   liveness semantics and their occurrence-scoped formal representation are
   complete;
6. lists model-only abstractions and finite bounds as C-class choices rather
   than product requirements;
7. authorizes no runtime, Rust, API, DSL, persistence, or harness mechanism.

## READY-BEFORE-FIRST-SAFETY-MODEL

- [ ] The first-model scope consumes the then-current accepted definition-binding
      semantics or explicitly excludes behavior outside its declared state
      space.
- [ ] The first-model scope identifies every represented invariant or property
      and every planned property intentionally left outside the model.
- [ ] The first-model scope contains no liveness formula, fairness assumption,
      or universal progress claim.
- [ ] Every semantic behavior exercised by the model has accepted authority or an
      explicit model-scope exclusion.
- [ ] The property-level obligation and verification-mode metamodel is available
      before any modeled or checked claim.
- [ ] The first-model scope consumes the current authoritative terminology for
      workflow-owned and non-agent-mediated control without implying output or
      trace determinism.
- [ ] The minimum structural and authority meaning of bounded raw-LLM and
      independent-agent regions is consumed without implying resource limits or
      universal completion.
- [ ] Every restricted context in which nested invocation is admitted has an
      explicit transitive composition rule or an explicit model-scope exclusion.
- [ ] Declared workflow-to-workflow invocation behavior is either represented or
      explicitly excluded as a C-class model-scope choice.
- [ ] Model identities, sequences, stacks, opaque cognition values, and finite
      instance bounds are documented as C-class abstractions only.
- [ ] Every remaining B-class semantic choice is decided, abstracted over, or
      explicitly excluded before the model is authored.
- [ ] A separately scoped Issue owns executable model work before model
      authoring begins; this tracker is not treated as implementation
      authorization.

## Deferred beyond first model

The first safety-only model does **not** require resolution or implementation of:

- #2's universal/conditional liveness decisions when all liveness claims are excluded;
- #3's occurrence-scoped fairness encoding;
- `WF` versus `SF`, fairness profiles, actor/environment progress assumptions, or liveness TLC evidence;
- runtime UUIDs, activation IDs, counters, tokens, handles, or concrete stack representations;
- exact turns, tokens, tool calls, cost, wall-clock limits, provider settings, retries, timeout, cancellation, failure propagation, or guaranteed termination;
- main-agent concurrency, sibling workflow concurrency, or workflow invocation as a parallel branch unless separately accepted;
- workflow DSL/API syntax, Rust crate/runtime architecture, persistence, packaging, release, or harness-specific conformance;
- stress-profile bounds, exhaustive coverage claims, or successful verification claims.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The readiness record identifies the exact authoritative semantic subset
      that the first safety model may represent.
- [ ] The record confirms the property-level obligation and evidence metamodel
      is available before any modeled or checked claim.
- [ ] The record consumes the current authoritative control-terminology and
      bounded-execution-form semantics.
- [ ] Every semantic behavior exercised by the declared state space has accepted
      authority or an explicit model-scope exclusion.
- [ ] The record contains no liveness formula, fairness assumption, or liveness
      claim.
- [ ] The safety-model checklist distinguishes hard prerequisites from behaviors
      that may be explicitly excluded under the Discovery Classification
      Protocol.
- [ ] Model-only abstractions and finite bounds are recorded as C-class choices
      rather than product requirements.
- [ ] The record names the separately scoped modeling work required before
      executable model authoring.
- [ ] Deferred topics are retained without becoming requirements for the first
      safety model.
- [ ] No accepted ADR, invariant, model, API, DSL, runtime identity, or
      repository file is created or modified by this tracking task.
- [ ] A final re-read confirms the tracker states only stable semantic inputs and
      mirrors no live work state.

## Required semantic inputs

The tracker consumes these stable semantic inputs. Grouping expresses the
gating class, not the current state of any work item.

### Hard readiness inputs

- property-level obligation, verification-mode, fairness, and evidence
  semantics from the verification metamodel (#1);
- authoritative terminology separating workflow-owned or non-agent-mediated
  control from output or trace determinism (#7);
- minimum structural and authority meaning of bounded raw-LLM and
  independent-agent regions (#8).

### Conditional semantic inputs

- active-invocation definition binding: required if definition edits are
  represented; otherwise the behavior must be explicitly excluded. The accepted
  semantics are ADR-027, ADR-028, and `TL-INV-037`;
- declared workflow-to-workflow invocation: include the behavior accepted by
  ADR-022 and clarified by ADR-023, or record an explicit C-class scope
  exclusion;
- transitive composition admissibility: required for every restricted context
  in which nested invocation is admitted (#6).

### Liveness-only inputs

- product-level liveness guarantees and occurrence scope (#2);
- occurrence-scoped formal representation consuming the verification
  metamodel (#3).

## Non-goals

- Writing or approving `formal/Turnlock.tla`.
- Deciding any child Issue's B-class product question in the tracker.
- Promoting a planned property to `modeled` or `checked`.
- Treating the tracker or Project fields as semantic or verification authority.
- Creating an ADR, invariant, runtime mechanism, API, DSL, Rust artifact, or harness requirement.
- Modifying any repository file.

## Validation

This tracker itself changes only GitHub Issue/Project metadata. When its child Issues later change repository artifacts, use the current repository-required sequence and regenerate affected projections:

```bash
.venv/bin/python scripts/adr-metadata.py render
.venv/bin/python scripts/render-formal-mapping.py
.venv/bin/python scripts/tests/test-adr-metadata.py
.venv/bin/python scripts/adr-metadata.py check
.venv/bin/python scripts/check-formal-traceability.py
git diff --check
```

## Relevant repository references

- [TURNLOCK normative specification](https://github.com/fanilosendrison/turnlock-rust/blob/main/docs/specification/turnlock-spec.md)
- [ADR-015 — evolve normative and formal specifications together](https://github.com/fanilosendrison/turnlock-rust/blob/main/docs/adr/adr-015-evolve-the-normative-and-formal-specifications-together.md)
- [Formal verification policy](https://github.com/fanilosendrison/turnlock-rust/blob/main/docs/formal/README.md)
- [Formal workspace status](https://github.com/fanilosendrison/turnlock-rust/blob/main/formal/README.md)
- [`formal/verification.yaml`](https://github.com/fanilosendrison/turnlock-rust/blob/main/formal/verification.yaml)
- [`formal/tlc-result.schema.json`](https://github.com/fanilosendrison/turnlock-rust/blob/main/formal/tlc-result.schema.json)
- [TURNLOCK Discovery Classification Protocol](https://github.com/fanilosendrison/turnlock-rust/blob/main/docs/repository-governance/turnlock-rust-discovery-classification.md)
- [Turnlock-Rust Engineering Project](https://github.com/users/fanilosendrison/projects/5)
